A formal, well-maintained academy with professional training grounds and rescue exercise facilities. Enhanced security measures include reinforced shelters for civilians and families. Connected by underground tunnels to allied schools, the campus reflects institutional pride through uniformed students and official logos displayed prominently throughout. During wartime, portions serve as fortified civilian refuges with emergency protocols.

cardPool.title: Heights Alliance
cardPool.value:
Name: Heights Alliance Dormitory Complex

Location: U.A. High School campus, Musutafu, Japan. Five separate five-story residential buildings, one per class, arranged within walking distance of the main school building.

Inhabitants: Young hero students (ages 15-17) of U.A. High School, organized by class. Each building houses approximately twenty students divided by gender into left (male) and right (female) wings. Teachers conduct regular surveillance and maintain order.

Appearance: Large, modern residential buildings with white first floors and brown upper levels, each marked with the class designation and "Alliance" signage. Low hedge borders frame the main entrance, flanked by park benches and illuminated towers. Each building features a courtyard and is accessible via double doors. Interior common areas on the ground floor include lounges, kitchens, bathrooms, and laundry facilities. Upper floors (2-5) contain eight individual student rooms per floor—four per gender per side—each equipped with air conditioning, private bathrooms, beds, refrigerators, closets, and balconies. Rooms vary in decor based on student customization.

cardPool.title: Musutafu, Japan
cardPool.value:
Name:
Musutafu

Location:
A sprawling coastal city in modern-day Japan, nestled between mountains and the sea. Known as the academic and cultural heart of the region, with both traditional temples and contemporary urban architecture.

Inhabitants:
Diverse population of Japanese citizens, students, merchants, and travelers. Home to prestigious schools and training academies that attract scholars and ambitious individuals from across the nation.

Appearance:
Bustling streets blend neon-lit storefronts with historic wooden structures and stone temples. The harbor gleams with fishing vessels and merchant ships, while tree-lined avenues lead to educational districts where young people gather. Mountains loom in the distance, their slopes dotted with shrines and observation points overlooking the glittering city below.

cardPool.title: Ketsubutsu Academy High School
cardPool.value:
Name: Ketsubutsu Academy High School

Location: A prestigious hero training academy rival to U.A. High, known for competitive excellence in the Provisional Hero License Exam preliminaries and rigorous fieldwork training.

Inhabitants: Ambitious students training to become Pro Heroes, including Class 2-2 led by Yo Shindo; Ms. Joke serves as Second Year Class 2 teacher and maintains the school's fierce rivalry tradition.

Appearance: Modern academic campus featuring training facilities and rescue exercise arenas. Students wear gray polo shirts with striped ties or bows, dark trousers and skirts, and blazers bearing the school logo. During training, students don white and blue tracksuits. The school exudes competitive atmosphere with well-maintained equipment for hands-on hero preparation.

cardPool.title: Tartarus
cardPool.value:
Name: Tartarus

Location: A fortified island prison situated five kilometers offshore, accessible only via a monitored bridge through the Bronze Gate. The facility extends 500 meters below sea level, divided into six cell blocks across multiple levels, with the most dangerous inmates confined to the deepest tier, B10.

Inhabitants: The "worst of the worst" Quirk users deemed threats to society—murderers, psychopaths, defectors, and individuals with catastrophically dangerous abilities. Each prisoner is classified by threat level and confined accordingly. Guards and monitoring personnel operate under strict protocols with authorization for lethal force.

Appearance: Imposing fortress of reinforced steel and blast doors with narrow, heavily armored corridors. Prisoners sit immobilized in high-tech restraint chairs with full-body straitjackets. Ceiling-mounted automated machine guns, continuous biometric sensors, and observation screens dominate the interior. Surrounding walls tower above a checkpoint-controlled bridge. The deeper levels are austere, oppressive concrete bunkers sealed beneath the ocean floor.

cardPool.title: Aldera Junior High
cardPool.value:
Name: Aldera Junior High
Location: A sprawling educational complex in a bustling town district, situated between residential neighborhoods and commercial streets, with athletic fields extending behind the main brick building.
Inhabitants: Hundreds of students aged 11-14, dozens of teachers and staff members, custodians, cafeteria workers, and occasional visiting parents or administrators.
Appearance: A multi-story brick structure with long hallways, rows of classrooms with large windows, a gymnasium, cafeteria, library, and administrative offices. Lockers line the corridors, bulletin boards display student work, and the grounds feature basketball courts, soccer fields, and a playground area. The building shows signs of wear from constant use, with polished floors and walls decorated with school spirit posters and student achievements.

cardPool.title: Captain Celebrity Corporation HQ
cardPool.value:
Name: Captain Celebrity Corporation Headquarters

Location: Urban metropolis, towering above surrounding cityscape

Inhabitants: Corporate staff, mission coordinators, elite heroes awaiting deployment, Captain Celebrity and associates

Appearance: A gleaming skyscraper with the Captain Celebrity logo emblazoned across its crown. The top floor features a retractable launch pad that extends when heroes receive urgent mission assignments, allowing them to launch skyward instantly. The interior suggests luxury and cutting-edge technology, befitting an organization of heroes and their support infrastructure.

cardPool.title: Central Hospital
cardPool.value:
Name: Central Hospital

Location: A towering medical facility dominating the city center, rising above surrounding buildings with modern architecture and reinforced security infrastructure.

Inhabitants: Doctors, nurses, Recovery Girl, police guards, Hero patients recovering from war wounds, imprisoned spies under interrogation, comatose subjects in restorative research, and occasional villainous assault forces.

Appearance: A sprawling complex of sterile white corridors and advanced medical wards equipped with cutting-edge treatment technology and specialized containment rooms. Multiple security checkpoints and reinforced sections house dangerous patients and experimental subjects. Emergency rooms overflow with intensive care units, research laboratories, and secure holding cells beneath the main hospital.

cardPool.title: Conference Room
cardPool.value:
Name:
U.A. High School Conference Room

Location:
A prestigious hero academy's administrative wing, serving as the primary meeting place for faculty and staff during emergencies and strategic planning sessions.

Inhabitants:
Faculty members of U.A. High School, including Present Mic and other veteran instructors; occasionally attended by administrative staff during crisis management discussions.

Appearance:
A spacious, professional room with light blue walls and large pane glass windows overlooking academy grounds. A central conference table—constructed from three joined desks—is surrounded by numerous chairs. Potted plants provide subtle greenery throughout the space, creating a calm atmosphere despite its use for high-stakes security discussions and tactical planning sessions.

cardPool.title: Deika City
cardPool.value:
Name: Deika City

Location: A mountain stronghold nestled in remote highlands with limited entrance and exit routes, surrounded by dense natural terrain ideal for concealment and defense.

Inhabitants: Approximately 90% of the population are soldiers dedicated to the Liberation Army cause, including civilians who have embraced the movement; the city operates as a militarized society under unified command.

Appearance: A moderately-sized fortified city dominated by a imposing central tower that serves as the military headquarters, with architecture integrated into the mountainous landscape and natural vegetation providing camouflage and strategic advantage.

cardPool.title: Detnerat
cardPool.value:
Name: Detnerat Manufacturing Complex

Location: A sprawling industrial metropolis district featuring sleek corporate towers, manufacturing floors, and research laboratories designed to accommodate diverse clientele with specialized physical modifications.

Inhabitants: Corporate workers, specialized craftspeople, engineers, and security personnel; leadership is currently in flux following the arrest of former CEO Rikiya Yotsubashi. Underground operatives and black market dealers occasionally conduct illicit business within hidden sectors.

Appearance: A modern corporate facility with advanced customization technology, three-day production assembly lines, and prototype testing chambers. The architecture is distinctly adaptive—walls, doorways, and workstations adjust for clients of varying sizes and physical configurations. Hidden black market distribution centers operate beneath public-facing manufacturing areas, connected by sealed underground tunnels. Recent security lockdowns and governmental investigation have left portions of the complex abandoned and cordoned off.

cardPool.title: Eishu High School
cardPool.value:
Name: Eishu High School
Location: Japan, competing venue for National Hero Course events
Inhabitants: High school students training in heroics, ski jump athletes, coaching staff
Appearance: A competitive hero academy with athletic facilities, known for its skilled ski jump team that earned third place in the National Tournament with 91/100 points; modern training grounds typical of prestigious Japanese schools focused on hero development

cardPool.title: Esuha City
cardPool.value:
Name: Esuha City

Location: A urban patrol district where heroes Fat Gum, Tamaki Amajiki, and Eijiro Kirishima conduct regular enforcement operations.

Inhabitants: Professional heroes, street thugs, and desperate criminals willing to use Quirk-erasing drugs and experimental performance enhancers like Trigger to gain advantage in combat.

Appearance: A modern city block featuring typical urban infrastructure suitable for superhero patrols, with enough open space for dynamic confrontations between heroes and villains during daylight hours.

cardPool.title: Fat Gum Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Fat Gum Agency

Location: Between two buildings in an urban district; connected to police operations across Osaka and Tokyo

Inhabitants: Fat Gum (owner and hero), Tamaki Amajiki (intern hero), Eijiro Kirishima (intern hero), administrative staff

Appearance: A large rounded-roof building whose entire facade is designed to resemble Fat Gum's face—black mask area with two circular eye windows, a row of windows forming his distinctive smile, and stylized F-G-F lettering around the entrance door. A decorative relief on the left side depicts Fat Gum's arm holding a takoyaki ball. The interior is austere with minimal furnishings: a table, a single massive dark chair, and sparse pieces of furniture arranged functionally.

cardPool.title: Fourth Kind Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Fourth Kind Agency

Location: Urban hero agency building with yellow-black construction warning stripes on exterior; situated within a city that hosts U.A. hero training programs.

Inhabitants: Fourth Kind, a stern and demanding hero instructor known for his strict teaching methods and community service emphasis; occasionally hosts young hero interns like Eijiro Kirishima and Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu during their work-study programs.

Appearance: The agency features worn wooden furniture, signage, and window frames throughout. Traditional Japanese paper lanterns (chōchin) and Japanese-language posters adorn the walls. A prominent safe sits in one corner of the office. Fourth Kind's desk dominates the workspace. The interior shows signs of practical use over aesthetic polish, though the overall setup conveys a functioning hero agency focused on training and community work rather than flashy modernization.

cardPool.title: Fujitani Hospital
cardPool.value:
Name: Fujitani Hospital

Location: A large medical facility housing a psychiatric ward where patients receive long-term mental health treatment and recovery.

Inhabitants: Medical staff, psychiatric patients, and occasional visitors including family members seeking reconciliation with loved ones struggling with trauma and mental illness.

Appearance: A sprawling white-walled building with rows of windows overlooking the outside world. Patient rooms are small but furnished with essential amenities. The interior maintains the sterile, quiet atmosphere typical of hospitals, with cafeteria facilities for communal dining. A prominent sign bearing the hospital's name sits atop the roof, visible from a distance.

cardPool.title: Fukuoka
cardPool.value:
Name: Fukuoka

Location: A sprawling metropolis on Kyushu's northern shore, dominated by towering skyscrapers and dense urban districts. The city blends modern commerce with conflict zones marked by recent villain attacks.

Inhabitants: Hawks and his sidekicks operate from the agency headquarters; civilians fill the streets and restaurants; dangerous villains like Dabi and Doctor Ujiko have targeted the city; young heroes conduct internships and work-study programs here.

Appearance: Fukuoka Tower stands as a prominent landmark with observation decks offering scenic vistas. The Umai building rises with restaurant-filled floors, its top damaged from recent battles. Streets are bustling with foot traffic. Hawks' Agency perches atop an administrative building. Scorch marks and debris remain from villain encounters, creating an atmosphere of recovering urban resilience.

cardPool.title: Genius Office
cardPool.value:
Name: Genius Office

Location: A modernist hero agency headquarters housed in a pearly white building with green-tinted windows, located in an urban hero district accessible during agency internship programs.

Inhabitants: Best Jeanist, a composed hero mentor who operates the agency and oversees intern development; various office staff managing daily operations; rotating interns including ambitious young heroes seeking to refine their abilities and heroic philosophy.

Appearance: A spacious, upscale interior dominated by two long workstations lined with state-of-the-art computers and monitoring equipment. Colorful, trendy modernist furniture fills the open floor plan. Display shelves along the walls showcase trophies, commendations, and decorative ornaments reflecting the agency's prestigious reputation. The building's exterior features bold signage with "Genius" and "Office" prominently displayed separately, creating a striking architectural statement.

cardPool.title: Gran Torino's Apartment
cardPool.value:
Name:
Gran Torino's Apartment

Location:
A decrepit urban dwelling surrounded by a tall fence and rusted gates, accessible through a crumbling front entrance marked by a falling "Welcome" sign.

Inhabitants:
Gran Torino, an elderly resident; occasional visitors seeking his wisdom or assistance.

Appearance:
The exterior is severely weathered with broken windows and crumbling masonry. Inside, cluttered but lived-in spaces feature worn furniture—a sagging couch, wooden table, and mismatched chairs arranged for conversation. The back wall displays a cluttered bookshelf, a simple stool, and a large board covered in scattered papers and notes. A tarnished chandelier hangs from the ceiling, casting dim light across the modest rooms.

cardPool.title: Gunga Mountain Villa
cardPool.value:
Name: Gunga Mountain Villa

Location: Eighty kilometers from Jaku General Hospital, nestled in mountainous terrain with multiple underground levels extending beneath the primary structure.

Inhabitants: Paranormal Liberation Front leadership and warriors; Skeptic organizes strategy meetings in the assembly room while rank-and-file combatants gather in the vast underground hall for speeches and briefings.

Appearance: A fortified compound now largely in ruins, with partially collapsed walls and floor sections. The villa features an ornate assembly room above ground and a sprawling underground sanctuary with five main entrances, one concealed passage, and three distant exits (positioned 800m southeast, 1km west, and 800m north). Damaged by cement walls, jagged ice formations, and massive structural breaches. Crumbled stone, exposed underground chambers, and rubble-strewn passages characterize the current state.

cardPool.title: Gym Gamma
cardPool.value:
Name:
Gym Gamma

Location:
A massive enclosed training facility within U.A. High School, constructed entirely of malleable concrete capable of instant reconfiguration.

Inhabitants:
Cementoss (the concrete-manipulating overseer), Ectoplasm (a supervising instructor), Midnight (a supervising instructor), and rotating groups of Class 1-A and Class 1-B students undergoing hero license examination training.

Appearance:
A sprawling, austere concrete chamber with bare gray walls and floor that shift and reshape at Cementoss's command to create obstacles, platforms, and environments suited to individual student training needs. The empty expanse echoes with the sounds of combat practice and technique development, its featureless design allowing infinite customization for hero-in-training exercises.

cardPool.title: Haibori Woods
cardPool.value:
Name:
Haibori Woods Mansion

Location:
A remote mountain hideout nestled deep within the dense Haibori Woods, surrounded by towering coniferous trees that provide natural concealment and isolation from the outside world.

Inhabitants:
Currently abandoned, though previously housed Tomura Shigaraki, Dabi, Spinner, and Skeptic under All For One's command. Scattered remnants of the Creature Rejection Clan may still linger in the area.

Appearance:
A sprawling, weathered mansion hidden among ancient pines, its structure showing signs of past conflict and decay. Dark stone walls blend into the shadowed forest, with overgrown grounds and vine-covered entrances suggesting years of abandonment. Interior chambers are sparse but functional, containing abandoned supplies and evidence of hasty departures. The building carries an ominous atmosphere, as though danger still lurks within its halls.

cardPool.title: Hawks Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Hawks Agency
Location: Atop a white building with sloped upper floors, accessible by internal stairs or external lift
Inhabitants: Agency operatives, administrators, and visiting clients seeking intelligence or investigative services
Appearance: A modern facility featuring soaring ceilings and minimalist furnishings; satellite dishes crown the rooftop for communications; the distinctive angular architecture creates shadow-filled corridors and creates natural sightlines across the cityscape below

cardPool.title: Hero Office
cardPool.value:
Name: Hero Office

Location: Urban metropolitan district, typically in a high-rise building or specialized facility dedicated to heroic operations and training.

Inhabitants: The owning Hero, their employed Sidekicks, Hero student interns working toward provisional licenses, and administrative staff managing operations and dispatch.

Appearance: A professionally themed workplace reflecting the hero's personal brand and powers, featuring training areas, equipment storage, briefing rooms, and administrative offices; displays of past achievements and commendations line the walls, while modern technology and hero-specific gear are prominently visible throughout.

cardPool.title: Hopper's Cafe
cardPool.value:
Name: Hopper's Cafe

Location: A low-rise building in east Naruhata, built from the ruins of a former warehouse and recycle shop. Multiple branches now operate across the city.

Inhabitants: The Hotta Brothers (proprietors, reformed Trigger dealers), Ikajiro Takobe (oversized former Instant Villain), Kirihito Kamachi (reformed villain), Teruo Unagisawa (reformed staff), and various reformed minor criminals and rehabilitated thugs working toward redemption. Pro Hero Eraser Head frequents the establishment.

Appearance: A welcoming cat-themed café with multiple cat trees throughout, comfortable seating, and accessible bathrooms designed for customers of all physical conditions including those of enlarged stature. Warm, lived-in atmosphere blending cozy coffee shop comfort with evidence of its redemptive purpose—a place where second chances are served alongside excellent coffee.

cardPool.title: Hosu City
cardPool.value:
Name: Hosu City

Location: A sprawling urban district located west of Tokyo, dominated by industrial and residential zones with narrow alleyways connecting major streets. The Hosu General Hospital stands as its most prominent landmark, a large medical facility serving the district's population.

Inhabitants: Pro Heroes Manual and Endeavor patrol the streets regularly. The district is home to ordinary citizens, hospital staff, and increasingly, dangerous Nomu creatures unleashed by villainous forces. The Hero Killer Stain operates from the shadows, targeting corrupt heroes.

Appearance: A gritty, modern cityscape of concrete buildings, street lamps, and winding alleys shrouded in urban decay. Dark corners and side streets create perfect ambush points for danger. The hospital's sterile white corridors contrast sharply with the grimy outdoor streets, where hero battles leave scorch marks and destruction in their wake.

cardPool.title: Hosu General Hospital
cardPool.value:
Name:
Hosu General Hospital

Location:
An urban medical facility serving the city of Hosu, accessible via main entrance marked by dual signage and fronted by large windows.

Inhabitants:
Medical staff, patients recovering from injuries or illness, visiting heroes and civilians. Notable patients may include injured adventurers or those afflicted by rare conditions.

Appearance:
A substantial multi-story structure featuring expansive windows overlooking the city. Interior corridors are sterile and functional with modern equipment. Patient rooms contain wheeled beds separated by curtains, medical monitors displaying vital signs, and side windows for natural light. The atmosphere is clinical yet comforting, designed for recovery and treatment.

cardPool.title: I-Island
cardPool.value:
Name:
I-Island

Location:
An artificial, self-contained island composed primarily of iron, accessible only by plane through a heavily guarded airport. The island is divided into four separate cities connected by water channels and natural foliage, featuring residential districts, business sectors, schools, and beaches. The centerpiece is a 200-story central tower at the island's core, reinforced like a bomb shelter and serving as the command hub for all island functions.

Inhabitants:
Thousands of scientists and their families conducting Quirk research and developing Pro Hero support equipment. The island houses the world's top researchers in a controlled environment where confidentiality is strictly enforced. Students attend I-Island Academy to study advanced science, and Pro Heroes visit during the annual I-Expo event.

Appearance:
A technological paradise of gleaming iron structures with stunning natural elements—beautiful beaches, great lakes, and lush green spaces. The central tower dominates the skyline with its towering height and fortress-like construction. The island features advanced facilities including research labs, a plant factory, museums showcasing cutting-edge support equipment, and a sprawling I-Expo pavilion. Security is visible everywhere through drones and surveillance systems, yet elegant architecture creates a peaceful, scientific atmosphere.

cardPool.title: Isami Academy High School
cardPool.value:
Name: Isami Academy High School

Location: A prestigious hero-training institution located near Musutafu, possibly within the same metropolitan region as U.A. High School. The exact geographic position remains undisclosed, but proximity to U.A. suggests it occupies a similar urban-suburban setting.

Inhabitants: Students training to become professional heroes, dressed in distinctive uniforms of white dress shirts, red ties or bow ties, dark blue blazers, gray pants or skirts, and brown loafers. The academy maintains an organized student body capable of coordinated training exercises, though no faculty members have been formally documented.

Appearance: A modern educational institution designed for hero training with facilities capable of hosting structured combat and quirk-development exercises. The academy maintains professional standards comparable to U.A. High School, featuring formal aesthetics reflected in its standardized uniform code and organized training programs. Its architecture and layout accommodate inter-academy visitation programs and collaborative training events.

cardPool.title: Jaku City
cardPool.value:
Name: Jaku City

Location: A sprawling Japanese metropolis scarred by recent catastrophic conflict, situated near Jaku General Hospital district.

Inhabitants: Traumatized civilians, reconstruction workers, medical personnel at the hospital, occasional paranormal fighters and vigilantes investigating the destruction.

Appearance: A large urban center with approximately one-third devastated by reality-warping decay and colossal trampling, creating jagged ruins of toppled skyscrapers, fractured streets, and collapsed infrastructure amid still-standing residential and commercial blocks. Dust clouds linger over debris fields; makeshift barriers and warning signs mark dangerous zones. The surviving portions remain functional but scarred by rubble and scorched earth.

cardPool.title: Jaku General Hospital
cardPool.value:
Name:
Jaku General Hospital

Location:
Roughly eighty kilometers from Gunga Mountain Villa, a sprawling medical complex disguised as a legitimate healthcare facility serving the surrounding communities.

Inhabitants:
Dr. Kyudai Garaki (director and secret researcher), hospital staff unaware of true operations, patients, nursing home and orphanage residents, experimental Nomu creatures in hidden laboratory.

Appearance:
A multi-building hospital complex with public wards, patient rooms, and nursing facilities on upper levels. The morgue conceals entrance to a hidden corridor leading to Garaki's underground laboratory—a high-tech research facility featuring test chambers, Quirk extraction machinery, operating theaters, and containment vessels for Nomu specimens. The entire structure has been reduced to dust and decay following the Heroes' raid and Tomura Shigaraki's awakening.

cardPool.title: Jiro House
cardPool.value:
Name: Jiro House

Location: A residential neighborhood, standing as a modest single-family dwelling set apart from its neighbors.

Inhabitants: Music enthusiasts and collectors who have devoted their lives to their passion, filling every corner with evidence of their devotion to sound and melody.

Appearance: A rectangular home with pale, cream-colored walls that contrast sharply with interior walls lined with framed band posters, vintage LP records stacked on wooden shelves, compact discs arranged in careful rows, and an array of speakers and music players positioned throughout. The air seems to hum with potential melody, and the scent of aged vinyl mingles with the faint electrical hum of dormant equipment.

cardPool.title: Juko News
cardPool.value:
Name: Juko News Office
Location: Urban News District
Inhabitants: Editor-in-Chief (obsessed with All Might stories), journalists, administrative staff, delivery personnel
Appearance: A modest publishing house with cluttered desks, filing cabinets overflowing with archives, bulletin boards plastered with All Might clippings and competitor publications. The main office is dominated by a large editorial workspace where the driven Editor-in-Chief orchestrates coverage, with printing presses rumbling in the basement and stacks of recent publications lining the hallways. The atmosphere is tense and competitive, filled with the energy of a small outlet desperate to break the next major story.

cardPool.title: Kamino, Yokohama
cardPool.value:
Name:
Kamino Ward, Yokohama

Location:
A sprawling urban district in Yokohama that serves as both a thriving commercial hub and a site of legendary conflict. The ward contains abandoned warehouses, run-down bars, cheap shops, and a central plaza dominated by a colossal statue of All Might at "ground zero"—the epicenter of a devastating battle between heroes and villains.

Inhabitants:
Pro Heroes, civilian merchants, and occasionally members of villain organizations seeking refuge. The ward is frequented by everyday citizens, though many harbor growing distrust of hero society. Security is notably increased following major incidents.

Appearance:
Kamino is a gritty mix of rebuilt modern structures and neglected, weathered buildings. The iconic All Might statue stands in the central plaza with arms raised in victory, though it now bears signs of vandalism and distrust. Crumbling warehouses with reinforced storage areas sit alongside shabby storefronts and forgotten bars. The architecture reflects both urban decay and recovery, with visible scars of past destruction alongside new construction. An atmosphere of unease persists despite attempts at restoration.

cardPool.title: Kiyashi Ward Shopping Mall
cardPool.value:
Name: Kiyashi Ward Shopping Mall

Location: Urban commercial district in a populated metropolitan area, easily accessible by public transit and foot traffic.

Inhabitants: Shop proprietors, clerks, and patrons of all body types and abilities browsing merchandise; occasional security personnel monitoring the premises.

Appearance: A sprawling indoor mall featuring numerous storefronts and boutiques with specialized inventory. Corridors are well-lit and climate-controlled, displaying windows showcasing clothing, accessories, and equipment tailored for unusual physiques and supernatural abilities. The atmosphere is bustling and cosmopolitan, with polished floors, vendor stalls, and communal seating areas throughout. Signage in multiple styles advertises customized goods for diverse clientele.

cardPool.title: Klayd
cardPool.value:
Name: Klayd

Location: An egg-shaped island at the southwestern rim of the Celtic Sea, larger than Ireland and sharing landmass with the neighboring nation of Otheon.

Inhabitants: The people of Klayd remain largely mysterious to outsiders, though their culture and customs appear broadly similar to those of their Otheon neighbors.

Appearance: Rugged and maritime, with the character of a temperate island nation. The landscape likely features coastal cliffs, rolling terrain, and Celtic-influenced settlements, though much of Klayd's true geography remains shrouded in obscurity and legend.

cardPool.title: Knuckleduster's Warehouse
cardPool.value:
Name: Knuckleduster's Warehouse

Location: Hidden within the Naruhata Station district, accessible only to those who know of its existence and possess the keys to its unmarked entrance.

Inhabitants: Currently inhabited by Soga and occasionally visited by Koichi Haimawari, Moyuru, and Rapt. Once served as the secret training ground of Knuckleduster before his three-year absence.

Appearance: A large, dilapidated building that appears abandoned from the outside, masking its true purpose. Inside, the warehouse is equipped with extensive training gear including punching bags, weights, and Wing-Chun dummies, alongside firearms and research equipment. A prominent wall-mounted map of the Naruhata Station area displays marked routes and tactical positions used for planning operations against Villains. The space serves as both a training facility and strategic command center.

cardPool.title: Koichi's Penthouse
cardPool.value:
Name:
Koichi's Penthouse

Location:
A cramped, illegally-constructed penthouse atop a deteriorating urban building, accessible by narrow stairs to the rooftop.

Inhabitants:
Koichi, a vigilante who cycles through All Might hoodies as disguises, and occasionally Kazuho Haneyama who uses a curtained alcove to change clothes.

Appearance:
A modest open-plan studio combining bedroom, living room, dining area, and kitchen. The left half features tatami flooring with a bed, small table, cushions, dresser stuffed with collectible hoodies, bookshelves, and a flat-screen television. The right half has hardwood flooring with a compact kitchen featuring a sink, dish rack, stove, and wall cupboards. A small refrigerator stocked with snacks sits near the laundry room entrance, topped with a rice cooker. A traditional genkan entryway with a rear door leading to laundry facilities and a small bathroom complete the space.

cardPool.title: Lunch Rush Cafeteria
cardPool.value:
Name:
Lunch Rush Cafeteria

Location:
A sprawling food court within a prestigious academy, accessible through imposing double doors that open onto a bustling dining hall.

Inhabitants:
Lunch Rush, a Pro Hero renowned for culinary mastery, oversees the operation and prepares first-rate cuisine alongside support staff serving the school's student population.

Appearance:
Rows of long communal tables, each seating ten, dominate the space beneath Chinese-inspired decorative motifs. The cafeteria radiates efficiency and warmth, with multiple food service venues lining the periphery offering affordable, high-quality meals to hungry students throughout lunch periods.

cardPool.title: Makeshift Fortress: Troy
cardPool.value:
Name:
Troy Fortress

Location:
A hastily constructed stronghold built on neutral ground away from U.A. High School, designed as a temporary military installation and safe haven.

Inhabitants:
Class 1-A students, their families, and the heroic support staff including Cementoss, Power Loader, and Ectoplasm who maintain the fortress's structural integrity and defenses.

Appearance:
Rough concrete walls reinforced with earth-based quirk abilities, industrial metal framework, and practical fortifications. The structure bears evidence of rapid construction with visible reinforced bunkers, training grounds, and defensive barriers. Interior features makeshift barracks, supply rooms, and a command center for coordinating resistance operations.

cardPool.title: Marukane Department Store
cardPool.value:
Name: Marukane Department Store

Location: A sprawling urban retail complex positioned directly in front of Naruhata Station, featuring a distinctive cubic logo structure crowning its rooftop. The building recently reopened after damage repairs from a superhero confrontation.

Inhabitants: Store directors and event planners who actively support local entertainment, band members of FeatherHATS who use the assigned conference room as a green room, visiting performers and talent scouts, Captain Celebrity Agency representatives, and rotating crowds of shoppers and event attendees.

Appearance: A large modern department store with multiple levels, a food court offering snacks, and a rooftop venue with 300-person capacity hosting the iconic cubic franchise logo. The rooftop stage area has been upgraded with professional equipment and staging to host Narufest—intimate live events showcasing local young talent. The interior includes a dedicated conference room for band rehearsals and meetings.

cardPool.title: Masegaki Primary School
cardPool.value:
Name: Masegaki Primary School

Location: An urban educational institution serving as a training ground and rehabilitation facility for gifted but undisciplined young students with powerful supernatural abilities.

Inhabitants: Unruly primary school children with exceptional Quirks and poor respect for authority, led by a smug blond-haired boy. Their stressed teacher Komari Ikoma struggles to maintain order. Remedial course students, particularly Bakugo and Todoroki, now serve as mentors and frequent visitors.

Appearance: A classroom and recreational space transformed by student Quirks into dynamic play environments. Features ice sculptures, slides, and castles created during training sessions. The grounds host an annual "Summer Cool-Off Five Weenies Festival" celebrating the students' growth and Shoto's ice-crafting prowess. Despite its chaotic reputation, the school has evolved into a place of camaraderie between gifted children and their hero student guides.

cardPool.title: Midoriya Apartment
cardPool.value:
Name: Midoriya Apartment

Location: Urban residential district, five-story danchi complex marked with a large "2" on its side, surrounded by similar apartment buildings with visible power lines overhead.

Inhabitants: A modest family dwelling in a densely populated neighborhood; typical of middle-class urban residents.

Appearance: Cramped but functional interior featuring a simple dining table with chairs, wall-mounted cabinets storing dishes and cups, minimal furnishings reflecting practical living. Weathered exterior blends with surrounding gray concrete structures; power lines crisscross the skyline above.

cardPool.title: Might Tower
cardPool.value:
Name:
Might Tower

Location:
A towering skyscraper crowned with a massive dual-ringed planet sculpture, rising above the city as a gleaming beacon of heroic authority.

Inhabitants:
All Might (in both heroic and true forms), his dedicated staff, administrative personnel, Detective Naomasa, and occasional visitors conducting official business.

Appearance:
A luxurious, imposing structure of steel and glass featuring a top-floor statue of All Might, a mechanized rooftop gate for heroic arrivals, the impenetrable Might Gate guarding All Might's personal department, a mid-level cafeteria with expansive windows overlooking the townscape, and upper-floor meeting rooms where strategy and schedules are discussed. The tower exudes both grandeur and institutional purpose.

cardPool.title: Mt. Agency
cardPool.value:
Name:
Mt. Agency

Location:
A multi-story office building in the heart of the urban district, marked by a prominent sign on its facade and distinctive twin horn-like structures jutting from its roof, mirroring the design of Mt. Lady's signature domino mask.

Inhabitants:
Mt. Lady and her staff of administrative workers, sidekicks, and support personnel managing her hero agency operations from within the building's various floors.

Appearance:
A modern office structure bearing recent reconstruction marks from accidental demolition damage, its architectural design compromised by the impracticality of Mt. Lady's gigantification Quirk in confined city spaces, yet strategically positioned to maximize public visibility and maintain the agency's prominent profile despite these limitations.

cardPool.title: Mustafa Private Middle School
cardPool.value:
Name: Mustafa Academy
Location: A sprawling compound in a temperate urban district, surrounded by stone walls and iron gates. The grounds occupy several interconnected buildings arranged around a central courtyard.
Inhabitants: Dozens of scholars, instructors, and administrative staff oversee the education of 200+ students aged 11-14. A headmaster governs the institution, assisted by teachers specializing in various disciplines and maintenance workers.
Appearance: The main structure features classical architecture with arched doorways and columned halls, decorated in earth tones of cream and rust. Classrooms line the upper floors with tall windows, while a library, assembly hall, and dormitory annexes occupy separate wings. The courtyard contains a fountain, flowering gardens, and weathered stone benches beneath spreading trees.

cardPool.title: Nabu Island
cardPool.value:
Name: Nabu Island

Location: A subtropical island in southern Japan (29°24'N 125°54'E), isolated far from the main archipelago. The main settlement sits in the south, with agricultural fields to the east and northwest, subtropical forests covering most terrain, and a smaller neighboring island to the northwest connected by a narrow sea-crossing path.

Inhabitants: Approximately 1,000 residents living in a tight-knit community of detached houses and cottages. Few Heroes are stationed here due to the island's remoteness from villain activity; those present handle minor tasks like finding lost items and odd jobs suited to their abilities.

Appearance: A peaceful, idyllic island with sandy beaches featuring beach bars and rocky no-swim zones, a small wind farm with seven turbines, a commercial district in the main town with a hospital and school, a working harbor for fishing boats and ships, agricultural fields and a nearby factory, and a northwestern mountain (Mount Shiroyama) crowned with extensive ancient fortress ruins built atop natural caves large enough to shelter the entire population.

cardPool.title: Nabu Middle School
cardPool.value:
Name:
Nabu Middle School

Location:
An unnamed Japanese city, situated in an unremarkable district far from the prestigious U.A. High School

Inhabitants:
Students of middle school age, teachers, and faculty staff; known as the place where the quirkless or those with lesser-known abilities study before attempting entrance exams to elite academies

Appearance:
A standard institutional building with typical Japanese school architecture—concrete walls, multiple floors, plain corridors, and modest classrooms. The atmosphere carries the weight of obscurity, lacking the prestige and advanced facilities of top-tier schools, with worn furniture and basic training grounds.

cardPool.title: Naruhata
cardPool.value:
Name: Naruhata District

Location: Tokyo metropolitan area; bordered by NR Naruhata Station shopping district to the west and old Higashi Naruhata town to the east

Inhabitants: Sparse residential population in outlying neighborhoods; convenience store delivery workers frequent early mornings; occasional spontaneous villains and vigilantes in confined areas

Appearance: Mixed urban sprawl of aging buildings and forgotten infrastructure; maze-like network of abandoned local roads rarely traveled since the expressway bypass opened a decade ago; quieter residential zones with crumbling structures contrasting against the busier shopping district; early morning fog hangs over empty streets broken only by delivery truck sounds

cardPool.title: Naruhata Disaster Medical Center
cardPool.value:
Name: Naruhata Disaster Medical Center

Location: Urban medical district, accessible via large landscaped parking lot with ample vehicle access

Inhabitants: Hospital staff, physicians, nurses, patients in recovery, occasional emergency responders

Appearance: Large white building with blue signage in Japanese and English. Interior features brown and beige corridors leading to gray-toned patient rooms divided by curtains, each containing two beds. Smoke detectors positioned throughout enforce strict fire safety protocols.

cardPool.title: Nighteye Agency
cardPool.value:
Name:
Nighteye Agency

Location:
A five-story professional hero office building in Japan, serving as both headquarters and training facility for Sir Nighteye's hero operation.

Inhabitants:
Sir Nighteye (the agency director and hero with Foresight quirk), his two sidekicks Bubble Girl and Centipeder, U.A. student interns including Izuku Midoriya and Mirio Togata, and various support staff.

Appearance:
The building features a large meeting room on the second floor and Sir Nighteye's personal office decorated with All Might posters, merchandise, and a desk with laptop overlooking a substantial bookshelf filled with case files and research materials. The agency functions as a strategic operations center for hero work, investigations, and quirk training.

cardPool.title: Okuto Island
cardPool.value:
Name: Okuto Island

Location: A tropical island renowned for its expansive sandy shoals and panoramic ocean vistas, dotted with luxury resorts and vacation lodges catering to domestic and international visitors.

Inhabitants: Gang Orca, the aquarium director, oversees the island's primary attraction and coordinates with military forces during wartime. Various resort staff, tourists, and soldiers occupy the island depending on the season and conflict status.

Appearance: The island features pristine beaches with shallow waters ideal for swimming, dense tropical vegetation inland, and a prominent aquarium complex serving as the architectural centerpiece. Military fortifications and containment barriers have been erected across the island, particularly near the aquarium, creating an unusual contrast between vacation destination and wartime stronghold.

cardPool.title: Onomura Pharma Corp.
cardPool.value:
Name:
Onomura Pharma Corp. Kanto R&D Center

Location:
Tokyo, operating as a legitimate pharmaceutical manufacturer and wholesaler with a hidden criminal division

Inhabitants:
Pharmaceutical researchers and staff in public areas; Villain Factory operatives, mad scientists, and kidnapped test subjects in the isolated research wing

Appearance:
A nondescript midsize corporate facility with sterile white corridors and standard laboratories. One corner wing remains deliberately segregated from the rest, its entrance restricted and unmarked. Inside this hidden section: advanced experimental chambers, containment cells, synthesis equipment for illicit Trigger production, and shadowy figures moving between reinforced doors.

cardPool.title: Otheon
cardPool.value:
Name: Otheon

Location: Southwestern Celtic Sea island, egg-shaped and larger than Ireland, bordered by the Bay of Biscay; capital city bisected by a river and connected by suspension bridge

Inhabitants: Multilingual Europeans influenced by French, Spanish, and Portuguese cultures; wealth concentrated among prosperous downtown dwellers and tourists; impoverished communities in riverside slums plagued by crime and neglect

Appearance: Mountainous terrain with grasslands and forests transitioning to barren landscape near Klayd border; capital features elegant European-style architecture, four distinctive wavy skyscrapers (Otheon Towers), tree-lined boulevards, plazas, and modern transit systems on the prosperous north bank; south bank sprawls with densely packed shacks, deteriorating housing units, and abandoned trailers adjacent to the airport

cardPool.title: Purple Revolution Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Purple Revolution Agency

Location: Urban district amid palm-lined streets, a gleaming structure of contemporary design rising above the cityscape.

Inhabitants: Operatives and agents of the Purple Revolution, support staff managing missions and logistics, administrative personnel directing operations from sleek offices.

Appearance: A sprawling modern building with clean lines and expansive windows, flanked by tropical palms swaying in the breeze. Interior features well-appointed shower facilities for field operatives to decontaminate after assignments, polished corridors connecting mission-briefing rooms, tactical centers, and administrative quarters.

cardPool.title: Pussycats Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Pussycats Agency

Location: A mountainous region, featuring both a distinctive pink headquarters building and an expansive wooded training facility called The Beast's Forest nearby.

Inhabitants: The Wild Wild Pussycats team members, each occupying personalized desks and seats color-coded to their identities. Visitors and trainees utilize the Beast's Forest cabins seasonally.

Appearance: The main agency is a striking pink structure designed as a giant cat's face—the front door forms a grinning mouth with whiskers, round windows serve as eyes, and the roof displays pointed cat ears with paw pad decorations. "Pussycats" lettering adorns the facade. Interior spaces showcase whimsical cat-themed furniture throughout. The Beast's Forest comprises dense woodland with rustic cabins, a communal dining hall, natural hot springs, and dormitory buildings for extended training sessions.

cardPool.title: Qing Qing City, China
cardPool.value:
Name: Qing Qing City Hospital

Location: Qing Qing City, China—an unremarkable urban hospital that became the birthplace of documented Quirk manifestation.

Inhabitants: Medical staff of varying ages, curious scholars and researchers investigating Quirk origins, occasional pilgrims seeking connection to the phenomenon's genesis.

Appearance: A weathered institutional building with sterile white corridors and dim fluorescent lighting, marked by a peculiar glow emanating from the maternity ward where the luminous child was born; faded plaques and records document the historic event, and certain rooms retain a subtle phosphorescence at night.

cardPool.title: Recovery Girl's Nurse's Office
cardPool.value:
Name: Recovery Girl's Nurse's Office

Location: U.A. High School Campus, with branch offices throughout the school and temporary stations at event venues like the Sports Festival Stadium

Inhabitants: Recovery Girl, a skilled healer and school nurse who tends to injured students; various injured students seeking medical treatment

Appearance: A clean, clinical room featuring a wooden work desk with computer and medicine drawer, two beds for patients, medicinal posters covering the walls, and simple chairs for consultations. Branch offices maintain similar layouts in different campus locations, with portable tent versions deployed during major events for emergency care.

cardPool.title: Recycle Shop: Hoppers
cardPool.value:
Name: Hoppers Recycle Shop

Location: Naruhata district, with a secondary warehouse on the outskirts (now destroyed)

Inhabitants: The Hotta Brothers—eccentric shop owners with grasshopper-based Quirks who deal in second-hand goods and pharmaceutical supplements. Eraser Head occasionally uses the shop as a covert investigation base. Local residents and customers browse the cluttered aisles.

Appearance: A cluttered recycle shop dominated by a massive storefront sign featuring two grasshoppers emblems. Shelves overflow with second-hand furniture, appliances, and utensils in varying states of repair. The interior is cramped and worn, with exposed wooden beams and dim fluorescent lighting. Behind the counter sits the brothers' legitimate pharmaceutical supply. The air smells of dust, old wood, and coffee. Recently, the owners have begun converting a section into a modest cafe to recover from warehouse destruction.

cardPool.title: Ryukyu Agency
cardPool.value:
Name:
Ryukyu Agency

Location:
A sprawling open-plan office within a brown-facade building featuring dark glass windows, prominently displaying a billboard for the Dragoir clothing line.

Inhabitants:
Agency staff and personnel conducting business; clients visiting for representation or fashion-related matters.

Appearance:
The interior is dominated by warm reddish tones and features an ornate Chinese aesthetic with golden dragon-adorned columns, guardian lion statues, and decorative elements throughout. Office tables, shelving units nestled between columns, and a plasma TV displaying news occupy the spacious, wall-free layout.

cardPool.title: Salty Banks Middle School
cardPool.value:
Name: Salty Banks Middle School
Location: A sprawling academic compound situated on the outskirts of a coastal town, bordered by salt marshes and accessible via a long, tree-lined drive.
Inhabitants: Hundreds of students aged 11-14, harried teachers, administrative staff, and custodial workers; occasional visitors and parents during school hours.
Appearance: A cluster of single-story brick and concrete buildings arranged around courtyards, featuring wide corridors lined with lockers, fluorescent-lit classrooms, a cafeteria with industrial kitchens, and a gymnasium with bleachers; the grounds include athletic fields, a small library, and weathered playground equipment near the marsh's edge.

cardPool.title: Seiai Academy
cardPool.value:
Name: Seiai Academy

Location: High school campus situated within a major metropolitan area; serves as a training ground for aspiring Heroes during the Provisional Hero License Exam period.

Inhabitants: Ambitious students training to become Heroes, led by the calculating Saiko Intelli and her strategically-minded cohort. Faculty overseeing Hero development and exam administration. Currently hosts rival encounters with U.A. High School Class 1-A students.

Appearance: A structured academic institution with training facilities designed for Quirk development and combat scenarios. Classrooms and halls reflect a competitive, militaristic atmosphere. The campus contains examination arenas where students demonstrate their Hero potential through tactical combat against other aspiring Heroes.

cardPool.title: Seijin High School
cardPool.value:
Name: Seijin High School

Location: Industrial area of Takoba National Stadium, a sprawling hero training institution within a urban industrial district

Inhabitants: Ten unnamed students with diverse combat Quirks including Gigantification, Landslide, Torrent, and Bulk abilities; staff and instructors dedicated to hero training

Appearance: A modern academic facility adjoining the stadium's industrial sector, featuring training grounds equipped for combat simulation and Quirk practice. The school grounds contain open areas suitable for large-scale tactical exercises, with access to an industrial landscape of metal structures and open spaces ideal for hero license examinations.

cardPool.title: Sekoto Peak
cardPool.value:
Name:
Sekoto Peak

Location:
A remote mountain training ground visible from the city, featuring scorched terrain and a nearby stream. The peak was once a natural landscape but is now largely barren and blackened from the catastrophic wildfire that swept through it.

Inhabitants:
Rarely visited now; once frequented by skilled fire-wielders seeking solitude for Quirk training. Occasional adventurers or investigators may explore the ruins searching for artifacts or answers about the great conflagration.

Appearance:
A desolate, ash-covered mountain with exposed charred rock and skeletal remains of vegetation. The air shimmers with residual heat, and the ground is cracked and blackened. A cold stream cuts through the burned landscape—one of the few sources of water and life remaining on the scarred peak.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai Compound
cardPool.value:
Name:
Shie Hassaikai Compound

Location:
A fortified yakuza stronghold disguised as traditional Japanese office buildings, completely gated with a tree-filled courtyard. The structure conceals a vast underground labyrinth stretching for miles beneath the surface.

Inhabitants:
Members of the Eight Precepts of Death yakuza organization, including leadership, soldiers, and support staff operating from both the surface offices and hidden underground chambers.

Appearance:
The exterior presents as an elegant Japanese residence with refined architectural details. The gated courtyard features mature trees and a formal main entrance. Inside, the first floor mimics a standard Japanese office with tatami and wooden furnishings. Beneath a concealed vase lies a secret switch revealing stone stairs descending into a sprawling underground maze of passages, meeting rooms, and an infirmary, designed for covert movement and multiple escape routes.

cardPool.title: Sports Festival Stadium
cardPool.value:
Name: Sports Festival Stadium

Location: Urban arena district; oval-shaped open-air structure with three-tiered stands, multiple entry gates, and surrounding staff facilities.

Inhabitants: Tournament judges, medical staff, security Pro Heroes (Mt. Lady, Death Arms, Kamui Woods), competing athletes, spectators filling the stands, and Cementoss who constructs and monitors the arena platform.

Appearance: A massive concrete and grass arena with tiered seating overlooking a central circular field. The competition floor features a flat concrete square surrounded by grass, with multiple gates for entry and exit. During tournaments, a concrete platform rises in the center, ringed by torches at each corner and topped by a judge's throne. Large screens display action to distant spectators. Beneath the stands lie medical offices, participant waiting rooms, and a staff break room for security personnel.

cardPool.title: Symbol of Paradise
cardPool.value:
Name: Symbol of Paradise

Location: A massive transmuted fortress hovering over Japan, created from Dark Might's flying yacht through alchemical modification. The structure contains multiple distinct biomes connected by corridors, tunnels, and manholes, capable of spatial transportation and self-repair.

Inhabitants: Dark Might (the alchemist tyrant), members of the Gollini Family, numerous brainwashed henchmen, kidnapped Japanese civilians being converted into living weapons, and various hostile forces throughout the fortress sectors.

Appearance: A sprawling artificial megastructure divided into five interconnected zones: a deceptive jungle with fake vegetation and illusory walls, a fully operational amusement park with a Ferris wheel and haunted mansion, a European-style walled city with an All Might statue, a snowy mountainous region with a concealed lake and forest, and a coastal beach area surrounded by cliff walls. The entire fortress features hidden doors, trapdoors, and pitfalls designed for Dark Might's protection, with self-healing properties that allow rapid reconstruction after damage. The environment is a labyrinth of shifting hazards and tactical chokepoints.

cardPool.title: Takoba Municipal Beach Park
cardPool.value:
Name:
Takoba Municipal Beach Park

Location:
A sprawling coastal beach situated along the seaside, featuring a wooden pier extending into the water with a small gazebo pavilion for gathering. Once strangled by accumulated sea debris, the park has been restored to public accessibility.

Inhabitants:
All Might frequents this location to train worthy students in secret, using it as a sanctuary for teaching and mentorship. Young heroes and civilians now visit as it has become a popular dating destination following its restoration.

Appearance:
Sandy shores now clear of trash and pollution stretch beneath open sky. The weathered pier stands as a focal point, its gazebo offering shelter. The beach carries the scent of salt water and renewal, marked by the contrast between reclaimed sand and the distant memory of its ruined state. Waves lap gently against the shore, while the open expanse invites both physical training and quiet reflection.

cardPool.title: Takoba National Stadium
cardPool.value:
Name: Takoba National Stadium

Location: A massive modern arena facility designed for large-scale hero training exams and combat scenarios, capable of holding over one thousand participants simultaneously.

Inhabitants: Hero students undergoing licensing exams, exam organizers and judges, professional stuntmen acting as disaster victims, occasional heroes and trainees deployed during wartime conflicts.

Appearance: A sprawling complex featuring multiple destructible environmental zones including dense forests with waterfalls, urban cityscapes, highway bridges, rocky mountain terrain, and industrial factory sections. The stadium contains foldable briefing and rest chambers that open during exam phases, allowing applicants to disperse into the arena. During second-phase exams, elaborate explosives simulate disasters, reducing the pristine environments to rubble and debris fields for rescue training scenarios.

cardPool.title: Tatooin Station
cardPool.value:
Name:
Tatooin Station

Location:
A bullet train station perched on an overpass crossing a major street in a sprawling urban district, adjacent to the Tatooin Shopping District below. The station features prominent billboards and television screens displaying hero advertisements throughout.

Inhabitants:
During peacetime, the station bustles with commuters and travelers. Currently abandoned due to the Final War, with all residents evacuated. Pro Heroes occasionally respond to incidents in the area, including those summoned to contain dangerous villains.

Appearance:
The station shows significant battle damage and disrepair from multiple villain encounters—crumbling structures, collapsed sections, and weathered infrastructure. Debris litters the platforms and surrounding streets. Abandoned trains sit dormant at loading areas, while flickering screens cast eerie light across the desolate overpass. The adjacent shopping district below features alleys where dangerous confrontations have occurred, creating a haunting juxtaposition of commercial signage against urban decay.

cardPool.title: Teachers Lounge
cardPool.value:
Name: Teachers Lounge

Location: Unforeseen Simulation Joint, administrative wing

Inhabitants: School faculty and staff; occasionally All Might when recovering from Quirk usage

Appearance: A modest rest chamber with gray tile floors and tan walls, featuring two comfortable sofas flanking a low coffee table and a functional coffee machine in the corner. Simple but functional furnishings suited for brief respites between duties.

cardPool.title: Terakoya
cardPool.value:
Name: Terakoya
Location: Oku Island, a remote private hero academy nestled among coastal ruins and ancient stone structures
Inhabitants: Ikkaku and dozens of rowdy students training to become heroes, overseen by a patient teacher; occasional grave robbers and treasure hunters drawn to the island's ruins
Appearance: A modest schoolhouse with weathered wooden buildings where energetic children practice their Quirks indoors and outdoors, surrounded by dense vegetation and crumbling stone ruins hidden beneath the island's surface, with concealed trap systems throughout the underground passages

cardPool.title: The Beast's Forest
cardPool.value:
Name: Beast's Forest

Location: Dense woodland adjacent to a mountain range, home to the Wild Wild Pussycats' training headquarters

Inhabitants: Wild Wild Pussycats (including Pixie-Bob), student trainees, Earth Flow monsters summoned by Pixie-Bob's Quirk, occasional League of Villains operatives

Appearance: Towering trees form an impenetrable canopy; scorched clearings and gas-poisoned areas mark recent conflict. The forest contains the Pussycats' hidden office building with adjoining cabins, dining hall, hot springs, and dormitories. Rocky terrain and varying elevations create natural obstacles. Patches of charred wood and withered vegetation indicate past destruction from fire and toxic gas attacks.

cardPool.title: Todoroki Abode
cardPool.value:
Name: Todoroki Abode
Location: A traditional Japanese estate nestled within a quiet residential district, accessible by stone pathways lined with carefully maintained gardens.
Inhabitants: The Todoroki family—a prestigious clan of warriors and mages, including Enji Todoroki and his children who possess elemental powers, along with household servants and attendants.
Appearance: The residence features classic Japanese architecture with sliding shoji doors, paper-screened windows, and tatami mat flooring throughout interior chambers. An enclosed garden courtyard occupies the home's center, providing natural light and tranquility. Wooden beam supports and dark-stained timber frames contrast with white plaster walls, while the sloped tile roof is typical of traditional design. Outside walkways offer scenic views of the manicured grounds, creating both an air of elegance and strategic defensibility.

cardPool.title: Tokyo Sky Egg
cardPool.value:
Name: Tokyo Sky Egg

Location: Tokyo, a massive dome-shaped auditorium tower in the heart of the city

Inhabitants: Thousands of spectators during events, security personnel, venue staff, and occasional heroes responding to threats

Appearance: A colossal domed structure with seating capacity for 50,000, featuring reinforced security systems including emergency staircases and automated elevator shutdowns during crises. The dome's interior is grand and modern, designed for large-scale shows and spectacles. Emergency lighting and structural supports are visible throughout. Currently bears scars from a catastrophic attack—the dome was nearly destroyed but miraculously saved from total collapse, leaving visible damage and repair work ongoing.

cardPool.title: U.A.'s Development Studio
cardPool.value:
Name: U.A.'s Development Studio

Location: U.A. High School, adjacent to Heights Alliance dorms

Inhabitants: Mei Hatsume (inventor), Power Loader (supervisor), occasional student visitors seeking costume modifications

Appearance: A cluttered workshop filled with tools, materials, and machinery scattered across workbenches. One corner overflows with Mei's completed and half-finished inventions. The room bears scorch marks and signs of previous explosions, evidence of frequent experimental mishaps. Equipment for costume development and enhancement dominates the space.

cardPool.title: Unforeseen Simulation Joint
cardPool.value:
Name: Unforeseen Simulation Joint

Location: A specialized training facility consisting of a large dome-shaped building divided into eight main sections, situated within hero academy grounds.

Inhabitants: Pro Hero Thirteen (facility designer and instructor), Class 1-A students during training sessions, minor villains during invasion scenarios, and security personnel monitoring the sensor network.

Appearance: A distinctive dome structure with eight interconnected sections, six of which are designed to simulate major disaster scenarios including urban collapse, flooding, and fire zones. Advanced sensor arrays line the walls to detect unauthorized entry. The interior features varied terrain and hazard conditions that shift between training modes, from flooded areas to unstable rubble fields.

cardPool.title: Uraraka Apartment
cardPool.value:
Name:
Uraraka Apartment

Location:
A modest white three-story residential building in an urban neighborhood, accessible via open hallways on each level.

Inhabitants:
Working-class residents occupying small private units; the building houses multiple families in close quarters.

Appearance:
A compact, utilitarian structure with minimalist design and sparse furnishings. Each apartment contains only essential living facilities—basic furniture, simple fixtures, and limited amenities. The building's white exterior shows practical wear; open hallways allow sounds and light to carry freely between units.

cardPool.title: Verize Islands
cardPool.value:
Name: Verize Islands

Location: A sprawling archipelago scattered across treacherous waters, comprising dozens of islands, rocky islets, towering sea stacks, and hidden reef systems. The maze-like geography creates countless coves and passages ideal for concealment.

Inhabitants: A modest but established settlement on one of the larger islands, supported by trade and maritime activity. Smugglers, traders, and opportunists are rumored to operate throughout the archipelago's hidden anchorages.

Appearance: Rocky, wind-carved terrain dominates most islands, with dense coastal vegetation clinging to cliff faces. A functioning airfield marks the main settlement, while countless secluded harbors and underwater reefs present both danger and opportunity. Weathered driftwood, salt-spray damage, and the constant crash of waves against stone characterize the harsh seascape.

cardPool.title: Class 1-A
cardPool.value:
Name: Class 1-A Homeroom
Location: U.A. High School, Hero Course Wing
Inhabitants: Twenty elite hero students including Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo, Shoto Todoroki, Ochaco Uraraka, and others; taught by various Pro Heroes. The class is bound by trials of fire—villain attacks, internships, and wars—that forged unbreakable loyalty among them.
Appearance: A standard Japanese classroom transformed into a nexus of heroic potential, filled with desks bearing the marks of passionate students. Walls display evidence of their victories and hardships; the space feels charged with the energy of young heroes who have survived impossible odds together and refuse to abandon their bonds, despite the world's scorn.

cardPool.title: Endeavor Agency
cardPool.value:
Name: Endeavor's Hero Agency

Location: Luxurious skyscraper in a major metropolitan city, with satellite operations extending to Hosu City and beyond.

Inhabitants: Over thirty passionate sidekicks known as the "Flaming Sidekickers" (including Burnin), most possessing fire and heat-type Quirks. Endeavor, the No. 1 Pro Hero, commands from his sparse personal office. Interns and visiting heroes rotate through constantly.

Appearance: A gleaming high-rise dominated by a stylized flaming "E" at the front entrance. The main floor features a bustling open office with multiple desks, computers, and request boards. Endeavor's personal office is cavernous but minimalist—dominated by his large desk with only a small table as additional furniture. The building hums with constant activity, patrols departing hourly and sidekicks managing hero work requests around the clock.

cardPool.title: P.E. Grounds
cardPool.value:
Name: P.E. Grounds

Location: U.A. High School campus, an expansive outdoor training facility divided into specialized test zones

Inhabitants: Robotic proctors stationed at each test station, student athletes, supervising instructors like Shota Aizawa

Appearance: Multiple distinct athletic areas including a 50-meter running track with timing mechanisms, a sand-filled long jump pit, and a marked pitching circle for softball throws. Each zone features a stationary robotic proctor equipped with measurement and recording systems. The grounds are open-air and well-maintained, designed to accommodate Quirk usage during physical assessments. Equipment and markers denote official test boundaries.

cardPool.title: Principal's Office
cardPool.value:
Name: Principal's Office

Location: U.A. High School, administrative wing

Inhabitants: Nezu (Principal), occasionally visited by faculty and staff including All Might, Aizawa, and Kan; parents and officials conducting school business

Appearance: A professional executive space with blue-gray floors and gray walls dominated by a massive back window. A large wooden desk with custom-sized swivel chair anchors the room, flanked by file cabinets of varying sizes. Two black sofas with a coffee table between them provide seating for meetings and consultations. The room serves as the decision-making heart of U.A., where critical administrative matters and safety protocols are deliberated.

cardPool.title: Marvelous Central University
cardPool.value:
Name: Marvelous Central University

Location: A sprawling academic institution situated in the heart of a major metropolitan district, accessible by grand stone archways and tree-lined boulevards.

Inhabitants: Scholars, mages, clerics, and students of various disciplines; aged professors in robes, ambitious young apprentices, library keepers, and administrative officials who maintain the institution's traditions and mysteries.

Appearance: Imposing Gothic and classical architecture features towering spires, domed libraries, and interconnected stone buildings adorned with arcane symbols and historical plaques. Courtyards overflow with fountains and bronze statues of legendary scholars; interior halls glow with enchanted lanterns and contain endless shelves of leather-bound tomes, lecture halls with tiered seating, and secluded study chambers.

cardPool.title: U.A. Faculty
cardPool.value:
U.A. Faculty consists of:

Principal Nezu
All Might (Teacher)
Midnight (Teacher)
Present Mic (Teacher)
Power Loader (Teacher / Support Hero)
Gran Torino (Teacher)
Recovery Girl (Pro Hero / Healer / Stationed at Infirmary)
Cementoss (Teacher)
Snipe (Teacher)
Ectoplasm (Teacher)

cardPool.title: Villain Factory
cardPool.value:
[Villain Factory]

Type: Criminal Organization

The Villain Factory is a dangerous underground organization known for conducting illegal Quirk-based experiments. The group is responsible for the creation of both Instant Villains and Next-Level Villains, making them one of the greatest threats in the Naruhata area.

The organization was named “Villain Factory” by the Police Force due to its mass production of artificial villains and experimental subjects.

The true leaders of the organization are All For One and Dr. Kyudai Garaki. Their ultimate objective is to create the perfect being — a weapon powerful enough to rival or surpass All Might.

Using advanced Quirk manipulation, biological experimentation, and ruthless human testing, the Villain Factory operates in secrecy while expanding its influence throughout the criminal underworld.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai
cardPool.value:
[Shie Hassaikai]

Type: Yakuza Organization

The Shie Hassaikai is a former Yakuza organization that once operated within Japan’s criminal underworld. Originally led by a man known only as The Boss, the group followed traditional Yakuza values centered around loyalty, discipline, and honor.

The Boss later took in and raised Kai Chisaki, who would eventually become known as Overhaul. Unlike the older generation, Chisaki sought to restore the Yakuza’s lost power through ruthless methods and dangerous experimentation.

During the rise of All Might and the growing influence of Pro Heroes, the Yakuza lost much of their authority and influence. The Shie Hassaikai, along with many other syndicates, was forced into the shadows and placed under constant surveillance by law enforcement.

Under Overhaul’s leadership, the organization became feared for its brutality, secrecy, and ambition to reclaim dominance over the criminal world.

cardPool.title: Paranormal Liberation Front
cardPool.value:
[Paranormal Liberation Front]

Type: Villain Organization

The Paranormal Liberation Front is a massive and highly organized villain faction created through the merger of the League of Villains and the remaining forces of the Meta Liberation Army.

The organization is led by Grand Commander Tomura Shigaraki, whose goal is to destroy the current hero society and create a world ruled by absolute freedom and power.

The Paranormal Liberation Front is divided into multiple regiments, each specializing in a different aspect of warfare, strategy, or operations. Every regiment is identified by a unique color and commanded by a Lieutenant.

Supporting each Lieutenant are three elite Advisers, regarded as the most skilled and trusted members within their respective regiment. These Advisers oversee operations, command troops, and ensure the organization’s influence continues to spread across the country.

With immense manpower, resources, and military structure, the Paranormal Liberation Front became one of the most dangerous villain organizations in Japan.

cardPool.title: Octo-Lover's Brigade
cardPool.value:
[Octo-Lover's Brigade]

Type: Animal Rights Organization

The Octo-Lover’s Brigade is an animal rights group originating from Osaka that campaigns against the capture, cooking, and consumption of octopuses. Their members believe octopuses are intelligent creatures deserving of protection and freedom.

The organization is primarily composed of individuals with sea-creature-like appearances and mutations, including traits resembling fish, mollusks, cephalopods, and other aquatic lifeforms.

While members dress in different styles, they all wear dark cloth accessories marked with white spots resembling octopus suckers. These scarves and kerchiefs serve as the Brigade’s symbol and identifying mark.

Although many members participate in peaceful activism and demonstrations, extremist factions within the organization are willing to resort to intimidation, sabotage, and violence to force others to accept their beliefs.

Because of these radical elements, the Octo-Lover’s Brigade has gained a controversial reputation throughout Japan.

cardPool.title: Meta Liberation Army
cardPool.value:
[Meta Liberation Army]

Type: Villain Organization

The Meta Liberation Army, often shortened to M.L.A., was a large and influential villain organization built around the belief that the unrestricted use of Quirks is a fundamental human right.

The original Meta Liberation Army was founded by the infamous Destro, who sought to free society from laws and restrictions placed upon Quirk usage. His ideology inspired countless followers and gave rise to a powerful liberation movement.

Years later, the organization was revived by Destro’s descendant, Re-Destro, who rebuilt the army into a massive and well-organized force with political, financial, and military influence across Japan.

Unlike many villain groups driven purely by chaos or destruction, the M.L.A. focused on achieving total liberation through ideology, propaganda, and overwhelming power.

Following its conflict with the League of Villains, the Meta Liberation Army eventually merged with them to create the Paranormal Liberation Front under the leadership of Tomura Shigaraki.

cardPool.title: League of Villains
cardPool.value:
[League of Villains]

Type: Villain Organization

The League of Villains, also known as the Villain Alliance, was a notorious criminal organization composed of powerful and dangerous villains united by their hatred of hero society.

The group was originally founded by All For One, who operated from the shadows while grooming Tomura Shigaraki to become his successor. Over time, Shigaraki rose to leadership and transformed the League into one of the greatest threats facing Japan.

Unlike traditional criminal organizations, the League of Villains sought not only destruction, but the complete collapse of the hero system and the society built around it.

The League attracted criminals, outcasts, and extremists from across the country, many of whom possessed exceptionally dangerous Quirks and deep resentment toward the world of heroes.

Following the events of the Revival Celebration, the League of Villains merged with the Meta Liberation Army to form the Paranormal Liberation Front under Tomura Shigaraki’s command.

cardPool.title: K3 Gang
cardPool.value:
[K3 Gang]

Type: Villain Group

The K3 Gang is a small villain group made up of three young men who idolize famous criminals and anti-hero figures such as Stain. Inspired by the image and reputation of powerful villains, the trio attempts to imitate them through reckless acts of intimidation and public disturbance.

The group is known for terrorizing residents in snowy mountain regions while riding around on snowmobiles. All three members share a stereotypical punk-inspired appearance and travel together as a unit.

Despite calling themselves villains, the K3 Gang is relatively inexperienced and lacks the power or influence of larger criminal organizations. Most of their actions amount to harassment, vandalism, and creating public chaos rather than causing serious destruction.

The members are aware of their own weaknesses, but continue chasing the image of feared villains in hopes of gaining recognition and respect.

cardPool.title: Gollini Family
cardPool.value:
[Gollini Family]

Type: Mafia Crime Family

The Gollini Family is a powerful European mafia organization led by the ruthless Valdo Gollini. The family existed long before the rise of All Might and established itself as one of the most feared criminal syndicates in the region.

Little is known about the organization’s early history, though its original leader was said to value honor, loyalty, and traditional principles over greed and power.
