Those ideals eventually led to his downfall when his own son, Valdo Gollini, murdered him in his office and seized control of the family.

Under Valdo’s leadership, the Gollini Family transformed into a far more brutal and ambitious organization. Through violence, intimidation, and organized crime, the family expanded its influence across Europe while remaining beyond the reach of Heroes and law enforcement.

As their territory and power continued to grow, the Gollini Family became infamous for its wealth, secrecy, and deadly reputation within the criminal underworld.

cardPool.title: Creature Rejection Clan
cardPool.value:
[Creature Rejection Clan (CRC)]

Type: Extremist Religious Organization

The Creature Rejection Clan, commonly known as CRC, is a villainous cult-like organization driven by extreme ideology and religious fervor. Its members are recognized by their ritualistic habits and their signature skull-shaped masks, which conceal their identities and reinforce their collective doctrine.

The CRC rejects individuals with physical “abnormalities,” with a particular focus on discrimination against those possessing Mutant-type Quirks. Despite the stabilization of a modern superpowered society, the group continues to uphold deeply rooted prejudice and exclusionary beliefs.

Originally formed as a protest movement, the organization gradually became more radical over time. Their activities escalated from public demonstrations to acts of violence and targeted attacks, significantly damaging their reputation and public support.

As a result of their extremist shift, the CRC lost much of its influence and membership, eventually fragmenting into smaller scattered cells that continue to operate independently in secrecy.

cardPool.title: Avant-Garders
cardPool.value:
[The Avant-Garders]

Type: Artistic Extremist Group

The Avant-Garders is a small villainous group composed of three young men who identify as artists. Each member embodies a different stereotypical artistic persona, and all three possess Quirk abilities related to artistic expression.

The group follows a radical philosophy that views explosions as the highest form of art, believing that the true essence of beauty lies in the moment of destruction. This belief drives their actions and defines their creative worldview.

To pursue their ideology, the Avant-Garders target art installations, studios, and creative works created by others, destroying them through explosive means in order to “complete” the artwork.

Despite their destructive methods, they genuinely see themselves as artists rather than criminals, and they are particularly fascinated by explosion-based Quirks, which they consider the purest medium of artistic expression.

cardPool.title: Abegawa Tenchu Kai
cardPool.value:
[Abegawa Tenchu Kai]

Type: Former Yakuza Organization

The Abegawa Tenchu Kai was a Yakuza syndicate that once operated within the criminal underworld before being officially classified as a villain organization by law enforcement.

Following this designation, the group’s activities and influence came under heavy scrutiny, weakening its structure and stability. During this period of decline, the vigilante known as Stendhal launched an assault on the organization’s headquarters.

The attack resulted in the deaths of all high-ranking executives during direct combat, effectively dismantling the leadership of the Tenchu Kai.

With its command structure destroyed and its operations disrupted, the organization collapsed soon after, marking the end of the Abegawa Tenchu Kai as a functioning criminal group.

cardPool.title: Mad Hatters
cardPool.value:
[The Mad Hatters]

Type: Rock Music Group

The Mad Hatters is a four-member rock band based in Naruhata, Tokyo. Originally formed by a group of young musicians, the band developed a shared identity under the name “Mad Hatters” and built a reputation for strong musical talent and energetic performances.

They were later invited to perform at the Marukane Department Store Live Event, marking one of their notable public appearances. While they are recognized for their skill and stage presence, it remains unclear whether they have ever performed on a major stage such as Narufest.

Despite their growing popularity, the Mad Hatters are still considered an emerging band, steadily building their reputation within the local music scene.

cardPool.title: World Heroes Association
cardPool.value:
[World Heroes Association]

Type: International Hero Governing Body

The World Heroes Association is a global organization responsible for overseeing and coordinating Hero activity across multiple nations. It is composed of representatives from various countries, each working together to regulate and manage Hero operations on an international scale.

The organization’s primary role is to organize cross-border missions, facilitate cooperation between Hero agencies, and respond to large-scale threats that require global coordination. In times of crisis, the Association can deploy Pro Heroes to assist nations in need, although such interventions are relatively rare.

Due to uneven distribution of Hero forces worldwide, some regions experience higher crime rates when fewer Heroes are stationed locally. This imbalance remains one of the ongoing challenges the World Heroes Association seeks to address.

cardPool.title: Police Force
cardPool.value:
[Police Force]

Type: Law Enforcement Organization

The Police Force is the official law-enforcing body responsible for maintaining public order and handling criminal activity within society. Their primary role is to arrest, detain, and process Villains who have already been subdued by Pro Heroes.

In the early days of Quirks, the Police Force avoided recruiting officers with Quirks due to concerns that such abilities could be misused as weapons. This gap in enforcement led to the rise of Pro Heroes, who took on the role of licensed Quirk users fighting crime under strict legal and ethical regulations.

Today, the Police Force works in coordination with Heroes but focuses mainly on non-Quirk-related crimes and lower-level offenses. Heroes are required to transfer ordinary criminals to police custody, as such cases fall outside Hero jurisdiction.

The Police Force also handles interrogation, investigation, and incarceration of suspects and captured Villains, ensuring due process within the legal system.

cardPool.title: Hero Public Safety Commission
cardPool.value:
[Hero Public Safety Commission]

Type: Government Law Enforcement Agency

The Hero Public Safety Commission is a national authority responsible for regulating Heroes and overseeing their role within society. It manages the relationship between Pro Heroes and the public, ensuring that Hero activity remains lawful, controlled, and effective.

The Commission is led by a committee of non-Hero officials, designed to maintain balance and prevent excessive influence from Hero society over civilian governance. It also serves as a major criminal investigative body, handling high-level and complex cases involving serious threats.

One of its key responsibilities is administering the Provisional Hero License Exam, held twice a year in June and September. Those who successfully pass are granted official Hero licenses, allowing them to legally perform Hero duties.

The Commission works closely with the Police Force to coordinate operations, assign Hero teams, and respond to emergencies requiring structured cooperation between law enforcement and Heroes.

cardPool.title: Feathers
cardPool.value:
[Feathers]

Type: Underground Idol Duo

Feathers is a twin-based underground idol duo composed of sisters Miu and Yu. The pair performs together under a shared stage identity, building their reputation within the local entertainment scene through synchronized performances and strong stage presence.

They were invited to perform at the Marukane Department Store Live Event, marking one of their notable public appearances and giving them wider exposure beyond the underground idol circuit.

Although still considered emerging talents, Feathers have gained attention for their chemistry as twins and their coordinated performance style, steadily growing their fanbase in smaller live venues and events.

cardPool.title: FeatherHATS
cardPool.value:
[FeatherHATS]

Type: Music Band

FeatherHATS is a music group formed by Makoto Tsukauchi and sponsored by the Marukane Department Store. The band brings together young musical talents from Naruhata, aiming to showcase rising performers from the local scene.

Supported by corporate sponsorship, FeatherHATS performs at organized events and promotional stages, helping to introduce emerging artists to a wider audience.

The group is known for its collaborative structure, blending different musical styles from its members while maintaining a cohesive, youthful performance identity.

cardPool.title: East Naruhata High Dance Squad
cardPool.value:
[East Naruhata High Dance Squad]

Type: School Dance Group

The East Naruhata High Dance Squad is a four-member dance team formed at East Naruhata High School. The group represents the school in public performances and local events, showcasing coordinated choreography and youthful stage energy.

They were invited to perform at the Marukane Department Store Live Event, marking one of their most notable appearances outside of school activities.

Leadership within the group is informal, with the “president” role attributed to the member with the strongest stage presence and natural ability to guide performance flow. Together, the squad focuses on synchronization, expression, and improving their performance skills through live events and competitions.

cardPool.title: Kanidoge
cardPool.value:
[Kanidoge]

Type: Food Distribution Company

Kanidoge is a food-products corporation based in Osaka that specializes in the import, distribution, and sale of various types of crab across Japan. The company supplies both fresh seafood and farm-to-table crab products to markets and businesses nationwide.

In addition to its commercial operations, Kanidoge is notable for its use of crab-shaped mechanical units. These mechs are primarily designed to assist in transporting and handling goods, but they also serve a secondary role as mobile advertising displays for the company’s brand.

Through its combination of logistics innovation and seafood specialization, Kanidoge has established a unique presence within Japan’s food distribution industry.

cardPool.title: Help Us Company
cardPool.value:
[H.U.C. (Help Us Company)]

Type: Training & Simulation Organization

The Help Us Company, commonly abbreviated as H.U.C., is a professional organization specializing in rescue and disaster-response training simulations. Its members are trained to act as realistic “victims” in controlled scenarios, placing themselves in danger simulations so that Heroes and trainees can practice rescue operations.

Because Pro Heroes play a central role in society, there is high demand for realistic training environments. H.U.C. fulfills this need by staging scenarios that replicate disasters, accidents, and villain attacks with high accuracy.

Members of H.U.C. are skilled at simulating panic situations, injuries, and crisis conditions, while also observing and evaluating the rescue methods used by Heroes and trainees. They provide structured feedback on whether the response techniques used were appropriate, efficient, and safe.

Through their work, H.U.C. contributes to improving Hero training standards and emergency response effectiveness across society.

cardPool.title: Heroes
cardPool.value:
[Heroes / Pro Heroes]

Type: Licensed Quirk Users / Public Protectors

Heroes are individuals legally authorized to use their Quirks to protect civilians from Villains, natural disasters, and other forms of danger. Those who pursue heroism as a profession are known as Pro Heroes.

In Japan, Heroes are regulated by the Hero Public Safety Commission, while international coordination and oversight of Hero activity is handled by the World Heroes Association. Most Heroes operate through structured groups called Hero Agencies, which organize missions, training, and public safety operations.

According to Endeavor, Hero work is built around three core responsibilities: rescue, evacuation, and combat. Depending on their specialization, Hero Agencies may focus on one of these areas—such as rescue operations or direct combat—or handle all three roles.

Heroes are widely respected by the public and often operate under public visibility, with civilians frequently witnessing and supporting their battles against Villains.

cardPool.title: Villains
cardPool.value:
[Villains]

Type: Criminal Individuals / Organizations

Villains are individuals who use their Quirks to commit crimes, cause destruction, and endanger innocent lives. They exist in many forms, including thieves, murderers, extremist groups, and terrorist organizations.

According to Naomasa Tsukauchi, the overall crime rate in the modern era is relatively low, largely due to the strong presence and pressure of Pro Heroes. However, Villains remain a persistent threat across society.

Motivations for becoming a Villain vary widely, including economic hardship, political ideology, social rejection, or personal tragedy. In many cases, Quirks add an additional layer to criminal activity, allowing for more complex and dangerous forms of crime.

Some individuals become Villains after experiencing life-altering trauma, leading them to reject societal norms entirely. While certain Villains operate alone, others form groups or organizations, often structured with clear leadership hierarchies.

Despite differences in scale and intent, all Villains share one common trait: the use of illegal Quirk activity that places society at risk.

cardPool.title: Vigilantes
cardPool.value:
[Vigilantes]

Type: Unauthorized Quirk Users / Civilian Protectors

Vigilantes are individuals who carry out Hero-like activities without legal authorization, often acting independently of Hero agencies and law enforcement regulations. Due to strict Hero licensing and Quirk usage laws, such actions are considered illegal and fall under vigilantism.

Although unlawful, Vigilantes exist in a legal and moral gray area. In situations where Pro Heroes are unavailable or delayed, their intervention can result in lives being saved, and in some cases, they may even cooperate with Heroes during emergencies.

This dual nature has led to ongoing debate within law enforcement and regulatory bodies regarding how Vigilantes should be treated—whether as criminals to be punished or as unofficial assets in crisis situations.

As a result, Vigilantes remain a controversial presence in society, balancing between public necessity and legal violation.

cardPool.title: Sidekicks
cardPool.value:
[Sidekicks]

Type: Hero Agency Support Staff

Sidekicks are licensed Hero assistants who work under the supervision of a Pro Hero at a Hero Agency. Typically less experienced or less prominent than the agency’s lead Hero, Sidekicks provide operational support during missions and emergencies.

While the Pro Hero serves as the primary field operative responsible for rescue operations and combat against Villains, Sidekicks act as backup and support, assisting with coordination, logistics, and on-site response.

The size and structure of Sidekick teams vary widely. Some agencies employ only a few Sidekicks, while others maintain large teams. Certain Pro Heroes may also choose to operate without any Sidekicks at all.

Hiring decisions are made at the discretion of the agency head, who may select Sidekicks based on experience, skills, or Quirk utility. In some cases, even unlicensed Vigilantes may be recruited as Sidekicks, providing them with a legal pathway into Hero society.

cardPool.title: Todoroki Family
cardPool.value:
[Todoroki Family]

Type: Family

The Todoroki Family is a prominent Hero family consisting of Enji Todoroki (Endeavor), his wife Rei Todoroki, and their four children: Toya Todoroki, Fuyumi Todoroki, Natsuo Todoroki, and Shoto Todoroki.

Enji Todoroki is a top-ranked Pro Hero known for his exceptional combat ability and leadership within Hero society. Rei Todoroki is the family’s mother, while their children each have their own distinct paths and relationships shaped by the family’s complex history.

Toya, Fuyumi, Natsuo, and Shoto each carry the legacy of the Todoroki name, with differing experiences and perspectives shaped by their upbringing and connection to Hero society.

cardPool.title: Shimura Family
cardPool.value:
[Shimura Family]

Type: Family

The Shimura Family was the birth family of Tomura Shigaraki before he became a Villain. They were an ordinary household whose history became closely tied to the origins of one of society’s most dangerous criminals.

The family is most notably connected to the legacy of Nana Shimura, a former Pro Hero, whose lineage indirectly influenced later events involving Tomura Shigaraki.

Very little is known about the Shimura Family.

cardPool.title: Ida Family
cardPool.value:
[Ida Family]

Type: Hero Family Lineage

The Ida Family is a prestigious hero family with a long-standing tradition in professional heroics spanning multiple generations. For decades, members of the family have served as Pro Heroes, building a reputation rooted in discipline, responsibility, and service to society.

Most members of the Ida Family are born with the Engine Quirk, characterized by engine-like exhaust pipes that grant enhanced speed and mobility. This Quirk has become a defining trait of the family lineage, particularly associated with Tenya Ida and his ancestors.

Tenya’s grandfather developed a unique training method intended to enhance the Engine Quirk’s performance across generations. The process involves removing the exhaust-like organs through intense and painful means, followed by rigorous training. Over time, stronger and more efficient engine components regrow, resulting in improved speed and endurance.

Through this tradition, the Ida Family has maintained and refined their Quirk abilities, passing down both their hero legacy and their specialized training methods.

cardPool.title: Wild, Wild Pussycats
cardPool.value:
========================================
STORYCARD — WILD WILD PUSSYCATS
========================================

[OVERVIEW]
The Wild, Wild Pussycats are a professional Hero team specializing in rescue operations, wilderness survival training, and disaster response. They are known for their strong coordination, high mobility, and deep experience in field-based Hero work rather than urban combat.

The group consists of Mandalay (strategic leader and communicator), Pixie-Bob (terrain manipulation through earth-based Quirk use), Ragdoll (enhanced sensory tracking and analysis of Quirks), and Tiger (close-combat powerhouse and physical trainer).

Members:
- Shino Sosaki (Mandalay)
- Ryuko Tsuchikawa (Pixie-Bob)
- Tomoko (Ragdoll)
- Tiger

----------------------------------------

[ROLE IN HERO SOCIETY]
Unlike combat-focused Hero agencies, the Wild, Wild Pussycats prioritize survival training, evacuation strategy, and environmental adaptability. They often assist in U.A. student development programs, especially in preparing students for real-world disaster scenarios outside controlled environments.

Ragdoll’s Quirk allows her to monitor and track multiple individuals simultaneously, making the team extremely effective in locating missing persons and coordinating rescue operations across large territories.

cardPool.title: Kota Izumi
cardPool.value:
Real Name: Kota Izumi

Alias: None

Quirk Name: Water Control

Occupation/Role: UA High School Hero Course Student, Class 1-A

Personality: Initially withdrawn and cynical following his parents' deaths, Kota was cold toward heroes and those aspiring to become them. After being rescued by Izuku Midoriya, he has slowly opened himself to others, though he remains somewhat indifferent and prideful. He is principled and refuses indecency, punishing rule-breakers without hesitation.

Appearance: A short boy with spiky black hair standing roughly Mineta's height. He wears a short-sleeved collared button-up shirt with dark shorts and a distinctive red cap adorned with two golden spike-shaped horns. His hero costume features a dark green vest with a dark gray helmet matching his parents' design, complete with large spike-shaped horns. He wears red high-top sneakers that match Izuku's footwear.

Backstory: Kota is the son of the pro hero team Water Hose, both deceased. Raised by his aunt Shino Sosaki of the Wild Wild Pussycats, he initially despised heroes, believing they abandoned him through their deaths. Meeting Izuku Midoriya and being rescued from the villain Muscular proved transformative, allowing Kota to understand his parents' noble sacrifice and recognize that heroes put others' lives before their own.

Additional Information: Kota enrolled at UA High School eight years after the Final War to follow his parents' and Izuku's example. He is beginning his hero journey with newfound purpose and emotional maturity, though still guarded about his past trauma.

cardPool.title: Arc 1
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 1 — U.A. ENTRANCE EXAM
========================================

Izuku Midoriya arrives at U.A. for the Hero Course entrance exam. Candidates enter a simulated city filled with combat robots. Points are earned by destroying robots, with rescue points awarded for saving others.

Izuku initially cannot use One For All safely. During the exam, he notices Uraraka trapped under debris from a falling robot and chooses to save her instead of pursuing points.

He jumps in and destroys a zero-point robot to prevent its collapse from killing her. This action grants him rescue points.

After evaluations, Izuku is accepted into U.A. despite low combat score due to rescue performance. Bakugo is accepted as one of the highest scorers. Class 1-A is formed.

cardPool.title: Arc 2
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 2 — QUIRK APPREHENSION TEST
========================================

Class 1-A is subjected to Aizawa’s Quirk Apprehension Test on their first day. The test includes sprinting, grip strength, ball throw, endurance, and agility measurements using Quirks.

Aizawa states that the lowest-performing student may be expelled, forcing immediate pressure on the class.

Izuku repeatedly breaks his own fingers while trying to control One For All in the ball throw test. Uraraka uses zero-gravity to send the ball out of orbit range. Bakugo dominates multiple physical categories through explosive mobility.

Each student is ranked based on total Quirk efficiency and physical output. After results, Aizawa reveals expulsion was a bluff meant to measure potential under pressure.

cardPool.title: Arc 3
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 3 — U.S.J. INCIDENT
========================================

Class 1-A arrives at U.S.J. for rescue training under Aizawa, Thirteen, and other Pro Heroes. The facility is divided into disaster simulation zones.

Kurogiri activates a warp gate, allowing the League of Villains to enter the facility. Students are scattered across zones like flood, fire, landslide, and urban collapse.

Shigaraki targets Aizawa and Izuku directly. Villains coordinate attacks across multiple groups.

A Nomu is deployed specifically to kill All Might. All Might arrives despite limited stamina and engages the Nomu in extended combat.

All Might defeats the Nomu and forces the villains to retreat through Kurogiri’s warp gate. The attack confirms organized villain coordination targeting Hero society.

cardPool.title: Arc 4
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 4 — U.A. SPORTS FESTIVAL
========================================

U.A. hosts a national sports festival broadcast across Japan. Students compete in obstacle races, cavalry battles, and elimination tournaments.

Izuku modifies One For All usage to avoid breaking his body. Todoroki refuses to use his fire Quirk initially due to family conflict. Bakugo advances through brute force and aggression.

During the final rounds, Todoroki uses his fire for the first time against Izuku after emotional confrontation about his past. Bakugo defeats Todoroki in the final match.

Bakugo is declared overall winner of the festival. Hero agencies begin recruiting students for internships based on performance exposure.

cardPool.title: Arc 5
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 5 — HERO INTERNSHIPS & STAIN INCIDENT
========================================

Students begin internships at Hero agencies. Izuku trains under Gran Torino and learns advanced movement control. Iida joins Ingenium’s agency.

In Hosu City, Stain attacks Pro Heroes, targeting those he deems unworthy. His Quirk allows paralysis through ingestion of blood.

Nomu activity occurs simultaneously in the city. Iida confronts Stain alone and is paralyzed. Izuku and Todoroki intervene during overlapping combat situations.

Endeavor defeats a Nomu while Stain is later subdued after combined efforts. Stain is arrested, but his ideology spreads across Villain groups and causes wider instability in Hero perception.

cardPool.title: Arc 6
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 6 — FOREST TRAINING CAMP ARC
========================================

Class 1-A trains in wilderness survival and Quirk control at a remote camp.

The League of Villains Vanguard Action Squad attacks the facility.

Students are split across forest terrain and forced into survival situations.

Bakugo is captured during chaos.

Multiple students are injured during escape and regrouping.

Villains withdraw after achieving capture objective.

cardPool.title: Arc 7
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 7 — KAMINO INCIDENT
========================================

League of Villains holds Bakugo in a hidden Kamino Ward location.

Hero intelligence locates the hideout.

A rescue operation is launched involving multiple Pro Heroes.

All Might confronts All For One during the raid.

A large-scale battle unfolds across Kamino Ward.

All Might fights in his weakened state and defeats All For One using remaining power.

Bakugo is rescued.

All For One is critically injured and forced into retreat.

All Might’s final Hero form is publicly revealed, ending his era as Symbol of Peace.

cardPool.title: Arc 8
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 8 — PROVISIONAL HERO LICENSE EXAM
========================================

Students take the national Hero License Exam.

Candidates complete large-scale rescue simulations with competing schools.

Successful students gain legal authorization for supervised Hero work.

cardPool.title: Arc 9
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 9 — SHIE HASSAIKAI RAID ARC
========================================

Hero teams investigate Shie Hassaikai Yakuza operations.

Eri is identified as source of Quirk-erasing bullets.

A coordinated underground raid begins.

Mirio fights Overhaul alone and is hit by a Quirk-erasing bullet.

Mirio loses his Quirk permanently.

Izuku reaches Eri and engages Overhaul.

Overhaul is defeated.

Eri is rescued and placed under Hero protection.

cardPool.title: Arc 10
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 10 — CULTURAL FESTIVAL ARC
========================================

U.A. prepares a Cultural Festival performance.

Class 1-A builds stage and performs live show.

Gentle Criminal and La Brava infiltrate U.A.

Izuku intercepts Gentle Criminal during intrusion.

Gentle Criminal is defeated.

La Brava surrenders.

Festival continues successfully.

Eri attends performance.

cardPool.title: Arc 11
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 11 — META LIBERATION ARMY ARC
========================================

League of Villains enters Deika City.

Meta Liberation Army engages League forces.

Twice is killed during early battle.

Shigaraki fights Re-Destro across collapsing city.

Shigaraki’s Quirk fully awakens and destroys large areas.

Re-Destro is defeated.

MLA submits to Shigaraki.

Paranormal Liberation Front is formed.

cardPool.title: Arc 12
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 12 — WAR PREPARATION ARC
========================================

Hero Commission confirms PLF as nationwide threat.

Heroes assemble multi-agency strike teams.

U.A. students receive operational briefing.

Shigaraki undergoes stabilization procedure under AFO influence.

Both sides prepare simultaneous large-scale operations.

Hero forces deploy across multiple targets.

cardPool.title: Arc 13
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 13 — PARANORMAL LIBERATION WAR
========================================

Heroes attack Jaku Hospital and Gunga Mountain.

High-End Nomu engage Hero teams.

Shigaraki awakens mid-operation and begins massive destruction.

Dabi reveals identity as Toya Todoroki during battle.

Twice is killed, collapsing Villain coordination.

Gigantomachia advances across Japan.

Shigaraki expands decay across battlefield zones.

Heroes begin evacuation and containment operations nationwide.

cardPool.title: Arc 14
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 14 — DARK HERO ARC
========================================

Izuku Midoriya leaves U.A. and begins operating independently across Japan as a solo Hero, tracking Villain activity and protecting civilians without agency support.

He encounters multiple escaped prisoners released during societal collapse events, engaging them in isolated urban battles while transporting civilians to safety zones.

During this period, Izuku is ambushed by Kaina Tsutsumi (Lady Nagant), a former Hero Public Safety Commission assassin deployed to capture him alive.

Nagant engages Izuku using long-range precision rifle Quirks across extreme distances, forcing Izuku to adapt One For All usage with Blackwhip, Fa Jin, and Danger Sense in combination.

Nagant reveals information about the Hero Commission’s internal corruption and her past role as an assassin executing covert eliminations of targets labeled threats to Hero society.

Izuku refuses to kill her and instead attempts to break her resolve while avoiding lethal retaliation.

During extended combat, Izuku closes distance despite repeated sniper suppression and ultimately defeats Nagant without killing her.

After defeat, Nagant suffers Quirk overload collapse and is captured alive rather than eliminated.

She later provides intelligence on Hero Commission operations and the existence of deeper control structures influencing Hero society.

Izuku continues his solo operations but begins relying more heavily on coordinated support strategies after this encounter.

Class 1-A later locates Izuku and forcibly brings him back to U.A., ending his solo operation phase.

Hero society formally begins emergency restructuring due to increasing internal instability and Villain resurgence.

cardPool.title: Arc 15
cardPool.value:
========================================
ARC 15 — FINAL WAR ARC
========================================

Heroes launch coordinated final war against All For One and Shigaraki.

Bakugo engages Shigaraki.

Todoroki confronts Dabi.

Ochaco engages Toga.

All Might confronts All For One using armored support.

Izuku fights Shigaraki as One For All vestiges appear.

All For One is separated from Shigaraki.

Shigaraki collapses after final exchange.

Major battles conclude across all fronts.

Heroes have won - but with a major cost.

cardPool.title: Momo Yaoyorozu

Personality: Prudent and dedicated natural leader who remains levelheaded in danger, though capable of panic. Kind and polite yet blunt about others' mistakes; she seeks to help peers improve. Her wealthy upbringing instilled sensible respect for others, though she finds crude behavior discouraging. Despite her revealing costume, she maintains an innocent, non-lewd view of nudity and is sensitive to vulgarity and sexual advances.

Long black hair tied in a spiky ponytail with a strand falling down her right side; sharp onyx eyes with determined expression. Wears UA female uniform: gray dress jacket with teal stripes and golden buttons over white dress shirt, red tie, and teal pleated skirt, paired with brown shoes and knee-high black socks. Her hero costume is a high-collared crimson sleeveless leotard with white trim, open from neck to navel to expose skin for her Quirk use, calf-length red heeled boots, and two beige utility belts.

Backstory: A recommendation student at UA High School training to become a Pro Hero. From a wealthy family that instilled discipline and responsibility. Recently participated in the UA Sports Festival where she suffered a rapid loss to Fumikage Tokoyami, shaking her initial confidence through unfavorable comparisons to other students.

Additional Information: As Class 1-A's vice representative, she demonstrates leadership qualities and has tutored classmates at her home. Her Quirk requires exposed skin to function, necessitating her revealing costume design within UA regulations.

cardPool.title: Mon
cardPool.value:
Real Name: Mon
Alias: None
Quirk Name: None
Occupation/Role: Pet dog of the Shimura Family
Personality: Friendly, protective, and compassionate; enjoys play and walks; demonstrates loyalty by comforting distressed loved ones despite lacking human understanding.

Later that night, Mon sat with the crying boy, offering comfort—but in that moment, Tenko's Quirk, Decay, manifested uncontrollably, killing Mon instantly. Mon became the first victim of the catastrophe that would claim the entire family.
Additional Information: Non-combat character; significant to Tenko Shimura's tragic origin story and psychological development; his death marks the pivotal moment of Tenko's Quirk manifestation and family tragedy.

Lady Nagant

Personality:
Serious, disciplined, and ruthless in pursuing objectives, yet capable of displaying a casual, happier side beneath her stoic exterior. Direct and fearless, she doesn't hesitate to use force when necessary but possesses an underlying capacity for change and redemption.

Tall pointed zip-up boots with black pinstripes complete her outfit.

Once a bright young student, Kaina was shaped by the Hero Public Safety Commission into a capable pro hero. Her path eventually led her into darker work, resulting in imprisonment in Tartarus. Freed during All For One's escape, she initially continued as a villain before being convinced by Izuku Midoriya and Hawks to rejoin the heroes' cause.

Additional Information:
Not a current UA student; an adult operative with extensive combat and marksmanship training. Her Rifle Quirk enables her to fire projectiles with precision. She operates independently and carries ammunition in her utility belt canisters.

Personality: Tough, blunt, and fearless with an independent streak. Rumi respects those who speak their mind and disdains team-based heroism, believing heroes should rely solely on their own strength. Despite her brash demeanor, she will assist others when needed and isn't afraid to ask for help in genuine danger.

She has narrow red eyes with long eyelashes, straight white hair reaching her thighs with right-parted bangs to her waist. Her Quirk grants her long white rabbit ears and a small round tail. She wears a sleeveless white leotard with dark purple trim, a yellow crescent moon design across her chest, purple thigh-high boots, thick white gloves with triangular protrusions, and a metal plate around her midriff resembling rabbit feet.

Backstory: A former middle school hooligan expelled for fighting, Rumi channeled her love of combat into the Underground Masquerade fight rings during high school. There she earned respect and established herself as a formidable future Pro Hero, refusing compensation and vowing to make it big independently through raw strength alone.

Additional Information: Mirko operates as a solo hero across Japan, actively pursuing villains. She earned the respect of notable figures like O'Clock and once came to Endeavor's aid during a major villain encounter, demonstrating her willingness to collaborate despite her independent philosophy.

Backstory: A highly skilled Pro Hero and the strongest member of the Wild, Wild Pussycats, Ryuko has built her reputation on mastering earth manipulation for mountain rescues and hero operations. Her confidence in her abilities matches her eccentric personality, though beneath her wackiness lies genuine care for the next generation of heroes.
Additional Information: During the Quirk Apprehension Test arc, Ryuko demonstrates her combat prowess by overwhelming Class 1-A students with her Quirk, forcing them to exhaust their powers. Her Earth Flow is recognized as dangerous enough to threaten even formidable villains, making her a valuable asset to hero society.
