• Information gathering
• Concealment
• Technique subtlety
• Emotional discipline
• Public presentation

Their sorcerers are often trained to operate without appearing to use sorcery at all.

SPECIALTY
Tachibana Techniques commonly favor:
• Sensory interference
• Concealment
• Memory effects
• Illusions
• Tracking
• Emotional manipulation
• Information extraction

Not every member develops these traits, but the clan actively cultivates them.

ARTIFACTS
Their vaults contain:
• Concealment tools
• Recording artifacts
• Sensory objects
• Ritual mirrors
• Communication tools
• Restricted information archives

STRUCTURE
The clan maintains an elegant public image while keeping its internal affairs heavily compartmentalized.

REPUTATION
Among sorcerers:
Polished, secretive, socially dangerous, and rarely as harmless as they appear.

The Tachibana prefer to know everything before anyone realizes they were involved.

cardPool.title: Kuma Clan
cardPool.value:
Kuma Clan

Entry:
The Kuma Clan is one of the four major sorcerer clans.

Publicly, they are associated with construction, heavy industry, private security, and mountain estates.

Privately, they are famous for physically powerful sorcerers and brutally practical training.

TRADITION
The Kuma value:
• Reinforcement
• Close-quarters combat
• Durability
• Weapon mastery
• Endurance
• Direct results

Even clan members without exceptional innate Techniques are expected to become dangerous through raw Quirk-Energy control and physical training.

TRAINING
Kuma training is notoriously severe.

Sorcerers are conditioned through:
• Heavy impact training
• Long endurance exercises
• Reinforced weapon drills
• Live sparring
• Harsh environmental exposure

ARTIFACTS
Their vaults favor practical equipment:
• Reinforced weapons
• Heavy combat tools
• Armor
• Restraint artifacts
• Durable Quirk-Energy materials

STRUCTURE
Rank is heavily influenced by strength, reliability, and combat performance.

REPUTATION
Among sorcerers:
Blunt, disciplined, stubborn, and extremely difficult to put down.

The Kuma rarely start political conflicts, but ending one by force is usually a bad idea.

cardPool.title: Fujiwara Clan
cardPool.value:
Fujiwara Clan

Entry:
The Fujiwara Clan is one of the four major sorcerer clans.

Publicly, they are an old aristocratic family tied to finance, law, education, and cultural institutions.

Privately, they are known for precision, scholarship, and highly technical Quirk-Energy Techniques.

TRADITION
The Fujiwara value:
• Technique refinement
• Barrier theory
• Contracts and Binding Vows
• Formal education
• Record keeping
• Political influence

Their sorcerers are often trained as analysts, barrier specialists, negotiators, and tacticians rather than simple frontline fighters.

ARTIFACTS
Fujiwara vaults are especially known for:
• Technique manuscripts
• Barrier tools
• Sealed contracts
• Ritual implements
• Historical records
• Quirk-Energy research

STRUCTURE
The clan is rigidly hierarchical and highly educated.

Succession favors competence, lineage, political usefulness, and rare innate Techniques.

REPUTATION
Among sorcerers:
Cultured, calculating, difficult to deceive.

They prefer control through information, agreements, and preparation rather than open force.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Higher-Ups
cardPool.value:
Jujutsu Higher-Ups


Entry:
The Jujutsu Higher-Ups are the secret governing body overseeing sorcerers, Quirk-Energy Techniques, Remnants, restricted artifacts, and hidden clans.

They operate completely outside normal hero society.

STRUCTURE
The Higher-Ups are composed mainly of:
• Elder sorcerers
• Representatives of major clans
• Barrier specialists
• Archivists
• Artifact custodians
• Conservative administrators

Most members value secrecy, stability, lineage, and control over reform.

AUTHORITY
They regulate:
• Sorcerer ranks and assignments
• Exorcism operations
• Restricted Techniques
• Domain users
• Artifact ownership and transport
• Hidden training institutions
• Dangerous bloodlines
• Internal executions and sanctions

They may authorize surveillance, confinement, forced retirement, or execution when someone is considered too dangerous.

RELATIONSHIP WITH HERO SOCIETY
The Higher-Ups do not answer to the Hero Commission.

The Hero Commission generally does not know they exist.

When sorcerer activity overlaps with hero incidents, records are altered, witnesses are redirected, and events are given conventional Quirk-based explanations.

POLITICS
The organization is deeply conservative.

Common priorities:
• Preserve secrecy
• Protect old clans
• Control dangerous Techniques
• Prevent public exposure
• Maintain existing hierarchy

Younger or independent sorcerers frequently view them as corrupt, stagnant, and overly willing to sacrifice individuals for institutional stability.

CLANS
Major sorcerer families possess significant influence but do not completely control the Higher-Ups.

Clan alliances, inheritance disputes, rare Techniques, and artifact ownership heavily affect internal politics.

PUBLIC STATUS
To ordinary society, the Jujutsu Higher-Ups do not exist.

Even most heroes would assume any evidence of them refers to a private religious organization, old family council, or classified government department.

cardPool.title: Non-Sorcerer Perception
cardPool.value:
Non-sorcerer Perception

Entry:
Non-sorcerers live largely unaware of the hidden Quirk-Energy world.

They know Quirks, support technology, hero work, and villain incidents. They do not understand sorcery, Quirk-Energy Techniques, Domains, or Quirk Remnants as distinct systems.

GENERAL PERCEPTION
When confronted with sorcery, non-sorcerers usually assume:
• An unknown Quirk
• A mutation
• Support equipment
• Hallucination or stress
• Hidden technology
• A villain effect
• An unexplained accident

They interpret unfamiliar phenomena through the Quirk framework because that is what modern society understands.

SORCERERS
Sorcerers are usually mistaken for unusual Quirk users.

Even when a Technique behaves unlike a normal Quirk, observers tend to assume the person's Quirk is simply poorly documented, highly complex, or deliberately concealed.

QUIRK REMNANTS
Non-sorcerers cannot normally see Quirk Remnants.

They perceive only indirect effects such as:
• Unexplained injuries
• Objects moving or breaking
• Sudden pressure or nausea
• Environmental damage
• Apparent attacks from empty space

Heroes often misclassify these cases as villain activity, Quirk accidents, structural failures, or unknown phenomena.

DOMAINS
A Domain may be perceived as abrupt spatial distortion, sensory disruption, disappearance, or an abnormal Quirk effect.

Observers outside usually lack the framework to identify what actually occurred.

PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE
There is no accepted scientific or governmental model for sorcery.

Scattered rumors, folklore, classified reports, and unexplained incidents exist, but most people dismiss them individually.

To ordinary society, the hidden system does not look like a second power system.

It looks like a collection of very strange Quirks and impossible incidents.

cardPool.title: Meta Restricted Individuals
cardPool.value:
Meta Restricted Individuals

Entry:
Meta Restricted individuals are extremely rare humans born with zero Quirk-Energy and no Quirk Factor whatsoever.

In exchange, their bodies develop far beyond normal human limits.

CORE TRAIT
They possess:
• No Quirk-Energy core
• No Quirk Factor
• No Quirk
• No innate Quirk-Energy Technique
• No ability to use Reinforcement or standard sorcery

This absence is absolute.

PHYSICAL COMPENSATION
Their bodies compensate with extreme natural ability:
• Superhuman strength
• Extreme speed and reflexes
• Exceptional durability
• Enhanced senses
• High stamina
• Precise coordination
• Rapid physical adaptation

The strongest Meta Restricted individuals can physically compete with top heroes and sorcerers despite possessing no supernatural energy source.

PERCEPTION
Because they emit no Quirk-Energy signature, they are unusually difficult for sorcerers, barriers, and Techniques to detect.

Highly developed senses may allow them to perceive Quirk Remnants indirectly through movement, pressure, smell, sound, temperature changes, or disturbances in the environment.

INTERACTION
Many Quirk-Energy systems treat them incorrectly or fail to recognize them entirely.

Possible effects:
• Some barriers may not register them as valid targets
• Certain sure-hit systems may fail to automatically lock onto them
• Quirk-Energy sensing cannot locate them
• Techniques requiring an energy signature may behave unpredictably

They are still physically vulnerable to attacks once struck.

EQUIPMENT
Because they cannot reinforce themselves or weapons, Meta Restricted fighters often rely on specialized Quirk-Energy artifacts or exceptionally durable conventional weapons.

RARITY
Meta Restriction is congenital and cannot normally be chosen, induced, or removed.

It is not considered a Quirk.

It is the complete absence of the systems from which Quirks and sorcery originate.

cardPool.title: Quirk Remnant
cardPool.value:
Quirk Remnant

Type:
Quirk-Energy Phenomenon

Entry:
Quirk Remnants are hostile entities formed when residual Quirk-Energy, negative emotion, trauma, and repeated Quirk activity accumulate and become self-sustaining.

Nearly everyone possesses Quirk-Energy, but almost no one can consciously perceive or manipulate it.

ORIGIN
Remnants commonly form around:
• Death
• Fear
• Hatred
• Severe trauma
• Repeated Quirk use
• Mass-casualty events

Common locations include hospitals, prisons, disaster zones, battlefields, and major villain incident sites.

FORMATION
Residual Quirk-Energy can retain fragments of emotion, instinct, and Quirk behavior.

When enough accumulates, it may organize into an independent entity.

A Remnant's form and abilities are shaped by:
• Emotions surrounding its creation
• Nearby Quirks
• Cause of trauma or death
• Local fears and beliefs
• Environment

VISIBILITY
Normal civilians and heroes cannot see Quirk Remnants.

They may only notice indirect effects such as unexplained injuries, pressure, nausea, environmental damage, or movement with no visible source.

Sorcerers and trained Quirk-Energy users can perceive them directly.

SORCERERS
Sorcerers locate and exorcise Remnants.

Hero agencies usually misclassify these incidents as villain activity, Quirk malfunctions, accidents, or unexplained phenomena.

COMBAT
Remnants are best destroyed through:
• Quirk-Energy reinforcement
• Quirk-Energy Techniques
• Specialized artifacts
• Domain-based methods

Destroying the visible body may not be enough if its Quirk-Energy core survives.

THREAT
Weak Remnants behave like pests or animals.

Stronger ones may develop intelligence, speech, Techniques, Domains, and independent goals.

The strongest can threaten entire districts while remaining invisible to ordinary heroes.

cardPool.title: Domain Expansions
cardPool.value:
Domain Expansions

Type:
Quirk-Energy Technique

Entry:
A Domain Expansion is an advanced Quirk-Energy Technique that creates a controlled territory and imprints the user's personal Technique into it.

CORE MECHANIC
The user releases a large amount of Quirk-Energy, forms a barrier, and defines an interior space governed by their Technique.

Normally, a Technique is activated through the user's body.

Inside a Domain, the barrier itself carries the Technique.

This allows effects to originate from anywhere within the Domain instead of only from the user.

SURE-HIT EFFECT
A completed Domain can automatically recognize valid targets and apply the user's Technique directly to them.

"Sure-hit" does not mean unlimited power.

It means normal requirements such as aiming, reaching, or establishing contact are bypassed.

Actual effectiveness still depends on:
• Technique output
• User skill
• Target resistance
• Available Quirk-Energy
• Domain rules

BARRIER
Most Domains create a sealed barrier around the affected area.

The barrier determines:
• Size
• Durability
• Entry and exit conditions
• Target selection
• Sure-hit rules
• Internal environment

The interior may appear much larger or structurally different from the physical area outside.

OPEN DOMAIN
Exceptionally skilled users can impose a Domain directly onto real space without sealing it inside a barrier.

This removes containment but can greatly increase range and makes conventional barrier destruction less useful.

DOMAIN CLASHES
When Domains overlap, their barriers, rules, and Techniques interfere.

The more refined Domain usually gains control, though output, structure, and compatibility also matter.

LIMITS
• Extremely high Quirk-Energy cost
• Requires advanced barrier control
• Requires mastery of a personal Technique
• Heavy neurological and physical strain
• Technique control may temporarily worsen after collapse

cardPool.title: Simple Domain
cardPool.value:
Simple Domain

Type:
Quirk-Energy Technique

Entry:
Simple Domain is a defensive barrier Technique designed to counter Domain Expansion and other barrier-based sure-hit effects.

CORE MECHANIC
The user deploys a small controlled field around themselves using Quirk-Energy.

Unlike a full Domain Expansion, Simple Domain does not imprint a personal Technique into the space and does not create a true sure-hit effect.

Its purpose is neutralization.

Inside the field, hostile sure-hit targeting is disrupted by interfering with the barrier logic that automatically applies Techniques to the user.

EFFECT
Simple Domain can:
• Cancel or weaken sure-hit effects
• Create a temporary safe zone inside hostile Domains
• Interfere with automatic Technique targeting
• Give the user time to escape, counterattack, or deploy another barrier

The field normally stays centered on the user and moves with them only if their version is specifically trained to do so.

LIMITS
• Small effective radius
• Does not overpower a Domain itself
• Strong or highly refined Domains can erode it
• Requires constant Quirk-Energy control
• Losing stance, concentration, or output can collapse the field
• Provides little protection against ordinary attacks that do not rely on sure-hit mechanics

Simple Domain is easier and cheaper than Domain Expansion, making it one of the most practical anti-Domain Techniques.

cardPool.title: Barrier Techniques
cardPool.value:
Quirk-Energy Technique — Barrier Techniques

Entry:
Barrier Techniques are Quirk-energy methods used to create artificial boundaries and controlled spaces.

Core Function:
A barrier defines an area and applies rules to its boundary. Depending on the user's skill, barriers can block entry, conceal an area, contain danger, protect targets, divide space, or create controlled combat zones.

Known Uses:

* Basic Barrier — Surrounds and protects a limited area.
* Curtain — Creates near-perfect camouflage around a designated space. It bends or suppresses sensory information crossing the boundary, including visible light, sound, heat signatures, movement, attack flashes, and Quirk-energy emissions. Outsiders may see the area as normal, empty, darkened, or otherwise unremarkable while people inside can still perceive outward normally. Curtains usually conceal rather than physically block entry.
* Conditional Barrier — Allows or rejects specific people, objects, or conditions according to preset rules.
* Containment Barrier — Prevents something dangerous from leaving a defined area.
* Domain Framework — Provides the structural foundation required for advanced Domain-based techniques.

Complexity:
Simple barriers can be learned relatively quickly, but advanced barriers require precise Quirk-energy control and carefully defined conditions.

Limits:
Poorly constructed barriers can crack, leak energy, collapse under pressure, trap unintended targets, or incorrectly accept or reject something.

Curtains can also produce visual inconsistencies, muffled sound artifacts, strange shadows, or energy leakage if poorly made.

Stronger barriers generally require more energy, tighter conditions, smaller areas, or longer setup times. Complex rule-based barriers are much harder to maintain than simple walls.

cardPool.title: Binding Vows & Chants
cardPool.value:
Binding Vows & Chants — Quirk-Energy Lore

Binding Vows:
Binding Vows are self-imposed Quirk-energy contracts. The user voluntarily accepts a real restriction, risk, or condition in exchange for increased efficiency, output, control, or another defined benefit.

Rules:
- The restriction must meaningfully limit the user.
- Greater sacrifice produces greater compensation.
- Vows can be temporary, situational, or long-term.
- Breaking a vow causes severe backlash, usually loss of the granted benefit, energy disruption, injury, or worse depending on the vow.
- A vow cannot grant abilities the user fundamentally lacks; it only amplifies or modifies what is already possible.

Example:
A sorcerer declares that for the duration of a battle he will not activate his Quirk-Energy Technique once in the battle.

In exchange, his Reinforcement output rises to roughly 50% more of its normal maximum for as long as the vow remains active.

Chants:
Chants are spoken formulas used to stabilize complex Quirk-energy control. They do not create power from nothing; they improve precision, efficiency, timing, or output by forcing the user through a deliberate activation sequence.

Chants often use metaphorical words, and don't actually have any outside effect while being said. (aka. they won't do anything on the outside)

For example, 'Nine Ropes, Polarized Light, Crow & Declaration, Between The Front & The Back' is a functioning chant.

Chants effectively award creativity and its truth metaphorically, and the wasted breath and stamina during the chant.

cardPool.title: Reverse Flow Technique
cardPool.value:
Quirk-Energy Technique — Reverse Flow Technique

Entry:
Reverse Flow Technique, or RFT, is an advanced Quirk-energy healing method. It is not a Quirk, magic, or ordinary regeneration.

Core Function:
RFT converts inherently negative Quirk-energy into positive restorative energy.

Formula:

Negative Energy × Negative Energy = Positive Energy

The conversion takes place inside the brain, requiring immense precision and Quirk-energy expenditure. The resulting positive energy is then circulated through the body to repair damage.

Healing:
RFT can close wounds, stop bleeding, repair torn tissue, mend bones, restore organs and nerves, and at advanced levels regenerate limbs or major body parts.

A skilled outside user can also repair another person's damaged Quirk-energy core.

Current State:
RFT is extraordinarily difficult to learn. Most users require extensive knowledge, instinctive understanding, and exceptional control. In rare cases, a near-death experience can cause the process to suddenly "click."

Caveats:

* RFT is intentionally extremely powerful once mastered.
* Severe wounds can be healed in seconds if enough energy is available.
* Missing limbs and organs can be regenerated, but the energy cost rises sharply with the amount and complexity of tissue restored.
* Repeated regeneration in a short period can rapidly drain even a large Quirk-energy reserve.
* Healing another person is generally harder and less efficient than self-healing.
* Core repair is especially demanding and requires precise outside application.
* RFT can keep damaged brain tissue alive during oxygen deprivation as long as energy remains.
* It cannot restore someone after complete brain destruction or once the user's Quirk-energy reserves are fully exhausted.

Limits:
RFT does not grant immortality. Catastrophic brain damage, overwhelming energy disruption, extreme toxins, or simply running out of Quirk-energy can still kill the user.

cardPool.title: Quirk-Energy
cardPool.value:
Quirk-Energy

Entry: Quirk-Energy is the undocumented energy that powers Quirks. It circulates through an internal system centered around a Quirk-Energy core, usually near the upper waist. Almost everyone has it, but ordinary people cannot consciously perceive or manipulate it. Only sorcerers and trained users understand it directly.

NATURE
Quirk-Energy is highly malleable. It can be shaped into:
• Reinforcement
• Barriers
• Cutting force
• Heat
• Spatial effects
• Soul effects
• Domains
• Other specialized phenomena

INNATE TECHNIQUES
Some people are born with an innate Quirk-Energy Technique. At birth, a unique blueprint is embedded into their energy system, defining the Technique's core function. The user discovers, refines, and builds applications from that blueprint. Inheritance is possible but never guaranteed, inheritance can be:
• The same Technique
• A modified or related blueprint
• No innate Technique
Bloodlines only increase likelihood.

TECHNIQUES
Techniques are NOT Quirks. Innate Techniques come from a birth blueprint, while other Quirk-Energy Techniques can be learned manually through training. Advanced Techniques can equal or exceed powerful Quirks, especially when affecting space, souls, barriers, or energy directly.

REINFORCEMENT
Reinforcement is not a true Technique. The user pools raw Quirk-Energy into the body, weapon, or object to increase strength, speed, durability, or resistance.

CORE
The Quirk-Energy core regulates circulation and output. Severe damage can cause instability, Quirk malfunction, organ stress, loss of output, or death. Reverse-Flow Technique can repair core damage, but requires extreme precision.

ERASURE
Erasure can suppress Quirks and interfere with active Techniques. It cannot erase raw Quirk-Energy or basic Reinforcement.

ANALOGY
Quirk-Energy is processing power. Quirks are biological programs. An innate Technique is a blueprint given at birth. Everything else is what the user learns to build from it.

cardPool.title: Black Flash
cardPool.value:
Technique — Black Flash

Entry:
Black Flash is an extremely rare Quirk-energy impact phenomenon. It has no official registry entry, no public classification, and almost no known precedent.

Core Function:
Black Flash occurs when a physical strike lands and Quirk-energy Reinforcement is applied within 0.000001 seconds of impact.

The timing causes the physical force and Quirk-energy to overlap almost perfectly, creating a violent spatial distortion at the point of contact.

Formula:

Physical Strike + Quirk-energy Reinforcement to the power of 2.5

Effect:
The resulting impact is vastly stronger than a normal reinforced hit and transfers force deeper through the target rather than only across the surface.

Visual:
At contact, Quirk-energy flashes black. Sparks lash outward like inverted lightning, the air visibly dents, and the sound of the impact seems to arrive a fraction late.

The strike feels less like being hit and more like the impact detonated through the body.

Difficulty:
Black Flash cannot normally be activated on command.

The timing window is so absurdly small that it requires exceptional instinct, concentration, combat rhythm, and Quirk-energy control. Even highly skilled manipulators may never experience one.

Repeated Black Flashes can temporarily place the user into an extreme state of focus where Quirk-energy control becomes dramatically more precise.

cardPool.title: Quirk-Energy Reinforcement
cardPool.value:
Quirk-Energy Technique — Reinforcement

Entry:
Quirk-Energy Reinforcement allows a Quirk-Energy manipulator (Jujutsu Sorcerer) to 'reinforce' their bodies, enhancing strength, speed, durability and other physical capabilities.

This function is very often mistaken for a strength/physical prowess Quirk. However unlike strength Quirks, a person can also reinforce their weapons to make them sharper, more durable or just deal more damage as a whole.

Formula:

Physical Force + Quirk-Energy Reinforcement = Reinforced Hit.

Creative Uses:

Quirk-Energy has layers, for example, an individual that reinforces his entire body that gets hit on his stomach will be more hurt than an individual that is only reinforcing their stomach.

Also, unlike conventional strength Quirks, this is not flashy and looks as if the individual is just this strong, and due to it not requiring any flashy moves or activations, this makes Reinforcement very fast to deploy and so much more smoother than the average Quirk.

Limitations:

Quirk-Energy control here is also often critical, as a mistimed reinforcement will more than often cause the user to get hurt, due to them not reinforcing themselves in a fight fast enough.

cardPool.title: The Nao Clan
cardPool.value:
Entry:
The Nao Clan is an old, extremely wealthy Japanese family publicly known through the Naogumi name.

To outsiders, they are simply old money: executives, doctors, philanthropists, landowners, and cultural patrons.

Almost nothing about their internal life is known.

SECRET TRADITION
The Nao are one of several hidden clans that preserve direct Quirk-Energy manipulation, and the Nao Clan is a major Jujutsu Sorcerer clan.

Sorcerers may learn to:
• Reinforce the body with raw Quirk-Energy
• Reinforce weapons and objects
• Shape crude effects directly from Quirk-Energy
• Develop personal Techniques
• Sense Quirk-Energy disturbances
• Study Quirk cores and circulation

This knowledge is not public, not taught by hero schools, and is never shared with authorities.

SECRECY
The clan is obsessively compartmentalized.

Most members know only what their rank allows. Records are private, sensitive meetings are face-to-face, and outsiders are given mundane explanations.

Hero agencies and the Commission know the Naogumi are wealthy and influential.

They do not know what the clan actually is.

ARTIFACTS
The Nao maintain sealed vaults containing:
• Family weapons
• Technique manuals
• Quirk-reactive materials
• Restricted medical research
• Historic support items
• Objects tied to unusual Quirk-Energy phenomena

PUBLIC FRONTS
• Naogumi Holdings
• Private hospitals
• Pharmaceutical firms
• Traditional estates
• Museums and cultural foundations
• Security and logistics companies

STRUCTURE
The clan has a main household and branch families.

A senior Nao relative serves as clan head, controlling succession, marriages, vault access, major assets, and restricted knowledge.

Women are seen as lesser than men, and are often treated harshly or into servitude, those who can become a sorcerer are tolerated but not seen equal.


WIDER WORLD
The Nao are not unique.

Other old clans preserve their own Quirks, Techniques, sorcerers, artifacts, and traditions.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Sorcerers
cardPool.value:
Sorcerers

Entry: A sorcerer is an individual who can percieve and manipulate Quirk-Energy. Sorcerers are not known at all publicly, and many, many, including All For One or Nezu has no clues about them. 

To outsiders they appear as traditionalists, as they wear traditional clothes most of the time. All sorcerers are born with a Quirk, and %60 of them are born with an innate Quirk-Energy technique.

Jujutsu Sorcerers call what they do 'Jujutsu' and refer to them as 'Jujutsu Sorcerers'

Clans: Sorcerer clans exist, these clans are often structured, very old and powerful, many don't know they even exist as they use public covers, as well as barrier techniques (Quirk-Energy related, not known publicly) to stay hidden.

There are 4 Major sorcerer clans:
• Nao Clan
• Fujiwara Clan
• Kuma Clan
• Tachibana Clan

And many other minor clans.

There are approximately 200-300 Quirk-Energy sorcerers around the world total at all times, and most originate from Japan.

cardPool.title: Steel
cardPool.value:
Quirk Name:
Steel

Description:
The user transforms their entire body into steel, becoming a nigh-impenetrable living weapon. This dramatically increases physical strength to superhuman levels and provides exceptional resistance to physical damage, extreme cold, and moderate heat with training.

Functions/Applications:
Steel allows the user to withstand bullets, blades, and extreme cold without injury. Enhanced strength enables breaking through obstacles and delivering powerful strikes. The user can serve as a human shield. Iron intake extends duration and potency.

Limits:
Prolonged use causes iron fatigue, reducing hardness until deactivation is necessary. Steel has a hardness ceiling that cannot be improved through training.

cardPool.title: Softening
cardPool.value:
Quirk Name:
Softening

Description:
Juzo Honenuki transforms solid objects into semi-liquid mud through touch, then reverts them with a second touch. Works on ice, metal, stone, and structures but not living beings. Softened materials trap and sink anything on them.

Functions/Applications:
Creates environmental traps by softening ground or structures. Restricts enemy mobility and controls battle positioning. Allows rapid traversal or escape through softened material. Neutralizes solid-based attacks.

Limits:
Cannot affect living organisms. Targets with propulsion abilities can escape softened traps. All softened objects revert if Juzo loses consciousness. Requires direct physical contact to activate and deactivate.

Additional Notes:
Pairs with Juzo's reflexes for defensive countering.

cardPool.title: Scales
cardPool.value:
Quirk Name:
Scales

Description:
The user generates hard, sharp reptilian scales across their body for protection and ranged attacks. Scale production requires adequate collagen and calcium intake. Scales are sharp enough to cut through vines and damage metal.

Functions/Applications:
Deploy scales as full-body armor for damage mitigation. Launch individual scales as cutting projectiles at medium to long range. Switch between melee and ranged combat. Scales can be stored in specialized gauntlets for rapid-fire attacks.

Limits:
Scales break easily under sufficient force, providing inferior protection compared to hardening quirks. Continuous production depletes collagen and calcium reserves. Projectile accuracy depends on user skill and line of sight.

cardPool.title: Razor Sharp
cardPool.value:
Quirk Name:
Razor Sharp

Description:
The user generates sharp blades of varying shapes and sizes from any body part. These blades are composed of an unknown material strong enough to cut steel and withstand explosions, serving as both offensive and defensive tools.

Functions/Applications:
Blades can be produced from forearms, feet, or any body part as needed. The user controls blade geometry and deployment in real-time, allowing simultaneous offense and defense.

Limits:
Blade generation requires conscious effort and energy expenditure. Sustained combat depletes stamina. The user must be within melee range, and blades cannot be thrown or separated from the body.

Additional Notes:
Best suited for close-quarters combat specialists.

cardPool.title: Control Glass
cardPool.value:
Quirk Name:
Control Glass

Description:
The user commands and reshapes glass matter within their vicinity, altering its physical state between solid and liquid forms at will.

Functions/Applications:
Create levitating glass platforms for flight and movement. Absorb glass from windows and structures to augment available mass. Form glass projectiles for ranged attacks. Liquefy glass to trap and immobilize foes. Construct barriers and shields.

Limits:
Requires existing glass sources—cannot generate glass from nothing. Ineffective in glass-scarce environments. Liquefied glass is difficult to control precisely. Large-scale reshaping consumes significant stamina.

Additional Notes:
Excels in urban environments with abundant glass. User can sense glass composition within operational radius.

cardPool.title: Jogo
cardPool.value:
Name:
Jogo

Classification:
Cursed Spirit

Grade:
Special Grade

Origin:
Human fear of the earth, volcanoes, fire, and natural catastrophe.

Cursed Technique / Jujutsu:
Extremely destructive fire and volcanic Cursed Techniques; Domain Expansion: Coffin of the Iron Mountain.

Personality:
Proud, irritable, ideological, and convinced that curses born from honest negative emotion are the true humans.

Appearance:
A short humanoid curse with a single large eye and a volcano-shaped head.

Combat Profile:
Exceptional speed and enormous destructive output. Jogo fights through direct flames, volcanic eruptions, Ember Insects, and Maximum: Meteor while remaining physically dangerous at close range. His completed Domain Expansion is Coffin of the Iron Mountain; the Domain's mechanics are documented separately.

Background:
One of the intelligent Disaster Curses seeking a world ruled by curses rather than humans.

Personality and Combat:
Jogo is proud, volatile, intelligent, and deeply invested in the belief that curses are more authentic beings than humans. He becomes furious when underestimated, yet he is capable of planning and cooperating with other Disaster Curses. His small physical frame hides enormous speed and destructive output. Volcanic blasts, flame, Ember Insects, and Maximum: Meteor let him attack across a wide area rather than relying on close combat.

Detailed Appearance:
Jogo is a short one-eyed curse with a large volcano-shaped head, grayish skin, black teeth, and plugs or openings around the sides of the head. Heat and flame often vent from the volcanic crown when his emotions rise. His compact, almost caricatured body can mislead opponents about his speed and output; physically he moves far faster and hits much harder than the appearance suggests.

His pride is therefore a tactical weakness only when an opponent can survive long enough to exploit it.

cardPool.title: Hanami
cardPool.value:
Name:
Hanami

Classification:
Cursed Spirit

Grade:
Special Grade

Origin:
Human fear and exploitation of forests and nature.

Cursed Technique / Jujutsu:
Plant-based Cursed Energy attacks, cursed buds, roots, and nature manipulation.

Personality:
Calm, solemn, alien in values, and hostile toward humanity for its destruction of the natural world.

Appearance:
A tall, heavily built curse with pale bark-like skin, black markings, and branches emerging from the head.

Combat Profile:
Extremely durable with strong close combat, ranged plant attacks, and the ability to drain or disrupt opponents through cursed growths.

Background:
A Disaster Curse aligned with Jogo, Mahito, and Dagon.

Personality and Combat:
Hanami speaks and thinks more calmly than Jogo or Mahito and expresses hatred of humanity through concern for the natural world. Its body is extremely durable, with a pale armored exterior, dark markings, branch-like structures, and a flower growth associated with its techniques. Hanami uses plant creation, roots, wooden projectiles, cursed buds that feed on Cursed Energy, and environmental control to wear opponents down rather than relying on one straightforward attack.

Durability:
Hanami's defensive strength is a defining part of the spirit. The armored body can absorb repeated high-level attacks while continuing to control roots and plant growth across a wide area. Damage to weaker exposed regions matters more than simply striking the thickest armor. The technique also encourages battlefield control—blocking routes, creating distance, and punishing opponents for relying too heavily on Cursed Energy.

cardPool.title: Dagon
cardPool.value:
Name:
Dagon

Classification:
Cursed Spirit

Grade:
Special Grade

Origin:
Human fear of the ocean and aquatic disaster.

Cursed Technique / Jujutsu:
Water-based jujutsu and shikigami; Domain Expansion: Horizon of the Captivating Skandha.

Personality:
Initially childlike and quiet, later more articulate and fiercely attached to fellow Disaster Curses.

Appearance:
Begins as a small aquatic cursed womb and can evolve into a large muscular humanoid sea-creature form.

Combat Profile:
Controls large volumes of water and summons endless aquatic shikigami inside a completed Domain.

Background:
A Disaster Curse associated with Jogo, Hanami, and Mahito.

Development and Combat:
Dagon initially exists as a quiet cursed womb with limited speech, staying close to the other Disaster Curses and showing strong attachment to them. After Hanami's death and direct combat pressure, Dagon matures into a much larger humanoid form with sharply increased physical power, durability, Cursed Energy, and water manipulation. He can generate large volumes of water without relying on a natural source and can summon aquatic shikigami as part of his innate technique. His mature body combines heavy durability with enough speed and close-range strength to pressure several experienced sorcerers at once. His completed Domain is Horizon of the Captivating Skandha, recorded separately.

Detailed Appearance:
Before maturation, Dagon resembles a small red womb-like creature with simple limbs and an almost harmless expression. The evolved form becomes a large muscular humanoid with an octopus-like head, dark markings, and a far more imposing body. That transformation is not cosmetic: intelligence, speech, physical power, and Domain use all rise sharply after maturation.

The mature form is a major combatant rather than as the passive womb-like creature seen earlier.

cardPool.title: Rika
cardPool.value:
Name:
Rika

Classification:
Special manifestation connected to Yuta Okkotsu

Description:
A massive, frightening jujutsu entity associated with Yuta's bond to Rika Orimoto. The original vengeful curse was released, while a later Rika-like manifestation remains tied to Yuta's technique and stored power.

Abilities:
Can manifest immense strength, store cursed tools, support Copy, supply Cursed Energy, and fight independently for limited periods.

Relationship / Role:
Functions as Yuta's closest supernatural partner and external support for his technique.

Nature:
Rika is the cursed spirit created when Yuta Okkotsu unconsciously bound the soul of his childhood friend Rika Orimoto after her death. The original curse became an overwhelming manifestation of Yuta's grief and Cursed Energy, earning the title Queen of Curses. After Orimoto's soul was released, a remnant called Rika remains connected to Yuta as an external storage and combat partner. The remnant is not the same continuing human soul and should not be treated as a normal shikigami.

Appearance and Manifestation:
Rika appears as a huge pale monstrous figure with a broad upper body, long arms, dark clawed hands, a single large eye, and a mouth filled with sharp teeth. Partial manifestation can bring out only part of the body, while full manifestation gives Yuta access to the complete external support for a limited period. Her physical presence is overwhelming, but her role is specifically tied to Yuta rather than functioning as an independent roaming curse.

Her manifestation is strongest when treated as part of Yuta's own jujutsu system rather than as a separate character with an unrelated power set.

cardPool.title: Mahito
cardPool.value:
Name:
Mahito

Classification:
Cursed Spirit

Grade:
Special Grade

Origin:
Fear and hatred humans hold toward other humans.

Cursed Technique / Jujutsu:
Idle Transfiguration; Domain Expansion: Self-Embodiment of Perfection.

Personality:
Childlike, curious, sadistic, philosophical, and fascinated by the shape of souls and the emotional collapse of humans.

Appearance:
A pale humanoid curse with patchwork stitching across his face and body, long bluish-gray hair, and mismatched eyes.

Combat Profile:
Reshapes his own soul to alter his body and directly transforms the souls of others through touch. Against ordinary non-sorcerers with no soul defense, a clean application is typically catastrophic or instantly fatal.

Background:
A young but rapidly evolving curse whose experiments on humans make him one of the most dangerous threats to civilians and inexperienced sorcerers.

Personality and Development:
Mahito is curious, playful, sadistic, and intellectually fascinated by the soul. He treats human suffering as experimentation and rapidly changes his tactics when new experiences teach him more about his own technique. His body is unusually flexible because he can reshape his own soul, so wounds that would cripple another curse may be meaningless unless they damage the soul itself. His growth during combat is one of his defining dangers.

Detailed Appearance:
Mahito has a humanlike body with patchwork seams running across the face and limbs, mismatched gray-blue hair, and eyes that can look playful even during violence. He frequently reshapes his own body into blades, enlarged limbs, animal-like forms, or distorted combat bodies, so no single silhouette remains permanent. The stitched appearance reflects his technique's obsession with the boundary between bodily shape and the soul beneath it.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Attitudes Toward Quirks
cardPool.value:
Sorcerer View of Hero Society

General Attitude:
Jujutsu Society understands Quirks as a separate biological phenomenon. What varies is how much respect sorcerers have for the people using them.

From a Sorcerer's Perspective:
Sorcerers routinely fight invisible monsters born from human misery. A bad mission can mean being torn apart by something civilians cannot see, dying to an unknown Cursed Technique, being trapped inside a Domain, suffering soul damage, or watching teammates die without recognition.

Many sorcerers do not expect long careers. Dying young and violently is common enough to shape the culture, and a sorcerer killed without Cursed Energy may even risk returning as a Vengeful Cursed Spirit.

Cultural Resentment:
Pro Heroes receive rankings, salaries, sponsorships, interviews, merchandise, and public praise.

Sorcerers may save dozens of lives in secrecy, receive little recognition or compensation, and then be sent on another lethal mission. Some deeply resent that difference.

Quirks:
Practical sorcerers respect dangerous Quirks as real threats. Others dismiss them as crude or "lesser Cursed Techniques," especially compared with abilities involving souls, Domains, barriers, binding vows, or conditional effects.

Example — Suguru Geto:
Geto represents the extreme end of this resentment. He came to view non-sorcerers as the source of curses and therefore the source of sorcerers' suffering.

In Hero Society, that mindset could make public hero worship especially insulting: celebrated non-sorcerers receive fame and protection while sorcerers die anonymously cleaning up supernatural horrors created by humanity itself.

Respect:
Not every sorcerer hates heroes. Respect depends on the individual, their experiences, and the person being judged.

To many sorcerers, heroism looks glamorous.

Jujutsu is simply the job that has to be done.

cardPool.title: A Sorcerer's Reality
cardPool.value:
Sorcerer Combat Baseline

Core Principle:
A trained sorcerer is not comparable to an ordinary civilian who happens to possess an unusual ability.

Cursed Energy reinforcement, lethal field experience, weapon training, reaction speed, and constant exposure to ambushes produce unusually complete fighters even before an Innate Technique is considered.

Physical Baseline:
Reinforcement enhances:
- strength
- speed
- jumping
- durability
- reaction time
- striking power
- weapon handling

The exact level varies by output, control, training, and experience, but competent sorcerers are expected to survive encounters that would kill ordinary humans almost immediately.

Technique Does Not Equal Strength:
A mediocre Cursed Technique does not make someone a weak sorcerer.

A fighter with ordinary reserves but excellent reinforcement, martial skill, timing, and combat instincts can still threaten powerful Quirk users without relying heavily on their technique.

Reaction and Experience:
Sorcerers regularly fight enemies that may be invisible, attack from unusual angles, use unfamiliar abilities, or kill with one clean hit.

Because of this, they are trained to react quickly, read opponents, adapt under pressure, and exploit openings instead of depending on a single ability.

Against Quirk Users:
Matchups still matter. An overwhelming Quirk can defeat a weaker sorcerer.

However, Hero Society should never assume that a harmless-looking registered Quirk reflects a sorcerer's real combat ability.

A sorcerer's greatest threat may come from reinforcement, skill, cursed tools, and experience rather than the ability listed on their public record.

cardPool.title: Technique Engraving and Quirk Compatibility
cardPool.value:
Cursed Technique Engraving

Core Rule:
When an incarnated sorcerer attempts to engrave their Cursed Technique onto a host, compatibility depends on how deeply the host's Quirk has altered their body.

Compatible Bodies:
Quirkless bodies are naturally compatible.

People with minor or accessory Quirks may also remain compatible if their core neurology and internal physiology are still mostly ordinary.

Examples can include:
- cosmetic traits
- horns
- tails
- extra limbs
- simple structural mutations

Appearance alone does not determine compatibility.

Emitter Quirks:
An emitter-type Quirk is not automatically compatible or incompatible.

A simple external effect may be acceptable if it does not require major changes to the brain, metabolism, organs, or nervous system.

Incompatible Bodies:
Engraving is likely to fail when a Quirk heavily alters:
- neurology
- sensory processing
- cognition
- regeneration
- metabolism
- internal organs
- cellular structure
- whole-body physiology

Multiple Quirks:
Several individually minor alterations can accumulate and make the body incompatible.

Full Incarnation:
If the original host is completely overwritten by the incarnated sorcerer, normal incarnation rules take priority.

At that point, the original host's compatibility matters less because their body and control are being fundamentally replaced.

Important Principle:
Compatibility is based on internal biology, not visual appearance.

A dramatic-looking mutation may still be compatible, while a normal-looking emitter Quirk can be incompatible if it depends on deep neurological or systemic changes.

cardPool.title: Soul Mechanics
cardPool.value:
Soul Mechanics

Definition:
In jujutsu, the soul is a real part of a living person rather than a metaphor. The body and soul are closely connected, and certain techniques can directly perceive, damage, reshape, or interact with the soul itself.

Soul Damage:
Physical durability does not automatically protect the soul.

A technique that directly targets the soul can bypass defenses that only protect the body. Likewise, healing the body does not always repair damage or changes made to the soul.

Quirk Users:
Known Quirk users have essentially no natural awareness of their own souls.

A Quirk that changes the body, enhances regeneration, alters appearance, or transforms anatomy does not automatically grant soul perception or soul defense.

Because of this, soul-targeting jujutsu is especially dangerous to Quirk users.

One For All:
The vestiges inside One For All are treated as consciousness preserved through the Quirk Factor, not as ordinary independent souls.

Soul-targeting jujutsu therefore interacts with the host's actual soul unless the technique's specific mechanics say otherwise.

Vessels:
Under certain cursed-object and incarnation conditions, multiple souls or consciousnesses can exist within one body.

They remain distinct rather than becoming a single soul. Control of the body can depend on compatibility, strength, binding vows, incarnation, and other jujutsu mechanics.

Sukuna:
Yuji and Sukuna follow normal vessel and soul rules.

Sukuna exists as a separate soul within Yuji rather than as a Quirk or biological mutation. Quirk-based abilities cannot detect, erase, steal, suppress, or separate him simply because he inhabits Yuji.

Separation From Quirks:
Soul structure and the Quirk Factor are separate systems.

Quirk scanners, medical tests, and analysis abilities cannot simply identify or remove an additional soul occupying the same body.

cardPool.title: Cursed Energy Reinforcement
cardPool.value:
Cursed Energy Reinforcement

Definition:
Sorcerers strengthen their bodies by circulating Cursed Energy through them. This increases strength, speed, durability, reaction time, and striking power.

How It Works:
Reinforcement is not a permanent force field. Cursed Energy must be actively directed through the body, and skilled sorcerers constantly adjust where that energy is concentrated.

A sorcerer can reinforce:
- fists for stronger strikes
- legs and feet for movement
- the torso against incoming attacks
- specific organs or vulnerable areas
- weapons held in their hands

Dynamic Use:
Good reinforcement depends on timing and control.

Instead of wasting maximum output across the entire body, an experienced sorcerer can shift Cursed Energy to wherever it is needed most. A fist can be strengthened at the moment of impact, while the torso is reinforced immediately afterward to absorb a counterattack.

Defense:
Reinforcement can let a sorcerer survive or block the physical effects of Quirks if their output and durability are high enough.

It does not erase, suppress, or interfere with the Quirk itself.

Limits:
Reinforcement can still be overwhelmed.

Poor timing, low output, exhaustion, depleted reserves, or attacks that bypass normal physical durability can injure a sorcerer.

Combat Importance:
Reinforcement is one of the foundations of sorcerer combat.

Even someone with a mediocre Cursed Technique can become extremely dangerous through excellent reinforcement, physical training, timing, and close-quarters skill.

cardPool.title: Reverse Cursed Technique
cardPool.value:
Reverse Cursed Technique

Definition:
Reverse Cursed Technique, or RCT, converts negative Cursed Energy into positive energy.

Sorcerers create it by multiplying Cursed Energy against itself. Producing positive energy is extremely difficult, which is why RCT is considered an advanced skill.

Healing:
Positive energy can restore living tissue.

Depending on the user's skill and output, RCT can:
- close wounds
- repair organs
- restore damaged flesh
- regrow lost body parts
- recover from otherwise fatal injuries
- recover from permanent neurological damage

Healing yourself is difficult. Healing another person is even harder because positive energy must be output into someone else's body.

Limits:
RCT is not unlimited regeneration.

Severe injuries require much more output and precision than minor wounds. Brain damage, massive blood loss, destroyed organs, poison, or repeated catastrophic injuries can overwhelm what a user is capable of repairing.

Soul Damage:
RCT does not automatically repair damage to the soul.

If a technique changes or destroys the soul itself, simply restoring the flesh may not fix the underlying problem. Healing soul damage requires the necessary understanding and ability to perceive the soul.

Cursed Spirits:
Positive energy is extremely harmful to cursed spirits because their bodies are made from negative Cursed Energy.

A sorcerer capable of outputting positive energy directly into a curse can cause severe or potentially fatal damage.

Quirk Injuries:
RCT can heal injuries caused by Quirks just like any other physical injury, provided the damage is within the user's healing ability.

It does not erase, restore, suppress, or modify a person's Quirk Factor simply because their body is being healed.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Barriers
cardPool.value:
Jujutsu Barriers

Definition:
Barriers are jujutsu techniques used to create, divide, conceal, or control spaces through Cursed Energy.

They are the foundation for Curtains, Domain Expansion, concealed facilities, and many large-scale jujutsu systems.

Curtains:
A Curtain is a barrier commonly used to hide jujutsu activity from ordinary people.

Depending on the conditions placed on it, a Curtain can:
- block visibility from outside
- prevent certain people from entering
- prevent certain people from leaving
- allow one group through while excluding another

Conditions:
Barrier strength can be changed through restrictions and conditions.

For example, making a barrier weak from the inside may allow it to become much stronger from the outside. A barrier can also be designed to recognize specific individuals or categories of people.

Quirk users are treated as ordinary non-sorcerers unless they independently possess jujutsu.

Barrier Skill:
Creating a basic Curtain is far easier than constructing a Domain Expansion.

Highly skilled barrier users can manipulate:
- size
- location
- entry conditions
- internal structure
- durability
- coordinates
- who the barrier recognizes as a target

Tengen is considered the greatest barrier user in modern jujutsu society, and many important jujutsu facilities depend on Tengen's barrier network.

Breaking a Barrier:
A barrier is not simply a physical wall.

Brute force may work against some barriers, but others must be broken by:
- finding a weak point
- destroying the source or anchor
- exploiting its conditions
- using another barrier technique
- overwhelming it with superior jujutsu

Technology:
Ordinary cameras, sensors, Quirk-analysis equipment, and scientific instruments cannot understand or detect the Cursed Energy structure maintaining a barrier.

cardPool.title: Domain Expansion
cardPool.value:
Domain Expansion

Definition:
Domain Expansion is one of the highest forms of jujutsu. The user manifests their innate domain through a barrier and imbues it with a Cursed Technique.

Sure-Hit Effect:
Most completed Domains grant a guaranteed-hit effect. Once a target is properly caught inside, normal dodging is often no longer enough because the Domain itself applies the technique.

Not all Domains are lethal. Some impose rules, trials, conditions, or other effects instead of immediately attacking.

Quirk Users:
Quirk users are treated as ordinary non-sorcerers by Domain mechanics.

Having a Quirk does not grant:
- Domain resistance
- Cursed Energy perception
- barrier knowledge
- protection from sure-hit effects

A Domain does not erase a Quirk unless its actual technique specifically causes that result.

Counters:
Common responses include:
- another Domain Expansion
- Simple Domain
- Hollow Wicker Basket
- specialized barrier techniques
- escaping before the barrier fully closes
- exploiting the Domain's specific rules or weaknesses

Domain Amplification can help against certain techniques, but it is not a universal answer to every Domain.

Domain Clashes:
When two Domains overlap, refinement, barrier skill, Cursed Energy output, construction, and imposed conditions determine which one gains the advantage.

A more refined Domain can overwhelm a weaker one.

Cost:
Domain Expansion consumes enormous Cursed Energy and requires exceptional skill.

After using one, most sorcerers experience temporary Cursed Technique burnout, making their innate technique difficult or impossible to use for a short period.

Variations:
Domains can be:
- open or closed barrier
- lethal or rule-based
- large or highly compressed
- simple or extremely refined

Each Domain follows the mechanics of its own user and technique.

Additional Notes
- If a domain's inside is hard, its outside is brittle, and vice versa.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Secrecy
cardPool.value:
Jujutsu Secrecy

Public Knowledge:
Hero Society does not know Jujutsu Society exists. Pro Heroes, U.A. staff, police, the Hero Public Safety Commission, scientists, and civilians have no reliable knowledge of Cursed Energy, curses, sorcerers, or Jujutsu High.

Even highly intelligent outsiders like Nezu normally lack enough connected evidence to form a serious theory.

How Secrecy Is Maintained:
Sorcerers prevent exposure through:
- Curtains and barriers
- restricted access
- fake identities
- false records
- controlled evacuations
- staged explanations
- administrative interference

Cover Stories:
Visible curse incidents are usually blamed on things ordinary society already understands.

Common explanations include:
- villain attacks
- illegal Quirk use
- terrorism
- accidents
- structural failures
- hazardous materials
- fabricated criminals with fake Quirk profiles

Because Hero Society already expects bizarre powers, these explanations are usually believable.

Witnesses:
There is no standard memory-wipe system.

Jujutsu Society prefers to stop people from seeing too much in the first place, then bury whatever remains under a convincing mundane explanation.

Investigations:
Secrecy does not require controlling the entire government.

A small number of manipulated records, trusted intermediaries, forged paperwork, compromised officials, and redirected investigations are usually enough to make suspicious incidents lead to ordinary dead ends instead of Jujutsu Society.

The goal is simple: make the supernatural explanation unnecessary.

cardPool.title: Cursed Techniques Against Quirk Users
cardPool.value:
Cursed Techniques Against Quirk Users

Core Rule:
Cursed Techniques affect Quirk users the same way they affect other non-sorcerers. Having a Quirk does not grant natural Cursed Energy defense, soul awareness, barrier knowledge, or resistance to Domains.

What Quirks Can Do:
A Quirk can still counter the physical result of a technique if its actual mechanics allow it.

Examples include:
- blocking physical projectiles
- resisting heat or force
- breaking created matter
- escaping through speed or mobility
- surviving damage through genuine durability

This does not mean the Quirk is interacting with Cursed Energy itself.

Soul Techniques:
Most Quirk users have no natural awareness of their own soul. Techniques that directly target the soul are therefore extremely dangerous.

Physical durability, transformation, or regeneration does not automatically protect the soul. A Quirk must genuinely affect the soul to provide meaningful resistance.

Healing:
Quirk-based healing repairs the body. It does not normally repair soul damage.

Domains:
Inside a Domain Expansion, a Quirk user is treated as a non-sorcerer unless they independently possess jujutsu.

They do not automatically gain:
- Simple Domain
- Cursed Energy reinforcement
- barrier knowledge
- resistance to sure-hit effects

Practical Danger:
Quirk users may be physically powerful while still having no idea how a Cursed Technique works.

They cannot naturally read Cursed Energy flow, technique activation, barrier structure, soul targeting, or sure-hit conditions.

Against unfamiliar jujutsu, even a powerful hero can be at a major disadvantage.

cardPool.title: Non-Sorcerer Perception
cardPool.value:
Non-Sorcerer Perception

What They Cannot See:
Ordinary people and Quirk users cannot normally see cursed spirits, Cursed Energy, shikigami, or the supernatural layer of Cursed Techniques.

In rare extreme situations, a non-sorcerer may briefly perceive a curse, but this is not normal and does not grant lasting jujutsu awareness.

What They Do See:
Non-sorcerers can still witness physical consequences.

They may see:
- someone suddenly thrown across a room
- walls or doors breaking
- blood appearing without a visible attacker
- objects moving on their own
- a sorcerer striking empty air
- unexplained injuries or destruction

They see the result, not the supernatural cause.

Technology:
Cameras, Quirk scanners, support equipment, medical devices, scientific instruments, and analysis Quirks cannot detect Cursed Energy itself.

They can record physical damage or movement, but not the jujutsu responsible.

Physical Exceptions:
Cursed corpses, transfigured humans, and cursed tools are physical and can be seen and touched normally.

Cursed spirits and most shikigami remain invisible to non-sorcerers.

Misinterpretation:
Because unusual powers are already normal in Hero Society, witnesses usually assume the cause is a Quirk.

Cursed Energy reinforcement may be mistaken for a strength or speed Quirk. Invisible shikigami can look like telekinesis. Curse attacks may be blamed on an unseen villain ability.

This makes jujutsu incidents much easier to hide, because the wrong explanation often sounds completely reasonable.

cardPool.title: Cursed Energy
cardPool.value:
Cursed Energy

Definition:
Cursed Energy is supernatural energy created by negative human emotions. Everyone produces it, including Quirk users and Quirkless people. Ordinary people leak it unconsciously, while sorcerers learn to control and use it.

Separate From Quirks:
Cursed Energy is not a Quirk, Quirk Factor, mutation, or biological ability. It exists on a completely different metaphysical wavelength.

Quirk science cannot detect, measure, reproduce, erase, steal, copy, suppress, or properly classify Cursed Energy.

Sorcerers:
Only an extremely small number of people are naturally capable of perceiving and manipulating Cursed Energy. Roughly 200–400 true sorcerers exist worldwide.

Most people, even if Quirkless, will never consciously perceive or control it.

How It Is Used:
Sorcerers can use Cursed Energy to reinforce their bodies, strengthen weapons and attacks, power Cursed Techniques, create barriers, summon shikigami, and perform advanced jujutsu.

Core Statistics:
Reserves — How much Cursed Energy someone possesses.

Output — How much they can release at once.

Control — How accurately they can direct and shape it.

Efficiency — How little energy they waste while using it.

These are separate qualities. Someone with smaller reserves but excellent efficiency and control can outperform a person with far more total energy.

Control:
Sorcerers do not need to remain angry or miserable to use Cursed Energy. Training focuses on preventing leakage, maintaining steady flow, reinforcing the correct part of the body, and releasing the right amount of energy at the right moment.

Skill and efficiency are often just as important as raw reserves.

cardPool.title: Sorcerer Eligibility
cardPool.value:
Sorcerer Eligibility

Natural Rule:
Natural sorcerers are born Quirkless. Being Quirkless alone does not make someone a sorcerer; almost all Quirkless people are still ordinary non-sorcerers.

What Actually Matters:
A natural sorcerer must be born with the rare constitution needed to perceive and control Cursed Energy. Without that, training, trauma, curse exposure, or instruction cannot turn an ordinary person into a sorcerer.

Innate Quirk Factors:
Someone born with a natural Quirk Factor cannot later become a natural sorcerer. The two systems are fundamentally incompatible at the level required for normal sorcery.

Receiving a Quirk Later:
A person born with genuine sorcerer potential can potentially keep using jujutsu after receiving a Quirk, but only if that Quirk does not heavily alter the body.

Minor or accessory Quirks may remain compatible.

Quirks that significantly alter the brain, senses, regeneration, cognition, metabolism, internal organs, nervous system, or whole-body structure will block normal jujutsu use.

Artificial Exception:
A soul-altering Cursed Technique such as Idle Transfiguration can forcibly rewrite a Quirk user into a jujutsu-compatible state.

If this happens, the conflict between systems destroys the Quirk in the process. If the soul and body are later fully restored to their original state, the lost Quirk may return as well.

Rarity:
Sorcerers are extraordinarily rare even among Quirkless people. Someone can live their entire life without a Quirk and still never see a curse, control Cursed Energy, or develop an Innate Technique.

Quirklessness is only a prerequisite. Actual sorcerer potential must already exist.

cardPool.title: Cursed Corpses
cardPool.value:
Cursed Corpses

Definition:
Cursed corpses are physical dolls, bodies, or constructed vessels animated through Cursed Energy. Because the vessel itself is real matter, ordinary people can see, touch, photograph, and physically interact with them.

Creation:
Most cursed corpses are simple creations powered by an external source of Cursed Energy or programmed through a core. They can follow instructions, guard locations, attack intruders, or perform basic tasks without being truly independent.

Autonomous Cursed Corpses:
Fully self-sustaining cursed corpses are extremely rare. Masamichi Yaga discovered a secret method for creating them by reproducing a person's soul information from physical information and placing it into a cursed-corpse core.

True autonomy requires three compatible cores containing different soul information. The three cores continuously observe one another, and after roughly three months the cursed corpse can develop stable self-awareness and begin generating its own Cursed Energy.

This process is highly classified. Yaga is the only known modern sorcerer capable of reliably creating fully autonomous cursed corpses, and Jujutsu Headquarters considers the knowledge dangerous enough to treat him as a potential Special Grade threat.

Soul Information:
The process uses replicated soul information rather than literally transplanting a person's complete soul. Yaga has used information based on real deceased humans, including Takeru, who was modeled after Kusakabe's deceased nephew. The exact limits and ethical requirements of obtaining suitable soul information remain obscure.

Panda:
Panda is Yaga's greatest autonomous cursed corpse. He possesses three cores, independent personality, emotions, memory, judgment, and self-sustaining Cursed Energy.

Visibility:
Unlike cursed spirits and most shikigami, cursed corpses are physically visible to non-sorcerers. Hero Society would likely mistake one for unusual Quirk biology or advanced technology.

cardPool.title: Cursed Tools
cardPool.value:
Cursed Tools

What They Are:
Cursed tools are physical weapons or objects infused with Cursed Energy. Because the energy is already contained within the object, they can directly interact with and damage cursed spirits.

Why They Matter:
A non-sorcerer can wield a cursed tool and harm a curse without being able to manipulate Cursed Energy themselves. This makes cursed tools extremely valuable, especially because ordinary weapons and Quirks cannot directly exorcise curses.

A non-sorcerer still cannot naturally see or sense the curse they are fighting, so using one effectively requires skill, information, or guidance.

Grades:
Lower-grade cursed tools are mainly durable weapons capable of harming curses.

Higher-grade cursed tools may possess unique supernatural properties, specialized effects, or exceptional durability. Named high-grade tools can be worth enormous amounts of money due to their rarity, combat value, and importance within jujutsu society.

Skill Still Matters:
A cursed tool does not automatically make its wielder powerful. Strength, timing, weapon skill, positioning, and awareness still matter. An untrained person can easily lose even while holding an exceptional weapon.

Value and Secrecy:
Cursed tools are worth a great deal, both financially and strategically. Rare tools can become prized clan assets, black-market targets, bargaining chips, or mission-critical equipment.

They are therefore carefully stored, transported, and tracked. Losing one is serious, especially if it falls into the hands of heroes, police, researchers, curse users, or criminals who might investigate it or expose evidence of jujutsu.

Handling:
Named cursed tools are judged by both their physical quality and the cursed property attached to them. Some are valuable simply because they can damage curses; others are priceless because their abilities cannot be easily replaced.

cardPool.title: Sorcerer Grading System
cardPool.value:
Sorcerer Grades:

Grade 4:
Lowest recognized level. Suitable for weak curses and basic missions. Also recognized as the provisional sorcerer grade.

Grade 3:
Competent sorcerers trusted with routine independent work.

Grade 2:
Experienced sorcerers capable of handling serious threats.

Semi-Grade 1:
Sorcerers approaching Grade 1 but not yet fully recognized at that level.

Grade 1:
Elite professional standard. Highly reliable and trusted with dangerous missions.

Special Grade 1:
A special designation mainly used for powerful sorcerers from major clans who operate outside the normal school ranking structure.

Special Grade:
Exceptional anomalies whose strength, abilities, or potential cannot be meaningfully contained by the normal grading system.

cardPool.title: Curses and Vengeful Spirits
cardPool.value:
Cursed Spirits

Classification:
Supernatural beings formed from Cursed Energy.

Nature:
Curses are born when negative emotions accumulate and take form. Fear, grief, hatred, resentment, anxiety, and trauma can gather around places, people, events, or concepts until they become independent entities.

Perception:
Non-sorcerers cannot normally see, sense, touch, or interact with curses. This includes civilians, police, Pro Heroes, Quirk users, and researchers. A curse can attack while remaining imperceptible, leaving them at its mercy. Under extreme circumstances, a non-sorcerer may briefly perceive one.

Many unexplained disappearances and missing-person cases are secretly caused by curses. Victims may vanish or leave evidence misread as villain activity, accidents, or crime.

Exorcism:
Curses must be damaged through Cursed Energy, a Cursed Technique, or a cursed tool. Quirks cannot directly damage, restrain, sense, or exorcise them.

Grades:
Grade 4: Weak pests causing headaches, back pain, nausea, nightmares, fatigue, or unease.

Grade 3: Physically dangerous to non-sorcerers. They usually lack Cursed Techniques and rely on instinct and physical attacks.

Grade 2: Possess Cursed Techniques and basic intelligence. They can ambush, retreat, recognize danger, and use simple strategy, but rarely communicate.

Grade 1: Intelligent dangerous curses with mid-to-high level Cursed Techniques. They can reason, adapt, plan, and exploit opponents.

Special Grade: Exceptional curses. They may possess full intelligence, speech, long-term goals, Cursed Techniques, barriers, Domain Expansion, and developed personalities.

Vengeful Cursed Spirits:
Humans with enough Cursed Energy, supernatural potential, or overwhelming resentment can return as vengeful cursed spirits if killed without Cursed Energy. Sorcerers are especially vulnerable, but powerful non-sorcerers can also return under exceptional circumstances. They may retain memories, grudges, abilities, or Cursed Techniques.

cardPool.title: Disaster Curses
cardPool.value:
Name:
Disaster Curses

Type:
Alliance of intelligent cursed spirits

Overview:
A loose alliance of powerful curses born from major human fears who seek a world where curses replace humans.

Structure / Role:
Core members include Jogo, Hanami, Dagon, and Mahito, often working through schemes connected to Kenjaku.

Relations:
Their existence is completely unknown to hero society.

Practical Note:
Disaster Curses must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Purpose:
The group consists of intelligent high-level cursed spirits who identify with fears tied to humanity and the natural world. They cooperate because they share the belief that curses should replace humans as the true people of the world. Their alliance is strategic rather than a formal bureaucracy: individual members retain distinct personalities, techniques, and priorities while coordinating around plans that weaken sorcerer resistance and protect one another.

Cohesion:
The members recognize one another as fellow curses with a shared future, which gives their alliance a genuine emotional element uncommon among ordinary curse outbreaks. They mourn losses, argue strategy, and protect plans larger than a single feeding ground. That intelligence makes them far more dangerous than isolated curses because they can gather information, set traps, and exploit human institutions over time.

Their ability to coordinate patiently is one of the clearest differences between them and ordinary curse outbreaks driven mainly by instinct.

cardPool.title: Kamo Clan
cardPool.value:
Name:
Kamo Clan

Type:
Major sorcerer family

Overview:
One of the Three Great Families, strongly associated with conservative jujutsu politics and the inherited Blood Manipulation technique.

Structure / Role:
Maintains rigid expectations regarding lineage, heirs, and inherited techniques.

Relations:
Noritoshi Kamo is a major modern student representative of the clan.

Practical Note:
Kamo Clan must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Culture:
The Kamo family is one of the Three Great Sorcerer Families and is closely associated with inherited Blood Manipulation. It prizes lineage, legitimacy, and conservative political influence. Heir status is therefore both a combat matter and a family tool. The historical crimes committed under the name Noritoshi Kamo also burden the clan's reputation, even though the modern student bearing that name is a different person.

Succession:
Because inherited Blood Manipulation carries both combat prestige and symbolic value, the clan pays close attention to legitimate heirs and politically useful descendants. Family decisions can therefore shape a young sorcerer's career before personal preference matters. The clan's conservatism gives it influence inside the broader higher-up structure even when individual members disagree with that culture.

Political usefulness and inherited technique value can therefore outweigh personal preference within succession decisions.

cardPool.title: Gojo Clan
cardPool.value:
Name:
Gojo Clan

Type:
Major sorcerer family

Overview:
One of the Three Great Families of jujutsu society, historically associated with Limitless and the Six Eyes.

Structure / Role:
Its political weight is enormous whenever a Six Eyes/Limitless user is alive. Satoru Gojo is its dominant modern figure.

Practical Note:
Gojo Clan must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Influence:
The Gojo family is one of the Three Great Sorcerer Families and derives enormous prestige from inherited Limitless and the extraordinarily rare Six Eyes. In the modern era Satoru Gojo's personal strength eclipses the visible activity of most of the clan, making his political position inseparable from the family's reputation. The clan's importance is therefore less about a large public organization and more about inherited jujutsu, lineage, and leverage.

Inheritance:
The family's prestige is tied to techniques that cannot be manufactured through money or political appointment. Limitless may appear without the Six Eyes, but the combination is exceptionally rare and transforms the clan's balance of power. As a result, the birth of a user possessing both is a political event for jujutsu society, not merely a private family matter.

Outside observers know nothing of this inheritance structure because the clan's real significance exists entirely inside hidden jujutsu society. Lineage is therefore the clan's central source of leverage.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Headquarters
cardPool.value:
Name:
Jujutsu Headquarters

Type:
Governing body

Overview:
The conservative administrative center that issues missions, classifications, restrictions, punishments, execution orders, and policy for recognized sorcerers.

Structure / Role:
Relies on higher-ups, school leadership, clan influence, and support staff. It can quietly manipulate ordinary records and institutions without openly controlling the government.

Relations:
May assign observe, capture, or eliminate objectives to human-target missions.

Authority:
Headquarters issues missions, records grades, approves or blocks promotions, manages execution orders, and represents the conservative center of jujutsu administration. Its power is bureaucratic and political rather than a public police force. Senior officials can pressure schools and sorcerers through assignments, regulations, and rulings, but exceptionally powerful individuals or clan interests can challenge that authority in practice.

Methods:
Headquarters relies on information flow and legitimacy. It can classify a threat, assign personnel, declare a human or vessel for execution, approve mission priorities, and shape careers through promotion. It does not need to be visibly present at every incident; the authority works because schools, managers, and professional sorcerers are expected to recognize its rulings unless they deliberately rebel.

Its influence is strongest when other sorcerers accept its classifications and orders; resistance from powerful individuals can expose the limits of bureaucratic authority. Orders remain political instruments as well as mission directives.

cardPool.title: Masamichi Yaga
cardPool.value:
[ MASAMICHI YAGA

Name:
Masamichi Yaga

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Principal

Grade:
Grade 1 Sorcerer

Personality:
Yaga is stern, disciplined, patient, and principled. He expects students to understand why they risk their lives and tests resolve because sorcerers face lethal consequences. His teaching style is intimidating and confrontational, but not needlessly cruel. Beneath it, he is practical, perceptive, protective of his students, and treats autonomous cursed corpses as people rather than tools.

Appearance:
Yaga is a large, broad-shouldered middle-aged man with a heavy, imposing build, closely cropped dark hair, dark sunglasses, and a trimmed mustache and goatee. He usually wears practical dark clothing with a high collar. His size, posture and unreadable expression make him look threatening even while calm.

Cursed Corpse Technique:
Yaga is an exceptional creator of cursed corpses. His greatest achievement is creating fully autonomous cursed corpses able to generate their own Cursed Energy through three compatible cores containing replicated soul information. This knowledge is highly classified because it could create independent cursed-corpse forces.

Panda:
Panda is Yaga's greatest autonomous cursed corpse, possessing three cores, personality, memory, judgment, emotions, and self-sustaining Cursed Energy.

Combat:
Yaga is a skilled Grade 1 sorcerer with strong reinforcement, close-quarters combat ability, and solid jujutsu fundamentals. He can deploy prepared cursed corpses as support.

Background:
Yaga taught Satoru Gojo, Suguru Geto, and Shoko Ieiri before becoming Principal of Tokyo Jujutsu High. ]

cardPool.title: Hana Kurusu
cardPool.value:
[ HANA KURUSU

Name:
Hana Kurusu

Classification:
Dormant Vessel

Personality:
Hana is compassionate, earnest, emotional, and strongly driven by the idea of saving others. She tends to act from the heart before thinking through every consequence and can become reckless when someone she cares about is involved.

Her attachment to Megumi Fushiguro comes from childhood. After being trapped among cursed spirits, she remembers Megumi and his Divine Dog as the ones who led her to safety. That memory became deeply important to her, shaping both her admiration for him and her desire to become someone capable of helping others in return.

Hana is generally friendly, sincere, and easy to read emotionally. She can be stubborn when her feelings clash with caution, especially where Megumi is concerned, but her motivations are genuinely altruistic rather than selfish.

Appearance:
