Kusakabe teaches Tokyo Jujutsu High's second-years. He is deeply grateful to Masamichi Yaga, who once created a cursed corpse using the soul information of Kusakabe's deceased nephew to help his grieving sister. ]

cardPool.title: Akari Nitta
cardPool.value:
[ AKARI NITTA

Name:
Akari Nitta

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Assistant Manager; Kyoto Jujutsu High Graduate

Grade / Classification:
Assistant Manager / Non-combatant Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Akari has no known Cursed Technique and can only barely perceive cursed spirits. As an assistant manager, she has basic jujutsu training but is not a frontline combatant. Her role centers on mission support, transportation, communication, logistics, and supervising students in the field.

Personality:
Akari is bright, approachable, practical, and responsible. She speaks casually and can be a little rough around the edges, reflecting her past as a delinquent, but she takes her work seriously.

She is compassionate toward civilians and willing to reassure frightened people even with harmless lies if it helps them stay calm. Akari has a strong sense of duty and believes that if she gives someone reassurance, she should follow through and help them. She also cares deeply about her younger brother Arata and originally pursued assistant-manager work partly to keep an eye on him.

Appearance:
Akari is a young woman of average height with pale skin, pale blue eyes, and neck-length light-blond hair with dark roots. Her hair is slightly messy with uneven bangs, and she wears earrings.

She usually dresses professionally in a black vest over a white long-sleeved shirt, red tie, dark trousers, and heeled shoes, giving her the appearance of an ordinary staff member rather than a combat sorcerer.

Relationships and Background:
Akari graduated from Kyoto Jujutsu High and later became an assistant manager at Tokyo Jujutsu High. She is the older sister of Arata Nitta and respects senior assistant manager Kiyotaka Ijichi as a more experienced colleague. ]

cardPool.title: Shoko Ieiri
cardPool.value:
[ SHOKO IEIRI

Name:
Shoko Ieiri

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Physician

Grade / Classification:
Jujutsu Doctor / Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Shoko is one of the rare sorcerers capable of using Reverse Cursed Technique to heal other people. She converts Cursed Energy into positive energy and applies it directly to damaged bodies, allowing her to repair severe injuries that ordinary treatment cannot handle.

She is not known for an Innate Cursed Technique and serves primarily as a healer rather than a combatant.

Personality:
Shoko is calm, dry, intelligent, and difficult to rattle. She has a detached bedside manner, speaks bluntly, and often uses dark humor, but she takes her medical responsibilities seriously and remains reliable under extreme pressure.

She is less outwardly emotional than Gojo or Geto and tends to observe rather than dramatize situations. Despite this, she cares deeply about her classmates and students and quietly carries the burden of being one of the few people capable of healing others with RCT.

Appearance:
Shoko is a slim woman with shoulder-length brown hair, tired brown eyes, and noticeable dark circles caused by years of exhausting medical work. She usually wears a white doctor's coat over dark casual clothing.

As a student, she had shorter bob-cut hair and a more youthful appearance without the heavy dark circles seen later.

Combat Style:
Shoko is not a frontline fighter. Her value lies in emergency treatment, surgery, examination of cursed injuries, and keeping wounded sorcerers alive.

Relationships and Background:
Shoko studied at Tokyo Jujutsu High alongside Satoru Gojo and Suguru Geto under Masamichi Yaga. She remained at the school as its physician and is also close with Utahime Iori. She formerly smoked and is known for drinking heavily. ]

cardPool.title: Megumi Fushiguro
cardPool.value:
[ MEGUMI FUSHIGURO

Name:
Megumi Fushiguro

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — First Year

Grade / Classification:
Grade 2 Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Megumi possesses the Ten Shadows Technique, an inherited Zenin Clan technique that uses shadows as a medium to summon up to ten shikigami. Known summons include Divine Dogs, Nue, Great Serpent, Toad, Max Elephant, Rabbit Escape, and combinations such as Well's Unknown Abyss.

He can also use his shadow for storage, concealment, and movement. His incomplete Domain Expansion, Chimera Shadow Garden, floods the area with shadow and greatly expands his ability to summon shikigami and attack from the terrain.

Personality:
Megumi is calm, serious, private, and blunt. He rarely shows strong emotion and often appears distant, but he is deeply protective of people he considers good.

Rather than believing everyone should be saved equally, Megumi chooses to help people he personally judges worthy, a worldview shaped heavily by his sister Tsumiki. He is intelligent, highly tactical, and willing to take dangerous risks, but has a self-sacrificial streak that makes him undervalue his own life.

Appearance:
Megumi is a slim fifteen-year-old boy with pale skin, sharp green eyes, and spiky black hair that points outward in several directions. He wears the dark Tokyo Jujutsu High uniform with a high collar, matching pants, and dark shoes.

Combat Style:
Megumi fights tactically, combining shikigami, hand-to-hand combat, weapons, traps, and shadow movement. He adapts quickly and prefers controlling space over straightforward exchanges.

Relationships and Background:
Megumi is Toji Fushiguro's son and a descendant of the Zenin Clan. After Toji disappeared, Satoru Gojo became involved in Megumi's life and arranged his path into Jujutsu High. Tsumiki Fushiguro is the person he values most. ]

cardPool.title: Toge Inumaki
cardPool.value:
[ TOGE INUMAKI

Name:
Toge Inumaki

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Second Year

Grade / Classification:
Semi-Grade 1 Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Cursed Speech lets Inumaki infuse spoken commands with Cursed Energy, forcing listeners to obey. Commands such as "Don't move," "Sleep," or "Crumble away" can instantly restrain or damage targets.

The stronger the command and the stronger the target, the greater the backlash on his throat. Overuse can leave him coughing blood or unable to speak. To avoid accidentally cursing people, Inumaki normally communicates using rice-ball ingredients such as salmon, kelp, and tuna mayo.

Personality:
Inumaki is quiet by necessity, but he is caring, observant, playful, and fiercely protective of his friends. He communicates heavily through tone, gestures, and expression, and people close to him learn to understand his limited vocabulary.

He willingly damages his own throat to protect others and rarely hesitates when someone is in danger. Despite appearing reserved, he enjoys jokes and teasing and is more expressive than his speech restriction initially suggests.

Appearance:
Inumaki is a slim seventeen-year-old boy with pale skin, light-colored hair, violet eyes, and the Inumaki Clan's Snake Eyes and Fangs seals on his tongue and around his mouth.

He usually wears the dark Tokyo Jujutsu High uniform with a high collar that covers his mouth, helping conceal the seals when he is not fighting.

Combat Style:
Inumaki specializes in ranged control and support. He uses short, decisive commands to immobilize enemies, create openings, or protect allies, while carefully managing the damage to his throat.

Relationships and Background:
Inumaki is a descendant of the Inumaki Clan, whose inherited technique is Cursed Speech. He is classmates with Maki Zenin, Panda, and Yuta Okkotsu and is trusted in dangerous situations. ]

cardPool.title: Maki Zenin
cardPool.value:
[ MAKI ZENIN

Name:
Maki Zenin

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Second Year; Zenin Clan

Grade / Classification:
Grade 4 Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Maki has no Innate Cursed Technique and only a trace of Cursed Energy due to an incomplete Heavenly Restriction. In exchange, she has greatly enhanced strength, speed, reflexes, durability, and senses.

Because she cannot naturally see curses, Maki wears cursed glasses that let her perceive them. She specializes in cursed tools and exorcises curses through the tools' own Cursed Energy.

Personality:
Maki is blunt, proud, disciplined, fiercely independent, and extremely determined. She despises the Zenin Clan's obsession with inherited techniques and refuses to accept the low status forced on her.

She can be sharp-tongued and demanding, especially during training, but is dependable and protective of her classmates and juniors. Maki respects effort and competence over pedigree, pushes herself relentlessly, and intends to become clan head to prove the Zenin wrong.

The technique depends on Takaba being certain that he is funny. If criticism, fear, or self-doubt destroys that confidence, Comedian shuts down and he becomes vulnerable again. Comedian is constrained by Takaba's authentic humor and confidence, not by whatever result would be most tactically convenient. He cannot simply decide that an enemy's death would be useful and obtain it unless the situation genuinely satisfies the technique's comedic condition.

cardPool.title: Shrine

Shrine

Core Mechanic:
Shrine is built around precise slashing attacks and a destructive flame application. Its primary slashes are Dismantle, a fast ranged cut, and Cleave, a cut that adjusts its power according to the target's toughness and Cursed Energy. Outside Malevolent Shrine, Cleave normally requires physical contact while Dismantle can be projected at range.

Dismantle:
Dismantle launches invisible high-speed slashes capable of cutting living targets, cursed spirits, and structures. Sukuna later learns to broaden Dismantle's target to space itself by using Mahoraga's adaptation as a model, creating the slash that cuts the world. Sukuna's binding vow prevents him from using it against multiple opponents outside his Domain; inside Malevolent Shrine, that restriction enables a far larger explosive interaction with pulverized matter.

Shrine's cutting power depends on the user's output; possessing the formula does not reproduce Sukuna's strength. Cleave normally requires contact outside the Domain. The world-cutting Dismantle has demanding post-vow conditions, and Divine Flame's speed, range, sequence requirements, and binding vow prevent it from being freely spammed.

cardPool.title: Projection Sorcery
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Projection Sorcery

Classification:
Inherited Cursed Technique of the Zenin Clan.

Known User(s):
Naobito Zenin; Naoya Zenin.

Core Mechanic:
Projection Sorcery divides one second into twenty-four animation frames using the user's field of view as the projection angle. The user predetermines a sequence of movement across those frames, then executes the entire sequence in one second. Repeated valid sequences can build extraordinary speed, making the user's motion appear unnaturally fast even to experienced sorcerers.

Twenty-Four-Frame Rule:
Once a movement sequence begins, it cannot be freely rewritten halfway through. The planned trajectory must remain physically plausible enough for the technique's rules. If the user attempts an invalid movement that excessively violates those rules, the user can be frozen in an animation frame for one second.

Touch Condition:
Anything touched by the user's palm is also forced to obey the twenty-four-frames-per-second movement rule for its next movement. If the target fails to follow the imposed sequence, it is immobilized inside a frame for one second and becomes completely vulnerable.

Acceleration:
Projection Sorcery has an upper limit on how sharply the body can accelerate in a single sequence, but maintaining valid activation lets speed compound over consecutive seconds. This is why experienced users can reach extreme movement speeds rather than instantly starting at their maximum.

Limits and Counters:
The user must commit to predetermined motion and can punish themselves by planning an impossible route. A target that understands the frame rule can attempt to move within it instead of freezing. Contact is required to impose the rule on another person, and breaking a frozen frame releases the target while usually injuring them.

Security: Master Tengen's barriers conceal and protect the site. Ordinary outsiders do not discover the school by accident, and access to restricted areas depends on invitation, authorization, or knowledge of the barrier system. Curtains and secondary barriers may be added for specific emergencies.

Notable Areas: Training courtyards, student dormitories, medical facilities used by Shoko Ieiri, the principal's offices, concealed rooms used for sensitive instruction, the cursed warehouse, and the path leading toward the Tombs of the Star.

Operational Character: Despite its school designation, the campus functions like a fortified headquarters for a small profession whose students may be dispatched into lethal situations.

cardPool.title: Satoru Gojo
cardPool.value:
[ SATORU GOJO

Name:
Satoru Gojo

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Teacher; Gojo Clan

Grade / Classification:
Special Grade Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Gojo possesses the Limitless and the Six Eyes. The Six Eyes grant extraordinary perception and extremely efficient Cursed Energy control.

Infinity slows anything approaching him until it cannot reach him. Blue creates attraction; Red produces repulsion; Hollow Purple combines both into a devastating attack.

Domain Expansion:
Unlimited Void overwhelms targets with endless information, paralyzing thought and movement.

Personality:
Gojo is playful, cocky, irreverent, and deliberately irritating, especially toward authority figures. Beneath the joking attitude, he is highly perceptive, fiercely confident, and protective of his students.

He despises jujutsu society's conservative leadership and wants to change it by raising a generation strong enough to challenge the old order. Gojo is arrogant and emotionally guarded, but forms deep attachments and takes failures involving people close to him personally.

Appearance:
Gojo is a very tall (6ft 3), lean, athletic man with messy white hair and vivid blue eyes produced by the Six Eyes. He usually hides them behind a black blindfold to reduce sensory strain, though he sometimes wears dark sunglasses.

He normally wears a high-collared black Jujutsu High uniform. Without his eye covering, his blue eyes and sharp features make him immediately recognizable.

Combat Style:
Gojo combines overwhelming speed, reinforcement, elite hand-to-hand combat, Reverse Cursed Technique, spatial manipulation, and advanced barrier skill. His precision and efficiency let him use Limitless at an exceptional level.

Relationships and Background:
Gojo studied alongside Suguru Geto and Shoko Ieiri under Masamichi Yaga. He is head of the Gojo Clan and widely regarded as the strongest modern sorcerer. ]

cardPool.title: Sugisawa Municipal High School #3
cardPool.value:
Name: Sugisawa Municipal High School #3

Classification: Ordinary municipal high school.

Location: Sendai City, Miyagi Prefecture.

Appearance and Layout: The school is a conventional civilian campus with classrooms, club rooms, athletic facilities, corridors, stairwells, storage spaces, and a rugby field. Students and faculty treat it as an ordinary educational institution; there are no permanent jujutsu defenses or trained sorcerers assigned to the grounds.

Known Students: Yuji Itadori attended the school before entering Tokyo Jujutsu High. He spent time with Sasaki and Iguchi in the Occult Research Club, preferring the club's relaxed schedule because it allowed him to visit his hospitalized grandfather.

Cursed Object Incident: A sealed finger belonging to Ryomen Sukuna was kept at the school as a protective talisman. Its paper seal weakened over time. Rather than safely suppressing curses, the exposed special-grade object attracted them, particularly around the school at night. The rugby field had already developed a reputation for strange activity and illness before the danger became obvious.

Jujutsu Relevance: Megumi Fushiguro was dispatched to recover the object, leading him into contact with Yuji. When members of the Occult Research Club removed the seal, curses converged on the school. Yuji's decision to swallow the finger created an extraordinarily rare vessel situation and permanently connected him to Sukuna.

Security and Perception: Teachers, students, cameras, and police cannot normally perceive the curses drawn to the finger. Damage can therefore appear to come from invisible attacks or structural accidents. Only jujutsu personnel can correctly identify the residuals and object responsible.

cardPool.title: Kinema Cinema
cardPool.value:
Name: Kinema Cinema

Classification: Civilian movie theater and curse-related crime scene.

Location: Kawasaki City, Kanagawa Prefecture.

Appearance and Layout: Kinema Cinema is an ordinary urban theater that screens films, including older releases favored by Junpei Yoshino. It contains a public lobby, ticket and concession areas, enclosed screening rooms with tiered seating, interior corridors, restrooms, stair access, and rooftop access. Nothing about the building is designed for jujutsu activity, making supernatural violence inside especially difficult for civilians to interpret.

Known Civilian Use: Junpei regularly skips school to watch movies here, using the theater as a refuge from bullying and social isolation. The dark screening rooms and anonymous crowds allow him to spend long periods alone without drawing much attention.

Jujutsu Relevance: The cinema becomes the scene of grotesque deaths connected to Mahito. To normal investigators, victims killed through soul manipulation present a baffling physical crime with no visible attacker or conventional mechanism. For trained sorcerers, residual cursed energy can turn the theater from an ordinary crime scene into the beginning of a pursuit.

Investigative Considerations: Security footage may capture people entering or leaving but cannot reveal cursed energy itself. Witnesses can report visible human behavior, sudden injuries, or physical aftermath while completely missing the supernatural mechanism. A sorcerer investigating the site would examine residuals, victim condition, entry routes, roof access, and connections among the dead rather than relying solely on police evidence.

Tactical Considerations: Narrow aisles, packed seating, darkness, and civilians make open combat undesirable. A hostile technique could cause casualties before anyone understands an attack has begun.

cardPool.title: House of the Children of the Star
keys: House of the Children of the Star
cardPool.value:
Name: House of the Children of the Star

Classification: Public headquarters of the Star Religious Group and principal gathering place of the Time Vessel Association.

Appearance and Layout: The complex is a large, expensive-looking modernized temple or church building. Its public-facing architecture supports the image of a wealthy religious movement, while the interior includes broad assembly space, a raised stage for large congregations, and secluded rooms suitable for private meetings among directors and senior members. The grounds are spacious enough to host important visitors and to keep sensitive exchanges away from casual observers.

Function: The Star Religious Group uses the site for worship, administration, recruitment, speeches, and organized gatherings centered on devotion to Master Tengen. Behind that public identity, the Time Vessel Association historically opposed Tengen's merger with a Star Plasma Vessel, believing such a union would contaminate the being they revered.

Jujutsu Relationship: Most members are non-sorcerers. This is strategically important because the group can employ ordinary assassins and intermediaries without directly belonging to jujutsu society. Their lack of cursed techniques does not make them harmless; wealth, information, bounties, and hired specialists can still threaten protected targets.

Historical Significance: Toji Fushiguro delivered Riko Amanai's body to the organization here after completing his assassination contract. Satoru Gojo later confronted Toji nearby after reviving through Reverse Cursed Technique. The same institution later became vulnerable to takeover by a sufficiently powerful curse user.

Security: Protection comes from money, secrecy, loyal members, hired personnel, and private access rather than innate supernatural defenses. The building can therefore appear completely legitimate to police or civilians.

cardPool.title: Mahito's Underground Lair
cardPool.value:
Name: Mahito's Underground Lair

Classification: Hidden curse hideout and experimentation site.

Location: Beneath Kawasaki City, inside the sewer system near a flowing body of water. An access point lies beneath a bridge, allowing entry into the underground network without passing through a normal building.

Appearance and Layout: The lair occupies a broad subterranean chamber connected to concrete drainage passages, pipes, runoff channels, and sewer corridors. Water, damp surfaces, low artificial light, and heavy structural walls isolate the space from ordinary pedestrians above. It is large enough for Mahito to meet allies, speak with Junpei, keep transfigured humans, and conduct experiments without attracting immediate civilian attention.

Function: Mahito uses the area as a laboratory for Idle Transfiguration. Human victims are brought underground so he can test how altering the shape of the soul changes the body, how small a person can be compressed, how multiple bodies can be combined, and how transformed humans behave when deployed as weapons. These experiments are not medical; the victims are treated as disposable material.

Security: The lair relies primarily on secrecy, underground access, curses, and Mahito himself rather than formal institutional defenses. Non-sorcerers have little reason to enter the sewers and cannot perceive the cursed activity within. Even investigators who identify the general area must navigate confined passages where Mahito can reshape himself and attack from unexpected angles.

Tactical Considerations: Close quarters favor sudden contact, making Idle Transfiguration especially dangerous. Concrete walls and narrow routes restrict escape, while transfigured humans can be released as distractions. Cursed-energy residuals provide a trail for trained sorcerers but remain invisible to ordinary pursuit.

cardPool.title: Eishu Juvenile Detention Center
cardPool.value:
Name: Eishu Juvenile Detention Center

Classification: Civilian detention facility and potential high-risk curse site.

Location: West Tokyo City, in a relatively isolated area away from dense civilian traffic.

Normal Layout: The facility is built to confine juvenile inmates and includes secure dormitory blocks, reinforced corridors, locked rooms, controlled entrances, staff areas, exercise spaces, and institutional concrete construction. Building Two is the section associated with the cursed-womb emergency.

Jujutsu Hazard: A powerful cursed womb can transform the site from an ordinary detention center into territory dominated by a curse. Once an incomplete or innate domain manifests, the interior no longer needs to obey the building's normal dimensions. Corridors can stretch into impossible spaces, exits can become difficult to locate, darkness can swallow rooms, and team members can be separated despite entering together.

Operational Conditions: Civilian authorities evacuate the surrounding area while jujutsu personnel establish a Curtain to conceal the response. A rescue mission may begin with incomplete information because the people trapped inside cannot perceive or report the curse accurately. If a cursed womb finishes developing into a special-grade spirit, a mission intended only to confirm survivors can immediately exceed the assigned team's grade.

Tactical Considerations: Reinforced doors and prison architecture offer little protection against a curse that ignores ordinary barriers. Navigation becomes the first problem; exorcism comes second. Shikigami capable of tracking scent or residuals are valuable, while splitting the team can be fatal.

Public Explanation: To ordinary authorities, the facility can be sealed under an emergency involving structural danger, violence, toxic exposure, or an unidentified villain. The true supernatural cause remains compartmentalized.

cardPool.title: Shinjuku Showdown
cardPool.value:
Event: Shinjuku Showdown

Overview: The surviving jujutsu forces organize a final large-scale campaign against Ryomen Sukuna after his incarnation reaches an unprecedented level of threat. The battle is structured around successive plans, prepared contingencies, Domain clashes, soul-targeting strategies, cursed tools, binding vows, and attempts to separate Sukuna from Megumi Fushiguro.

Opening Duel: Satoru Gojo confronts Sukuna directly. Their battle pushes Limitless, Shrine, Reverse Cursed Technique, barrier construction, Domain Expansion, and Mahoraga's adaptation to extreme limits. Repeated clashes between Unlimited Void and Malevolent Shrine reshape the battlefield. Sukuna ultimately uses Mahoraga's adaptation as a model for a slash that targets the world itself, killing Gojo.

Successive Assault: Kashimo challenges Sukuna next, followed by coordinated attacks from Yuji, Higuruma, Yuta, Maki, Kusakabe, Choso, Todo and others. The fighters rotate in as injuries accumulate, each trying to exploit a different weakness. Higuruma's Deadly Sentencing, Yuta's copied techniques, Maki's Split Soul Katana, and Yuji's ability to strike the boundary between souls become central tools.

Sukuna's Adaptation: Sukuna repeatedly alters his tactics through binding vows, Domain use, Reverse Cursed Technique, Black Flash, and control over his incarnation. The battle becomes less about matching him individually and more about forcing cumulative damage faster than he can recover.

Final Objective: Yuji focuses on reaching Megumi and separating Sukuna's soul from the body he has taken. Nobara's late use of Resonance against Sukuna's final finger creates another opening from a distance.

Consequences: The confrontation determines the fate of Sukuna, Megumi, and the surviving modern jujutsu world, leaving severe casualties even among the strongest available sorcerers.

cardPool.title: Zenin Clan Collapse
cardPool.value:
Event: Zenin Clan Collapse

Overview: Conflict inside the Zenin clan reaches a breaking point after succession disputes, long-standing abuse, and the family's treatment of Maki and Mai. The clan's internal political struggle becomes a direct massacre within the Zenin household.

Succession: Naobito Zenin's death creates uncertainty over leadership and cursed-tool ownership. Megumi Fushiguro is placed in a position to inherit the clan under the conditions of Naobito's will, infuriating Naoya Zenin and other relatives who expected power to remain with established insiders.

Maki and Mai: Maki returns to the estate intending to collect cursed tools. Ogi Zenin attacks his daughters and leaves them inside a chamber with cursed spirits. Mai uses the last of her strength and Construction to create an exact replica of the Split Soul Katana, taking with her the cursed energy shared between the twins. Her death completes Maki's Heavenly Restriction, leaving Maki with a body comparable to Toji Fushiguro.

Massacre: Maki kills Ogi and then destroys the clan's combat forces. The Kukuru Unit is overwhelmed in close combat. The Hei's sorcerers use their techniques against her but cannot stop her physical speed, perception, and the Split Soul Katana. Jinichi and other senior fighters are killed. Maki later defeats Naoya after he attempts to prove his superiority.

Consequences: The Zenin clan's organized fighting strength is effectively annihilated. Remaining members outside the estate are later hunted down, and the clan's position among the major families collapses.

Key Participants: Maki Zenin, Mai Zenin, Naoya Zenin, Ogi Zenin, Jinichi Zenin, Ranta Zenin, Chojuro Zenin, Nobuaki Zenin, and the Kukuru Unit.

cardPool.title: Culling Game
cardPool.value:
Event: Culling Game

Overview: Kenjaku activates a massive ritual that links barrier colonies across Japan and forces awakened modern sorcerers, incarnated ancient sorcerers, and selected non-sorcerers into a lethal point-based game. The ritual is designed to generate cursed energy and drive human evolution toward Kenjaku's merger plan involving Master Tengen.

Rules: Participants become players after entering colonies or being designated through prior arrangements. Killing another player awards points according to their status. Existing rules restrict withdrawal and create severe consequences for refusing participation. Players can spend one hundred points to propose new rules, provided the game accepts them without undermining its fundamental purpose.

Sorcerer Objectives: Yuji's allies enter the colonies seeking ways to save Tsumiki Fushiguro, locate Hana Kurusu and Angel for their ability to unseal Gojo, gather points, and add rules that reduce compulsory killing. Teams deliberately split across colonies because communication and movement are restricted.

Major Players: Hiromi Higuruma, Hajime Kashimo, Fumihiko Takaba, Reggie Star, Takako Uro, Ryu Ishigori, Dhruv Lakdawalla, Kurourushi, Hana Kurusu, and numerous incarnated or newly awakened sorcerers become active threats or allies.

Colonies: Tokyo No. 1, Tokyo No. 2, Sendai, Sakurajima and other barrier zones develop their own power balances. Battles frequently involve Domain Expansion, anti-domain techniques, binding-vow logic, and unfamiliar ancient techniques.

Consequences: The game destabilizes the entire country, gives Sukuna opportunities connected to Megumi, and advances Kenjaku's plan far beyond ordinary curse outbreaks.

Operational Character: Unlike a simple tournament, the Culling Game is a self-sustaining barrier ritual whose rules, geography, and point economy shape every decision made inside it.

cardPool.title: Shibuya Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Shibuya Incident

Date: October 31, 2018.

Overview: Kenjaku and allied cursed spirits launch a coordinated operation across Shibuya with the primary objective of sealing Satoru Gojo inside Prison Realm. Multiple Curtains divide civilians, sorcerers, and transit zones according to carefully chosen conditions. Huge Halloween crowds are deliberately trapped so Gojo cannot fight without considering mass casualties.

Opening: Gojo enters Shibuya alone and confronts Jogo, Hanami, Choso, and waves of transfigured humans underground. He uses a 0.2-second Unlimited Void to incapacitate nearby enemies without permanently destroying the civilians around them, but Kenjaku exploits the shock of appearing in Suguru Geto's body to satisfy Prison Realm's mental timing condition and seal him.

Wider Battle: Sorcerer teams enter the station complex, break commissioned Curtains, fight curse users, and attempt to recover Prison Realm. The conflict fractures into numerous battles across streets, platforms, tunnels, and buildings. Toji Fushiguro is temporarily manifested through a séance. Dagon opens his Domain. Jogo later force-feeds Yuji several Sukuna fingers.

Sukuna and Mahoraga: Sukuna gains control, destroys Jogo, confronts Mahoraga, and devastates a large section of Shibuya with Malevolent Shrine. Yuji returns to awareness amid the destruction.

Mahito: Mahito kills or grievously injures multiple sorcerers and finally clashes with Yuji and Todo before being defeated and absorbed by Kenjaku.

Consequences: Gojo remains sealed, jujutsu authority destabilizes, Tokyo suffers catastrophic casualties and destruction, and Kenjaku begins the next stage of his plan.

Key Participants: Gojo, Yuji, Megumi, Nobara, Nanami, Todo, Maki, Naobito, Kusakabe, Panda, Mei Mei, Ui Ui, Kenjaku, Mahito, Jogo, Hanami, Dagon, Choso, Sukuna and numerous others.

cardPool.title: Origin of Obedience / Death Painting Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Origin of Obedience / Death Painting Incident

Overview: A chain of deaths connected to open doorways and an old incident beneath Yasohachi Bridge draws Yuji Itadori, Megumi Fushiguro, and Nobara Kugisaki into an investigation supervised by Akari Nitta. The victims share a past connection to the bridge, a location already associated with curse activity.

Investigation: Initial checks on the bridge reveal little. The team eventually determines that the relevant barrier is accessed from beneath the bridge under specific nighttime conditions. Entering the hidden space divides the students between separate threats.

Death Paintings: Mahito and Kenjaku have already incarnated Cursed Womb: Death Paintings No. 1-3 in human vessels. Eso and Kechizu confront Yuji and Nobara. Their Rot Technique and poisonous blood create a lethal shared condition, but Nobara uses Resonance to turn the connection against both brothers. Yuji and Nobara coordinate their attacks and kill them.

Megumi's Battle: Megumi confronts a finger-bearer connected to Sukuna's finger and is forced beyond his normal limits. He manifests an incomplete Domain Expansion, Chimera Shadow Garden, and defeats the spirit before recovering the finger.

Consequences: Choso senses the deaths of Eso and Kechizu through their blood connection and develops a personal desire for revenge. Sukuna gains another reason to observe Megumi's growth. Yuji and Nobara are left with the emotional burden of having killed opponents who possessed physical human bodies and a genuine sibling bond.

Key Participants: Yuji Itadori, Nobara Kugisaki, Megumi Fushiguro, Akari Nitta, Eso, Kechizu, Choso, the finger-bearer.

cardPool.title: Kyoto Sister-School Goodwill Event
cardPool.value:
Event: Kyoto Sister-School Goodwill Event

Overview: Tokyo and Kyoto Jujutsu High hold their annual student exchange competition. The event begins as a supervised contest between the two schools but is complicated by secret orders, personal rivalries, and a coordinated attack by hostile cursed spirits and curse users.

Internal Conflict: Conservative authorities instruct Kyoto students to kill Yuji Itadori because he is Sukuna's vessel. Not every student accepts the order with equal enthusiasm, and individual relationships quickly complicate the plan. Aoi Todo becomes fascinated with Yuji after learning his taste in women and effectively abandons the assassination effort to fight and train him instead.

Competition: Students clash across a forested course using Cursed Techniques, cursed tools, shikigami, and close combat. The event displays the contrast between Tokyo's unconventional students and Kyoto's more traditional hierarchy.

Attack: Mahito's allies deploy a Curtain that specifically keeps Satoru Gojo out while allowing others inside. Hanami enters the grounds, forcing students from both schools to cooperate against a special-grade cursed spirit. Todo helps Yuji refine his cursed-energy timing, leading Yuji to repeatedly achieve Black Flash during the battle.

Diversion: While the defenders focus on Hanami, Mahito infiltrates Tokyo Jujutsu High's storage area and steals Sukuna fingers and Death Painting Wombs No. 1-3.

Consequences: The attack demonstrates that Jujutsu High's barriers can be manipulated through carefully constructed conditions and gives Mahito's faction material needed for later incarnations.

Key Participants: Tokyo and Kyoto students, Satoru Gojo, Utahime Iori, Yoshinobu Gakuganji, Mahito, Hanami, and allied curse users.

cardPool.title: Junpei and Mahito Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Junpei and Mahito Incident

Overview: A series of grotesque deaths at Kinema Cinema leads Kento Nanami and Yuji Itadori toward Mahito, a newly developed cursed spirit capable of reshaping souls through Idle Transfiguration. At the same time, Mahito befriends isolated student Junpei Yoshino and encourages his resentment toward the people who bully him.

Junpei's Awakening: Mahito alters Junpei's brain so that he can use jujutsu, allowing his innate technique and shikigami Moon Dregs to manifest. Junpei initially sees Mahito as someone who validates his anger rather than understanding that the curse is experimenting on him.

Escalation: Mahito arranges circumstances that push Junpei toward violence at Satozakura High School. Yuji reaches him and begins breaking through his hostility, but Mahito intervenes. In front of Yuji, Mahito uses Idle Transfiguration to grotesquely alter Junpei's soul and body. Junpei dies moments later.

Conflict: Yuji attacks Mahito with genuine intent to kill. Because Yuji houses Sukuna and can perceive the contours of the soul, his strikes can injure Mahito in a way ordinary attacks cannot. Nanami later joins Yuji, forcing Mahito into a desperate Domain Expansion. Sukuna retaliates when Mahito's domain touches his soul, allowing Yuji and Nanami to survive.

Consequences: Yuji's hatred of Mahito becomes intensely personal. Mahito gains practical experience with his technique, domain, and manipulation of human emotion.

Key Participants: Yuji Itadori, Junpei Yoshino, Mahito, Kento Nanami, Nagi Yoshino.

Operational Significance: The incident establishes how dangerous soul manipulation is against people with no awareness of their own souls. It also demonstrates that an ordinary non-sorcerer can be forcibly altered to use jujutsu, while the process remains completely outside normal medical or Quirk-based understanding.

cardPool.title: Fearsome Womb Detention Center Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Fearsome Womb Detention Center Incident

Period: Early in Yuji Itadori's first year.

Overview: A cursed womb appears at the Eishu Juvenile Detention Center in West Tokyo. Five inmates remain trapped inside when Yuji Itadori, Megumi Fushiguro, and Nobara Kugisaki are assigned to confirm survivors and avoid direct confrontation if the womb has matured into a special-grade curse.

Escalation: The interior is transformed by the curse's domain, separating the students and making the building's normal layout unreliable. The newly born finger-bearer is far stronger than the first-years. Yuji loses Slaughter Demon and suffers catastrophic injuries while trying to hold the spirit back.

Sukuna's Intervention: Yuji allows Ryomen Sukuna to take control so the special-grade curse can be defeated. Sukuna effortlessly overwhelms the finger-bearer, retrieves the finger it consumed, and then exploits Yuji's inability to immediately regain control. He tears out Yuji's heart and forces Megumi into a direct confrontation. Yuji eventually retakes his body despite the fatal condition and dies.

Consequences: Sukuna becomes more interested in Megumi's Ten Shadows Technique. Yuji later revives under a binding vow made inside Sukuna's innate domain, while his survival is temporarily concealed from the other students.

Key Participants: Yuji Itadori, Megumi Fushiguro, Nobara Kugisaki, Kiyotaka Ijichi, Ryomen Sukuna, the finger-bearer.

Location: Eishu Juvenile Detention Center, particularly Building Two and the curse-distorted interior.

Operational Significance: The mission becomes a textbook example of catastrophic threat misclassification. A team dispatched for rescue and confirmation can become trapped against a newly matured special-grade spirit before reinforcement arrives, making retreat and survival more important than completing the original objective.

cardPool.title: Night Parade of a Hundred Demons
cardPool.value:
Event: Night Parade of a Hundred Demons

Date: December 24, 2017.

Overview: Suguru Geto declares war on jujutsu society and releases large numbers of cursed spirits in Shinjuku and Kyoto. The public attacks force Jujutsu High personnel to divide their strength while Geto pursues his real objective: killing Yuta Okkotsu and taking control of Rika.

Strategy: Geto's mass curse deployment is both terrorism and diversion. Sorcerers, students, and allied personnel are pulled into urban exorcism battles where protecting civilians limits their freedom to fight. Miguel is assigned to delay Satoru Gojo using the Black Rope, one of the rare tools capable of disturbing Limitless. Geto's other followers support the wider assault.

Tokyo Jujutsu High: Geto confronts Yuta after defeating Maki, Toge, and Panda. Yuta's bond with Rika reaches its peak, and he offers himself to her in exchange for the power to defeat Geto. Their clash leaves Geto mortally wounded. Gojo later finds him and ends his life.

Consequences: Rika's curse is released when Yuta realizes he had cursed Rika rather than the reverse. Geto's body later becomes available for Kenjaku's body-hopping technique, creating consequences far beyond the attack itself.

Key Participants: Suguru Geto, Yuta Okkotsu, Rika, Satoru Gojo, Maki Zenin, Toge Inumaki, Panda, Miguel, Geto's followers, Tokyo and Kyoto jujutsu personnel.

Public Interpretation: Civilian observers encounter mass destruction and unexplained casualties without seeing the cursed spirits responsible.

Operational Significance: The attack demonstrates how mass curse releases can overwhelm normal deployment capacity by forcing sorcerers to protect multiple cities at once. It also shows how anti-technique cursed tools and civilian-heavy battlefields can be used to delay even the strongest sorcerers.

cardPool.title: Hidden Inventory / Premature Death
cardPool.value:
Event: Hidden Inventory / Premature Death

Period: 2006, during Satoru Gojo and Suguru Geto's student years.

Overview: Gojo and Geto are assigned to escort Riko Amanai, the Star Plasma Vessel intended to merge with Master Tengen. The mission becomes a contest between jujutsu protection, curse-user attacks, the Time Vessel Association's bounty, and assassin Toji Fushiguro.

Major Developments: Toji exhausts Gojo through prolonged pressure, bypasses Infinity with the Inverted Spear of Heaven, defeats him, kills Riko, and later defeats Geto. Gojo survives by finally mastering Reverse Cursed Technique and returns with a far deeper understanding of Limitless, defeating Toji in their rematch. Riko's death prevents the planned merger.

Consequences: The mission becomes a defining fracture point for both Gojo and Geto. Gojo grows into the strongest modern sorcerer and later focuses on raising a stronger generation. Geto becomes increasingly alienated by the endless cycle of protecting non-sorcerers from curses born from those same people. Haibara's later death and Yuki Tsukumo's discussion of eliminating curses deepen that crisis. Geto eventually massacres a village, abandons Jujutsu High, and becomes a curse user.

Key Participants: Satoru Gojo, Suguru Geto, Riko Amanai, Misato Kuroi, Toji Fushiguro, Shiu Kong, Shigeru Sonoda, Master Tengen.

Important Locations: Tokyo Jujutsu High, Okinawa, Riko's school, Tombs of the Star, House of the Children of the Star.

Operational Significance: The failure of the escort mission proves that a sorcerer without Cursed Energy can still defeat elite jujutsu through preparation, cursed tools, physical superiority, and exploitation of technique conditions. It also leaves Tengen to continue evolving without the intended merger.

cardPool.title: Chain of a Thousand Miles
cardPool.value:
Name: Chain of a Thousand Miles

Classification: Specialized cursed tool built around extreme variable reach.

Appearance: A metal chain that appears ordinary when only a short length is exposed. Its true property becomes apparent when the user conceals the chain's rear end and continuously draws out additional links.

Core Property: The chain can continue extending without a known practical limit as long as the far end remains unseen by observers. If the end is concealed, the user can produce length far beyond what could physically be stored in the visible portion of the weapon.

Known Use: Toji Fushiguro exploited the condition by hiding the chain's end inside the mouth of his inventory curse. Because the terminating link could not be seen, he could draw out enormous lengths during combat without carrying a physically massive coil.

Weapon Combinations: The chain's greatest value comes from attaching another weapon to its visible end. Toji connected it to the Inverted Spear of Heaven, transforming a short technique-nullifying dagger into a long-range threat. He could swing, launch, redirect, and retrieve the spear from a distance while preserving the chain's extension condition.

Combat Applications: The chain can control a large radius, attack from unexpected angles, wrap around obstacles, change trajectories, and force an opponent to track both the attached weapon and the line connecting it to the user. Its reach can also help a close-range specialist threaten airborne or distant targets.

Limits: The extension condition is essential. If the terminal end becomes visible, the unusual length cannot continue being produced under the same rule. The chain itself does not automatically guide attacks or guarantee penetration; the attached weapon and the user's strength determine what a successful hit accomplishes. Flexible weapons also demand exceptional coordination to avoid tangling or losing control.

cardPool.title: Dragon-Bone
cardPool.value:
Name: Dragon-Bone

Classification: High-grade cursed tool and the masterpiece of cursed-tool craftsman Juzo Kumiya.

Appearance: A thick, single-edged sword with a strongly mechanical design. Three engine-like openings are set along the back of the blade, while the hilt includes a broad angular guard and engineered components.

Core Property: Dragon-Bone stores kinetic force and cursed energy generated during exchanges, then releases that accumulated power through the three openings along the blade. The discharge can propel the weapon and dramatically increase the force of a cut or counterattack.

Combat Use: The sword rewards a fighter who can survive and redirect pressure rather than simply swing harder. Energy received during a clash can be collected and expelled moments later, allowing the wielder to turn an opponent's force into sudden acceleration. Maki Zenin used this property against Ogi Zenin, exploiting the fact that he did not initially understand how the weapon worked.

Origin: Juzo Kumiya, a curse user obsessed with constructing unusual weapons, regarded Dragon-Bone as his finest creation. After his capture, the location of his workshop remained valuable information. Master Tengen later provided Maki with the workshop's whereabouts, allowing her to retrieve the sword.

Limits: Dragon-Bone does not generate unlimited force from nothing. Its strongest bursts depend on accumulated kinetic pressure and cursed energy. The wielder must understand timing, blade control, and when to release stored power. A sufficiently skilled opponent can still evade, disarm, or overwhelm the user before a useful charge is built.

Interaction with Quirks: The tool can physically clash with Quirk-generated matter or attacks and can store kinetic force produced by those impacts when the weapon actually receives that force. Its cursed mechanism remains separate from the Quirk itself.

cardPool.title: Slaughter Demon
cardPool.value:
Name: Slaughter Demon

Classification: Cursed tool intended for direct exorcism combat.

Appearance: A large combat knife with a broad dark-edged blade, two circular openings near the blade, bandaging around the lower portion, a brown handle, and a black fur-like guard. Its compact size makes it easier to carry than heavier polearms or special-grade tools.

Core Property: Slaughter Demon is imbued with cursed energy, allowing its physical blade to damage and exorcise cursed spirits. It does not require the wielder to possess a sophisticated Innate Technique, making it useful as an introductory weapon for someone who can fight physically but has limited cursed-energy control.

Known Use: The tool originally belonged to Maki Zenin. Satoru Gojo borrowed it and gave it to Yuji Itadori during Yuji's earliest field work so that he would have a reliable means of harming curses before learning to channel cursed energy consistently through his own attacks.

Combat Role: The knife favors close-range fighting. A physically gifted user can combine ordinary martial movement with a cursed edge, stabbing or slashing spirits that would otherwise be intangible to a non-sorcerer. Because the tool carries the necessary jujutsu property itself, even a person without normal sorcerer perception or technique can theoretically injure a curse if they can locate and strike it.

Limits: Slaughter Demon has no known special innate technique, automatic targeting, defensive effect, or unusual range. Its effectiveness depends heavily on the wielder's physical skill and ability to reach the target. Against a vastly stronger curse, the weapon can be destroyed like any other object; a finger-bearer severed Yuji's hand and broke the tool almost immediately.

Secrecy: In ordinary society it can pass as an unusual knife, but its cursed-energy function cannot be explained through normal weapon analysis.

cardPool.title: Black Rope
cardPool.value:
Name: Black Rope

Classification: Rare cursed tool created by Miguel's sorcerer clan in Africa; comparable in function to special-grade anti-technique equipment.

Appearance: A thick, dark braided rope carried and wielded as a flexible striking weapon. Its construction appears simple compared with elaborate cursed tools, but the material itself was produced through prolonged jujutsu craftsmanship over decades.

Core Property: When the rope makes effective contact, the curse woven into it interferes with and disrupts cursed techniques. Rather than overpowering a technique through raw force, it disturbs the technique's operation, allowing effects that are normally difficult to touch or bypass to be interrupted.

Combat Use: Miguel used the rope while fighting Satoru Gojo during the Night Parade. By striking through Limitless, he could disturb Infinity enough to force direct exchanges that would ordinarily be impossible. The rope's flexible length also makes it useful for whipping attacks, entangling motions, and controlling space while threatening technique disruption.

Consumption: The Black Rope has a severe limitation: every activation burns away part of the rope itself. The stronger and more frequently its property is used, the shorter the weapon becomes until no usable material remains. It is therefore a finite resource rather than a permanent anti-technique solution.

Strategic Value: Because technique-disrupting tools are exceptionally rare, the Black Rope is relevant to barriers and seals that cannot be overcome through physical force. Its properties were considered one possible method for opening the Back Gate of Prison Realm.

Limits: The rope interferes with cursed techniques specifically. It does not erase Quirks or dissolve ordinary physical matter. The user must still land the rope, survive the opponent's attacks, and ration a weapon that destroys itself through use.

cardPool.title: Split Soul Katana
cardPool.value:
Name: Split Soul Katana

Classification: Extremely valuable cursed tool with a soul-cutting property.

Appearance: A broad, curved Japanese blade with a distinctive fur-wrapped guard and dark handle. Two known versions exist: the original weapon used by Toji Fushiguro and an exact replica created by Mai Zenin through Construction at the cost of her life.

Core Property: The blade ignores ordinary physical toughness and cuts directly at the soul. Armor, hardened flesh, reinforced bodies, and exceptionally durable material do not provide normal protection when the katana's full property is being expressed. The effect applies to living targets and can also recognize the souls of inorganic matter.

Requirement for Full Use: The katana's greatest effect requires a wielder capable of perceiving the souls of objects, not merely swinging the blade with strength. A fighter who lacks that perception can still use it as a dangerous cursed weapon but cannot fully exploit its ability to disregard physical resistance.

Healing Interaction: Wounds made directly to the soul are difficult to repair. Reverse Cursed Technique can only properly heal such injuries if the healer or injured person can perceive and understand the contours of the soul well enough to restore what was cut. Ordinary bodily regeneration does not automatically solve the underlying damage.

Known Users: Toji used the original blade against Suguru Geto's curses, including highly durable spirits. Maki later received Mai's replica and made it her principal weapon. Hagane Daido could draw out remarkable cutting performance through pure swordsmanship, while Maki's later perception allowed her to use the weapon at its intended level.

Limits: The katana does not make its user untouchable. It still requires a successful cut, can be avoided or disarmed, and its full soul-bypassing property depends on the wielder's perception.

cardPool.title: Playful Cloud
cardPool.value:
Name: Playful Cloud

Classification: Special-grade cursed tool.

Appearance: A three-section staff joined by metal rings. Each heavy segment is decorated near the connecting hardware, allowing the weapon to flex, whip, rotate, and strike from changing angles while still delivering the mass of a solid staff.

Core Property: Playful Cloud is unusual among special-grade cursed tools because it is not imbued with an innate cursed technique. Its destructive ability instead scales with the raw physical strength of the person wielding it. The tool's cursed energy allows that physical power to be transferred effectively against cursed spirits and reinforced opponents.

Best Users: The weapon is exceptionally dangerous in the hands of people with extraordinary bodies. Toji Fushiguro and Maki Zenin can exploit it without relying on large cursed-energy reserves, while physically powerful sorcerers such as Aoi Todo can also produce devastating strikes. A weaker wielder receives far less benefit because the tool has no independent technique to compensate.

Combat Use: The articulated design supports sweeping blows, chained combinations, sudden changes of direction, grappling motions, and powerful thrusts. It can be swung with enough force to damage special-grade cursed spirits. Toji demonstrated an even more brutal application by rubbing and sharpening the broken ends, turning the staff into improvised stabbing weapons before repeatedly driving them into Dagon.

History: Playful Cloud originally belonged to Toji and later passed through Suguru Geto's possession after Geto absorbed Toji's inventory curse. Following Geto's defeat, the tool came under Jujutsu High control and was used by several sorcerers.

Limits: Its power is entirely dependent on the wielder's body, technique with weapons, and ability to maintain control of a flexible three-section staff. It offers no automatic defense, targeting, or technique nullification.

cardPool.title: Inverted Spear of Heaven
cardPool.value:
Name: Inverted Spear of Heaven

Classification: Special-grade cursed tool.

Appearance: A compact spearhead with a short handle and a distinctive two-pronged, jitte-like blade. Its size allows it to be used like a heavy dagger in close combat or attached to another weapon for greater reach. Toji Fushiguro carried it among the weapons stored within his inventory curse.

Core Property: The tool is imbued with a foreign type of cursed energy and a technique that forcibly nullifies cursed techniques on contact. It does not merely block an attack through durability; touching an active technique causes that technique's effect to be stopped at the point of interaction.

Applications: Toji used the blade to bypass Satoru Gojo's Infinity, allowing direct physical strikes against a defense that normally prevents contact. The same property makes the weapon useful against technique-created barriers, constructs, and other effects whose continued existence depends on cursed technique activation.

Range: The spear is naturally a close-range weapon, but Toji connected it to the Chain of a Thousand Miles and hid the chain's far end inside his inventory curse. This created a long-range configuration that allowed him to repeatedly send the technique-nullifying blade toward an opponent without approaching normally.

Limits: The weapon nullifies cursed techniques, not all supernatural or physical phenomena. A normal blade, projectile, Quirk-created object, or purely physical strike does not cease to exist merely because the spear touches it. Its user must still possess the speed, accuracy, and combat ability to make contact with the relevant technique.

Strategic Value: Technique nullification is rare enough that the spear is considered one of the most dangerous anti-sorcerer tools known. Its properties are also relevant to seals such as Prison Realm, whose Back Gate requires technique-negating means to force open.

cardPool.title: Cursed Womb: Death Paintings
cardPool.value:
Name: Cursed Womb: Death Paintings

Classification: Nine cursed objects created from pregnancies involving a human woman capable of bearing a curse-human hybrid. Death Paintings No. 1 through No. 3 are special grade.

Origin: During the early Meiji era, a woman whose body could conceive a child by a cursed spirit sought refuge after being ostracized. Kenjaku, while inhabiting the body of Noritoshi Kamo, used her circumstances for experimentation. Nine pregnancies were produced and terminated, with Kenjaku mixing his own blood into the process. The resulting fetuses became the Death Painting Wombs.

Appearance: While sealed as objects, the Death Paintings resemble small preserved human fetuses. They are conscious only in an extremely limited sense, yet the brothers retained awareness of one another during roughly a century and a half of confinement.

Sealing: Jujutsu sorcerers secured the nine objects and bound them so they could continue existing without freely acting or harming others. They were stored within Tokyo Jujutsu High's cursed warehouse behind Tengen's concealment.

Incarnation: A Death Painting can incarnate when ingested by a human vessel. Unlike many cursed objects, the vessel does not need natural sorcerer talent. The incarnation produces a flesh-and-blood being that combines human and cursed-spirit characteristics. Choso, Eso, and Kechizu are the first three Death Paintings incarnated in this way.

Properties: Incarnated Death Paintings are visible to ordinary people because they possess physical human bodies. They can use jujutsu and leave corpses rather than vanishing like ordinary cursed spirits. Their mixed physiology also gives the blood of the first three brothers poisonous properties against humans.

Known Wombs: Nos. 1-3 are Choso, Eso, and Kechizu. The remaining six are Noranso, Sho-oso, Tanso, Sanso, Kotsuso, and Shoso.

cardPool.title: Prison Realm
cardPool.value:
Name: Prison Realm

Classification: Special-grade cursed object; living barrier and sealing device.

Appearance: In its inactive state, Prison Realm is a small cube wrapped in talisman-like restraints, compact enough to carry by hand. When activated with the command to open the gate, it unfolds into a grotesque fleshy structure stretched between the cube's corners, dominated by a large bloodshot eye. The transformation makes clear that the object is not a normal container but a living barrier.

Origin: Prison Realm is formed from the remains of the Buddhist monk Genshin. It is considered a taboo object because its barrier is capable of sealing virtually any target if its activation conditions are fulfilled.

Activation: The target must remain within approximately four meters of the opened Prison Realm for one minute measured by the target's own mental perception. Once the condition is met, the barrier rapidly binds the target, immobilizes them, and cuts off access to cursed energy before the gate closes. Only one occupant can be held at a time.

Interior: The sealed person is confined inside an isolated pocket dimension surrounded by skeletal remains. Time does not meaningfully pass for the occupant. Escape through ordinary force is not available, and the object can contain even an overwhelmingly powerful sorcerer.

Processing: Sealing an exceptional target can cause the closed cube to become extremely heavy and temporarily difficult to move while the barrier processes its captive. Additional eyes may appear across its surface during this state.

Front and Back: Prison Realm has a Front Gate that controls sealing and a separate Back Gate connected to release. Possessing the Back does not grant authority to open the Front. Breaking the Back requires a means that can nullify or extinguish cursed techniques, such as the properties associated with the Inverted Spear of Heaven, Black Rope, or Technique Extinguishment.

cardPool.title: Sukuna's Fingers
cardPool.value:
Name: Ryomen Sukuna's Fingers

Classification: Twenty special-grade cursed objects containing fragments of Ryomen Sukuna's soul and power.

Appearance: Each object is a severed, mummified human finger darkened by age and saturated with an abnormal quantity of cursed energy. Ordinary decay cannot destroy them, and even exceptionally powerful modern sorcerers cannot simply erase the curse embedded in the remains. Protective paper seals can suppress their presence temporarily but do not eliminate what is inside.

Origin: Sukuna possessed twenty fingers because of his four-armed body. After his death, the remains became cursed objects through arrangements associated with Kenjaku, allowing Sukuna to persist across more than a thousand years. Each finger carries part of his soul and acts as both a reservoir of power and a beacon to cursed spirits.

Effects: An unsealed finger attracts curses that seek its energy. A cursed spirit can consume one and gain a major increase in power, sometimes producing a finger-bearer classified at special grade. A human who consumes one risks death, poisoning, possession, or incarnation. Suitable vessels are exceptionally rare.

Yuji Itadori: Yuji can ingest the fingers without immediately losing control of his body, making him an extraordinary vessel. Sukuna remains a distinct consciousness within him and can manifest under specific conditions. The fingers do not function as Quirks and cannot be erased, stolen, copied, or detected through Quirk-based systems.

Handling: Jujutsu personnel normally seal and store recovered fingers in protected facilities. Transport requires discretion because their presence can draw curses even when civilians cannot understand what is happening.

Destruction: The objects are effectively indestructible through ordinary means. The practical strategy is containment or controlled ingestion by a viable vessel followed by execution of that vessel once all fragments are gathered.

cardPool.title: Garuda
cardPool.value:
Name:
Garuda

Classification:
Shikigami

Description:
A long, serpent-like shikigami bound to Yuki Tsukumo and treated as a target of her Star Rage technique.

Abilities:
Can carry virtual mass, become an extraordinarily heavy striking weapon, restrain targets, and assist Yuki in close or ranged combat.

Relationship / Role:
Functions as Yuki's primary shikigami and combat partner.

Practical Note:
Garuda must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Function:
Garuda is Yuki Tsukumo's long segmented shikigami and is directly compatible with Star Rage. Yuki can assign virtual mass to Garuda just as she does to herself, turning its flexible body into an extremely heavy striking weapon without reducing its usefulness as a moving companion. It can wrap, restrain, swing, or be kicked like a projectile. Garuda's importance comes from extending Yuki's mass-based offense beyond her own fists rather than operating as an independent technique user.

Appearance and Handling:
Garuda has a long segmented body with a skull-like head and functions almost like a living flexible weapon. Its shape allows it to coil, wrap, swing, and change direction around Yuki's movement. Because Star Rage can increase its virtual mass, a seemingly simple kick or swing can turn Garuda into a devastating impact weapon without requiring the shikigami to possess a separate offensive technique.

Its combat identity is inseparable from Yuki's control and mass application, not from independent personality or a separate summoning lineage.

cardPool.title: Divine General Mahoraga
cardPool.value:
Name:
Eight Handled Sword Divergent Sila Divine General Mahoraga

Classification:
Ten Shadows shikigami

Description:
The most dangerous shikigami of the Ten Shadows Technique, historically untamed by ordinary users.

Abilities:
Possesses overwhelming physical ability and an adaptation wheel that progressively adjusts to phenomena it experiences, making repeated use of the same attack increasingly ineffective.

Relationship / Role:
Summoned through an exorcism ritual. An untamed Mahoraga attacks participants indiscriminately.

Practical Note:
Divine General Mahoraga must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Taming and Adaptation:
Mahoraga is the most dangerous shikigami of the Ten Shadows Technique and historically could not be tamed by its known inheritors. The user summons it through an exorcism ritual; outside participants can be drawn into the ritual, but outside assistance invalidates the taming result. The wheel above Mahoraga turns as it analyzes a phenomenon, and repeated exposure allows it to adapt defensively or offensively, and usually needs 4 turns for simple phenomena, or 8 turns for complex phenomena, each turn taking some time. Its Sword of Extermination carries positive energy, making it exceptionally lethal to cursed spirits.

Appearance:
Mahoraga is a towering humanoid shikigami with a heavily muscular pale body, four wing-like projections extending from the face, a long tail-like appendage, and an eight-handled wheel suspended above the head. It carries the Sword of Extermination on one arm. The wheel is the clearest sign of adaptation: each turn marks progress in adjusting to a phenomenon that has affected it.

cardPool.title: Rot Technique
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Rot Technique

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique of the Cursed Womb: Death Painting brothers Eso and Kechizu.

Known User(s):
Eso; Kechizu.

Core Mechanic:
Rot Technique gives the users dark blood with poisonous, corrosive properties and allows that blood to be shaped and manipulated. Contact can burn flesh directly, and blood entering a wound or mucous membrane creates the condition for the technique's more lethal extension, Decay.

Decay:
Once Eso's or Kechizu's blood enters the target, Decay can be activated and a floral pattern spreads from the point of contamination as the victim's body decomposes. Against an ordinary victim the process is expected to become fatal within roughly ten to fifteen minutes. Either brother can activate Decay after the relevant blood exposure.

Blood Manipulation:
Eso can reshape blood from his wounds into functional structures, including a temporary arm-like limb. Kechizu primarily expels corrosive blood directly. Their blood has its own poisonous quality and should not be treated as ordinary Blood Manipulation from the Kamo Clan.

Maximum: Wing King:
Eso's Maximum Technique reshapes blood flowing from his back into large wasp-like wings. The wings improve mobility and project long lines of blood at range. Maximum: Wing King and Decay cannot be maintained simultaneously, forcing Eso to choose between the two functions.

Limits and Counters:
Decay requires the brothers' blood to enter the target through a wound or mucous membrane before activation. The effect can be disrupted if Eso is forced to release it. Maximum: Wing King conflicts with Decay, and the technique's blood remains a physical medium that can be avoided before contamination occurs.

Technical Notes:
Rot Technique is distinct from the Kamo Clan's Blood Manipulation despite both using blood as a medium.

cardPool.title: Contractual Re-Creation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Contractual Re-Creation

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Reggie Star.

Core Mechanic:
Contractual Re-Creation reproduces the subject of a written contract, most commonly a receipt, by infusing the document with Cursed Energy and burning it. The recreated result corresponds to what the contract records. This includes physical goods as well as the effect of purchased services, allowing the technique to manifest far more than simple weapons.

Physical Goods:
Receipts can recreate objects such as knives, vehicles, appliances, or heavy equipment. Reggie carries a large stockpile of receipts so he can select a useful object for the situation instead of relying on one fixed summon.

Services:
A contract for a service can reproduce the service's effect. For example, a receipt for time spent at a spa can restore Reggie's stamina as though the recorded service had been received, demonstrating that the technique reproduces contractual fulfillment rather than merely manufacturing matter.

Commands:
Recreated physical items can be issued simple commands similar to shikigami, such as flying toward an opponent. Once an object completes its command, it disappears rather than remaining indefinitely as ordinary permanent property.

Limits and Counters:
The contract must be activated by burning it after applying Cursed Energy. Water is therefore a practical counter because a soaked receipt may remain readable but cannot be ignited normally. Each consumed contract is a finite resource, so Reggie's versatility depends on preparation and the receipts he actually carries.

Technical Notes:
The technique reproduces what a valid contract records; it does not let Reggie invent arbitrary goods or services without the corresponding document.

cardPool.title: Technique Extinguishment
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Technique Extinguishment

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique; the descriptive title 'Technique Extinguishment' is not an officially assigned personal technique name.

Known User(s):
Angel through the vessel Hana Kurusu.

Core Mechanic:
Technique Extinguishment nullifies jujutsu it comes into contact with. Its effect can erase or disrupt Cursed Techniques, barriers, seals, cursed spirits, and cursed objects rather than merely overpowering them with raw damage. The user can pass through barriers and can destroy a barrier by targeting its foundation.

Purifying Light:
Activation produces intense arrays of purifying light, often appearing as sharp cross-shaped beams. The light carries the extinguishing effect and can be used against active techniques, supernatural constructs, curses, or incarnated cursed objects within a vessel.

Jacob's Ladder:
Jacob's Ladder is an extension technique activated with a four-winged trumpet of light and a large ritual array overhead. A descending pillar of purifying light applies Technique Extinguishment at high output across the target area.

Incarnated Sorcerers:
Because incarnation depends on a cursed object merged with a vessel, Technique Extinguishment can attack that supernatural connection and potentially strip the incarnation away. Attempting to remove a powerful cursed object from its vessel remains extremely dangerous and can kill the host.

Limits and Counters:
The technique nullifies jujutsu rather than granting universal control over whatever it touches. Freeing a vessel from incarnation is not guaranteed to preserve the vessel's life, and destroying a barrier still requires the user to affect its relevant foundation or structure.

Technical Notes:
Jacob's Ladder is an extension of Technique Extinguishment, not a separate Innate Technique.

cardPool.title: Ice Formation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Ice Formation

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Uraume.

Core Mechanic:
Ice Formation lowers temperature to extreme levels and lets Uraume generate, shape, and control ice and frost. Ice can be formed from surfaces, expanded into large sheets or structures, suspended in the air, and directed telekinetically after creation. Uraume's output and precision are high enough to freeze multiple experienced sorcerers while deliberately reducing the effect on selected individuals.

Frost Calm:
Frost Calm releases a cloud of freezing mist that rapidly hardens around targets into thick ice, immobilizing them and making careless movement dangerous. Maximum Output: Frost Calm dramatically increases the affected area and can freeze a large section of a battlefield at once.

Icefall:
Icefall generates large quantities of ice, suspends them over or around targets, freezes targets on contact, and follows with massive icicles dropping from above. It combines restraint with a finishing attack rather than relying only on cold exposure.

Control:
Uraume can produce ice by touching surfaces and can maintain enough precision to select who is fully frozen inside a crowded fight. The generated ice becomes a physical battlefield obstacle that can restrain bodies, block routes, and damage structures.

Limits and Counters:
Maintaining large-scale ice requires concentration and Cursed Energy. When Uraume was seriously poisoned and their focus collapsed, the ice restraining multiple targets melted away. Heat or internal temperature manipulation can help resist freezing, but overcoming the technique still depends on the defender's actual output and circumstances.

Technical Notes:
Ice Formation controls ice produced through the technique; it is not a blanket ability to command every pre-existing source of ice without limit.

cardPool.title: Mythical Beast Amber
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Mythical Beast Amber

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique with a one-use release condition.

Known User(s):
Hajime Kashimo.

Core Mechanic:
Mythical Beast Amber reconstructs Kashimo's flesh so his body can manifest phenomena produced by electricity converted from his Cursed Energy. The transformation pushes human tissue beyond sustainable limits and massively expands what his naturally electric Cursed Energy can express. Once the technique ends, the reconstructed body collapses, so it can only be used once.

Neurological Acceleration:
The transformed body increases the activity of electrical signals in Kashimo's brain and nervous system, sharply improving perception, reaction, and movement. The technique can also alter sensory organs, including producing enhanced vision for analyzing an opponent's body.

Electrical Phenomena:
Kashimo can create electromagnetic waves that vaporize irradiated matter, release powerful sonic phenomena tuned through electrical effects, and reshape parts of his body into structures suited to those attacks. His ordinary Cursed Energy lightning remains available alongside the transformation.

Body Reconstruction:
The technique visibly changes Kashimo as it progresses, forming horn-like hair, altered eyes, clawed hands, and other nonhuman features needed to express electrical phenomena. These are functional transformations produced by the technique rather than cosmetic changes.

Limits and Counters:
Mythical Beast Amber is effectively suicidal. The altered body exceeds normal human limits and cannot return to its original state when the technique concludes. Kashimo therefore reserves it for a single decisive battle instead of using it as a routine transformation.

Technical Notes:
The one-use limit belongs to the technique's effect on Kashimo's body, not to an external cooldown.

cardPool.title: Sky Manipulation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Sky Manipulation

Classification:
Unnamed Innate Cursed Technique; 'Sky Manipulation' is a descriptive title rather than an officially stated technique name.

Known User(s):
Takako Uro.

Core Mechanic:
Sky Manipulation treats the surrounding 'sky' or space like a tangible two-dimensional surface that the user can grab, pull, stretch, and distort. The technique does not simply move objects with telekinesis. Instead, Uro manipulates the spatial surface through which attacks and bodies are perceived, letting her bend trajectories and alter apparent positioning.

Spatial Distortion:
Uro can pull the sky like cloth to warp the space around herself or an opponent. This lets her redirect incoming attacks, distort a limb's apparent path, conceal parts of her body behind bent space, and create unconventional movement angles. She also uses the technique to remain airborne.

Defense:
Because an attack's path can be bent away from her, Sky Manipulation is especially effective against straightforward projectiles and close-range blows. The technique changes the route through space rather than absorbing the attack's energy with a conventional barrier.

Thin Ice Breaker:
Thin Ice Breaker strikes the manipulated surface of the sky itself and shatters it like a thin sheet of ice. The resulting spatial shock hits the opponent with concentrated force, allowing Uro to attack around conventional guarding angles instead of needing to strike the body directly.

Limits and Counters:
Manipulating the sky does not grant unrestricted control over all space or allow Uro to crush a target merely by folding the surface around them. Technique burnout after Domain Expansion temporarily prevents use, and opponents who understand the distortion can adjust their timing and angle.

Technical Notes:
Uro can use Domain Expansion, but its canonical name, appearance, and sure-hit effect were never revealed.

cardPool.title: Yuji Itadori's Unnamed Domain Expansion
cardPool.value:
Name:
Unnamed Domain Expansion

User:
Yuji Itadori

Derived From:
Yuji's late-developed Shrine and barrier training

Classification:
Completed Domain Expansion; no canonical personal name is established.

Environment:
The interior recreates locations from Yuji's hometown with striking specificity. Familiar public spaces, a local statue, a park, shops, rural areas, and animals connected to his memories can appear within the Domain. The setting feels personal and ordinary rather than resembling Sukuna's shrine, reflecting Yuji's own inner world instead of copying Sukuna's imagery.

Sure-Hit Effect:
The barrier applies Yuji's Dismantle as a guaranteed attack. By this stage Yuji has learned to direct his Shrine-based slashes toward the boundary between an incarnated sorcerer's soul and the host soul. The Domain removes the need for ordinary physical contact when applying that soul-separating Dismantle to the target.

Barrier Development:
Yuji gains the fundamentals necessary to construct a Domain through intensive late-stage training that includes barrier instruction associated with Atsuya Kusakabe. His ability appears extremely late compared with the default starting point and should never be assumed available to first-year Yuji at the Quirk Apprehension Test-era world state.

Naming:
The manga does not provide an official unique name for Yuji's Domain Expansion. Descriptive fan labels such as 'Hometown Domain' are useful shorthand but are not treated here as the canonical title.

Timeline Status:
This card records a later potential development only. It does not retroactively give early Yuji Shrine, Reverse Cursed Technique, Simple Domain, or Domain Expansion.
