cardPool.title: Time Cell Moon Palace
keys: Naoya Zenin's Time Cell Moon Palace
cardPool.value:
Name:
Time Cell Moon Palace

User:
Naoya Zenin, after becoming a vengeful cursed spirit

Derived From:
Projection Sorcery

Classification:
Completed lethal Domain Expansion.

Prerequisite:
Naoya does not possess this Domain as an ordinary living human. It manifests only after his death, return as a vengeful cursed spirit, and further evolution. The Domain therefore belongs to that later cursed-spirit state rather than his default human character profile.

Environment:
The barrier creates a dark interior dominated by a long fleshy pathway leading toward a massive eye-like structure. The anatomy resembles a womb or internal organ, fitting Naoya's evolved cursed form and the cellular precision of his technique.

Sure-Hit Effect:
The Domain injects animation-frame film into targets and applies Projection Sorcery's twenty-four-frames-per-second rule at the level of individual cells. Any movement that fails to obey the imposed sequence causes cellular disruption throughout the moving body part. Even a small attempted motion can produce widespread cuts and internal damage; forcing a limb to move through the violation can destroy it entirely.

Precision:
Ordinary Projection Sorcery freezes a touched target for one second when they fail its movement rule. Time Cell Moon Palace greatly increases that precision by enforcing the rule across the target's cells through the Domain's guaranteed effect, turning normal movement itself into a lethal mistake.

Timeline Status:
This is a later-development Domain and is not available to the living Naoya present in the default world state.

Barrier Targeting:
A person with absolutely zero Cursed Energy can fall outside the automatic recognition rules of a conventional barrier unless they deliberately enter or the barrier is configured to account for them.

cardPool.title: Private Pure Love Train
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Private Pure Love Train

Classification:
Unnamed pachinko-themed Innate Cursed Technique; commonly identified by the in-universe series and game system 'Private Pure Love Train'.

Known User(s):
Kinji Hakari.

Core Mechanic:
Hakari's Innate Technique is built around the pachinko game and romance series Private Pure Love Train. Its complete rules are primarily expressed through his Domain Expansion, Idle Death Gamble. Outside the Domain, Hakari can manifest visual-effect indicators from the game as tangible Cursed Technique constructs rather than running the full jackpot system in open space.

Visual Effect Indicators:
Hakari can summon elements such as shutter doors outside his Domain and use them as physical obstacles or attacks. These manifestations are pieces of the same pachinko presentation that appears during Idle Death Gamble, but they do not by themselves grant a jackpot or automatic Reverse Cursed Technique.

Domain-Centered Design:
Unlike techniques with a large catalogue of independent attacks, the base technique is heavily tied to the rule system embedded into Hakari's Domain. The romance scenarios, probability indicators, reach animations, and jackpot logic belong to Idle Death Gamble's pachinko process.

Combat Integration:
Hakari supplements the limited open-field applications with aggressive hand-to-hand combat and Cursed Energy reinforcement. His naturally rough-textured Cursed Energy makes ordinary reinforced blows unpleasant to absorb even before the Domain's jackpot state is involved.

Limits and Counters:
The base technique's openly demonstrated applications are limited compared with the Domain. It should not be treated as generic probability manipulation or passive supernatural luck. Jackpot probability, bonus rounds, automatic healing, and consecutive Domain cycles belong specifically to Idle Death Gamble.

Domain Expansion:
Idle Death Gamble is documented separately.

cardPool.title: Love Rendezvous
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Love Rendezvous

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Kirara Hoshi.

Core Mechanic:
Love Rendezvous marks Cursed Energy with one of five stars based on the Southern Cross: Imai, Acrux, Mimosa, Ginan, and Gacrux. The marks impose an approach order. A target marked with one star cannot freely approach another star farther along the sequence without passing the intermediate stars in order, while objects or people bearing the same star attract each other.

Star Order:
The required route is Imai → Acrux → Mimosa → Ginan → Gacrux, following the stars from nearest to farthest distance from Earth. A person marked with Acrux, for example, must satisfy the intermediate route before they can approach Gacrux normally.

Applying Marks:
Kirara must make contact with Cursed Energy to assign a mark. One target's Cursed Energy carries one star at a time, although the same star can be assigned to multiple targets. Objects need Cursed Energy on them before they can be marked, allowing prepared vehicles or tools to become part of the technique.

Attraction:
Two targets sharing a star are forcibly drawn together and become difficult to separate. The target with greater Cursed Energy output dominates the attraction. Because a sorcerer and their shikigami share the same Cursed Energy signature, touching the shikigami can let Kirara mark both.

Limits and Counters:
Love Rendezvous depends on Cursed Energy marks and can be deciphered by an opponent who correctly identifies the constellation order. Kirara must manage their own mark carefully, removing it when necessary before marking another object with their Cursed Energy.

Technical Notes:
The technique controls routes and attraction between marked Cursed Energy signatures; it is not generic gravity or distance manipulation.

cardPool.title: Solo Forbidden Area
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Solo Forbidden Area

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique focused on support.

Known User(s):
Utahime Iori.

Core Mechanic:
Solo Forbidden Area creates a zone around Utahime that temporarily increases the Cursed Energy capacity and output of willing sorcerers within its range, including Utahime herself. It enhances the target's own Cursed Energy rather than granting them a new technique. The ability becomes substantially stronger when Utahime performs the full ritual instead of abbreviating its activation.

Ritual Amplification:
The complete ritual incorporates incantations, hand signs, dance, and music. Jujutsu normally rewards skilled users for subtracting unnecessary activation steps, but Utahime deliberately restores every step to elevate the technique's effectiveness. Performing the full ritual raises Solo Forbidden Area's potency to 120 percent.

Support Function:
The technique is best used before or during a prepared high-output attack because it strengthens the ally's available Cursed Energy and output. It does not aim or control the ally's technique for them, and the enhanced sorcerer still needs the skill and conditions required for their own ability.

Area Requirement:
The beneficiary must remain within the technique's effective zone when receiving the amplification. Utahime can include herself, but the technique is primarily valuable because it can boost another willing sorcerer at a critical moment.

Limits and Counters:
Full effectiveness requires preparation and completion of a visible ritual, making the technique poorly suited to sudden close-range exchanges. Interrupting Utahime, preventing the ritual steps, or forcing the intended ally outside the effective zone reduces its usefulness.

Technical Notes:
The technique's 120-percent state refers to Solo Forbidden Area's ritual potency, not a universal permanent 120-percent increase to every statistic.

cardPool.title: Auspicious Beasts Summon
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Auspicious Beasts Summon

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique and séance-style medium technique.

Known User(s):
Takuma Ino.

Core Mechanic:
Auspicious Beasts Summon turns Ino into a spiritual medium while his face is hidden. By covering his face and calling a beast's number and name, he channels one of four auspicious beasts through his own Cursed Energy. The technique does not summon independent shikigami to fight beside him; it manifests each beast's specific ability for Ino to use.

Number One — Kaichi:
Kaichi manifests as a spiraled horn that Ino can control telepathically and fire as a homing projectile. It pursues the target after an initial miss and delivers a strong piercing or stinging impact when it connects.

Number Two — Reiki:
Reiki transforms Cursed Energy into controllable water that coats Ino like a cushion. It can absorb impacts defensively, and Ino can slide his feet through the water to increase mobility and alter his movement in close combat.

Number Three — Kirin:
Kirin performs an intracerebral doping effect that suppresses Ino's sense of pain. The benefit carries a severe stamina cost; once the effect finishes, Ino becomes extremely exhausted, unable to sleep, and temporarily unable to move.

Number Four — Ryu:
Ryu concentrates Cursed Energy around Ino's hands and manifests a large serpentine dragon-like attack that rushes into the target. Unlike the other abilities, the manifested dragon can be struck and dispersed by sufficient damage.

Limits and Counters:
Ino must keep his face hidden to remain a valid medium. Removing or disrupting his mask can shut down access to the beasts. Each beast provides a specific function rather than a freely customizable summon, and Kirin carries an especially severe post-use penalty.

Technical Notes:
Auspicious Beasts Summon is not ordinary shikigami summoning despite its animal imagery.

cardPool.title: Black Bird Manipulation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Black Bird Manipulation

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Mei Mei.

Core Mechanic:
Black Bird Manipulation lets Mei Mei imbue crows with Cursed Energy, command them over long distances, and share their vision. The controlled birds are completely obedient, making them effective reconnaissance tools for mapping buildings, tracking movement, observing barriers, and watching several areas while Mei Mei remains elsewhere.

Surveillance:
Shared vision turns ordinary crows into a distributed observation network. Mei Mei can send multiple birds through separate routes, monitor locations that are unsafe to enter personally, and use the information to determine where civilians, curses, or barrier sources are located.

Direct Control:
The birds can be moved precisely and used for distraction or minor attacks, but an ordinary crow is physically weak. Mei Mei therefore trained her own body extensively instead of relying on the base technique as her primary method of killing strong opponents.

Bird Strike:
Bird Strike forces a controlled crow to sacrifice its life through a binding vow. In exchange, the restriction on the crow's Cursed Energy is removed and it is hurled into the target with overwhelming force. The suicidal exchange turns an otherwise weak familiar into a strike capable of exorcising extremely dangerous curses.

Limits and Counters:
Black Bird Manipulation depends on available crows, and losing birds reduces both surveillance coverage and potential Bird Strikes. Bird Strike consumes the crow permanently and is powerful because of that sacrifice; it is not the normal damage output of every controlled bird.

Technical Notes:
The technique controls crows specifically rather than granting generic domination over all animals.

cardPool.title: Ratio Technique
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Ratio Technique

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Kento Nanami.

Core Mechanic:
Ratio Technique divides a chosen target into ten portions and forcibly creates a weak point at the seven-to-three ratio. Striking that point produces a critical hit that can break through defenses far more effectively than an ordinary blow. The division can be applied to a whole body, a specific limb, or an inanimate object rather than requiring the target's entire height or width.

Critical Point:
Nanami can place the ratio line on different parts of a target and then strike the generated weak point with his wrapped blunt blade or with his bare hands. The weapon does not need a sharp edge because the technique creates the vulnerability being exploited.

Inanimate Targets:
The technique works on structures and objects as well as living beings. This lets Nanami turn walls, floors, supports, and debris into tactical targets instead of limiting Ratio Technique to direct attacks on an opponent.

Collapse:
Collapse is an extension technique that expands Ratio Technique from a single localized weak point to a broader area. By striking the generated weakness, Nanami can bring down a large section of the environment and weaponize the resulting destruction.

Limits and Counters:
The technique still requires Nanami to successfully strike the generated ratio point; it does not automatically damage a target from a distance. A critical hit can overwhelm reinforcement but does not ignore every supernatural defense or guarantee permanent damage against beings that can restore themselves through special mechanics.

Technical Notes:
Nanami's Overtime is a separate binding vow that increases his Cursed Energy output; it is not part of Ratio Technique itself.

cardPool.title: Puppet Manipulation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Puppet Manipulation

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Kokichi Muta.

Core Mechanic:
Puppet Manipulation allows Kokichi Muta to remotely control multiple cursed-corpse puppets and channel his Cursed Energy through them. The technique itself is remote control and energy transmission; the blades, cannons, boosters, shields, and other attacks associated with Mechamaru come from the design of the puppet bodies Kokichi operates. His Heavenly Restriction massively extends his effective range across Japan and increases available output.

Remote Operation:
Kokichi receives battlefield information through his puppets and can operate them while his real body remains far away. He can control multiple units, use unregistered puppets for surveillance, and treat the standard Ultimate Mechamaru body as a physical proxy for school and missions.

Mechamaru Armaments:
Standard Mechamaru puppets include commands such as Sword Option, Boost On, Ultra Spin, Ultra Cannon, Mode: Albatross, Ultimate Cannon, and Ultra Shield. These are applications of the controlled machine and Kokichi's transmitted Cursed Energy rather than separate Innate Techniques.

Mode: Absolute:
Ultimate Mechamaru Mode: Absolute is a giant combat puppet operated directly by Kokichi. It can spend years of previously stored Cursed Energy through large-scale attacks such as Miracle Cannon and Pigeon Viola, giving the technique an extreme prepared-output option.

Limits and Counters:
Puppet Manipulation depends on usable puppet bodies; destroying or disabling the current unit removes that platform even if Kokichi himself remains alive. The technique's extraordinary nationwide range is specifically amplified by Kokichi's Heavenly Restriction and should not be assumed to be the normal range of any hypothetical user.

Technical Notes:
Kokichi's stored Cursed Energy and mechanical engineering expand what the technique can accomplish but are not themselves part of its base formula.

cardPool.title: Construction
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Construction

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Mai Zenin; historical sorcerer Yorozu.

Core Mechanic:
Construction converts Cursed Energy into real physical matter created from nothing. Unlike temporary matter formed inside many Domains, a constructed object remains in existence after the technique ends. The tradeoff is extreme inefficiency: producing matter consumes enormous Cursed Energy and can cause significant physical backlash.

Mai Zenin:
Mai's limited reserves restrict her ordinary use to creating roughly one additional revolver bullet per day, an application she hides as a surprise seventh shot. Even that small object drains her heavily and can cause physical symptoms such as a nosebleed.

Yorozu:
With vastly greater reserves and technical understanding, Yorozu demonstrates the technique's broader ceiling by reproducing substances she understands, developing controllable liquid metal, insect-inspired armor, and an idealized perfect sphere. Her work shows that Construction's main limitation is efficiency rather than a narrow list of possible shapes.

Permanent Matter:
Created matter does not disappear simply because the technique is released. However, reproducing the special supernatural properties of an existing special-grade cursed tool is beyond ordinary Construction; creating the physical shape of an object is not the same as duplicating its unique cursed effect.

Limits and Counters:
Construction's Cursed Energy cost is exceptionally poor relative to the amount of matter produced. The user needs sufficient knowledge of what they are creating, and larger or more complex creations demand far more resources. Mai's personal one-bullet limit reflects her reserves, not a universal one-object rule for every user.

cardPool.title: Boogie Woogie
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Boogie Woogie

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Aoi Todo.

Core Mechanic:
Boogie Woogie instantly swaps the positions of two valid targets when Todo activates its trigger. A valid target must possess at least a sufficient amount of Cursed Energy, but Todo does not need to include himself in the exchange: he can swap two other people, a person with a cursed object, or other sufficiently energized targets.

Original Activation:
Todo originally activates Boogie Woogie by clapping his hands together. He can clap without performing a swap, turning the activation sound into a feint, and he can clap another person's hand to satisfy the trigger. Its simplicity becomes dangerous because opponents cannot know whether a clap will swap, what will swap, or whether nothing will happen.

Tactical Use:
Todo uses rapid exchanges to redirect attacks, pull allies out of danger, move enemies into incoming strikes, break formations, and create impossible-looking attack angles. The technique's effectiveness comes as much from Todo's timing and combat intelligence as from the raw teleportation effect.

Boogie Woogie: Revised:
After losing a hand, Todo later replaces the clap trigger with a vibraslap. The instrument permits up to fifty swaps per second. A binding vow can reduce the number of swaps per strike in exchange for expanded range and the ability to select multiple targets.

Limits and Counters:
The technique requires valid Cursed Energy targets and an activation trigger. Knowing the rules helps an opponent anticipate possible exchanges, but Todo's feints prevent simple prediction. Damage to or loss of the current trigger can disable the technique until Todo establishes another valid method.

Technical Notes:
The vibraslap revision is a later modification to Boogie Woogie, not a separate Innate Technique.

cardPool.title: Blood Manipulation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Blood Manipulation

Classification:
Inherited Cursed Technique of the Kamo Clan.

Known User(s):
Noritoshi Kamo; Choso.

Core Mechanic:
Blood Manipulation grants precise control over the user's own blood, both inside and outside the body. The user can alter blood flow, composition, shape, pressure, and trajectory, allowing the same technique to enhance physical performance, restrain targets, form weapons, or fire high-speed projectiles. Human users are limited by real blood loss; Death Painting physiology changes that limitation.

Convergence and Piercing Blood:
Convergence compresses and condenses blood into a dense orb. Piercing Blood fires that compressed blood through a narrow point as a high-speed beam capable of reaching the speed of sound. Convergence also serves as preparation for other techniques such as Choso's Supernova.

Flowing Red Scale:
Flowing Red Scale manipulates internal circulation, temperature, pulse, and red blood cell activity to sharply increase physical capability. Flowing Red Scale: Stack intensifies this state further at greater strain.

Other Extensions:
Crimson Binding forms a blood net for restraint; Slicing Exorcism shapes blood into cutting streams or discs; Blood Edge creates a high-speed rotating blood blade; Blood Meteorite hardens blood into a projectile. Choso's Supernova releases multiple compressed blood orbs as a buckshot-like burst.

Limits and Counters:
A normal human sorcerer can die from excessive blood loss and often prepares stored blood in advance. Too much water can prevent externally controlled blood from maintaining its shape. Choso can convert Cursed Energy into blood, greatly reducing the blood-loss problem, and his Death Painting blood is poisonous to ordinary humans and curses.

Technical Notes:
Blood Manipulation only controls the user's own blood unless another technique or circumstance provides a specific exception.

cardPool.title: Disaster Flames
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Disaster Flames

Classification:
Unnamed volcanic Innate Cursed Technique; 'Disaster Flames' is a descriptive name rather than an officially stated technique name.

Known User(s):
Jogo.

Core Mechanic:
Jogo's technique creates extremely concentrated cursed flames, heat, and volcanic eruptions. He can fire flames directly from his body or manifest small volcanic openings on nearby surfaces and have them erupt toward a target, letting attacks originate from angles unrelated to his own position. His immense Cursed Energy reserves allow him to produce enormous quantities of fire without immediately exhausting himself.

Volcanic Eruptions:
Jogo can create localized volcanic vents in walls, floors, and other surfaces and use them to launch high-output heat or flame attacks. This makes the technique dangerous at close and mid range because defensive positioning against Jogo's body alone does not cover every attack angle.

Ember Insects:
Ember Insects are flying insect-like manifestations released from Jogo's volcanic opening. They approach a target with large stingers, produce a high-pitched screech, and then detonate in a fiery explosion, combining pursuit, distraction, and delayed blast pressure.

Maximum: Meteor:
Maximum: Meteor creates a gigantic flaming meteor and hurls it toward the target. Its destructive power is enormous enough to devastate a broad area, but its scale makes it less suited to catching extremely fast opponents than Jogo's quicker ordinary attacks.

Limits and Counters:
The technique's raw output is exceptional but does not guarantee every attack will connect. Maximum: Meteor sacrifices speed and flexibility for destructive scale. Jogo's Domain and Maximum Technique are distinct advanced expressions rather than the default behavior of every flame he creates.

Domain Expansion:
Coffin of the Iron Mountain is documented separately.

cardPool.title: Idle Transfiguration
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Idle Transfiguration

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Mahito.

Core Mechanic:
Idle Transfiguration directly manipulates the shape of the soul. Because the body follows the soul's shape, changing a target's soul changes their physical body as a consequence. Mahito normally needs physical contact to transfigure another person's soul, while he can reshape his own soul freely to alter his body, recover its intended form, change size, or create weapons and mobility adaptations.

Transfigured Humans:
Humans whose souls are forcibly reshaped become physical transfigured humans. Mahito can shrink and store them, enlarge or deform them later, and use them as disposable attackers. Ordinary healing cannot simply restore a soul that has been fundamentally reshaped.

Soul Multiplicity:
Soul Multiplicity fuses two or more souls and exploits the natural rejection between them. Body Repel increases the resulting rejection into a high-output mass attack, while Polymorphic Soul Isomer merges souls with weak rejection into a stable combat body with explosive strength but poor durability.

Self-Transformation:
Mahito can reshape his limbs into blades, clubs, wings, mouths, or other structures and can alter his entire form. This is not conventional regeneration: physical damage is largely meaningless if his soul remains intact enough to restore the body's shape.

Limits and Counters:
A target with meaningful soul awareness can reinforce and defend the soul with Cursed Energy, forcing Mahito to spend repeated contacts instead of achieving immediate transfiguration. Attacks that directly damage Mahito's soul bypass his normal self-restoration. Touching a vessel can also expose Mahito to another soul occupying the same body.

Domain Expansion:
Self-Embodiment of Perfection is documented separately.

cardPool.title: Cursed Spirit Manipulation
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Cursed Spirit Manipulation

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Suguru Geto; later Kenjaku while inhabiting Geto's body.

Core Mechanic:
Cursed Spirit Manipulation allows the user to conquer cursed spirits, compress them into small black spheres, swallow those spheres, and thereafter summon and command the absorbed curses. A curse already bound to another master cannot simply be stolen; its master must first be dealt with. If the user's grade exceeds a curse by at least two levels, the curse can be absorbed with effectively no additional submission condition.

Storage and Summoning:
There is no demonstrated ordinary numerical cap on stored curses. The user can summon individual spirits or large groups through portals and exploit each curse's unique body, instincts, and Cursed Technique. Absorbed spirits stop naturally developing once taken into the user's stockpile.

Maximum: Uzumaki:
Maximum: Uzumaki combines selected stored curses into a single blast of extremely condensed Cursed Energy. Using semi-grade 1 or stronger curses in Uzumaki can extract their Innate Techniques for the manipulator to use afterward; an extracted technique is a one-use resource.

Death of the User:
The technique's stockpile is tied to its manipulator. If the user dies while curses remain stored, those cursed spirits are released rather than remaining permanently sealed.

Limits and Counters:
A powerful curse generally must be conquered before absorption, and swallowing each condensed spirit is physically revolting. Spending curses through Uzumaki permanently removes those spirits from the stockpile. Extracted techniques do not become an endlessly reusable second arsenal.

Technical Notes:
The technique controls cursed spirits, not shikigami or ordinary living creatures.

cardPool.title: Star Rage
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Star Rage

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique.

Known User(s):
Yuki Tsukumo.

Core Mechanic:
Star Rage grants Yuki the ability to add virtual mass to herself and to Garuda. The assigned mass produces force as though it were real when Yuki or Garuda strikes or presses against something, but it does not normally burden Yuki's own movement. This lets ordinary-looking punches carry catastrophic impact without making her move like an impossibly heavy object.

Virtual Mass:
The added mass increases offensive force and can also weigh down objects or opponents in direct contact with Yuki or Garuda. However, it does not proportionally increase the tensile strength or durability of Yuki's body, so greater striking power does not automatically make her equally resistant to incoming damage.

Garuda:
Garuda is the only external target directly affected by Star Rage. When loaded with virtual mass, it can be kicked like a projectile, swung like a heavy flexible weapon, wrapped around an enemy to pin them, or fight independently alongside Yuki.

Extreme Mass:
At sufficiently extreme values, the virtual mass begins affecting Yuki herself in ways it normally does not. Pushing the technique beyond that threshold can collapse her into a black hole with genuine gravitational effects, making this a suicidal catastrophic escalation rather than a normal attack.

Limits and Counters:
Injuries and reduced output can lower how effectively Yuki applies Star Rage. The technique improves force, not every defensive property of her body, and its black-hole limit is indiscriminate enough to endanger the user and everything nearby.

Technical Notes:
Yuki is capable of Domain Expansion, but its canonical name, appearance, and sure-hit effect were never revealed.

cardPool.title: Cursed Speech
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Cursed Speech

Classification:
Inherited Cursed Technique of the Inumaki Clan.

Known User(s):
Toge Inumaki.

Core Mechanic:
Cursed Speech reinforces spoken language with Cursed Energy so the meaning of the user's words becomes a compulsory effect on whoever hears them. Commands can restrain, move, injure, or otherwise force a target according to the wording used. The inherited Snake Eyes and Fangs markings around the mouth and tongue are associated with the technique.

Command Strength:
Short, direct commands such as 'Stop,' 'Sleep,' or 'Don't move' are comparatively efficient. More violent instructions place greater strain on the user, especially when the target is substantially stronger. The technique can affect living targets and inanimate objects when the command meaning can apply.

Electronic Transmission:
Cursed Speech remains effective through telephones, speakers, megaphones, and recorded audio. A stored command can be triggered later when the recording is played, although the original user still suffers the technique's backlash. Multiple recordings cannot simply be stacked into simultaneous commands without limit.

Defense:
A prepared sorcerer can defend by reinforcing the ears and brain with Cursed Energy so the cursed command is not properly registered. Merely hearing the ordinary sound is not the whole attack; the Cursed Energy carried by the speech is what enforces the command.

Limits and Counters:
Backlash scales with command severity, target strength, and the difference between user and target. Overuse can cause severe throat pain, coughing blood, or temporary loss of speech. Because ordinary conversation could unintentionally carry dangerous commands, Toge restricts his normal vocabulary to harmless rice-ball ingredients.

Technical Notes:
Using recorded or amplified speech changes delivery range, not the underlying recoil rules.

cardPool.title: Straw Doll Technique
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Straw Doll Technique

Classification:
Innate Cursed Technique inherited through Nobara Kugisaki's family line.

Known User(s):
Nobara Kugisaki; her grandmother.

Core Mechanic:
Straw Doll Technique channels Cursed Energy through a hammer, nails, and a straw effigy. The nails can be imbued with Cursed Energy, launched as projectiles, suspended for setup, or left embedded in targets and terrain. Its most dangerous feature is sympathetic linkage: material connected to a target can become a proxy for attacking them from elsewhere.

Resonance:
Resonance establishes a connection through a meaningful piece of the target, such as blood or a severed body part, and uses the straw doll as an effigy. Driving a nail into the linked doll transmits cursed damage to the target. Once a valid connection exists, physical distance is not the main limitation; the quality and value of the link determine effectiveness.

Hairpin:
Hairpin releases the Cursed Energy stored in previously placed nails by forcing their output past its normal limit. The energy expands explosively from the nails, turning harmless-looking placements into delayed detonations and allowing Nobara to prepare traps in the environment.

Nail Manipulation:
Nobara can reinforce nails and manipulate their positioning before impact, using them directly, placing them to restrict movement, or embedding them in surfaces before Hairpin.

Limits and Counters:
The technique relies heavily on physical tools and accurate placement. Resonance needs a meaningful connection to the intended target; not every object associated with someone provides an equally useful link. Direct nail attacks can be dodged or intercepted, and damage output still depends on the user's Cursed Energy and the target's resistance.

Technical Notes:
Resonance and Hairpin are extension techniques of Straw Doll Technique rather than separate Innate Techniques.

cardPool.title: Ten Shadows Technique
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Ten Shadows Technique

Classification:
Inherited Cursed Technique of the Zenin Clan.

Known User(s):
Megumi Fushiguro.

Core Mechanic:
The user's shadow acts as an intermediary for summoning ten shikigami and as a storage medium. A Ten Shadows inheritor begins with the paired Divine Dogs. Additional shikigami must be defeated in an exorcism ritual before normal control; outside help invalidates the taming result.

Shikigami:
The ten established types are Divine Dogs, Nue, Great Serpent, Toad, Max Elephant, Rabbit Escape, Round Deer, Piercing Ox, Tiger Funeral, and Eight-Handled Sword Divergent Sila Divine General Mahoraga. Each has its own Cursed Energy cost and combat role.

Destruction and Inheritance:
A shikigami that is completely destroyed normally cannot return in the same form. Its power can be inherited by another compatible shikigami, producing forms such as Divine Dog: Totality. Temporary combination summons such as The Well's Unknown Abyss follow different rules and can be destroyed without permanently losing their parent shikigami.

Shadow Manipulation:
The user can store physical objects in shadows, hide their own body within shadow, emerge from unexpected angles, and use shadows as battlefield routes. Stored objects retain real weight, which the user must bear.

Mahoraga:
Mahoraga is the most dangerous known shikigami in the technique and must be tamed through the same ritual principle before it can be commanded safely. Its adaptation ability makes an untamed invocation a desperate measure rather than an ordinary summon.

Limits and Counters:
Shikigami require Cursed Energy to maintain, and stronger summons cost more. Permanent destruction changes the user's future arsenal. Taming rituals cannot be bypassed by simply summoning an untamed shikigami beside allies, and the shadow-storage function does not negate the physical burden of stored mass.

Domain Expansion:
Chimera Shadow Garden is documented separately.

cardPool.title: Six Eyes
cardPool.value:
Name:
Six Eyes

Known User(s):
Satoru Gojo

Classification:
Inherited jujutsu trait of the Gojo Clan; not a Cursed Technique.

Mechanics:
The Six Eyes grant extraordinary visual perception of Cursed Energy and extremely precise control over how energy is processed and spent. Satoru can read the flow and properties of Cursed Energy at a level far beyond ordinary sorcerers, distinguish fine technique information, and regulate his own energy with almost no waste. The trait does not create Limitless, but the efficiency and precision it provides are what make the inherited spatial technique practical at its highest level.

Appearance and Sensory Load:
The eyes are an intense luminous blue with unusually detailed irises. Gojo normally covers them with a black blindfold or dark glasses because the amount of information processed through the Six Eyes is burdensome even for him. Covering them does not shut the trait off; it reduces unnecessary visual input while he continues to perceive Cursed Energy.

Relationship to Limitless:
Possessing Limitless and possessing the Six Eyes are separate inherited conditions. Their simultaneous appearance in one Gojo Clan member is extremely rare. Together they allow continuous Infinity, precise Blue and Red, Hollow Purple, advanced barrier work, and exceptionally efficient Reverse Cursed Technique use without normal levels of energy waste.

Practical Consequence:
The Six Eyes reduce waste so drastically that Gojo can sustain extremely demanding applications of Limitless with efficiency other sorcerers cannot reproduce. The trait also produces continuous sensory burden, explaining the routine use of a blindfold or dark glasses. Its value is therefore not a separate attack but the precision, perception, and energy economy it gives to every part of Gojo's jujutsu.

cardPool.title: Limitless
cardPool.value:
Technique Name:
Limitless

Classification:
Inherited Cursed Technique of the Gojo Clan.

Known User(s):
Satoru Gojo.

Core Mechanic:
Limitless brings the concept of infinity into reality and manipulates space through extremely precise Cursed Energy control. Its neutral state alters the distance an approaching object must cross rather than creating a conventional wall. Satoru's Six Eyes provide the perception and efficiency needed for continuous high-level use.

Neutral Limitless — Infinity:
Infinity repeatedly divides the remaining distance between Gojo and an approaching target, making the target slow as it nears him and preventing contact. After training, Gojo can maintain it automatically and filter threats instead of consciously stopping everything around him.

Cursed Technique Lapse — Blue:
Blue amplifies Limitless with Cursed Energy and forces space to converge toward an impossible point. The attraction can drag targets inward, crush them, damage structures, or accelerate Gojo's movement.

Cursed Technique Reversal — Red:
Red feeds positive energy from Reverse Cursed Technique into Limitless, reversing Blue's convergence into violent divergence. It produces concentrated repulsion with greater output and higher technical difficulty than Blue.

Hollow Technique — Purple:
Purple collides Blue's attraction with Red's repulsion into a high-output destructive spatial phenomenon. It devastates whatever lies along its path through overwhelming spatial force; it is not a generic automatic 'existence erasure' effect.

Limits and Counters:
Limitless is very difficult to control efficiently without the Six Eyes. Infinity can be bypassed by valid jujutsu that neutralizes or overrides the technique, including Domain Amplification, technique-nullifying cursed tools, and a Domain sure-hit. Blue, Red, and Purple require different levels of control and output; inheriting Limitless does not grant automatic mastery.

Domain Expansion:
Unlimited Void is documented separately.

cardPool.title: Kenjaku
cardPool.value:
[ KENJAKU

Name:
Kenjaku

Affiliation:
Former ally of the Disaster Curses

Grade / Classification:
Ancient Sorcerer / Body-Hopping Curse User

Jujutsu:
Kenjaku's innate technique lets him transplant his brain into another corpse, taking control of the body and inheriting its physical traits and Cursed Technique. The process leaves a stitched scar across the host's forehead.

Through Kaori Itadori's body, Kenjaku gained Antigravity System, which negates gravity around the user. Its Cursed Technique Reversal increases gravity instead.

Kenjaku is also an exceptional barrier user and possesses Domain Expansion: Womb Profusion, an open-barrier domain that manifests a grotesque pillar of fused bodies and delivers a devastating sure-hit attack.

Personality:
Kenjaku is patient, curious, manipulative, and disturbingly detached. After living for over a thousand years, he treats people, curses, and bloodlines as experimental material.

He favors long-term planning and exploiting other people's goals over simple domination. Highly intelligent and adaptable, he can remain conversational and amused even in dangerous situations.

Appearance:
Kenjaku's original appearance is unknown. His only consistent physical trait is the stitched seam circling the forehead of whichever body he inhabits.

His final host was Kaori Itadori, a youthful woman with side-swept black hair and a slender build. The forehead stitches were the main visible sign that her body was being controlled.

Combat Style:
Kenjaku combines advanced barriers, precise CE control, close combat, gravity manipulation, and centuries of jujutsu knowledge.

Relationships and Background:
Kenjaku secretly inhabited numerous bodies throughout history. His true identity was unknown to modern Jujutsu Society. While inhabiting Kaori, he cooperated with Jogo, Hanami, Dagon, and Mahito before being killed by Kuro Nao. ]

cardPool.title: Yuki Tsukumo
cardPool.value:
[ YUKI TSUKUMO

Name:
Yuki Tsukumo

Affiliation:
Independent Sorcerer

Grade / Classification:
Special Grade Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Yuki's Innate Technique, Star Rage, adds virtual mass to herself and her shikigami Garuda without normally increasing physical weight. This massively amplifies the force of their attacks.

Garuda is directly linked to Star Rage. Yuki can use it as a weapon, kick it as a projectile, or increase its mass for crushing attacks. At extreme output, Star Rage can push her mass far beyond normal limits.

Personality:
Yuki is bold, confident, unconventional, and fiercely independent. She dislikes jujutsu society's conservative structure and openly rejects missions she considers pointless.

She is relaxed and playful, famously asking people what type of woman they like, but is highly intelligent and serious about her ideals. Yuki wants to eliminate curses at their source rather than endlessly exorcising them, researching ways to free humanity from Cursed Energy. She is blunt, curious, and willing to challenge powerful institutions.

Appearance:
Yuki is a tall, athletic woman with long blonde hair, brown eyes, and a confident posture. Her hair falls past her shoulders with loose bangs framing her face.

She usually wears a sleeveless dark top, light-colored pants, and boots. Garuda often accompanies her as a long, segmented flying shikigami.

Combat Style:
Yuki is an exceptional close-range fighter who combines physical skill with Star Rage for devastating strikes. Garuda provides ranged pressure, restraint, and coordinated attacks.

Relationships and Background:
Yuki is one of only four Special Grade sorcerers and the mentor who discovered and trained Aoi Todo. She was also a former Star Plasma Vessel and has researched Heavenly Restriction and Tengen. ]

cardPool.title: Takuma Ino
cardPool.value:
[ TAKUMA INO

Name:
Takuma Ino

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High

Grade / Classification:
Grade 2 Sorcerer

Jujutsu:
Ino's Innate Technique, Auspicious Beasts Summon, turns him into a spiritual medium when he covers his face with a mask. He channels the abilities of four auspicious beasts through his body.

Kaichi creates a horn-like projectile that homes in on its target. Reiki coats Ino in water, improving defense and mobility. Kirin suppresses his sense of pain at the cost of severe fatigue afterward. Ryu is his strongest beast, though its full ability is unknown.

Personality:
Ino is earnest, upbeat, confident, and straightforward. He wants to prove himself as a sorcerer but is not arrogant, and he takes pride in doing things properly.

He deeply respects Kento Nanami and treats his opinion as the standard that matters most. Ino is willing to take dangerous assignments, but he still thinks carefully about responsibility and looks to experienced sorcerers for guidance. He is friendly, easygoing, and emotionally sincere.

Appearance:
Ino is a young man with short brown hair, dark eyes, and a lean athletic build. He usually wears a dark knit cap, loose casual clothing, and a black mask that can be pulled over his face to activate his technique.

Combat Style:
Ino is a capable close-range fighter who mixes hand-to-hand combat with the different effects of his auspicious beasts. His technique gives him options for pursuit, mobility, defense, and sustained fighting.

Relationships and Background:
Ino is strongly influenced by Nanami and considers him a mentor and role model. Although capable of advancing beyond Grade 2, he wants Nanami's approval before pursuing promotion. ]

cardPool.title: Kiyotaka Ijichi
cardPool.value:
[ KIYOTAKA IJICHI

Name:
Kiyotaka Ijichi

Affiliation:
Tokyo Jujutsu High — Assistant Manager

Grade / Classification:
Jujutsu Support Staff

Jujutsu:
Ijichi is not a frontline sorcerer, but he can use barrier techniques and basic Cursed Energy.

His main jujutsu skill is Curtain, a concealment barrier used to isolate mission areas from civilians. Depending on the conditions applied, Curtains can obscure an area, restrict entry or exit, interfere with communications, and alert the caster if breached.

Personality:
Ijichi is responsible, anxious, polite, and extremely hardworking. He is often nervous around powerful sorcerers, especially Gojo, but remains dependable under pressure and takes his duties seriously.

He tends to worry about students placed in dangerous situations and carries guilt when missions go badly. Despite lacking confidence as a combatant, Ijichi is brave enough to keep supporting sorcerers in lethal situations and is highly respected by other assistant managers for his reliability.

Appearance:
Ijichi is a slim twenty-seven-year-old man with short black hair neatly parted to one side, rectangular glasses, and a tired, serious expression.

He usually wears a dark business suit, white shirt, tie, and dress shoes, giving him the appearance of an overworked office worker rather than someone involved in jujutsu.

Combat Style:
Ijichi avoids direct combat whenever possible. His role centers on barriers, transportation, mission logistics, communication, evacuation, and administrative support.

Relationships and Background:
Ijichi originally intended to become a jujutsu sorcerer but recognized that combat was not his strength and became an assistant manager instead. He handles much of Tokyo Jujutsu High's paperwork, finances, transportation, mission coordination, and outside administration. ]

cardPool.title: Satozakura High School
cardPool.value:
Name: Satozakura High School

Classification: Ordinary civilian high school.

Location: Kawasaki City, Kanagawa Prefecture.

Appearance and Layout: The school consists of two connected main buildings with standard classrooms, corridors, stairwells, faculty areas, a cafeteria, an outdoor courtyard, and a large gymnasium. Its design is conventional enough that nothing about the campus suggests any connection to jujutsu. Students attend classes, socialize, join clubs, and move through the grounds under normal civilian expectations.

Known Students and Staff: Junpei Yoshino attended Satozakura alongside classmates who repeatedly bullied and isolated him. Teacher Sotomura also worked at the school. The ordinary social environment around Junpei is important because the school's problems are human long before supernatural violence reaches the campus.

Jujutsu Relevance: Once a curse user or cursed spirit becomes involved, the familiar school layout becomes dangerous very quickly. Hallways and classrooms provide numerous blind corners, while a gymnasium can hold many students at once. Non-sorcerers cannot see the cursed energy or shikigami involved and may interpret injuries as unexplained violence or an unknown ability.

Incident Potential: The school can become the endpoint of manipulation directed at a vulnerable student. A newly awakened technique used here can appear completely invisible to classmates, while transfigured humans remain physically visible and create confusion because they resemble grotesquely altered people rather than unseen curses.

Security: Satozakura has ordinary school security, not jujutsu protection. There are no permanent barriers, trained sorcerers, or cursed-tool stores on campus. Any supernatural containment must be established by responding personnel.

cardPool.title: Yasohachi Bridge
cardPool.value:
Name: Yasohachi Bridge

Classification: Public road bridge and recurrent curse hotspot.

Location: Koinokuchi Canyon, spanning a deep wooded ravine with a small river below.

Appearance: Yasohachi is a large stone bridge carrying vehicle traffic between forested mountain roads. A railed pedestrian walkway runs along the bridge, while the land below is densely covered in trees and uneven ground. The drop into the canyon is substantial enough that reckless students once used the location for bungee-jumping tests of courage.

Reputation: The bridge is associated with suicides, disappearances, and paranormal rumors. Local stories describe students being found unconscious beneath it with no memory of how they arrived there. Such incidents make the site a recurring point of interest for jujutsu personnel even when no obvious curse is visible during an initial inspection.

Jujutsu Conditions: The dangerous area is not limited to the roadway itself. Curse activity can be concealed beneath the bridge, within the forest, or behind a barrier whose entrance only becomes accessible under particular conditions. Investigators may need to enter the ravine at night and cross the stream below before the supernatural space reveals itself.

Operational Use: Tokyo Jujutsu High periodically checks the location because of its history. A routine inspection can involve searching for residuals, interviewing people linked to old bridge incidents, comparing patterns among later deaths, and testing whether an unseen barrier has formed beneath the public landmark.

Tactical Considerations: The bridge offers long sightlines above but poor visibility below. Steep terrain, trees, darkness, water, and hidden barrier boundaries can separate teams. Civilians on the roadway may remain completely unaware of an active curse beneath them.

cardPool.title: Shibuya Station
cardPool.value:
Name: Shibuya Station

Classification: Major metropolitan railway and subway complex.

Location: Shibuya, Tokyo, centered within one of Japan's busiest commercial districts.

Appearance and Layout: Shibuya Station is not a single simple building. It is a dense multilevel network of rail platforms, underground passages, ticket gates, escalators, exits, concourses, service corridors, and connections to surrounding commercial structures. Nearby complexes include Shibuya Hikarie, Tokyu facilities, Shibuya Mark City, major roads, and heavily trafficked pedestrian zones. The underground system links several train and subway lines at different depths.

Population: During normal operating hours the station and surrounding streets can contain enormous numbers of civilians. Crowds, narrow corridors, transit delays, and limited sightlines make evacuation difficult even without supernatural interference.

Jujutsu Relevance: The station's density and layered underground geography make it exceptionally dangerous during curse activity. A hostile barrier can divide surface teams from underground targets, trap civilians, disrupt communications, and turn ordinary transit infrastructure into a maze. Deep platforms can isolate battles from anyone above while still leaving thousands of non-sorcerers at risk.

Notable Areas: Surface entrances such as Exit 13, the Fukutoshin Line platforms, deep basement levels connected to Hikarie, long concourses, stairwells, restrooms, service routes, and adjoining commercial passages.

Tactical Considerations: Sorcerers must account for civilian crowds, multiple vertical levels, blocked exits, trains, structural damage, and Curtains with specialized entry conditions. Large techniques risk catastrophic collateral damage. Non-sorcerers caught inside a barrier are usually unable to understand the true source of danger.

cardPool.title: Zenin Clan Household
cardPool.value:
Name: Zenin Clan Household

Classification: Ancestral estate and operational center of the Zenin sorcerer clan.

Location: Japan; maintained as a private clan compound rather than a public institution.

Appearance and Layout: The property is a large traditional estate composed of wooden residences, covered walkways, courtyards, gardens, training spaces, storage buildings, and restricted clan facilities. Stone paths and small bridges cross landscaped areas, including a pond within the grounds. The architecture reflects the clan's wealth, age, and rigid internal hierarchy rather than modern hero-society design.

Function: The household serves simultaneously as family residence, political center, training ground, armory, and headquarters for the clan's combat forces. Senior members conduct succession discussions and clan business here, while younger relatives are evaluated according to inherited techniques, cursed energy, and usefulness to the family.

Combat Forces: The estate houses or supports the Kukuru Unit, composed largely of male clan members without notable innate techniques who undergo martial training, and the Hei, the clan's elite sorcerer unit. These forces allow the family to respond to threats internally without relying on the jujutsu schools.

Restricted Areas: The clan maintains a cursed-tool warehouse containing valuable weapons accumulated over generations. There are also secure internal chambers used for punishment, confinement, or training. Access is controlled through clan authority rather than ordinary law.

Culture: The estate embodies the Zenin family's obsession with inherited power. Members lacking prestigious techniques can be treated as failures regardless of skill, while politically valuable heirs receive disproportionate status. Women and relatives judged weak face especially harsh treatment.

cardPool.title: Tombs of the Star Corridor
cardPool.value:
Name: Tombs of the Star Corridor

Classification: Restricted barrier complex and residence of Master Tengen.

Location: Deep beneath Tokyo Jujutsu High, separated from the ordinary campus by multiple layers of concealment and access control.

Approach: Reaching the corridor requires passing Tengen's barriers and identifying the correct entrance among more than a thousand doors that continually change position. The true entrance opens above a vast drop into an enclosed forest-like space filled with old trees, earth, and grass despite being hidden within the school complex. A cursed warehouse lies along this route.

Layout: Deeper inside, an elevator descends toward the main corridor. The central area contains old structures arranged around an enormous tree, with a direct path leading toward Tengen's inner residence. Another barrier guards the final approach. Anyone not accepted or invited can be redirected into an empty white space rather than reaching Tengen.

Function: The Tombs serve as the innermost sanctuary of Tengen, whose barrier techniques support much of Japan's jujutsu infrastructure. Because of that role, the area is among the most strategically sensitive places in the country. It can also become a meeting point for sorcerers seeking Tengen's knowledge or assistance.

Security: Ordinary navigation is useless without jujutsu knowledge. Concealing barriers, shifting doors, invitation-based access, and layered spatial defenses make forced entry extraordinarily difficult. Even sorcerers familiar with Tokyo Jujutsu High may be unable to reach the true interior without guidance.

Historical Significance: The site was the destination of the Star Plasma Vessel escort mission involving Riko Amanai. Years later, the route and warehouse remained important because sealed cursed objects and Tengen's presence made the area central to several high-level conflicts.

cardPool.title: Time Vessel Association
cardPool.value:
Name:
Time Vessel Association

Type:
Religious front / anti-merger faction

Overview:
An organization connected to worship of Tengen and opposition to Star Plasma Vessel assimilation.

Structure / Role:
Uses ordinary money, hired intermediaries, and underworld contacts rather than open jujutsu authority.

Practical Note:
Time Vessel Association must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Function:
The Time Vessel Association is the broader organization surrounding the Star Religious Group's belief system and operations. Its central concern is preserving an idealized image of Tengen by preventing the Star Plasma Vessel merger. The association can mobilize money, intermediaries, informants, and hired killers without needing its rank-and-file members to understand Cursed Energy. That combination makes it dangerous despite being rooted largely in non-sorcerer religious fanaticism.

Secrecy:
The association can hide behind legitimate religious and financial activity because its public members do not need to understand the supernatural details of the merger. Only a limited circle needs enough information to direct funds and targets. This compartmentalization protects the organization from ordinary investigation and allows fanatical civilians to influence jujutsu affairs without becoming sorcerers themselves.

The organization's effectiveness depends on keeping ideology, money, and operational violence connected while revealing as little supernatural information as possible.

cardPool.title: Star Religious Group
cardPool.value:
Name:
Star Religious Group

Type:
Religious organization

Overview:
A cult-like religious organization historically obsessed with maintaining Tengen's perceived purity and opposing merger with a Star Plasma Vessel.

Structure / Role:
Members are non-sorcerers with distorted awareness of jujutsu-adjacent religious concepts rather than full access to Cursed Energy knowledge.

Relations:
An example of the rare fringe groups that suspect supernatural truths without understanding Jujutsu Society.

Public Face:
The Star Religious Group presents itself as a religious organization devoted to Master Tengen while hiding the violent implications of its doctrine. Its followers consider Tengen's purity sacred and oppose merger with a Star Plasma Vessel. Because many members are ordinary non-sorcerers, the group relies on money, influence, bounty networks, and hired specialists rather than direct jujutsu strength. Its public legitimacy gives it access that an openly supernatural cult would not possess.

Limitations:
Most believers cannot perceive curses and do not possess jujutsu, so their danger comes from organization rather than supernatural strength. Money can place bounties, hire killers, purchase information, and move people through ordinary society. Their religious certainty also makes negotiation difficult because preserving Tengen's perceived purity is treated as a sacred obligation rather than a practical political goal.

Its mundane resources make it dangerous precisely because believers can act through normal institutions without ever learning to manipulate Cursed Energy. Public respectability is part of its protection.

cardPool.title: Geto's Family
cardPool.value:
Name:
Geto's Family

Type:
Curse-user group

Overview:
A group of curse users gathered around Suguru Geto during his campaign against non-sorcerers.

Structure / Role:
Included adopted followers, foreign allies, and curse users who shared personal loyalty even when their exact ideology differed.

Relations:
Fragments may remain useful as independent NPCs in free play.

Practical Note:
Geto's Family must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Composition:
Geto's followers are curse users and rescued outsiders bound more by personal loyalty than by formal grade or school structure. Many regard Geto as the person who gave them belonging after rejection by ordinary society. The group can conduct coordinated attacks and manage front organizations, but its cohesion depends heavily on Geto himself. After his death, members do not all follow the same path, revealing that the 'family' was relational rather than institutional.

Operations:
The group can use religious fronts, money collected from followers, curses under Geto's control, and individual curse-user techniques to support coordinated plans. Members are not graded through a school hierarchy and do not share one standardized combat doctrine. Loyalty to Geto is the unifying force, so emotional bonds matter more than formal rank.

Without that personal center, shared history does not automatically guarantee that every surviving member will pursue the same objective.

cardPool.title: Zenin Clan
cardPool.value:
Name:
Zenin Clan

Type:
Major sorcerer family

Overview:
One of the Three Great Families, known for valuing inherited techniques, combat strength, and traditional hierarchy.

Structure / Role:
Associated with techniques such as Ten Shadows and Projection Sorcery, with numerous elite clan sorcerers and cursed tools.

Relations:
Maki, Mai, Megumi, Toji, Naobito, and Naoya are closely tied to its history.

Practical Note:
Zenin Clan must still be understood through established jujutsu conditions, Cursed Energy control, physical consequences, and the limits of the user or object involved. No ordinary Quirk-analysis method reveals the underlying supernatural mechanism.

Culture:
The Zenin family places extreme value on inherited techniques, combat usefulness, and traditional status. Members without prized abilities can be marginalized regardless of personal talent, while powerful inherited techniques influence succession and internal standing. The clan maintains armed sorcerer units and a large household structure. Its treatment of Maki, Mai, and Toji demonstrates how severely the family can punish people who fall outside its preferred model of jujutsu value.

Internal Power:
The household distinguishes between prized inherited techniques, ordinary sorcerers, and relatives considered failures. Combat units and family branches reflect that hierarchy. This obsession with bloodline creates strong fighters but also deep resentment, cruelty, and instability. A member's value can be judged more by technique inheritance than by actual judgment or character.

The clan's internal hierarchy therefore creates as much conflict inside the family as prestige outside it.

cardPool.title: Jujutsu Society
cardPool.value:
Name:
Jujutsu Society

Type:
Secret supernatural institution

Overview:
The hidden network of sorcerers, schools, clans, administrators, and support personnel responsible for controlling curses and managing jujutsu activity.

Structure / Role:
Operates through Jujutsu Headquarters, Tokyo and Kyoto schools, field sorcerers, assistant managers, clan influence, and barrier infrastructure. It is hierarchical, conservative, and willing to bend ordinary law to preserve secrecy.

Relations:
Fully aware Quirks exist, but hero society is unaware of Jujutsu Society.

Structure:
Jujutsu society is a loose hidden system of schools, clans, professional sorcerers, assistant managers, medical staff, and conservative administrators rather than one transparent public agency. Authority is fragmented between Headquarters, clan influence, school leadership, and powerful individuals. Missions are assigned according to curse reports and grade, while secrecy is maintained through the same network that handles transport, barriers, records, and aftermath.

Scale:
The population is extremely small, so the same people often occupy multiple roles as fighters, teachers, medics, managers, clan representatives, or administrators. This makes personal relationships unusually influential. A dispute between a powerful sorcerer and conservative leadership can affect assignments and policy far more directly than it would in a large public bureaucracy.

Its small size also means a single death, defection, or exceptional new sorcerer can noticeably change the balance of available manpower. Personal reputation can therefore influence policy unusually quickly.

cardPool.title: Domain Amplification
cardPool.value:
Domain Amplification coats the user in a thin, empty Domain-like barrier that can neutralize or bypass an opposing Cursed Technique on contact by allowing that technique to flow into the empty space.

Because the user generally cannot freely use their own Innate Technique at the same time, it is a highly specialized combat choice.

It targets jujutsu mechanics, not Quirk Factors. It does not simply switch off a Quirk, though the user can still physically defend against Quirk attacks while using it.

Detailed Mechanics:
Domain Amplification wraps the user's body in a thin domain that is deliberately left without the user's own innate technique. The empty space can accept an opposing technique and neutralize it on contact, allowing attacks to bypass defenses such as Infinity. The tradeoff is that the user generally cannot use their innate technique at the same time because the amplification must remain empty to receive the opposing technique.

Tradeoff:
The user coats the body in a thin, empty domain that can accept and neutralize an opposing technique on contact. Leaving the domain empty is what gives the technique somewhere to flow, so the user normally cannot run their own Innate Technique simultaneously. This makes Domain Amplification particularly useful for closing distance against technique-based defenses, but it forces the user to rely on reinforcement, physical attacks, and timing while the amplification is active.

Combat Use:
The technique is most useful when the enemy's defensive technique would normally prevent physical contact. By neutralizing that technique at the point of contact, the user can turn reinforcement and hand-to-hand skill back into viable weapons. The cost is tactical simplicity: while amplification is active, the user gives up simultaneous use of their own Innate Technique and must rely on movement, durability, and close-range combat.

cardPool.title: Simple Domain
cardPool.value:
Simple Domain is an anti-Domain barrier technique designed to protect the user from a Domain Expansion's sure-hit effect within a limited area.

It does not automatically erase an opponent's entire Innate Technique. Its key defensive purpose is to interfere with the Domain's guaranteed-hit function.

Different schools and users apply Simple Domain through distinct stances, sword styles, or learned forms.

Detailed Mechanics:
Simple Domain is an anti-domain barrier technique often associated with New Shadow Style. It creates a small domain around the user and can neutralize or interfere with an enemy domain's sure-hit effect within that space. It does not automatically overpower the enemy's full Domain Expansion, and maintaining the stance, barrier, or programmed conditions may be necessary depending on the version being used.

Purpose:
Simple Domain creates a small anti-domain space around the user and interferes with the sure-hit function of an opposing Domain Expansion. It does not erase the enemy's barrier or automatically defeat the technique, and the user may still be attacked physically inside the domain. Different schools and users apply it with different stances or programmed responses. Its value is buying survival and creating an opening, especially for sorcerers who cannot answer a full Domain with one of their own.

Limit:
Simple Domain is defensive jujutsu, not a miniature equivalent of every full Domain Expansion. It mainly protects against or interferes with the sure-hit function in the area around the user. The enemy's physical attacks, terrain, and other hazards remain dangerous, and a stronger or more refined domain can still pressure the Simple Domain until it collapses.

cardPool.title: Cursed Energy Residuals
cardPool.value:
Jujutsu use leaves residual traces that trained sorcerers can investigate. Residuals can reveal that a technique or curse was present even after the immediate phenomenon ends.

Ordinary people, Quirk users, and Quirk-analysis technology cannot perceive these residuals. Only jujutsu-capable senses, techniques, or tools can reliably follow them.

Sorcerers often use residuals for tracking, crime-scene reconstruction, and determining whether an incident involved a curse or curse user.

Tracking:
Use of Cursed Energy can leave traces that trained sorcerers recognize after an event. Residuals can indicate that jujutsu occurred, help reconstruct movement, or assist in following a curse or sorcerer. They are not guaranteed perfect fingerprints: time, distance, deliberate concealment, environmental interference, and overlapping energy can complicate interpretation. Ordinary scientific instruments and Quirk sensors do not read these traces as Cursed Energy.

Forensics:
Residual analysis is useful after a hidden fight because it gives sorcerers evidence ordinary investigators cannot access. A trail may reveal direction of travel, repeated technique use, or whether a known energy signature passed through an area. Skilled concealment can reduce those traces, and a crowded curse scene can produce overlapping contamination, so residuals are clues rather than an infallible tracking system.

Detection:
Residuals are meaningful only to people or methods capable of reading Cursed Energy. Ordinary cameras, Quirk scanners, forensic laboratories, and medical instruments can document physical aftermath but do not identify the residual itself. A sorcerer examining the same location therefore has access to a layer of evidence unavailable to conventional investigators.

cardPool.title: Shikigami
cardPool.value:
Shikigami are familiars manifested or controlled through jujutsu. They are typically formed from Cursed Energy and remain invisible to ordinary non-sorcerers under normal perception rules.

They can interact physically with the world and harm non-sorcerers even when those people cannot see them. A Quirk does not automatically reveal or control a shikigami.

Different techniques impose different summoning rules. The Ten Shadows Technique is a famous inherited example, but shikigami can also appear in other forms of jujutsu.

Function:
Shikigami are familiars manifested and controlled through jujutsu. Their form, intelligence, abilities, summoning medium, destruction rules, and independence depend on the parent technique. Some are simple support creatures; others are major combatants. They are not cursed spirits and do not possess Quirk Factors. Destroying one may dismiss it temporarily or permanently depending on the technique that created it, so there is no universal respawn rule.

Control:
A shikigami is normally bound to the technique or summoning method that produces it. The summoner may need a hand sign, talisman, shadow, medium, ritual, or other condition depending on the technique. Distance, destruction, and re-summoning rules are likewise technique-specific. Treating all shikigami as interchangeable summons would erase the very conditions that define how each one works.

Visibility:
Most shikigami are not directly visible to ordinary non-sorcerers because the summoned body is a jujutsu manifestation rather than an ordinary animal. The summoner can still use them to move objects, strike people, or create environmental effects that outsiders notice. Their invisibility therefore does not prevent them from producing physical consequences.

cardPool.title: Cursed Objects
cardPool.value:
Definition:
Cursed objects are items containing concentrated curses, sealed remnants, or incarnated sorcerer material. Many are dangerous even when dormant.

Vessels:
A Quirk user can become a vessel under normal jujutsu rules. Possession does not automatically remove their Quirk; the Quirk remains unless the host's body or soul is altered deeply enough to disrupt the Quirk Factor.

Secrecy:
Cursed objects are hidden from ordinary society. A few fringe occult or religious groups may possess distorted rumors, but reliable knowledge remains within jujutsu circles.

Nature:
Cursed objects contain persistent Cursed Energy or a sealed supernatural presence. Their danger is not measured by how threatening the physical container looks. Seals and storage can suppress influence without turning the object into ordinary matter, and some high-grade objects resist destruction entirely. Ingestion or compatibility can create vessels, incarnation, poisoning, possession, or other effects depending on the object rather than following a single universal rule.

Containment:
Seals reduce risk but do not necessarily erase the object's Cursed Energy. A sealed item can remain dangerous for decades or centuries, and weakening protection may attract curses or allow influence to leak outward. The correct response depends on the specific object: some can be destroyed, some must be stored, and some can only be neutralized through a vessel or specialized jujutsu.

Containment procedures must be chosen for the individual object's behavior rather than assuming every sealed relic responds to the same treatment.

cardPool.title: Black Flash
cardPool.value:
Definition:
Black Flash occurs when Cursed Energy impacts within an extraordinarily tiny interval of a physical strike, distorting space and massively amplifying the blow.

Nature:
It is not a conventional Innate Technique and cannot be activated reliably on command. Experiencing Black Flash can place a sorcerer into an unusually heightened understanding of Cursed Energy.

Interaction:
A Quirk user cannot perform Black Flash merely through physical speed. The attacker must be capable of manipulating Cursed Energy.

Detailed Mechanics:
Black Flash occurs when Cursed Energy is applied within one millionth of a second of a physical strike, producing a spatial distortion and an explosive increase in effective impact. It cannot be performed on command with certainty, even by elite sorcerers. Experiencing it can place a fighter into a heightened state of Cursed Energy understanding and control, which is why repeated Black Flashes often signal exceptional combat rhythm rather than a separate technique.

Effect:
The phenomenon occurs when Cursed Energy follows a physical hit within an extraordinarily narrow timing window, distorting space around the impact and amplifying the strike. It is not an Innate Technique and cannot be guaranteed on command. A sorcerer who experiences Black Flash often enters a state of heightened concentration in which Cursed Energy feels more intuitive, improving subsequent control even though another Black Flash is never certain.

Combat Meaning:
Landing Black Flash does not permanently multiply all of a sorcerer's attacks. The exceptional impact belongs to that specific strike, while the lasting benefit is the user's improved sense for Cursed Energy after experiencing the phenomenon. Repeated Black Flashes can occur during an intense flow state, but even someone who has landed several cannot simply choose the exact next punch that will trigger another.

cardPool.title: Heavenly Restriction
cardPool.value:
Definition:
A Heavenly Restriction is a condition imposed at birth that exchanges one aspect of a person's natural constitution for extraordinary capability.

Zero-Energy Physical Restriction:
Individuals following the Toji/Maki model can possess essentially zero Cursed Energy in exchange for extreme physical ability and sharpened senses.

Interaction Rule:
A Heavenly Restriction user is also born with zero Quirk Factor. Their physical gifts are not a Quirk and cannot be erased, stolen, copied, or detected as one.

Other Restrictions:
Heavenly Restrictions may take other forms according to ordinary jujutsu rules, such as severe bodily limitation exchanged for extraordinary Cursed Energy range or output.

Detailed Mechanics:
A Heavenly Restriction is imposed at birth rather than voluntarily negotiated. It exchanges one aspect of a person's constitution for another. The most extreme physically gifted state removes Cursed Energy entirely and grants extraordinary strength, speed, durability, senses, and freedom from many barriers that identify targets through Cursed Energy. , such individuals are also born with zero Quirk Factor.

Forms:
Heavenly Restriction is not one standardized ability. It is an involuntary condition imposed from birth that sacrifices one aspect of a person for an extreme advantage elsewhere. The most famous physical form removes Cursed Energy to an extraordinary degree and grants a body with exceptional strength and senses. Other restrictions can move in the opposite direction, crippling the body while granting enormous Cursed Energy range or output. The exchange is built into the person's constitution rather than chosen later.

cardPool.title: Binding Vows
cardPool.value:
Definition:
Binding Vows are supernatural agreements that impose conditions or sacrifices in exchange for power, efficiency, range, access, or another benefit.

Types:
A sorcerer may make a vow with themselves or enter a vow with another party. The consequences and risk depend on the vow.

Interaction:
Binding Vows operate through jujutsu, not Quirk Factors. Quirk suppression does not cancel them, and a Quirk cannot casually bypass a vow's supernatural terms.

Detailed Mechanics:
Binding vows are contracts made through jujutsu. A self-imposed restriction can increase effectiveness by accepting a real limitation, while vows made between people carry severe consequences if broken. The exchange must have meaningful value; merely stating a preference does not create power. Revealing how a technique works can itself become a binding vow that increases effectiveness by giving an opponent useful information.

Risk and Exchange:
A vow gains value only when the restriction or promise carries real consequence. Self-imposed vows trade freedom, information, timing, range, safety, or another meaningful advantage for greater effectiveness. Vows between people are more dangerous because violating an agreed condition can trigger consequences the participants cannot safely predict or control. Revealing a technique can itself become a vow when the information materially helps the opponent and the user accepts that risk for increased output.

Enforcement:
The power of a vow comes from restriction being real, not from a spoken formula by itself. A sorcerer cannot gain free strength by promising something that costs nothing. Self-imposed vows are usually more predictable because the user controls both the sacrifice and benefit. Interpersonal vows are more dangerous because breaking them risks consequences beyond ordinary strategic loss, making exact wording and mutual understanding important.

cardPool.title: Cursed Techniques
cardPool.value:
Definition:
A Cursed Technique is a jujutsu ability powered by Cursed Energy. Many are Innate Techniques engraved into the user's body, while some are inherited through sorcerer bloodlines.

Independence:
Cursed Techniques are completely separate from Quirks and Quirk Factors. An inherited Cursed Technique follows jujutsu lineage rather than Quirk genetics.

Learning:
Most Innate Techniques cannot simply be learned by another person. Sorcerers instead improve interpretation, efficiency, extension techniques, barrier use, and tactical application.

Visibility:
Non-sorcerers generally cannot perceive the Cursed Energy or supernatural visual component of a technique, though they can suffer its effects and observe physical aftermath.

Innate and Learned Jujutsu:
An Innate Technique is engraved into the sorcerer's body and usually manifests according to inherited or individual potential. Not every sorcerer possesses one, and possessing one does not replace fundamentals such as reinforcement or barrier knowledge. Learned techniques—Curtains, Simple Domain, weapon reinforcement, or other teachable jujutsu—can exist independently of an Innate Technique. Extensions and Domains are developments of a technique, not separate Quirks or automatic upgrades.

Variation:
