Combining features creates an adaptable fighting form, but each added change needs room and precise handling. What the body can manifest is constrained by the things actually consumed.

cardPool.title: Erasure
cardPool.value:
Ability: Erasure

Overview: Erasure temporarily nullifies affected Quirks when Shota Aizawa maintains visual focus on targets. Blinking and obstructed sight interrupt the effect. It cannot remove permanent anatomical features already present in heteromorphic bodies. Loss of an eye and major war injuries reduce his personal ability to perform his former frontline role.

Sight requirement: The user can prevent many active Quirks from functioning as long as a chosen target remains in view and the effect is maintained. Hair rising is a visible sign of activation. Hiding behind obstacles, shutting the eyes or losing consciousness can interrupt the suppression.

Boundaries: The ability does not reverse physical changes already made, erase a permanent extra limb or neutralize inert damage already caused by a Quirk. Mechanical weapons remain functional. Serious damage to the user’s eye in war changes future practical access; another person’s trained use of the same power must not be assumed.

Field detail: An erasing gaze may shut down an enemy’s emitted ability while an ally closes for a safe capture. It cannot reverse a fire already burning or remove the claws of someone born with claws. Maintaining open eyes under bright light, smoke and repeated impacts becomes increasingly difficult, making goggles, capture gear and teammate cover valuable.

cardPool.title: Rewind
cardPool.value:
Ability: Rewind

Overview: Rewind allows Eri to reverse the physical condition of a living body to an earlier state. The ability is hazardous without fine control and once required strict supervision. It cannot be treated as routine, consequence-free healing; catastrophic overuse might reverse someone beyond a survivable state. Her horn supplied stored energy when she broke it off during the Final War; it later regrew, but her full Quirk capacity is unverified.

Biological reversal: The Quirk returns a living body to an earlier condition. It can close injuries, restore a missing limb or undo bodily changes, but a severe uncontrolled application can move a target before existence. The horn near the forehead reflects stored power and becomes more prominent when a charge has built up.

Uncertainty: The mechanism involves accumulation over time, so the user cannot simply provide endless healing. It does not reverse broken buildings or alter history outside a living body. The horn was voluntarily broken to assist a rescue, later regrew, and no fully verified adult-era demonstration establishes exactly how much power remains available.

Field detail: Restoring a lost ability or healed limb requires the target’s body to have existed in a suitable prior state. A powerful reversal without accurate control can kill rather than heal. The energy accumulation makes it fundamentally different from an always-available medical machine, and its adult condition cannot be established merely because the horn grows back.

cardPool.title: Water Gun
cardPool.value:
Ability: Water Gun

Overview: Water Gun permits Kota Izumi to eject water from his hands. Although initially limited compared with destructive combat Quirks, practice can improve handling. Its usefulness in rescue, diversion or firefighting depends on output, supply and control rather than a presumed maximum blast strength.

Expression: Water is propelled from the palms, creating jets that can knock small threats aside or supply a limited amount for emergency use. Training increases control and confidence, especially where a stream must be directed through a narrow opening.

Practical limits: Available water, pressure and technique determine how much weight the stream can move. The power does not grant oceanic manipulation or the ability to control ordinary water across a city. Its apparent modesty should not be mistaken for an inability to perform useful rescue work.

Field detail: The water streams can startle an opponent or assist with extinguishing small flames when enough output is available. They can also offer a safer alternative to a damaging punch in close quarters. No evidence gives the Quirk control over rain, oceans or other people’s bodies; its practical value lies in its focused jets and the user’s initiative.

cardPool.title: Zoom
cardPool.value:
Ability: Zoom

Overview: Zoom allows Mei Hatsume to focus her vision on very distant details. Its long-distance magnification supports analysis and field observation, while her engineering expertise is a separate learned skill. A remarkable invention is not an automatic function of the Quirk.

Vision: The eyes magnify distant targets, allowing close inspection of objects many meters away without relying on a handheld telescope. This helps testing prototypes and reading small mechanical details from a safer position.

Limits: Magnification does not guarantee understanding of what is being seen or grant the power to build machines without study. Physical obstruction and poor lighting remain problems. The user’s creativity, engineering knowledge and risky experiments are separate accomplishments.

Field detail: An inventor can inspect whether a component moves as intended at a distance, track a prototype in flight or study details without entering a hazardous test zone. That observation must still be interpreted and recorded. Improved eyesight does not create materials, improve mechanical strength or automatically diagnose failures inside opaque objects.

cardPool.title: Copy
cardPool.value:
Ability: Copy

Overview: Copy permits Neito Monoma to reproduce a Quirk after touching its user. Borrowed powers expire after a limited duration and depend on physiological compatibility; Quirks requiring externally accumulated energy or resources may be unusable without those reserves. The user must manage the powers he has copied, and a copy is not ownership of the original Quirk.

Mechanism: Contact with another Quirk wielder temporarily duplicates their factor for a limited period. The borrowed function can be activated if its biological conditions are met. Experienced use improves the management of several copied abilities and the timing of each effect.

Blanks: Quirks that stockpile something over time are copied without automatically receiving the stockpiled reserve. A copy of a healing or accumulation factor may thus be useless without energy already built up. The user does not permanently steal the source ability, and contact alone does not confer the original wielder’s years of skill.

Field detail: Quick contact in crowded combat can supply an unexpected answer to a specific threat. Advanced preparation involves knowing which Quirk to borrow, the duration left on it and whether another user’s anatomy is needed to operate it. A borrowed emitter effect is not necessarily equally powerful without the donor’s control and training.

cardPool.title: Softening
cardPool.value:
Ability: Softening

Overview: Softening lets Juzo Honenuki change solid, nonliving material into a softer state by touching it. He can alter terrain to capture enemies, slow approaches or create pathways. The material can be restored toward its original hardness. Limits arise from range, reaction time and the need to avoid endangering allies inside affected surfaces.

Surface control: Solid ground, walls and other nonliving matter can become pliable or mudlike under contact, creating pits and slowing enemy movement. Restoring the affected surface to hardness permits rapid containment or makeshift protective structures.

Hazards: The technique can destabilize structures and endanger trapped civilians if used casually. Liquids and living beings are not interchangeable with the solid materials it softens. Team communication is essential before transforming floors that allies may be standing on.

Field detail: Terrain can be turned into a temporary trap beneath an advancing opponent, then hardened again to keep them from escaping. The same idea can open a shallow route through obstructed ground. Buildings must be examined before use: making a support column soft may endanger anyone inside, even if the target is a villain.

cardPool.title: New Order
cardPool.value:
Ability: New Order

Overview: New Order enabled Cathleen Bate to set extraordinary rules on targets touched and named by her. She could maintain only two rules at a time. Effects depended on accurate target identification, and changes to living beings had limits. The ability was destroyed through the conflict with stolen Quirks rather than surviving as an available power for later heroes.

Rule setting: A touched subject must be named, and the user must understand its identity. A rule can alter such things as the behavior of surrounding air or impose a specific property on a target. Only two simultaneous rules are possible, one often reserved for enhancing the wielder.

Boundaries: The Quirk cannot grant absolutely limitless personal strength and cannot reliably alter a living target if the named identity conflicts with the person’s self-conception. Losing contact is not always the same as dropping a rule, but creating a third requires replacing one. The factor no longer survives as an available personal ability.

Field detail: Large environmental changes are particularly useful because inanimate things do not have self-conceptions that resist identification. Rules can be set to shield comrades or affect a nearby material, but their wording and named subject matter. Losing a rule to establish another imposes decisions under pressure, especially when one rule maintains the user’s own enhancement.

cardPool.title: Decay
cardPool.value:
Ability: Decay

Overview: Decay disintegrated matter through Tomura Shigaraki’s touch and, after developing, could spread through connected surfaces. Its enormous danger included collapsing structures and chain destruction. Intervention before spread completed could sometimes limit losses. The Quirk’s origin and later modifications were bound up with All For One’s manipulation of Tomura.

Progression: Early activation involved all five fingers touching an object; severe emotional trauma and later growth expanded the reach and contagious spread across linked material. Floors, buildings and bodies could crumble through connected contact, producing chain destruction on a catastrophic scale.

Limits: Interrupted contact, separation of affected material or other defensive interventions can sometimes stop the advance. The original power was engineered by removing the rebuilding function from a derivative of Overhaul. It is not an expression of the original Quirk stolen from Tenko in infancy.

Field detail: A spreading disintegration wave turns the ground itself into a hazard; leaping away or isolating pieces of material can buy time. Destroying a building without touching every separate component became possible after the power evolved. Its devastating nature makes it dangerous to allies, rescue workers and enemies alike rather than a precise surgical instrument.

cardPool.title: Transform
cardPool.value:
Ability: Transform

Overview: Transform enabled Himiko Toga to take on the appearance of someone whose blood she consumed. The available transformation time depended on the quantity consumed. Under special emotional conditions she could also reproduce some transformed subjects’ Quirks. Her stored blood and disguise equipment mattered enormously to infiltration. She could not change another person’s identity without accessing their blood.

Disguise: A quantity of consumed blood determines how long a copied body can be maintained. Clothing can shift with the impersonated appearance, enabling deceptive social entry. Emotional attachment to certain people allowed reproduction of their abilities after the Quirk developed.

Limits: The user must obtain actual blood and cannot transform into someone chosen at random. Copying an appearance does not confer independent knowledge of that person’s private experiences. The ability does not make the wielder physically intangible or automatically control a target’s choices.

Field detail: After transformation, imitated mannerisms, speech and knowledge must still be learned independently if the disguise is to survive conversation. Consumed blood is a finite physical resource, so an infiltrator has to plan how much is available. The emotional basis for copying another Quirk cannot be reduced to transforming into any person at random.

cardPool.title: Blueflame
cardPool.value:
Ability: Blueflame

Overview: Blueflame generated extremely hot blue fire from Toya Todoroki’s body. His natural resistance to cold could not protect him adequately against the resulting heat, so continued use destroyed his tissue. The Quirk’s destructive output was inseparable from bodily injury and worsening emotional stress. It did not give him natural immunity to his own flames.

Heat: Brilliant blue combustion burns hotter than conventional orange flames and can incinerate massive targets. The user may form sweeping streams or tightly directed blasts, overwhelming many ordinary defenses. The fire responds to powerful emotion and can become exceptionally destructive when uncontrolled.

Self-harm: The body inherited a poor resistance to its own heat, so every sustained attack damages skin, muscle and internal tissues. Severe burns and extensive scarring were consequences of repeated use, not a costume effect. The ability offers enormous offense at the direct cost of survival.

Field detail: The extreme heat can overpower defensive constructs and create broad walls of fire, but every extended discharge worsens damage to its own wielder. Controlling direction does not confer full resistance to heat radiating back toward the body. The power illustrates a sharp division between spectacular output and biological suitability.

cardPool.title: Gecko
cardPool.value:
Ability: Gecko

Overview: Gecko gave Shuichi Iguchi reptilian adhesion for climbing on walls and other surfaces. His heteromorphic appearance was always visible and made him a target of prejudice. Additional forced Quirks during the uprising changed his physique and cognition, but they should not be confused with Gecko’s basic abilities.

Physiology: Reptilian limbs and adhesive skin enable the user to move across walls, cling to steep surfaces and climb where ordinary footing is impossible. A scaly exterior is part of the body, not a temporary disguise.

Separate alterations: Forced augmentation later made the user larger and less mentally stable. Those changes came from additional powers and medical manipulation, not from ordinary development of Gecko. The base factor supplies climbing and reptilian features; it does not inherently bestow giant size or superhuman regeneration.

Field detail: Adhesion gives practical advantages on buildings, ceilings and irregular surfaces, letting the user seek angles unavailable to ordinary climbers. A permanent nonhuman appearance can alter social interaction but does not determine loyalty or competence. The base power cannot explain later gigantic size without accounting for forced additional factors.

cardPool.title: Warp Gate
cardPool.value:
Ability: Warp Gate

Overview: Warp Gate created portals within black mist controlled by Kurogiri. It could transport people and objects between locations and redirect movement through connected openings. The power was embedded in a modified body made using Oboro Shirakumo’s remains. Its portals were not free of tactical constraints; accurate locations and user focus mattered.

Transit: The dark mist opens connected passages to locations the user can target, allowing an individual or group to step between distant points quickly. The technique supports extraction, reinforcement and redirection of attacks. Openings can be varied in size to accommodate different passengers.

Constraints: A portal must be placed accurately, and interruption of concentration can spoil an evacuation. The organic structure of the modified body is important to maintaining the ability. A gateway is not evidence that its user can read thoughts, stop time or teleport every object indiscriminately.

Field detail: A coordinated group can use portals to withdraw injured allies, insert a rescue team or separate opponents who rely on proximity. A badly chosen exit could place passengers in the path of danger, so reliable targeting is vital. The dark mist functions as a transport medium rather than smoke that merely hides the traveler.

cardPool.title: Fierce Wings
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fierce Wings

Overview: Fierce Wings originally gave Hawks broad red wings and precise independent control of individual feathers. They could carry people, detect subtle disturbances and cut or intercept targets. Damage weakened the feathers and prolonged use reduced his supply. Hawks ultimately lost the Quirk, so its past functions must not be presented as abilities he can still deploy in the adult epilogue.

Feather control: Large crimson wings once supplied high-speed flight. Individual feathers could be sent out to carry small loads, hear distant vibrations, intercept projectiles or cut targets. The ability excelled in performing several rescue tasks at once.

Loss: Repeated destruction reduced effective plumage and impaired flight. The factor was eventually stolen, leaving its former wielder unable to command the feathers naturally. His later public-safety role depends on experience and leadership rather than restored wings.

Field detail: Independent feathers can perform fine manipulations while the main body flies, making simultaneous rescue and scouting possible. A feather carrying a person requires strength and appropriate placement; smaller feathers are more suited to sensing. Repeated loss of feathers reduces lift and eventually makes airborne work impossible until they regrow—unless the Quirk itself has been stolen.

cardPool.title: Rabbit
cardPool.value:
Ability: Rabbit

Overview: Rabbit granted Mirko strong legs, powerful leaps, exceptional agility and rabbitlike senses. The Quirk did not regrow amputated limbs. Her subsequent extraordinary mobility depends on advanced mechanical prosthetics together with combat conditioning and relentless physical adaptation.

Traits: Powerful leg muscles allow great jumps, rapid kicks and tight changes of direction. Enhanced hearing and instinctive movement make the user a fearsome close-range fighter, with no need for an emitted projectile.

After injury: Rabbit did not prevent loss of limbs during battles with Nomu or restore them afterward. Mechanical prostheses return mobility through machinery and difficult retraining, not through an unmentioned regenerative ability. The effectiveness of each strike still depends on sound footing and personal conditioning.

Field detail: Leaping strength can close the distance to a fast opponent, while quick footwork makes sweeping attacks hard to predict. Rabbitlike hearing offers early awareness but does not function as a perfect lie detector or sonar. The user’s willingness to keep fighting through prosthetic damage is a matter of discipline rather than additional biological powers.

cardPool.title: Gigantification
cardPool.value:
Ability: Gigantification

Overview: Gigantification allows Mt. Lady to grow into a giant version of herself. Increased size brings formidable force and reach but creates serious risks of collateral damage in crowded spaces. She must manage terrain and the presence of civilians carefully. The power is transformation rather than the ability to make other people grow.

Transformation: The user enlarges into a giant while retaining human shape, increasing reach and physical impact substantially. She can brace against huge opponents, catch large falling structures and draw hostile attention away from ground-level evacuees.

Costs: Giant size makes narrow roads, fragile bridges and dense crowds hazardous. Mass and impact can cause destruction even when the hero intends to help. The transformation does not shrink other people or create additional space; coordination with evacuation crews is essential.

Field detail: Standing at enormous height can provide a view across collapsed districts and allow access to upper floors, while massive arms may shield a structure from a falling object. These advantages vanish in spaces that cannot contain the transformed body. The ability must be managed to prevent unintended damage to roads and buildings.

cardPool.title: Arbor
cardPool.value:
Ability: Arbor

Overview: Arbor grows and controls wooden structures from Kamui Woods’s body. Branches extend to bind opponents, anchor movement and form rescue supports. Wood remains vulnerable to fire and destructive force, and extensive growth requires accuracy when civilians occupy the same area.

Growth: Wood extends from limbs and torso as branching restraints and stakes, enabling long-distance captures and improvised anchors. A disciplined user can envelop an opponent without needing a weapon that causes severe injury.

Vulnerabilities: Fire and intense energy can damage the material. Destroyed branches and complex entanglements may restrict immediate reconfiguration. The branches arise from the user’s own body rather than from instant control of every tree nearby.

Field detail: The user can rapidly bind several fleeing targets by extending branches along a prepared route. A wooden cage or rail can also provide temporary support during evacuation. Heat-based opponents pose a special danger, and a construction is only as secure as its anchoring. The Quirk does not produce living forests independent of its user.

cardPool.title: Fiber Master
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fiber Master

Overview: Fiber Master grants Best Jeanist refined control over textile fibers, including those in clothing. Thick woven materials can create restraints and protective structures; garments on opponents may become a weakness. Use requires concentration, technical understanding and material to manipulate.

Manipulation: Textile threads respond to highly precise control, allowing fabric to bind a target or stretch into sturdy constructions. Denim is a favored material, but other woven fibers can be used. The finest applications involve individually controlled strands rather than brute force alone.

Boundaries: Fibers must be present, and opponents without useful textiles limit easy restraint. Fire, cutting or violent force can overwhelm a structure. The power does not generate cloth from nothing or control unrelated solids merely because they resemble thread.

Field detail: A long strip of woven material can be manipulated to catch a falling person or restrict a weapon arm. Multiple fine threads can apply force with great precision, but material choice strongly affects durability. The Quirk is particularly formidable when surrounded by clothing or heavy fabric, and weaker when there are few appropriate fibers available.

cardPool.title: Fat Absorption
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fat Absorption

Overview: Fat Absorption lets Fat Gum absorb impacts with an unusually resilient body and convert stored energy into forceful counterattacks. Expending these reserves can sharply alter his body shape. The Quirk is defensive and offensive but cannot absorb unlimited damage without consequences.

Defense: Impact sinks into a cushion of stored fat, reducing the harm of punches and other blows. Collected power can be turned into a concentrated strike, while spending too much reserve leaves the user drastically leaner.

Judgment: A major counterattack may sacrifice the very protection needed for subsequent rounds. Heavy penetration and repeated punishment can become dangerous even when softened. The Quirk is not unlimited healing and works best when a team can protect the user during recovery.

Field detail: A body that absorbs a punch can also help cushion another person against a crushing blow. The most decisive counterattack spends energy that was being held defensively, forcing a choice between immediate power and future safety. The dramatic body-shape change after releasing reserves is an intrinsic consequence of the ability.

cardPool.title: Dragon
cardPool.value:
Ability: Dragon

Overview: Dragon lets Ryukyu turn into a huge flying dragon. The transformed body provides flight, physical might, scales and claws, useful in both rescue and combat. Her size can obstruct movement in narrow indoor spaces and raises the stakes of collateral harm.

Transformation: A human body expands into a scaly dragon with wings, long neck, strong legs and powerful claws. Its mass supports carrying allies, shielding smaller people and confronting large enemies directly.

Practical limits: Large size complicates movement through tunnels and populated streets. Although scales improve durability, the dragon is not immune to extreme force. The power grants flight and physical transformation, not a separately established energy beam or automatic fire-breathing.

Field detail: Strong wings can lift an injured person away from a high ledge while armored scales endure impacts that would injure an ordinary rescuer. The dragon’s size is also a liability in close indoor passages. A transformed body has vulnerable points and can be restrained or wounded, so the power is not unconditional invulnerability.

cardPool.title: Elasticity
cardPool.value:
Ability: Elasticity

Overview: Elasticity allows Gentle to make touched materials elastic and springy. He can bounce across buildings, deflect movement and stretch surfaces into protective barriers. Elasticized spaces obey his tactical choices but cannot be assumed to cover every object or infinite distance.

Contact: Touched solid surfaces can take on spring-like qualities, absorbing a fall or redirecting motion. The user can create temporary trampolines and invisible-feeling footholds in the air by manipulating its elasticity, permitting agile movement without a flying Quirk.

Constraints: Altered surfaces are not indestructible and must be positioned before a collision. The power cannot guarantee control over an opponent’s entire body from across a city. Its strength is deception, trajectory control and cushioning rather than raw destructive force.

Field detail: Elastic surfaces redirect momentum, making a fall survivable or sending a pursuer back along their route. Several prepared surfaces can create an indirect movement path that a less observant opponent misunderstands. The ability can support daring rescues without being a conventional flight power; it still requires placement and timing.

cardPool.title: Love
cardPool.value:
Ability: Love

Overview: Love strengthens someone La Brava sincerely loves when she expresses that affection. Its output is tied to her emotional connection and cannot be deployed as an ordinary boost for any stranger. Her highly advanced computing skills are learned abilities, not manifestations of Love.

Empowerment: When the user declares sincere affection, the person who receives it can gain a dramatic, temporary boost. Depth of feeling determines the effect more than calculation or technical equipment. The Quirk can turn a companion’s desperate defense into a decisive stand.

Restriction: Love cannot be applied to an arbitrary colleague as if it were a battery. The boost is neither permanent nor a replacement for the subject’s own power. Programming, hacking and technology work are independent skills; they do not inherently result from this Quirk.

Field detail: The boost requires genuine emotional attachment, not merely reciting a password or pretending affection. Its effect is best understood through the recipient’s suddenly enhanced capacity to act, while the source remains physically vulnerable. It does not inherently rewrite the recipient’s personality or grant La Brava unrelated physical powers.

cardPool.title: Blackwhip
cardPool.value:
Ability: Blackwhip

Overview: Blackwhip was one of the inherited abilities within One For All, projecting dark energy tendrils useful for grappling, restraint, protection and mobility. Emotional turmoil could complicate control. Izuku no longer possesses this power after One For All’s loss; Blackwhip should be used as historical system information rather than a current natural ability.

Projection: Black, flexible tendrils spring from the user’s body and can bind opponents, hook structures, carry items and brace injured limbs. Their reach makes them highly valuable alongside enhanced movement, though delicate manipulation takes training.

Control: Emotional distress originally caused wild, uncontrolled tendrils, threatening allies and the user. Superior control required calm focus and repeated practice. The power existed inside the inherited stockpile and disappeared from Izuku’s natural repertoire when One For All ended.

Field detail: Multiple tendrils can anchor the user while a different strand carries an injured person or restrains an enemy. Using the energy internally to brace damaged limbs became possible through extraordinary control. That application came at real physical cost; once the inherited ability disappears, the same appearance would require engineered equipment rather than natural tendrils.

cardPool.title: Float
cardPool.value:
Ability: Float

Overview: Float was Nana Shimura’s levitation Quirk and later one of the powers accessible to Izuku through One For All. It enabled sustained aerial movement when combined with other mobility abilities. It is not among Izuku’s natural capabilities after the stockpiled Quirk disappears.

Effect: The bearer can rise off the ground and remain suspended, avoiding ordinary pitfalls and ground-based hazards. Combined with propulsion or grappling, levitation can create rapid three-dimensional movement; by itself it is not unrestricted high-speed flight.

History: Nana Shimura possessed the independent factor before its imprint became one of the powers carried within One For All. Izuku accessed it temporarily during his tenure as bearer. No independent, inherited copy remains available to him after the stockpiled power fades.

Field detail: Levitation frees the user from contact with unstable ground or a surface affected by Decay. For fast travel it works particularly well alongside a separate source of horizontal propulsion. A stationary hover alone does not catch a falling person safely, and it offers no independent protective barrier against ranged attacks.

cardPool.title: Danger Sense
cardPool.value:
Ability: Danger Sense

Overview: Danger Sense was a One For All predecessor ability that reacted to hostile danger and negative intent. It could produce painful warnings and became less useful against attackers without malice. It never guaranteed automatic evasion. Izuku lost access to it as One For All was sacrificed.

Warning: A sharp mental signal alerts the user to hostile intent and impending danger. Its severity can be painful when threats are intense or numerous. It aids positioning only when the body can move fast enough to react.

Blind spots: A person acting without malice may attack or inflict harm without triggering an equally useful warning. Crowded battlefields can produce overwhelming signals. The Quirk does not predict every accident or read all private thoughts and is no longer present in Izuku’s adult Quirkless body.

Field detail: The warning signal is particularly useful when a hostile opponent hides behind cover, but it is harder to interpret in a crowd with conflicting intentions. The sense alerts rather than defeating a threat: only awareness, speed and judgment turn it into successful defense. Well-meaning people can remain a blind spot.

cardPool.title: Smokescreen
cardPool.value:
Ability: Smokescreen

Overview: Smokescreen was an inherited One For All ability to emit dense smoke and obscure sightlines. It supported retreat and concealment but could also blind allies or its own user. Izuku no longer has its natural use in the epilogue.

Emission: Purple-gray clouds spread through the field, blocking sight and enabling escapes, ambushes or movement under cover. The user can adjust the quantity but must still navigate within the obscured area.

Limits: A cloud does not prevent area attacks, powerful gusts or opponents who can detect sound and movement by other means. Emitting too much smoke can hinder allies as much as enemies. The factor belonged to an earlier One For All wielder and is not naturally possessed by Izuku in the adult era.

Field detail: A thick visual barrier forces distant shooters to guess or close the gap. Allies with nonvisual senses can exploit it, while those relying on eyesight may become equally disoriented. Wind, powerful air pressure and broad attacks can clear the cloud. It is a concealment tool rather than a directly damaging emission.

cardPool.title: Fa Jin
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fa Jin

Overview: Fa Jin accumulated kinetic energy through repeated motions, then released that energy in bursts for enhanced movement or strikes. It was one of the prior users’ Quirks contained within One For All, not an independent power available to Izuku after losing the inheritance.

Storage: Repeated movement of a limb builds up kinetic energy that can be released as a temporary burst of force or speed. It permits a powerful action without requiring constant maximum output from the broader stockpiling power.

Use: Charging requires time and intentional motion, and the reserve cannot be assumed infinite. It existed as a distinct predecessor Quirk inside One For All. Its disappearance with the inheritance means later use would require separate equipment, not the restoration of the original biological factor.

Field detail: A few deliberate repetitive movements can build up a reserve before a sudden dash or strike. The technique rewards preparation and coordination with other mobility effects, not reckless continuous maximum effort. Exhausting stored kinetic energy demands more charging; the original reserve is not simply refreshed at the instant it is spent.

cardPool.title: Gearshift
cardPool.value:
Ability: Gearshift

Overview: Gearshift altered the speed of touched objects, later operating on far more potent scales after enhancement through One For All. Its advanced use created an extreme backlash and limited operating time. It was a predecessor ability within One For All and is no longer naturally accessible to Izuku.

Speed control: Contact changes the velocity of a target, bypassing some ordinary restrictions of acceleration. Initially associated with small objects, its power increased tremendously in One For All, allowing extraordinary maneuvers and explosive combat combinations.

Backlash: High-end activation rapidly imposes punishing bodily stress and creates a narrow window for effective use. Repeating extreme performance is far more dangerous than ordinary bursts of enhanced speed. The factor belonged to an earlier bearer and was sacrificed with the inheritance rather than kept by Izuku.

Field detail: Altering speed at close contact allows abrupt shifts in combat momentum that are difficult for an opponent to anticipate. When supercharged by One For All, those changes become exceptionally violent and stressful to the body. The short safe operating window makes the power suited to a decisive emergency, not an unlimited normal movement speed.

cardPool.title: U.A. High School
cardPool.value:
Location: U.A. High School

Description: Prestigious Japanese academy for hero education, general studies, business and support development. Its hero course emphasizes rescue, combat, ethics, field internships and the realities of professional licensing. Strong fortifications, movable campus infrastructure and experienced faculty make it a crucial refuge and training center. Years after the Final War, Izuku Midoriya teaches here and Kota Izumi attends as a student. Its role expands from preparing powerful fighters to shaping socially responsible protectors.

Campus and infrastructure: U.A. operates general studies, hero, support and business departments. Hero students study both classroom subjects and practical response, with specialist teachers responsible for combat, rescue and the ethics of professional intervention. Training spaces include artificial urban blocks, disaster environments, sports venues, workshops and dormitories. A protected campus can function as an emergency gathering point rather than just a school.

Present-day use: Enhanced security grew after repeated villain incursions. During the national crisis, mobile structures and underground systems helped shelter people under threat. Reconstruction allowed regular schooling to resume. The adult faculty includes educators who fought in the war; the campus continues admitting new students rather than remaining frozen as the former Class A’s home.

cardPool.title: Musutafu
cardPool.value:
Location: Musutafu

Description: Japanese city that contains U.A. High School and many locations associated with the formative years of Class 1-A. Residential streets, transit routes, commercial buildings and hero infrastructure provide both ordinary civilian life and disaster-prone spaces. The surrounding communities experienced instability during the villain crises and later joined national reconstruction. The city functions as a broad adventure setting rather than a single school campus.

Urban character: Musutafu contains ordinary family apartments and houses, shopping streets, roads, public transit and the school zone associated with U.A. The concentration of hero training and professional response makes it a busy place even between emergencies. Neighborhoods are inhabited by civilians whose daily needs continue regardless of famous hero activity.

Civic role: Evacuations and rebuilding changed how residents think about depending on lone celebrity heroes. Schools, businesses and roads remain useful settings for small rescues, investigations and ordinary interactions. It is a functioning city, not a permanent ruin or a self-contained academy compound.

Local texture: Residential blocks sit alongside stores, intersections and commuter routes linking neighborhoods to school and work. An incident here can involve an ordinary shopkeeper or pedestrian as easily as an academy student. After the war, reconstruction and public services coexist with restored business activity.

cardPool.title: Ground Beta
cardPool.value:
Location: Ground Beta

Description: U.A. training ground constructed to resemble an urban district, with concrete buildings, artificial roads and rooftops. It allows students and licensed personnel to practice mobility, searching, team tactics and urban rescue in an environment that resembles city blocks. Its structures are instructional assets, not a normal residential neighborhood.

Layout: Dense blocks of tall artificial buildings, streets, lanes and rooftops imitate the problems of a developed city. Students can practice climbing, ambush awareness, capture techniques and coordinated searches. Observation areas let instructors monitor safety and performance.

Purpose: Because the site is designed for repeated controlled exercises, structural damage can be repaired or reset. Staged fights are not evidence that civilians live in the replica buildings. Rescue instructors may adapt exercises to test communication, timing and restraint instead of simply defeating an opponent.

Safety operations: Instructors can stage missing-person searches and timed captures, observing whether students damage simulated infrastructure unnecessarily. Rooflines and building interiors permit controlled surprise encounters. The facility is not a real city borough and has no permanent civilian population.

cardPool.title: Unforeseen Simulation Joint
cardPool.value:
Location: Unforeseen Simulation Joint

Description: U.A.’s specialized disaster-response training facility, widely known as the U.S.J. It contains several artificial environmental zones for practicing rescue under varied hazards, including floods, fires, landslides and collapsed urban structures. It was the site of a major early League of Villains assault that reshaped the students’ understanding of danger.

Design: The enclosed training dome is split into themed disaster zones, including water hazards, urban wreckage and burning structures. It allows response teams to rehearse civilian evacuation and survival in conditions too dangerous to construct on ordinary city streets. The main plaza connects the hazard sections.

Security and significance: Its early invasion by villains exposed vulnerabilities in academy defenses and endangered an entire first-year class. The incident influenced later safety decisions, but the facility’s primary purpose remains training for catastrophes. The name is usually shortened to U.S.J.

Training areas: Different environmental compartments demand different equipment and choices. A water rescue requires buoyancy and communication, whereas a collapsing building requires careful handling of debris. Routes through the central area can be blocked during exercises to force teams to plan alternative access.

cardPool.title: U.A. Dormitories
cardPool.value:
Location: U.A. Dormitories (Heights Alliance)

Description: Student residential facilities established to improve security after villain attacks exposed the limits of commuting and ordinary home life. Class 1-A’s dorm building provides private rooms and shared social space where friendships were strengthened. Adult graduates no longer automatically live here; the facilities remain part of the school environment for successive student cohorts.

Living spaces: Private bedrooms are grouped around shared kitchens, lounges and other communal areas. Residents can study together, prepare meals and seek help from classmates without commuting through unsafe streets. The arrangement promotes trust but also requires consideration for quiet hours, privacy and shared responsibilities.

History and use: Dorm residence was introduced as a security response after attacks on students. The building became important to daily class life and the emotional recovery of frightened trainees. Graduating does not give former students permanent claim to their old rooms; subsequent cohorts occupy student housing.

Daily routines: The shared common room is used for conversation and class gatherings, while students personalize private rooms. Living together reduces some travel risks but means conflicts and worries follow residents home. The building is part of U.A.’s institutional housing, with staff oversight and ordinary school rules.

cardPool.title: Kamino Ward
cardPool.value:
Location: Kamino Ward

Description: Urban district notorious for the confrontation in which All Might defeated All For One publicly and lost the last usable strength of his former heroic identity. A memorial statue of All Might stands here. Following the Final War, the memorial was expanded with representations of ordinary civilians raising their arms to support heroes, acknowledging rescue and solidarity beyond individual celebrity.

Streets and memorial: A densely built urban ward with major roads and the site of an infamous showdown. The All Might statue later became a place where an unsure young person could pause and ask what heroism means. After the Final War, statues of ordinary civilians with raised arms joined the memorial, widening its symbolism.

Civic meaning: The area recalls both the dangers of relying on a single Symbol of Peace and the power of ordinary people to reach toward one another. Local stores and pedestrians continue to exist around the memorial. It is not merely an abandoned combat zone or the residence of All Might.

Ordinary visitors may approach the memorial not to celebrate a fight but to consider an uncertain future. Its newer civilian figures emphasize helping hands as much as the famous raised fist. The streets around the monument belong to a functioning community whose safety matters more than the site’s historical fame.

cardPool.title: Jaku City
cardPool.value:
Location: Jaku City

Description: City and hospital district devastated by the Paranormal Liberation War. A hidden medical facility was used for the modification of Tomura Shigaraki and the creation of dangerous Nomu. Massive destruction, evacuation and reconstruction transformed the district into a reminder of the danger posed by organized superhuman crime.

Medical district: Jaku was home to a major hospital secretly associated with illegal research and the creation or enhancement of Nomu. The hidden work was uncovered during a coordinated hero operation. When catastrophic power was unleashed, surrounding streets, buildings and infrastructure became scenes of mass evacuation.

Aftermath: Severe destruction made reconstruction, debris removal, housing and healthcare urgent priorities. Residents need ongoing services after the main battle ends. The city should be understood as a living community coping with disaster, not as a continuing headquarters for the defeated research network.

Reconstruction requires restoring water, power, roads, housing and medical access after sudden collapse. Large open ruins can conceal hazards even when no villains remain. Survivors have personal ties to homes and neighborhoods that cannot be replaced simply by clearing damaged structures.

cardPool.title: Gunga Mountain Villa
cardPool.value:
Location: Gunga Mountain Villa

Description: Remote complex formerly associated with the Paranormal Liberation Front. Its facilities and surroundings became part of major conflicts with organized villains. The area includes mountainous terrain, access roads and broad spaces that made coordinated attacks and mass mobilization possible.

Terrain and structure: A mountain property used as a concealed gathering center for the Paranormal Liberation Front. The main complex and its underground areas accommodated large meetings, personnel and preparations for coordinated operations. Its isolated approaches complicated surveillance while giving defenders routes through wooded terrain.

History and condition: Hero forces targeted the site during the wider conflict, and fighting damaged the compound. Nearby mountainous areas became associated with later clashes as well. By the adult reconstruction period the former organization is defeated; its old halls should not automatically be described as a thriving, fully staffed enemy base.

The mountain approaches, abandoned service roads and damaged underground areas offer very different conditions for movement. Snow, rubble or fallen timber can affect access at different times. An investigation into old facilities would encounter remnants of a defeated coalition, not a guaranteed standing army.

cardPool.title: Hosu City
cardPool.value:
Location: Hosu City

Description: City affected by the Hero Killer Stain, Nomu attacks and the broader problem of public confidence in professional heroes. Its streets and alleyways became a formative battleground for young heroes and police cooperation. The city remains a populated urban setting outside the U.A. campus.

Urban features: Broad commercial streets meet smaller alleys, hospitals and ordinary residential districts. Those narrow routes gave dangerous criminals places to ambush a lone responder. Emergency services and police have practical roles beyond the dramatic public battles associated with the district.

History: The Hero Killer’s attacks and simultaneous Nomu incidents shook confidence in professional protection. Young trainees learned how quickly a patrol could become a rescue or law-enforcement crisis. The city remains populated and rebuilds ordinary civic life rather than being permanently under villain control.

Hosu’s danger once came from ordinary blind alleys and public streets as much as from spectacular confrontations. Hospitals and transport routes kept functioning during emergencies. A present-day visit may be routine; the district’s notorious past does not prove that the same killers are still on patrol.

cardPool.title: Nabu Island
cardPool.value:
Location: Nabu Island

Description: Remote island community where young U.A. hero students undertook protective duties and confronted a dangerous villain assault. Rural and coastal scenery, residential facilities and transport limitations make it distinct from mainland hero cities. The island’s inhabitants depend heavily on coordinated local response during emergencies.

Geography: An outlying island community with coastal routes, beaches, farms, forested high ground, small settlements and limited access to mainland reinforcement. Residents know one another more readily than in major cities, and local emergencies may have to be handled with whatever people and equipment are immediately available.

History: Hero trainees once undertook community duties here and defended residents during a serious attack. Distance from large hero agencies shaped the danger and made evacuation routes vital. Outside that crisis, the island is primarily a quiet civilian home, not an established military site.

Transport is constrained by coastal approaches and distance from major cities. Local residents may need to organize supplies, shelter and communication before help arrives. Shorelines, fields and forest paths create varied response problems with fewer tall buildings and fewer agency resources than on the mainland.

cardPool.title: I-Island
cardPool.value:
Location: I-Island

Description: Artificial island devoted to technology, scientific research and support-industry innovation. A highly secured research culture, exhibition facilities and international engineering networks distinguish it from normal Japanese cities. Melissa Shield’s work is connected with this world of advanced engineering.

Research environment: This highly secured artificial island hosts laboratories, advanced support-device development and major technology exhibitions. International specialists and visitors gather to examine inventions intended for the professional hero industry. Security restrictions protect research while creating distinct challenges for anyone entering sensitive facilities.

Physical character: Modern towers, research centers and leisure areas coexist on a technologically sophisticated island. A public demonstration can draw audiences from outside Japan, but ordinary laboratories remain governed by access rules. The island’s scientific importance does not imply that every invention originates there or that it controls Japanese hero licensing.

The island’s exhibitions connect researchers, inventors and professional heroes, bringing attention to both promising prototypes and security risks. A complex device can be demonstrated to visitors while its underlying research remains restricted. Its facilities require power, safety staff and security coordination like any other major research center.

cardPool.title: Tartarus
cardPool.value:
Location: Tartarus

Description: High-security detention facility designed for extremely dangerous criminals with destructive or difficult-to-contain Quirks. Its systems relied on surveillance, confinement and heavily armed response. The facility suffered a catastrophic breakout during the collapse of national hero security, demonstrating the fragility of even advanced prisons.

Design and security: An island prison built for detainees whose powers make ordinary incarceration dangerous. Heavily layered defenses, surveillance and restrictions on movement were designed to prevent sudden escape or the use of destructive Quirks inside the facility. Its reputation reflected fears about criminals beyond the capacity of local jails.

Collapse: A coordinated escape overwhelmed the institution during the breakdown of national security, freeing dangerous inmates and destabilizing public confidence. It cannot be treated as a fully operational, untouched prison during the adult era without a separately established rebuilding. The site embodies the limitations of punishment as society’s only safeguard.

Defenses were designed around prisoners with unusual escape capabilities, so restraints and remote monitoring mattered as much as thick walls. A prison breach could allow many disparate threats into public areas at once. The collapse made clear that walls cannot substitute for a resilient society outside them.

cardPool.title: Central Hospital
cardPool.value:
Location: Central Hospital

Description: Major medical center involved in treating serious injuries and coordinating high-level medical response. Research and specialist care for unusual Quirk-related conditions were crucial during the Final War and the recovery that followed. It is a hospital, not a hero academy or criminal headquarters.

Medical operations: The hospital treats complex traumatic injuries and works with medical specialists familiar with unusual biological powers. It has held critically injured people requiring sustained monitoring and has been involved in emergency response following large-scale combat. Advanced care does not mean every condition is curable.

Professional character: Its wards, examination rooms and restricted areas are governed by medical needs, privacy and physical security. Treatment may last long after public battles are over. Patients can include heroes and criminal suspects, but that does not turn the institution into a secret villain organization or a routine detention center.

Staff must balance treatment with medical confidentiality, specialist monitoring and the unusual risks posed by uncontrolled Quirks. Extended critical care can follow battles by many months. Decisions about visitors, patient safety and recovery remain medical rather than political spectacles.

cardPool.title: Hassaikai Compound
cardPool.value:
Location: Hassaikai Compound

Description: Former headquarters of the Shie Hassaikai, a yakuza group that used underground facilities and secure rooms to conceal experiments and criminal operations. Its corridors and hidden infrastructure were central to the rescue of Eri. After the organization’s defeat it no longer serves as a legitimate operating hero facility.

Physical layout: A traditional-looking criminal headquarters concealing numerous interior passages and underground sections. Tight corridors and sealed rooms forced rescuers to consider hostages, escape routes and sudden changes to the building itself. The underground complex helped hide highly abusive experimentation.

Legacy: Police and professional heroes raided the premises to stop production of anti-Quirk ammunition and rescue a captive child. Once exposed, the compound ceased to function as a secure headquarters for the old syndicate. Its architecture and hidden passages remain relevant to investigations of past crimes.

Some corridors were altered during the raid, complicating rescue and separating teams. Small rooms and winding passages enabled ambushes without providing easy routes for civilians to escape. Investigators later had to reconstruct activities hidden beneath an outwardly traditional compound.

cardPool.title: Deika City
cardPool.value:
Location: Deika City

Description: City that witnessed large-scale fighting between the League of Villains and the Meta Liberation Army. The resulting destruction and political fallout aided the formation of the Paranormal Liberation Front. It represents the dangers of concentrated extremist mobilization within a seemingly ordinary urban community.

Civic structure: Deika appeared to operate as a normal municipality, but an exceptionally large proportion of its inhabitants were tied to liberationist organizing. Businesses, public spaces and the urban terrain were used to conceal mass political and militant activity. A visitor could mistake the organized preparation for ordinary civic life.

Destruction: Fighting between rival villain factions caused catastrophic damage and exposed the reach of the movement. The clash helped change an underground ideology into a broader paramilitary coalition. The city’s local population and injuries should not be reduced to mere scenery for one confrontation.

A concealed militant network among ordinary residents complicates assumptions about who is a combatant. Streets, civic buildings and business premises were used in the confrontation. Its scars illustrate the costs of ideological violence within a populated city, not merely damage to an enemy fortress.

cardPool.title: Lightly Labs
cardPool.value:
Organization: Lightly Labs

Description: Engineering company established by Mei Hatsume after her U.A. education. It develops advanced hero support technology and applies experimental design to real-world limitations. Mei’s work on Izuku Midoriya’s specialized hero suit demonstrates the importance of engineering alongside conventional Quirks.

Work: The company specializes in experimental support equipment and prototype development led by the inventor Mei Hatsume. Her workshop culture prizes testing, iteration and adapting inventions to a user’s movements, bodily limitations and tactical needs. Designs require calibration and repeated trial rather than emerging fully functional from imagination.

Postwar significance: Lightly Labs is associated with the technological project that restores Izuku Midoriya’s ability to serve actively as a hero without giving him a biological Quirk. Its work reflects a growing market for advanced protective systems. The company is a private design enterprise, not a second campus or an independent government agency.

Prototypes must be fitted to their users and tested under realistic movement, impacts and power conditions. A laboratory succeeds through design revision as well as bold invention. Its staff and tools contribute to the equipment industry without turning the company into a hero agency.

cardPool.title: GeL Inc.
cardPool.value:
Organization: GeL Inc.

Description: Company run by Gentle and La Brava following their rehabilitation. It represents their transition from online notoriety and criminal publicity seeking to a more constructive adult life. Gentle contributes unusual physical abilities and entrepreneurial flair; La Brava brings extraordinary technological ability. The enterprise is distinct from a licensed police agency.

Company: The enterprise is associated with Danjuro Tobita and Manami Aiba, who redirect their former flair for publicity and technical skill toward lawful work. Manami’s cybersecurity expertise gives the company a reputation for confronting digital crises. The name joins their former public identities without implying that either must continue criminal activity.

Place in society: The firm represents how people once dismissed as irredeemable can contribute after accountability and rehabilitation. Its employees and offices are not established in exhaustive detail; its identity is grounded in a legitimate company associated with the pair. No independent nationwide monopoly or secret armed force is established.

The firm’s cybersecurity reputation followed a period when hacking expertise was used to assist in a national emergency. Legitimate contracts differ fundamentally from the pair’s former illegal broadcasts. The business is known by its company name, without a fully documented catalogue of office locations or staff.

cardPool.title: Bakugo Hero Agency
cardPool.value:
Organization: Bakugo Hero Agency

Description: Professional hero agency led by Katsuki Bakugo, built around his aggressive combat style, heroic accomplishments and expanding leadership. His intimidating public manner and difficult interactions with cameras affect how the public perceives it. Bakugo attempted to invite Izuku Midoriya to work with him, but Izuku valued retaining his teaching responsibilities.

Agency character: Built around the public work of the explosively powerful Pro Hero Dynamight, the agency must manage field response, equipment and staff coordination as well as its leader’s confrontational manner. Strength in a battle does not eliminate scheduling, public trust or the need to cooperate with emergency services.

Adult history: Bakugo openly considers bringing Izuku into his professional operation and has an important role in the support-armor project. His professional standing fluctuates as citizens respond to both successful rescues and his harsh public behavior. The agency is separate from U.A. and from the broader collection of Class A alumni.

Hero agencies also need dispatch management, support staff and relationships with police and rescue teams. The leader’s explosive specialty may call for open terrain and careful evacuation before heavy action. His rivalry with another hero is personal history, not an agency-wide command doctrine.

cardPool.title: Uraraka Quirk Counseling Initiative
cardPool.value:
Organization: Uraraka Quirk Counseling Initiative

Description: Expanded counseling and education effort promoted by Ochaco Uraraka. It brings professional heroes to schools and prioritizes children whose Quirks or emotional circumstances may require support rather than punishment or neglect. Cooperation with Ingenium, Froppy and Creati helps normalize understanding of abilities and personal differences. Its objective is earlier intervention and a more compassionate civic environment.

Activities: Uraraka works with other professional heroes to visit elementary schools and improve access to guidance for young children with unusual powers. Their program combines reassurance, demonstrations and attention to students who might otherwise feel ashamed or misunderstood. Early help is meant to reduce harm before an unaddressed problem escalates.

Scope: The effort addresses both the practical control of abilities and the emotional circumstances surrounding them. It is a counseling and outreach initiative, not a combat unit or identified single building with a formal national chain of command. The work responds to lessons from the collapse of hero society while leaving room for local educators and specialists.

cardPool.title: Class 1-A Graduates
cardPool.value:
Organization: Class 1-A Graduates

Overview: Former students of U.A.’s Hero Course Class 1-A, who confronted the League of Villains and the Final War during their education. Many become Pro Heroes, while their careers diversify into teaching, counseling, independent agency work, and professional public service. Their relationships survive despite busy schedules, and their group funding makes Izuku’s return to hero work possible. Their former class membership is a shared history, not a single present-day command structure.

History and members: The class’s original core includes Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo, Ochaco Uraraka, Shoto Todoroki, Tenya Iida, Tsuyu Asui, Momo Yaoyorozu, Kirishima, Tokoyami and their peers. Yuga Aoyama voluntarily left school after the war to take responsibility for earlier wrongdoing; Hitoshi Shinso subsequently entered the class. Their shared past includes rescue exercises, school festivals and survival through several wars.

After graduation: Many work as licensed heroes, some with agencies or sidekick arrangements, while Izuku pursues teaching alongside field work. Adult careers make frequent gatherings difficult. They nevertheless maintain bonds and share funding and technical assistance for a suit that enables their Quirkless classmate to return to professional hero work. Class identity is social history rather than a permanent twenty-person tactical squad.

cardPool.title: Class 1-B Graduates
cardPool.value:
Organization: Class 1-B Graduates

Overview: Former U.A. students trained alongside Class 1-A in the same hero-course generation. Their group includes Neito Monoma and Juzo Honenuki, whose tactical talents attract increased public recognition. Old school rivalry can remain part of social banter, but alumni follow individual careers and agencies. They should not be depicted as present-day students or as subordinate to Class 1-A.

Training history: U.A.’s parallel hero-course class includes Neito Monoma, Juzo Honenuki, Itsuka Kendo, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, Setsuna Tokage, Manga Fukidashi and others with varied powers. The class engaged in joint training with Class A, developing its own strengths in teamwork, improvisation and Quirk combinations. Its homeroom teacher emphasized their success and encouraged spirited competition.

Professional life: Members pursued distinct licensed careers rather than serving under a single continuing class command. Monoma’s copying power and Honenuki’s terrain control contributed to high-profile operations and later professional recognition. School rivalry does not justify treating all graduates as hostile or subordinating their accomplishments to another class.

cardPool.title: Hero Public Safety Commission
cardPool.value:
Organization: Hero Public Safety Commission

Overview: National agency responsible for hero regulation and public-safety coordination. Earlier leadership relied on opaque covert tactics and sometimes sacrificed individuals for political stability. During postwar reforms, Hawks assumes a leadership role with a commitment to reducing the burden of violent hero work. The commission operates through institutions and policy rather than acting as a single Pro Hero.

Duties: The commission helps administer and regulate professional hero society, linking the licensed hero network with broader public policy. It has overseen responses to organized crime, confidential operations and the public image of heroes. It is an institution with personnel and procedures, not itself a Quirk or an individual fighter.

Record and reform: Earlier leadership recruited and controlled operatives for clandestine work, sometimes concealing the violence required to maintain a spotless public image. The death and exposure of senior figures opened space for new management. Under Keigo Takami the commission works toward a world that demands fewer constant violent confrontations, though administration cannot instantly erase historical damage.

cardPool.title: League of Villains
cardPool.value:
Organization: League of Villains

Overview: Criminal group that grew around Tomura Shigaraki and attracted outsiders rejected or wounded by society. Members included Himiko Toga, Dabi, Spinner, Twice and Mr. Compress, among others. Its campaigns escalated from targeted assaults to national destabilization and merger into a larger revolutionary network. The League’s core leadership was defeated in the Final War; it does not remain an intact active faction during the eight-year epilogue.

Composition: What began as a small alliance collected recruits with very different grievances, including alienation, personal cruelty, radical ideology and loyalty to Tomura Shigaraki. Members relied on coordinated ambushes, disguise, dangerous Quirk combinations and Kurogiri’s transport. Their connections could be sincere even while their actions harmed countless others.

History and end: The group assaulted U.A., abducted a student, struggled with rival criminal factions and eventually joined a much larger liberationist movement. Its members experienced death, capture and betrayal during the wars. By the adult period it is a defeated historical organization; individual survivors or their writings do not reconstitute a functioning national League.

cardPool.title: Paranormal Liberation Front
cardPool.value:
Organization: Paranormal Liberation Front

Overview: Massive villain coalition formed after the League of Villains defeated the Meta Liberation Army. It combined liberationist ideology, influential commercial resources and a widespread army under Tomura Shigaraki. Coordinated raids and uprisings inflicted enormous damage on hero society. Its wartime defeat and later repression leave lasting problems of radicalization and discrimination.

Structure: The coalition combined the League’s inner circle with the Meta Liberation Army’s vast infrastructure. Tomura Shigaraki held supreme command, with influential lieutenants and advisers coordinating different forces. Money, propaganda, businesses, hidden compounds and thousands of fighters gave the front nationwide reach.

Operations and collapse: Hero authorities discovered large connected centers of activity and launched simultaneous strikes. The conflict escalated into mass casualty warfare, prison crises and the near-breakdown of civilian confidence. The front’s defeat did not automatically eliminate the social anger and discrimination that some leaders exploited, but it ended its effectiveness as an organized revolutionary army.

Leadership and fighters came from two formerly separate groups and did not share identical motives. Liberationist commanders brought broad manpower and industry links, while Shigaraki’s closest companions focused on their own loyalties and destructive goals. The coalition’s enormous size made simultaneous law-enforcement action necessary.

cardPool.title: Meta Liberation Army
cardPool.value:
Organization: Meta Liberation Army

Overview: Clandestine organization advocating unrestrained use of Quirks and opposition to restrictive social norms. Re-Destro and allied executives built institutional influence before the group’s confrontation with the League of Villains. Its resources and followers were absorbed into the Paranormal Liberation Front. Its ideology cannot simply be equated with legitimate efforts to end heteromorph discrimination.

Ideology and resources: Inspired by Destro, the movement held that individuals should be free to use their Quirks without the restrictive norms imposed by modern government. Re-Destro built a network of executives, businesses, propaganda and dedicated followers. It presented itself as a liberation movement while preparing coercive, violent action on a massive scale.

Confrontation: The leadership invited the League of Villains into a trap at Deika, expecting to destroy the rival group. Instead, the battle devastated the city and ended with Re-Destro accepting Shigaraki’s authority. The resulting merger transformed the independent Army into one component of the Paranormal Liberation Front. Its extremist aims should not be conflated with peaceful disability or civil-rights advocacy.

cardPool.title: Wild, Wild Pussycats
cardPool.value:
Organization: Wild, Wild Pussycats

Overview: Professional rescue-hero team specializing in wilderness operations. Members include Mandalay, Pixie-Bob, Ragdoll and Tiger. Their teamwork, search capabilities and disaster preparation helped protect hero trainees during a forest training camp. The team is also part of Kota Izumi’s family and support network.

Team roles: Mandalay coordinates with telepathic messaging, Pixie-Bob alters the earth, Tiger specializes in close combat and Ragdoll was formerly able to Search for targets. The members combine wilderness rescue skills with unusually strong personal bonds and experience mentoring younger trainees. Their cat-themed presentation is deliberately cheerful and accessible.

Challenges: A violent training-camp attack placed the team and its young guests in severe danger. Ragdoll lost her Quirk after it was stolen but remained important to the team. Mandalay also cares for Kota Izumi, who lost his parents. The Pussycats are primarily rescuers and trainers; their identities do not depend on operating as a standing military force.

Ragdoll continued as a teammate despite losing Search, demonstrating that successful rescue teams rely on experience, planning and emotional support as well as powerful abilities. Their former camp site reflects the importance of wilderness preparedness when transport, terrain and communications become dangerous.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai
cardPool.value:
Organization: Shie Hassaikai

Overview: Criminal yakuza organization once led operationally by Kai Chisaki, also known as Overhaul. Its schemes involved exploiting Eri’s Rewind power to create Quirk-destroying ammunition and restore criminal authority. The group was dismantled and its leadership imprisoned. It is neither an active government agency nor an ordinary medical research organization.

Organization: An old yakuza group operated through debt, rank, loyalty and a reputation inherited from an earlier generation. Its aging boss was displaced in practice by Kai Chisaki, whose obsession with restoring criminal power drove a secret project involving Eri’s biological material. The group used specialized henchmen, restricted premises and clandestine distribution plans.

Fall: Pro Heroes and police traced its operation and raided the compound to free Eri and stop Quirk-destroying ammunition. Chisaki’s methods endangered even members supposedly under his protection. The raid ended the group’s ambitions and left its leader incapacitated. It is not a legitimate medical research company or an active hero agency in the adult era.

The group’s exploitation of Eri required secrecy and tight control over who could enter research areas. Criminal hierarchy did not protect its own subordinates from Chisaki’s violence. Police involvement was essential to gathering evidence and bringing the organization’s operations to an end.

cardPool.title: U.A. Faculty
cardPool.value:
Organization: U.A. Faculty

Overview: Teachers, administrators and support personnel responsible for educating future heroes and maintaining campus safety. Experienced heroes such as Shota Aizawa and Present Mic provide instruction, while All Might remains involved in school leadership. Izuku Midoriya joins the faculty in the postwar era. Teaching requires judgment, care and long-term student development rather than combat prowess alone.

Roles: The school employs educators with specializations in combat, rescue, academic study and support technology. Its familiar teachers include Shota Aizawa, Hizashi Yamada, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Snipe, Power Loader, Recovery Girl and others. Principal Nezu oversees the academy, with Toshinori Yagi serving in leadership in the later period. Faculty duties extend beyond fighting to student welfare and graduation decisions.

Experience: Teachers have protected students through campus assaults, mass evacuations and the Final War. Nemuri Kayama died during the earlier nationwide conflict and should be remembered as a former colleague rather than an active adult-era instructor. Veteran staff teach successive classes, balancing difficult practical assignments with the moral responsibility to keep children alive.

cardPool.title: Nomu
cardPool.value:
Organization: Nomu

Overview: Artificially modified beings created through human experimentation, often implanted with multiple Quirks. Many possess enhanced physical endurance, obedient conditioning and limited independent judgment. Higher-grade variants can show advanced intelligence and exceptionally dangerous adaptability. Nomu are a class of engineered subjects, not a conventional political faction. Their manufacture was associated with All For One and the doctor Kyudai Garaki.

Creation and varieties: Nomu are artificial beings built through severe modification and multiple Quirk implantation. Different examples range from relatively obedient low-level creatures to highly developed High-Ends with combat intelligence and exceptional physical ability. Surgical changes and regenerative factors can make them difficult for ordinary heroes to subdue.

Control and history: Their production relied on research associated with Kyudai Garaki and the All For One network. Some were designed as obedient shock troops while others retained fragments of personality or independent instincts. Kurogiri was an unusual case constructed around a deceased person’s remains. Nomu are not a naturally born animal species or a standard type of licensed professional hero.

cardPool.title: Pro Hero Licensing
cardPool.value:
Subject: Pro Hero Licensing

Context: Professional hero work is regulated by licensing, agencies, training standards and public accountability. U.A. students may receive provisional licenses during education; full careers demand years of development. Rankings and publicity influence employment but do not make a hero’s actions automatically ethical. Postwar policy increasingly values rescue, public education and social prevention alongside combat.

Legal framework: A person who wishes to act professionally as a hero must train, pass examinations and meet the licensing requirements for authorized response. Student provisional licenses allow supervised participation in specified situations. Heroes cooperate with police and other emergency services rather than having unlimited authority to attack anyone they suspect.

Practice and responsibility: Schools prepare candidates in teamwork, communication, rescue assessment and nonlethal capture. Licenses and hero status involve public accountability, and powers can be dangerous if used without considering bystanders. A civilian reaching out to help another person can display heroism without automatically acquiring official police powers.

Training alone does not entitle an ordinary person to disregard local law. Formal hero work generally demands recognized credentials, coordination and appropriate responsibility for casualties and property damage. Temporary student authorization differs from unrestricted professional status.

cardPool.title: Hero Billboard Chart
cardPool.value:
Subject: Hero Billboard Chart

Context: Public ranking of Pro Heroes that reflects reputation, contribution and effectiveness. Mirio Togata leads the adult-era chart, followed in the reunion-era ranking by Shoto Todoroki, Mt. Lady, Kamui Woods and Best Jeanist. Subsequent developments place Izuku Midoriya fourth and Katsuki Bakugo fifth, showing that standings change over time. A chart position is not a numerical measurement of sheer combat strength.

Ranking criteria: Professional heroes are listed according to a combination of achievement, public reputation and service, not a simple contest of combat strength. Positions respond to changing public attitudes and noteworthy rescues. A highly skilled hero can rank below someone more popular, and a sharp temperament can depress popularity despite extraordinary performance.

Later standings: In the adult period Mirio Togata holds first and Shoto Todoroki second, with Mt. Lady third. One public snapshot lists Kamui Woods fourth and Best Jeanist fifth while Bakugo sits fifteenth. A subsequent chart places the armor-equipped Deku fourth and Dynamight fifth, with the top three unchanged. The snapshots are sequential, not contradictory simultaneous rankings.

cardPool.title: Heteromorph Discrimination
cardPool.value:
Subject: Heteromorph Discrimination

Context: People with visibly nonhuman body types can face segregation, harassment, violence and exclusion. This prejudice contributed to widespread unrest and extremist recruitment. Mezo Shoji’s work emphasizes dialogue, dignity and meaningful action against hatred; public recognition of his efforts symbolizes a broader struggle. Not every heteromorph supports extremist politics, and appearances do not predict morality.

Nature of the harm: People whose Quirks permanently change their faces or bodies may experience exclusion from public spaces, social hostility and open violence. These traits do not turn a person into a criminal or reveal what they believe. Prejudice can flourish in isolated communities even where major urban districts claim to be more tolerant.

Response: Extremist organizers exploited real grievances to encourage violent confrontation, while other heteromorphs chose rescue, public dialogue and patient reform.
