Mezo Shoji’s actions and the resulting recognition highlight the difference between opposing prejudice and targeting innocent people. The problem requires lasting social change rather than one dramatic victory.

The problem often concerns ordinary moments, including whether a family can safely move through a neighborhood or whether a child feels welcome in school. Public recognition of activists and rescuers matters, but lasting improvement also requires a change in everyday behavior.

cardPool.title: Quirk Counseling
cardPool.value:
Subject: Quirk Counseling

Context: Support and guidance for children and adults adapting to innate superhuman traits, unusual bodily needs and social rejection. Inadequate counseling can compound fear, shame and dangerous habits, especially when powers involve biological compulsion. Ochaco Uraraka promotes school outreach and wider access to early assistance so support can begin before crises become violent.

Purpose: Counseling helps children understand the strengths, triggers and potential dangers of their individual powers. Some abilities are difficult to suppress, linked to biological urges or highly visible in ways that draw hostility. Early guidance should involve safety education, emotional support and appropriate professional help without teaching a child that their nature makes them monstrous.

Historical failings: Excessive pressure to appear normal and a lack of informed support left some children isolated and ashamed. Social rejection can worsen a dangerous situation long before violence occurs. Expanded school outreach encourages guardians and educators to notice distress, seek practical accommodations and hear what the child is actually trying to say.

An effective counselor distinguishes between dangerous conduct and a trait the child did not choose. Practical support may mean control training, a safe place to express distress or helping adults understand unfamiliar physiology. Treating shame alone as discipline can make the problem worse.

cardPool.title: Postwar Hero Society
cardPool.value:
Subject: Postwar Hero Society

Context: Following the defeat of All For One and the collapse of his criminal networks, Japan rebuilds damaged communities and its public institutions. Fewer new villains emerge, yet the work of heroes expands beyond battles to include education, prevention, rescue, reconciliation and addressing prejudice. Civilians are increasingly recognized as active participants in protecting one another. Remaining suffering and discrimination are not assumed to have vanished overnight.

Civic transition: Mass rebuilding demanded coordinated effort from heroes, medical workers, engineers, volunteers and ordinary residents. As organized villain attacks decline, emergencies do not disappear; rescue, counseling, prevention and community trust take a larger share of public attention. Hero status remains professional, but the idea of helping is no longer confined to a famous individual.

Institutional limits: The loss of an old Symbol of Peace revealed how fragile a society becomes when everyone assumes one person will handle its dangers. Reform efforts address discrimination and poor early intervention as well as security. Work remains unfinished, and reduced villain statistics do not mean poverty, hostility and family suffering have vanished.

cardPool.title: Support Technology
cardPool.value:
Subject: Support Technology

Context: Engineered equipment can complement Quirks, compensate for disability or give Quirkless people ways to work as heroes. Advances include adaptive prosthetics, armor, sensing systems, mobility supports and specialized training hardware. Equipment is subject to maintenance, durability, energy and cost limitations. It is not a biological Quirk and does not automatically reproduce every power it imitates.

Categories: The industry produces mobility systems, reinforced costumes, environmental sensors, rescue tools, prostheses, communication devices and weapons designed around individual fighting styles. Equipment can protect a body from its own Quirk or allow a person with an impaired ability to regain practical independence. Inventors collaborate with combat professionals to refine fit, handling and durability.

Engineering limits: A complex prototype takes testing and funding, while field use requires repairs, replacement parts and training. Mechanical devices may imitate the outcome of some Quirks without creating or restoring their biological factor. The development of sophisticated armor for a Quirkless professional demonstrates technological possibilities rather than proof that the former inherited power returned.

cardPool.title: One For All Vestiges
cardPool.value:
Subject: One For All Vestiges

Context: One For All carried impressions of previous holders inside a shared inner realm. These vestiges preserved memories and provided guidance or resistance to outside control. Their existence was tied to the Quirk’s accumulated factors, and their sacrifice during the final struggle ended Izuku’s access to the inherited abilities. They are not ordinary living people residing permanently in the adult-era physical world.

Inner landscape: The shared accumulated factor preserved impressions of successive bearers, often appearing as distinct figures with memories and advice. The space where they communicated was connected to the inherited power itself; it was not a physical room anyone could enter by ordinary travel. Some vestiges represented predecessors with individual Quirks that later became accessible.

Final conflict: These imprints could resist attempts at domination and ultimately served as a way to confront the hatred inside Tomura Shigaraki. Their deliberate transfer came with the destruction of Izuku’s natural access to the stockpiled inheritance. They should not appear as freely available, independent ghosts who can restore One For All by simply choosing a new vessel.

cardPool.title: Deku Support Suit
cardPool.value:
Item: Deku Support Suit

Overview: Advanced powered armor developed by Mei Hatsume and Melissa Shield, drawing on data gathered from All Might’s prior armored battle. Class 1-A alumni funded its construction, with Katsuki Bakugo instrumental in supporting the project. The suit allows Quirkless Izuku Midoriya to resume frontline rescue and hero work while he continues teaching. Its precise capabilities depend on engineered systems rather than an authentic restoration of One For All. It remains subject to technological constraints, durability and maintenance.

Design: The powered system combines protective plating, movement support and combat-response capabilities informed by accumulated data from advanced armor used in a major battle. It was engineered through international collaboration and financed by alumni who understood its intended user’s reflexes and style. The device is a mechanical platform rather than a Quirk factor.

Operation: The suit allows a skilled user without an innate power to join dangerous rescue work while relying on learned fighting tactics and situational awareness. Its exact inventory of weapons and duplicate Quirk effects is not completely documented; it should not be credited with every ability once possessed through One For All. Components may wear out or require repair, and being issued a suit does not eliminate physical risk.

cardPool.title: Armored All Might Suit
cardPool.value:
Item: Armored All Might Suit

Overview: Specialized armored fighting system used by Toshinori Yagi against All For One after his retirement from ordinary superpowered hero work. Its many tools were inspired by the abilities and experiences of Class 1-A, using engineering rather than restored One For All energy. Battle data from this equipment helped inspire the later suit built for Izuku. Its original wartime configuration should not be confused with Izuku’s newer armor.

Configuration: A high-grade technological combat system assembled to let an experienced but Quirkless former hero resist a vastly stronger adversary. It employs multiple specialized tools designed around the tactics of young hero students. These modules compensate for human limitations through protective structure, mobility and carefully timed countermeasures.

History and limitations: It was used under desperate conditions and suffered extreme destruction in combat. Its data later informed more advanced protective equipment for another Quirkless hero. The armor could be broken and its systems depleted; the original wearer’s past One For All strength was not restored by putting it on.

A number of battle functions drew inspiration from recognizable student abilities, letting its wearer respond to diverse threats through modular devices. The equipment was never as durable as the original Symbol of Peace himself, and successful use relied on extensive knowledge of an opponent’s habits.

cardPool.title: Mirko Prosthetic Limbs
cardPool.value:
Item: Mirko Prosthetic Limbs

Overview: Advanced replacement limbs used by Rumi Usagiyama after the loss of multiple natural limbs during major battles. They preserve a degree of explosive mobility appropriate to her uncompromising fighting style and are repeatedly upgraded. Their performance comes from engineering and personal training, not regeneration granted by the Rabbit Quirk.

Function: Artificial limbs restore mechanical leverage and combat movement after devastating amputations. Strong anchoring and repeated adjustments are essential to survive abrupt landings, kicks and rapid shifts in position. The hero’s body must adapt to the altered weight and contact points through intensive physical training.

Limits: A prosthetic can break, jam or need replacement after a hard fight. Designs may be upgraded as engineers learn more about the wearer’s movement, but they are not equivalent to biological regeneration. Mirko’s natural Rabbit Quirk and her engineered replacement limbs perform different roles in her fighting style.

Connection points must withstand tremendous impact when the wearer lands from a powerful leap. Repeated replacement and upgrades are part of the equipment’s history. A well-designed prosthetic preserves agency and mobility, but it can still be damaged independently of the remaining natural limbs.

cardPool.title: Shinso Voice Persona Chords
cardPool.value:
Item: Shinso Voice Persona Chords

Overview: Specialized voice-altering equipment allowing Hitoshi Shinso to imitate other people’s speech. Used with Brainwashing, it increases his ability to draw verbal responses from targets who know his powers. Voice imitation alone does not control anyone; the target must respond and the Quirk’s usual conditions still apply.

Mechanism: A voice-modifying apparatus worn near the mouth changes spoken sound into the recognizable voice of another person. It can draw a reply from someone who would refuse to answer Hitoshi Shinso directly. The equipment does not release mind-altering waves; the relevant Quirk must still activate through verbal response.

Operational cautions: Visual identification, suspicion and barriers to conversation can defeat the deception. The mask requires functional electronics and sufficiently intelligible speech. It is best combined with capture cloth, positioning and a plan for preventing a shocked target from immediately breaking free.

Its effect is most reliable when the target believes a familiar person is speaking. A wary listener who refuses to answer cannot be compelled merely by a convincing recording or disguise. The voice apparatus is useful in combination with the user’s restraint equipment.

cardPool.title: Aoyama Navel Laser Belt
cardPool.value:
Item: Aoyama Navel Laser Belt

Overview: Focusing equipment worn by Yuga Aoyama to channel laser output from his abdomen. It helps direct a biologically troublesome power and forms a prominent part of his hero costume. The device is not the source of his Quirk, and removal does not make his body naturally compatible with the ability.

Construction: The waist device surrounds the abdomen and directs a powerful beam from the body through an external focusing mechanism. It is a support item worn with other metallic and white hero-costume components, not an artificial gun whose power exists without the user. The equipment helps manage a difficult and painful Quirk.

Limitations: Increasing firing time does not eliminate digestive upset or the strain of mismatched biology. A damaged belt may interfere with aiming and allow dangerous leakage. Repairs and costume integrity matter, but replacing the device does not grant or remove the underlying Navel Laser factor.

The belt is visible at the center of his armored presentation and must stay aligned with the abdominal emission. A beam misdirected at close range can endanger nearby structures. The device supports control of the inherited-in-practice ability rather than serving as its actual source.

cardPool.title: Quirk-Destroying Bullets
cardPool.value:
Item: Quirk-Destroying Bullets

Overview: Special ammunition manufactured through the abuse of Eri’s Rewind biological material by the Shie Hassaikai. Their purpose was to attack Quirk factors rather than inflict ordinary ballistic injury alone. Both temporary and more lasting formulations were pursued. The project relied on coercion, secrecy and violence and was not a legitimate medical intervention.

Origin: The Shie Hassaikai developed these drugs from biological material associated with Rewind, exploiting a captive child to attack the Quirk factor of a target. Different formulations could temporarily suppress or, in the perfected form, permanently destroy normal access to a Quirk. The substance’s effects are not ordinary bullet trauma.

Aftereffects: Mirio Togata lost use of Permeation after being struck and later regained it through Eri’s power. The production process was brutally abusive and depended on secret research. Possession does not confer surgical control over a chosen Quirk, and their original manufacturing chain was dismantled rather than becoming an accepted public medical technique.

Although their project promised power over the hero profession, the underlying method depended on destructive interference with biology. Both the criminal supply chain and the victims’ treatment are distinct matters: ending manufacture did not immediately reverse injuries already caused.

cardPool.title: Rise of All Might
cardPool.value:
Event: Rise of All Might

Overview: Toshinori Yagi inherits One For All from Nana Shimura and dedicates his life to fighting organized villainy. His public image as the Symbol of Peace helps reduce fear and crime while also creating unrealistic dependence on a single extraordinary protector. His long struggle with All For One changes both national hero culture and the lives of their successors.

Before the peak of his career, Toshinori was trained by Nana Shimura and Gran Torino and learned that great strength carries responsibility as well as danger. His public rescues and repeated victories against organized crime persuaded many civilians that someone would always arrive with a smile. The number of open threats receded as he became the nation’s most visible protector.

Hidden consequences: His duel with All For One left lasting internal injuries that eventually restricted the time he could maintain his famous muscular appearance. The public rarely understood how fragile that symbol had become. The resulting culture celebrated exceptional individuals but struggled to share responsibility among ordinary people and institutions.

The Symbol of Peace’s reassuring smile became a cultural expectation, influencing advertising, education and young people who dreamed of wearing a hero costume. Yet peace built around a single body had hidden weaknesses. Succession therefore became a matter not only of strength but of teaching others to protect each other.

cardPool.title: U.A. Training Camp Attack
cardPool.value:
Event: U.A. Training Camp Attack

Overview: The League of Villains attacks students and professional instructors during a forest training camp. The assault places young heroes in deadly danger, leaves Kota Izumi deeply affected and results in Katsuki Bakugo’s abduction. The incident exposes the limits of ordinary school security and accelerates conflict between public institutions and organized villains.

A wilderness training program assembled first-year hero students under professional supervision. League attackers infiltrated the area, setting fires and launching separate assaults that scattered trainees and mentors. Several students fought to escape or protect nearby children despite limited experience and serious injuries.

The attackers’ principal goal included capturing Katsuki Bakugo, believing his fierce temperament made him recruitable. Their success triggered a hostage crisis and a police-hero operation to recover him. Public concern over student safety intensified, influencing the later decision to house students under closer campus protection.

The crisis showed that even supervised training could become a violent incursion and that teachers could not be everywhere at once. The students’ attempts to protect one another mattered alongside licensed intervention. What followed was a broader argument about institutional responsibility for children placed near danger.

cardPool.title: Kamino Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Kamino Incident

Overview: Professional heroes confront the League of Villains and All For One in Kamino. All Might defeats his old enemy in a decisive public battle but expends the remaining capacity of One For All. His retirement brings the end of the Symbol of Peace era and a new sense of insecurity. A memorial later transforms the location into a symbol of shared courage.

Heroes and police raided League positions to retrieve the abducted student. The confrontation drew out All For One, whose overwhelming collection of Quirks turned a neighborhood into a public battleground. All Might fought beyond his failing limits while other heroes focused on evacuation and preventing further destruction.

All Might ultimately defeated All For One with the final power he could muster and then publicly revealed he could no longer serve as the same superhuman protector. His declaration that the next generation must carry on reshaped national expectations. Kamino became both a site of enormous destruction and the location of a later memorial.

Ordinary people witnessed both the extraordinary force of the final fight and the exhaustion of the hero they had depended on for years. The battle’s aftermath therefore changed civic expectations even in places far from Kamino. Criminal organizations sensed an opening, while other heroes were forced to organize without a single guaranteed protector.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai Raid
cardPool.value:
Event: Shie Hassaikai Raid

Overview: Pro Heroes, police and students investigate and assault the Shie Hassaikai to rescue Eri and stop the manufacture of Quirk-destroying ammunition. The operation causes casualties and serious injuries, while exposing how criminal enterprise exploited a child’s power. The experience shapes Izuku and Mirio’s later responsibilities.

Investigation linked the yakuza to trafficking in ammunition capable of suppressing or erasing Quirks. A joint police and hero response entered the Hassaikai compound, navigating changing corridors, hidden rooms and dangerous defenders. Rescuers sought Eri while attempting to stop production without needlessly harming her or other captives.

Mirio Togata lost his Quirk while defending Eri, and Sir Nighteye died from injuries suffered in the raid. Izuku confronted Kai Chisaki after Eri escaped his control. The operation exposed the cruelty behind the group’s medical-sounding project and eventually opened a path for Eri to live under protective care.

The operation involved careful intelligence work before the assault. Participants had to choose between advancing against dangerous villains and keeping a traumatized captive safe. The casualties demonstrated that a victory in a criminal investigation can still carry lasting personal costs.

cardPool.title: Deika Liberation Conflict
cardPool.value:
Event: Deika Liberation Conflict

Overview: The League of Villains confronts the Meta Liberation Army in Deika City. Intense fighting devastates the region and strengthens Tomura Shigaraki’s destructive capabilities. After the battle, defeated liberationist leaders join forces with the League, helping create the Paranormal Liberation Front and escalating the threat beyond isolated gangs.

Meta Liberation Army leaders challenged the League of Villains in a city where many inhabitants were already aligned with their movement. Fighting spread among streets and buildings as the rival factions revealed dangerous abilities and personal histories. Enormous civilian and structural losses followed.

Shigaraki’s destructive Quirk reached an unprecedented scale and the Army’s leader accepted his power rather than continue futile resistance. The merger brought the League a broad network of fighters, financing and propaganda. The resulting Paranormal Liberation Front became much more difficult for public authorities to confront.

Powerful executives had relied on the support of ordinary-looking civic institutions and local followers. Their defeat did not dissolve that infrastructure; instead, much of it came under new leadership. The transition turned a battle between two criminal factions into a prelude to national-scale war.

cardPool.title: Paranormal Liberation War
cardPool.value:
Event: Paranormal Liberation War

Overview: A nationwide hero offensive targets the Paranormal Liberation Front and the hospital where Tomura Shigaraki is being altered. The battle unleashes multiple Nomu and causes widespread destruction, deaths and public distrust. Midnight dies and several leading heroes suffer grievous injuries. The ensuing collapse of confidence produces mass evacuations and violent unrest.

Professional heroes, police and trained students launched raids on a mountain assembly point and a hospital complex supporting the Front. The operation was intended to interrupt Shigaraki’s experimental transformation and arrest leaders before their forces could mobilize. Instead, numerous Nomu were released, giant combatants ravaged populated areas and Shigaraki’s Decay spread across the terrain.

Casualties included the hero Midnight and many civilians. Survivors such as Endeavor, Hawks, Eraser Head and Mirko sustained lasting injuries or losses. Public revelations about crimes, hero misconduct and the scale of disaster contributed to mass distrust, prison escapes and widespread demands for answers.

Large-scale evacuation and the spread of destructive powers made saving residents as urgent as subduing commanders. The conflict destroyed faith in several formerly admired institutions. A growing population of frightened evacuees needed food, shelter and medical care even after the frontline withdrew.

cardPool.title: Dark Hero Period
cardPool.value:
Event: Dark Hero Period

Overview: After mass prison breaks and mounting public anxiety, Izuku operates apart from his classmates while pursuing those connected to All For One. Exhaustion and self-sacrifice threaten his wellbeing. Former classmates intervene, demonstrating that communal support is necessary even for the most powerful protector. Public attitudes toward sheltering vulnerable heroes begin to shift.

With society frightened and villain attacks multiplying, Izuku left the shelter of ordinary school life to track enemies linked to All For One. He worked with remaining professionals while steadily exhausting his own health and avoiding friends to keep them from danger. His isolation embodied the old belief that a sufficiently strong hero must carry everything alone.

His classmates confronted him, refusing to abandon him simply because he wanted to protect them. They persuaded him to return to U.A., where frightened evacuees initially resisted sheltering him. Public compassion gradually outweighed suspicion. The period exposed why trust and shared responsibility mattered as much as victory in a fight.

Public fear made even well-meaning shelter operations politically tense. The returning hero was exhausted, dirty and physically endangered, undermining the familiar image of a triumphant savior. The intervention of friends and civilians challenged the assumption that a protector must always appear invulnerable.

cardPool.title: Final War
cardPool.value:
Event: Final War

Overview: Heroes launch a coordinated effort to separate All For One’s forces and prevent his schemes from succeeding. Many groups battle across Japan. Izuku confronts Tomura Shigaraki and sacrifices One For All in an attempt to reach the person beneath the villain’s hatred. Other clashes leave extensive injury and loss, including final confrontations involving the Todoroki family and Himiko Toga. All For One and Tomura are defeated and the surviving communities begin recovery.

A coordinated hero plan separated the main enemy forces into different battlefields so they could not easily combine their strengths. Conflicts took place over fortified arenas, cities and evacuation routes. Fighters faced All For One, Shigaraki, major Nomu and other remaining leaders while civilians and support workers contributed information, engineering and emergency aid.

Ochaco reached Himiko Toga but could not prevent her death; Shoto and his family stopped Toya’s self-destruction at immense personal cost. Katsuki returned from severe injury and fought in the wider final struggle. Izuku attempted to save the abused person beneath Shigaraki’s hatred, sacrificing the inheritable power of One For All. All For One’s last bid for control failed, and Shigaraki died.

cardPool.title: Reconstruction and Graduation
cardPool.value:
Event: Reconstruction and Graduation

Overview: The years immediately following the Final War involve funerals, rebuilding, rehabilitation, social reckoning and the completion of disrupted schooling. U.A. students continue training while grieving their losses. Izuku’s last One For All embers fade by graduation, and he eventually finds a vocation teaching future heroes.

International support and local volunteers joined professional teams clearing damaged neighborhoods and restoring transport, schools and homes. Survivors mourned lost people while injured heroes underwent prolonged treatment. U.A. resumed lessons and held delayed graduation activities, but the experience changed how its students understood future responsibilities.

Yuga Aoyama chose to leave school and begin earning his place independently after admitting his role as an unwilling informant. Hitoshi Shinso transferred into the hero class in his place. Over subsequent years, former pupils became licensed professionals while Izuku’s temporary embers faded. Education, rehabilitation and new careers unfolded alongside the slower work of social repair.

School resumed despite damage, grief and uncomfortable questions about hero culture. Some graduates continued frontline careers, while others were drawn to technology, education and outreach. Their professional choices reflect the many kinds of work necessary to keep a rebuilt community secure.

cardPool.title: Eight Years After the Final War
cardPool.value:
Event: Eight Years After the Final War

Overview: Approximately eight years after the decisive conflict, former Class 1-A students pursue professional careers and public-service work. Izuku Midoriya teaches at U.A. while many classmates work as Pro Heroes. Mirio Togata leads the ranking, Shoto Todoroki rises to second and Ochaco Uraraka expands Quirk counseling. Hero society seeks prevention and social care rather than celebrating battle alone.

Around eight years after the war, many former U.A. classmates are working as adults. The supply of new villains is lower, making the hero profession more competitive while opening possibilities in teaching, research and prevention. Mirio leads the professional chart and Shoto takes second place, while Ochaco expands school-based guidance on Quirks.

Izuku works as a U.A. teacher after losing One For All. New students arrive with worries about whether their small gifts are enough to help anyone. Rather than celebrating combat power alone, society increasingly recognizes ordinary intervention, assistance and care. An advanced suit eventually enables Izuku to return to active work without abandoning his profession as an educator.

Public aspirations begin shifting: children can imagine becoming engineers, clinicians or technical specialists rather than treating Pro Hero rankings as the only meaningful measure of success. Helping a stranger remains the simplest example of responsibility even as the professional world changes.

cardPool.title: Class 1-A Reunion
cardPool.value:
Event: Class 1-A Reunion

Overview: Former classmates gather to recognize Shoto Todoroki’s number-two ranking. Their conversation reveals different professional pressures, including Katsuki Bakugo’s volatile popularity and Izuku Midoriya’s intention to remain a teacher. Izuku and Ochaco Uraraka mutually acknowledge a desire to spend more time together. The gathering highlights lasting friendship without suggesting every graduate has the same career or relationship.

The former classmates gather to congratulate Shoto on reaching second place among professional heroes. Conversation turns from hero rankings to daily schedules, agency work and how falling rates of villain attacks are changing their jobs. Katsuki’s poor public relations contrast with his skills, and Izuku insists he likes teaching even after obtaining equipment for fieldwork.

Shoto expresses interest in enjoying ordinary parts of life, including creating bowls and chopsticks for soba. Ochaco reflects on the person she lost during the war and the emotional distance imposed by busy adult lives. Afterward, Izuku says he wants more chances to speak with her; they hold hands and move toward a closer personal bond. No wedding or publicly declared marriage follows from that exchange.

cardPool.title: Deku Returns to Hero Work
cardPool.value:
Event: Deku Returns to Hero Work

Overview: Class 1-A alumni fund an advanced suit developed by Mei Hatsume and Melissa Shield for their Quirkless former classmate. All Might delivers the equipment to Izuku, who resumes active Pro Hero work without abandoning teaching. Later hero rankings place him fourth, while Katsuki Bakugo rises to fifth. This development marks a technological path to heroism rather than the return of his lost biological inheritance.

Years of research into powered combat equipment build on data gathered during All Might’s desperate armored confrontation. Melissa Shield and Mei Hatsume collaborate on a new advanced system while former Class A members supply the funding, with Katsuki Bakugo strongly involved. All Might presents the finished equipment to Izuku as a way to act on his enduring desire to help people.

Izuku becomes active in professional operations alongside his teaching responsibilities. The suit provides mechanical abilities; the vanished One For All factor does not return. As the public sees his renewed work, a later Hero Billboard Chart places Deku fourth and Dynamight fifth, following Lemillion, Shoto and Mt. Lady.

The timing matters: the armor arrives years after the original power disappears, making the return the product of research and friendship rather than hidden stockpiled energy. The later ranking reflects actual public response to his professional activity, not a retrospective award for his earlier exploits.

cardPool.title: Toya Todoroki Final Years
cardPool.value:
Event: Toya Todoroki Final Years

Overview: After suffering catastrophic injuries in the Final War, Toya Todoroki remains in severe medical condition. His surviving family members confront their painful history while recognizing that neither apologies nor sacrifice can undo decades of harm. Toya dies during the years before the adult reunion, leaving the family to reckon with grief and the consequences of his choices.

After the war, Toya remains alive but severely damaged inside a special medical care unit. Speaking is painful and limited; his family is given only short opportunities to see him. Enji acknowledges the harm of his earlier treatment and promises visits without demanding forgiveness. Shoto learns that Toya also likes soba, a small connection made when almost no time remains.

Toya eventually dies before the eight-year reunion. The family mourns him while its surviving members continue making their own choices: atonement, distance, employment and new relationships do not all follow the same path. His death does not retroactively excuse his violence or erase the abuse that helped shape it.

No single meeting reconciles the family. Medical confinement permits only brief communication, and the surviving relatives differ in what they can forgive. By the time of the adult gathering, a memorial has replaced direct visits, making grief part of everyday life rather than a conflict that simply vanishes.

cardPool.title: Jin Bubaigawara
cardPool.value:
Name: Jin Bubaigawara

Age: 31 (at death)

Alias: Twice

Occupation: Deceased former League of Villains member

Abilities: Double created complete duplicates of people or objects when the user knew their measurements. Copies could multiply in large numbers; each was less durable than the original.

Personality: Jin was talkative, theatrical and frequently spoke in contradicting pairs of statements, as if arguing with himself. A terrible incident involving his own duplicates left him unsure whether he was the original, and this fear fed profound anxiety about personal identity. He was capable of petty crime and serious violence but also showed warmth toward people who treated him with acceptance. His friendship with Himiko Toga and loyalty to the League were unusually sincere. He could be terrified of being alone yet determined to risk everything for comrades.

Appearance: An adult man with a lean frame, messy blond hair and a small amount of facial hair. His villain attire was a tight black bodysuit with pale markings and a mask covering most of his face, leaving only the eyes visible. He sometimes removed the covering but feared losing control of his sense of self. His jerky gestures, changing tone of voice and restless posture contrasted with unexpectedly careful behavior toward injured companions. He was usually seen in equipment that allowed movement rather than heavy armor.

Background: His power became a serious strategic threat once he overcame fear of his own copies. He died during the period preceding the nationwide war; his loss deeply affected surviving allies.

cardPool.title: Mirai Sasaki
cardPool.value:
Name: Mirai Sasaki

Age: 38 (at death)

Alias: Sir Nighteye

Occupation: Deceased Pro Hero and former sidekick of All Might

Abilities: Foresight let him view a target’s future after specified contact and eye contact, with strict time limits and conditions. He also fought using specially weighted seals and precise tactics.

Personality: Mirai was austere, sharply analytical and unusually demanding of people who joined his agency. He prized humor in heroes but expressed that preference through severe and sometimes intimidating tests. He believed public reassurance required deliberate preparation rather than empty smiles. His painful disagreement with All Might arose from fear for the older hero’s survival, and it left him reluctant to accept optimistic promises. Despite a controlled demeanor he cared intensely for Mirio Togata, Bubble Girl and the people whose futures he wanted to improve.

Appearance: He was a tall, slim adult with a long angular face, narrow eyes, tidy dark hair and square glasses. He usually wore a fitted office suit, tie and clean gloves rather than a flashy hero uniform, carrying himself like a disciplined businessman. His expression was stern and often unreadable; a small change in his brows could signal disapproval. His precision and self-control made sudden movement with a weighted seal more startling than a loud fighting pose.

Background: He served as All Might’s sidekick before founding an independent agency. During the raid on the Shie Hassaikai, he sustained fatal injuries. His final words helped encourage Mirio’s future.

cardPool.title: Nezu
cardPool.value:
Name: Nezu

Alias: Principal Nezu

Occupation: Principal of U.A. High School

Abilities: High Specs grants exceptional intelligence and reasoning ability. His small animal body requires tailored equipment and cannot be confused with the human anatomy of most faculty.

Personality: Nezu is courteous, playful and intellectually formidable, frequently speaking in a tone that makes serious analysis sound almost whimsical. He enjoys elaborate tests of reasoning and tends to plan several layers ahead. His understanding of cruel experimentation gives him a deeply personal concern for how society treats beings perceived as unusual. He believes education needs strong protection but also sees the value of students making decisions under pressure. His manner can be intimidating when his sophisticated plans unfold, though he remains committed to the institution under his care.

Appearance: He is a small, white-furred mammalian figure with a pointed muzzle, dark eyes, rounded ears and a long tail. He often wears an immaculate suit, vest and shoes sized for his proportions, sometimes carrying a cup of tea. His body language is animated and expressive, combining the appearance of a friendly animal with a dignified administrator. Nothing about his size suggests the speed with which he can process complex problems.

Background: Nezu oversees U.A. through attacks, evacuations, expansion of defensive infrastructure and later rebuilding. His responsibilities include staff leadership, educational standards and student safety.

cardPool.title: Itsuka Kendo
cardPool.value:
Name: Itsuka Kendo

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Battle Fist

Occupation: Pro Hero; former U.A. Class 1-B student

Abilities: Big Fist enlarges both hands to huge size, increasing their usefulness in striking, restraint and shielding. It does not enlarge the entire body.

Personality: Itsuka is outgoing, sensible and dependable, frequently acting as a counterweight when classmates become competitive or arrogant. She has a strong sense of fair play and wants the people around her to perform well rather than simply humiliating a rival class. Her calm leadership becomes especially apparent during emergencies, where she delegates tasks and keeps people focused. She can be stern with Neito Monoma when his taunting gets out of hand, but her corrections come from familiarity rather than contempt. Practical compassion matters more to her than drawing applause.

Appearance: She is a tall, athletic young woman with a strong posture, turquoise eyes and orange hair tied in a high ponytail. Her hero clothing includes a dark, Chinese-influenced outfit designed to leave room for the rapid expansion of her hands. Her gestures are confident and her expressions direct; she tends to meet an opponent or nervous teammate head-on. The enlarged fists become enormous compared with her ordinary arms when her Quirk is active.

Background: She trained with Class 1-B and took part in the defense of hero society. Her professional ranking at the adult gathering was twenty-third.

cardPool.title: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu
cardPool.value:
Name: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Real Steel

Occupation: Pro Hero; former U.A. Class 1-B student

Abilities: Steel transforms the body into tough metal, supporting powerful physical combat and protection against impact. Prolonged exertion and heat impose limitations.

Personality: Tetsutetsu is loud, passionate and eager to prove himself in direct competition. He admires people with steadfast courage and is quick to treat a rival as a friend after a fair contest. His straightforward manner can appear reckless, yet he does not shy away from protecting someone when an attack would injure them. He believes in training through effort and physical endurance, and his uncomplicated enthusiasm can motivate quieter teammates. He is more comfortable charging toward a clear threat than performing prolonged deception.

Appearance: He is a broad-shouldered, muscular young man with spiky pale gray hair, dark eyes and a square, strongly expressive face. His appearance resembles a rough, energetic fighter even without using his Quirk. When transformed, his body takes on a metallic texture and shine. His hero gear is rugged and built for direct close-range movement rather than elaborate long-distance weapons.

Background: He belonged to U.A.’s parallel hero class and later entered professional hero work. His adult ranking at the reunion-era chart was twenty-sixth.

cardPool.title: Chiyo Shuzenji
cardPool.value:
Name: Chiyo Shuzenji

Alias: Recovery Girl

Occupation: U.A. school nurse and healing specialist

Abilities: Heal accelerates a patient’s natural healing processes through a kiss but consumes the patient’s stamina and cannot reliably overcome every critical injury.

Personality: Chiyo is practical, affectionate and capable of sharp reprimands when students take foolish risks. She does not confuse bravery with reckless self-injury and has repeatedly warned ambitious hero trainees against relying on medical recovery as an excuse to destroy their bodies. Her warmth appears through diligent treatment, stern advice and a willingness to speak honestly to celebrated heroes. The limits of her work make her more mindful of recovery time than people who imagine healing as magic. She values the ordinary discipline of proper first aid and rest.

Appearance: She is a very short elderly woman with pale gray hair arranged in small curls, a lined face and large dark eyes behind her medical headwear. Her white and pink nurse’s clothing and cane form a familiar part of U.A.’s infirmary. She often appears kindly at first glance, then fixes an injured student with a forbidding expression when she hears how the accident occurred. Her small body does not prevent her from being authoritative.

Background: She has treated generations of U.A. students, including those injured by rigorous hero training. Her ability is important but never substitutes for extensive medical care following extreme trauma.

cardPool.title: Naomasa Tsukauchi
cardPool.value:
Name: Naomasa Tsukauchi

Alias: None established

Occupation: Police detective involved in major villain investigations

Abilities: Experienced investigator and coordinator; no reliably established named Quirk is required for his professional role.

Personality: Naomasa is diligent, observant and earnest about civilian safety. He recognizes the importance of cooperation between police and licensed heroes and is willing to challenge decisions when they create unnecessary danger. His measured temperament provides a stabilizing influence among people whose powers could otherwise encourage impulsive action. He values evidence, timing and the legal responsibilities attached to arrests. Years of working with All Might and other experienced heroes allow him to treat even extraordinary events as investigations requiring discipline rather than spectacle.

Appearance: He is an adult man with neatly kept dark hair, a plain but professional appearance and a serious expression. A business suit or police clothing fits his everyday duties better than a battle costume. He commonly carries himself with calm attention, listening before offering a conclusion. His ordinary human appearance is deliberate context for a job dependent on method, judgment and cooperation rather than visible superhuman anatomy.

Background: He helped coordinate investigations into major villains and joined professionals in responding to threats against students and cities.

cardPool.title: Double
cardPool.value:
Ability: Double

Description: Double creates a near-identical duplicate of a known person or object based on accurate measurements. A copy can act independently, use its original’s Quirk and be destroyed by sufficient force. The user must retain enough information about the target to construct a convincing duplicate.

Applications: A duplicate can assist rescue, distract an opponent, act as a decoy or multiply into an army when copies reproduce themselves. Copies of a person are not mindless puppets; they carry recognizable habits and can disagree or act unpredictably.

Limits: A duplicate is less durable than its original and can collapse into mudlike material after taking damage. Multiplication does not erase the danger to innocent people caught between the copies. The original user suffered severe trauma after his own duplicates turned against one another.

History: The Quirk’s broad replication potential made it one of the League of Villains’ greatest strategic advantages. Its original bearer died before the last nationwide conflict.

cardPool.title: Foresight
cardPool.value:
Ability: Foresight

Description: Foresight grants the ability to perceive future actions and events associated with an individual. Activation requires close, deliberate interaction involving physical contact and eye contact. It is not continuous global awareness of every possible event.

Applications: The wielder can anticipate a chosen person’s movements, avoid attacks and investigate how an unfolding incident may proceed. The ability is especially valuable with disciplined observation and carefully prepared teams.

Limits: The power has strict timing restrictions and cannot be used without consequence on every person encountered. Its predictions can leave the user emotionally convinced that a terrible outcome is inevitable, leading to hesitation or overconfidence. Knowledge of a future is not a substitute for the physical ability to intervene.

History: Foresight was employed by the investigator and hero Sir Nighteye in professional operations before his death during the Shie Hassaikai case.

cardPool.title: High Specs
cardPool.value:
Ability: High Specs

Description: High Specs produces extraordinary intelligence and analytical ability in its bearer. It enhances reasoning, planning and the capacity to understand complicated systems. The ability does not add an ordinary human body or a superhuman strength factor.

Applications: The user can analyze vulnerabilities, design difficult examinations, coordinate protection and devise sophisticated contingency plans. Its value is often clearest in administrative or strategic decisions made before a crisis erupts.

Limits: Intelligence does not grant perfect foreknowledge, omniscience or immunity to deception. A plan can fail if essential information is missing or if people behave unexpectedly. Physical tasks still depend on the user’s body and on other people or equipment.

Context: This Quirk underpins Nezu’s leadership of U.A. High School and his ability to assess complicated threats to the institution.

cardPool.title: Big Fist
cardPool.value:
Ability: Big Fist

Description: Big Fist expands the hands to enormous size while keeping the rest of the user’s body at ordinary scale. The enlarged hands provide considerable striking surface, grasping ability and a means to shield someone from an approaching threat.

Applications: It can lift or block suitable debris, restrain a nearby opponent and reach across a gap more easily than normal hands. A well-timed blow can force an enemy off balance, while open palms may act as improvised shields.

Limits: Greater size does not provide automatic endurance against every weapon. The hands can become a larger target, especially if held motionless, and fighting inside narrow areas may be awkward. The user still needs stable footing and control over where displaced objects land.

Context: Big Fist is the Quirk used by the hero Battle Fist, who developed it through training and tactical teamwork at U.A.

cardPool.title: Steel
cardPool.value:
Ability: Steel

Description: Steel transforms the body into tough metallic material, enabling strong defense and close-range force. It resembles some hardening-type powers in combat role but produces a metallic appearance and has its own tolerance and endurance conditions.

Applications: The transformed body can take heavy impacts, push through obstacles and strike with increased weight and toughness. The ability is well suited to front-line protection when other heroes need room to evacuate people.

Limits: Toughness does not prevent all damage; enough force, heat or sustained strain can defeat the transformation. The user needs normal training for speed, teamwork and movement. Steel cannot instantly create external metal weapons or manipulate every nearby metal object.

Context: The Quirk belongs to Real Steel, a former U.A. Class 1-B student who favors bold, direct combat.

cardPool.title: Heal
cardPool.value:
Ability: Heal

Description: Heal accelerates an injured person’s natural bodily recovery, typically transmitted by a kiss. It can help close wounds and recover from damage far sooner than ordinary healing would allow.

Applications: The power is useful for treating sprains, bruises and battle injuries after stabilization. In a school infirmary it can help students recover from accidents, provided the condition is suitable and the patient can tolerate the effect.

Limits: The Quirk spends the patient’s own stamina to regenerate tissue; serious injuries can leave them severely exhausted, and some damage is beyond its safe range. It does not substitute for surgery or make repeated self-destruction harmless.

Medical practice: Recovery Girl emphasizes rest and careful judgment. Using Heal without allowing the body to recover can make the overall condition worse.

cardPool.title: Overhaul
cardPool.value:
Ability: Overhaul

Description: Overhaul disassembles matter through contact and can reassemble it, potentially restoring a damaged object or reconstructing a living body. Its combination of destruction and restoration made it exceptionally dangerous when used deliberately.

Applications: Touching the ground can break it into hazards or rebuild it into obstacles. Direct contact with a person can result in fatal harm, bodily alteration or restoration. The effect requires control and was used for severe medical abuse.

Limits: Ordinary operation depended on functioning hands; the original bearer’s loss of both arms left him unable to deploy it in his former manner. Reassembly is not a guarantee that a victim escapes harm or trauma. The Quirk is distinct from Decay, which was engineered from a derivative stripped of its restorative half.

Context: The power was wielded by Kai Chisaki and was central to the illegal research conducted by the Shie Hassaikai.

cardPool.title: Hellflame
cardPool.value:
Ability: Hellflame

Description: Hellflame produces and directs intense fire from the body. Its wielder can create sustained jets, envelop limbs in fire and form large-area attacks or controlled bursts for aerial movement.

Applications: The fire can prevent an approaching enemy from passing, destroy dangerous material or provide thrust, but careful direction is needed near civilians. It requires exceptional stamina and thermal management to use in long engagements.

Limits: The body can overheat from continuous generation, leading to exhaustion and reduced control. Dense smoke and fire spread can endanger bystanders. No power of this kind allows unrestricted use inside a crowded building without consequences.

Context: Hellflame was Endeavor’s signature Quirk during his career. His retirement from frontline hero work followed devastating physical injuries after the Final War.

cardPool.title: Slide and Glide
cardPool.value:
Ability: Slide and Glide

Description: Slide and Glide enables the user to move along surfaces by projecting repulsive force beneath contact points. With extensive practice, that force can support remarkable speed and more sophisticated movement through the air.

Applications: Sliding across roads and rooftops can enable fast arrival at accidents, while controlled repulsion may protect the user or redirect a small impact. Learning to preserve momentum permits complex movement in environments with obstacles.

Limits: The ability initially relies heavily on surface contact, stance and practice. Abrupt collisions remain dangerous, especially near pedestrians. Improved aerial techniques are acquired through experience and should not be assumed to exist in an untrained new user.

Context: It belongs to Koichi Haimawari, whose rescue-minded street activities eventually developed into professional hero work.

cardPool.title: Bloodcurdle
cardPool.value:
Ability: Bloodcurdle

Description: Bloodcurdle paralyzes someone temporarily after the user tastes that person’s blood. The effect can be activated using blood collected from a wound or weapon, without requiring the target to stand nearby when the blood is tasted.

Applications: A skilled fighter may immobilize an opponent who is physically stronger, creating an opening for restraint or flight. The ability is especially dangerous in a fight involving sharp weapons.

Limits: It cannot activate without obtaining the target’s blood, and the paralysis duration varies according to blood type. It does not kill someone simply by being activated. A defender who prevents blood access or avoids wounded surfaces denies its central condition.

Context: The power was used by the criminal known as Stain, whose attacks on professional heroes left many injured before his death.

cardPool.title: Search
cardPool.value:
Ability: Search

Description: Search identifies and tracks multiple observed people, showing where they are and revealing useful information about them, including weaknesses. It can retain data once a target has been registered, making it valuable for long-range pursuit and surveillance.

Applications: Rescue teams can locate missing people, monitor separated groups and direct searchers through difficult terrain. Criminal users can exploit the same information for targeted attacks.

Limits: Search is not unlimited omniscience; target registration and the number of people tracked impose constraints. Its information does not automatically reveal every thought or guarantee a means of reaching someone.

History: The Quirk belonged to Ragdoll of the Wild, Wild Pussycats before being stolen by All For One. Losing the factor did not erase her rescue experience or membership in the team.

cardPool.title: Voice
cardPool.value:
Ability: Voice

Description: Voice greatly amplifies the volume and power of the wielder’s own vocal sounds. It can broadcast orders over distance or unleash damaging sonic pressure when used as an attack.

Applications: Strong communication assists crowd control and emergency coordination, while focused shouting can disorient or overwhelm approaching opponents. Specialized audio-themed equipment supports safe public use and hero operations.

Limits: The power still depends on vocal production; injury, interference and the need to avoid harming civilians affect deployment. Extreme sound can endanger allies and does not distinguish friend from foe automatically. It is not telepathy or the ability to force listeners to obey.

Context: Voice is used by Hizashi Yamada, known as Present Mic, alongside his role as an instructor and broadcaster.

cardPool.title: Eraser Head Capture Weapon
cardPool.value:
Weapon: Eraser Head Capture Weapon

Description: A long, durable binding cloth used by Shota Aizawa in combat. It can loop around an opponent, secure limbs, grapple a structure or reposition the user quickly. The fabric is engineered to tolerate high-speed capture motions and repeated stress.

Use: The cloth supplements Erasure by restraining a target whose active Quirk has been disabled. A well-placed loop may stop an attack without the need for lethal force. It is also useful against ordinary weapons or people who have no Quirk to erase.

Limitations: It requires training, timing and sufficient room to move. An enemy can evade or sever a poorly placed binding, and physical restraint alone cannot cancel a Quirk factor. The scarf does not make its wearer invulnerable or replace the need for supportive teammates.

cardPool.title: Stain Bladed Weapons
cardPool.value:
Weapons: Stain Bladed Weapons

Description: A varied arsenal of swords and smaller edged weapons carried by Chizome Akaguro. Blades increase his reach and, more importantly, give him opportunities to draw blood. His clothing supports carrying multiple weapons while remaining mobile.

Use: Close-range cuts or a blade thrown in an ambush can create blood access necessary for Bloodcurdle. The same weapons can intimidate or deflect attacks in ordinary combat. Their danger comes from trained precision combined with a Quirk condition, not from an enchanted property of the metal.

Limitations: A blade can be lost, trapped, broken or intercepted. The Quirk is not contained inside the weapon, and another person wielding it does not automatically paralyze an opponent.

cardPool.title: Izuku Midoriya
cardPool.value:
Name: Izuku Midoriya

Age: 24 (later epilogue)

Alias: Deku

Occupation: U.A. High School teacher; active Pro Hero using powered support equipment

Abilities: Former holder of One For All. Its remaining embers vanished around graduation. He now fights and rescues through a sophisticated mechanized hero suit rather than a restored natural Quirk.

Personality: Empathetic, analytical and habitually self-sacrificing, Izuku instinctively reaches toward people in distress even when he is afraid. His notebooks, close observation of abilities and detailed tactical thinking remain central to his work. He values practical kindness more than impressive rankings.

Appearance: A young adult with unruly dark green hair, green eyes and freckles across both cheeks. He retains a compact, athletic build shaped by years of intensive training and difficult battles, with visible traces of past injuries on his body. His expressions range from bashful uncertainty to focused determination.

cardPool.title: Katsuki Bakugo
cardPool.value:
Name: Katsuki Bakugo

Age: 25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Great Explosion Murder God Dynamight

Occupation: Pro Hero; operates his own hero agency

Abilities: Explosion creates powerful blasts from nitroglycerin-like sweat in his palms. He also possesses exceptional reflexes and refined aerial mobility; rehabilitation helped him recover use of his severely injured arm.

Personality: Blunt, proud, competitive and easy to provoke, Katsuki is intensely serious about heroism and refuses to tolerate laziness or half-hearted effort. Beneath his abrasive speech lies unusual perseverance, practical intelligence and increasing consideration for the people who have fought beside him.

Appearance: A muscular young adult with sharp red eyes, wild ash-blond hair and an aggressive, alert bearing. His brows frequently draw together and his mouth twists into a challenging scowl. His body language is confrontational even when relaxed: squared shoulders, tense hands and abrupt movements.

cardPool.title: Ochaco Uraraka
cardPool.value:
Name: Ochaco Uraraka

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Uravity

Occupation: Pro Hero; leading advocate for expanded Quirk counseling

Abilities: Zero Gravity allows her to nullify the gravitational pull on things she touches with her fingertips and, with advanced mastery, affect numerous nearby targets. She is an accomplished rescue fighter.

Personality: Warm, observant and socially approachable, Ochaco can lift the spirits of anxious people with genuine encouragement. She is also determined and tough-minded when others are endangered, with a powerful concern for people whose suffering goes unseen.

Appearance: A young woman with a rounded face, large brown eyes and a characteristic warm smile. Her brown hair is usually arranged in a short, softly framing style, with longer variations as she matures. In quieter moments she folds her hands together or drops her eyes before finding the resolve to speak openly.

cardPool.title: Shoto Todoroki
cardPool.value:
Name: Shoto Todoroki

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Shoto

Occupation: Pro Hero; second-ranked hero on the adult Hero Billboard Chart

Abilities: Half-Cold Half-Hot produces ice from his right side and fire from his left; he developed techniques balancing their temperatures, including Phosphor.

Personality: Calm, candid and often unintentionally funny, Shoto speaks with unusual directness and does not seek attention for its own sake. He has grown more independent of the reputation and painful expectations associated with his family. His concern for others is expressed through dependable actions rather than elaborate speeches.

Appearance: A tall, fit young man immediately recognizable by hair divided into white on his right and red on his left, along with one gray and one turquoise eye. A burn scar surrounds his left eye. His bearing is upright and subdued, his facial expressions often restrained even during praise. The skin around his left eye bears a broad scar.

cardPool.title: Tenya Iida
cardPool.value:
Name: Tenya Iida

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Ingenium

Occupation: Pro Hero; assists school outreach and Quirk education

Abilities: Engine grants extraordinary running speed through engine-like structures in his calves; Recipro techniques enhance acceleration. His disciplined approach also supports rescue and coordination.

Personality: Formal, responsible and punctilious, Tenya approaches even ordinary tasks with earnest seriousness. He is inclined to correct disorder and can sound like a strict class representative, but his lectures are rooted in concern for others. Earlier mistakes taught him to weigh compassion above rigid rules. Even when he scolds someone, his concern for their future is genuine.

Appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered man with neatly arranged dark blue hair and rectangular glasses. He stands and moves with disciplined posture, often making emphatic chopping motions while speaking. His stern face readily softens around the people he trusts.

cardPool.title: Momo Yaoyorozu
cardPool.value:
Name: Momo Yaoyorozu

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Creati

Occupation: Pro Hero; participates in school outreach

Abilities: Creation converts body lipids into nonliving matter after she understands the needed material structure; she uses the ability for tools, support equipment and strategic rescue.

Personality: Intelligent, courteous and meticulously prepared, Momo prefers reasoned planning and places great value on study. A privileged upbringing did not make her dismissive of others; she instead tries to be helpful and generous. Earlier self-doubt gave way to stronger leadership through difficult training and real danger.

Appearance: A tall young woman with long black hair typically gathered into a high, spiked ponytail and dark eyes. Her carriage is poised and elegant, and her expression tends toward polite concentration. Her equipment reflects the balance between her power’s physical requirements and the demands of fieldwork.

cardPool.title: Tsuyu Asui
cardPool.value:
Name: Tsuyu Asui

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Froppy

Occupation: Pro Hero; supports elementary-school Quirk education

Abilities: Frog provides a powerful jumping ability, adhesive climbing, a long prehensile tongue, underwater capability and camouflage among other amphibian traits.

Personality: Practical, unflappable and honest, Tsuyu tends to state uncomfortable truths when she believes people need to hear them. She cares deeply about trust and team cohesion, and often notices emotional tension before louder personalities do. Her calm responses under pressure make her valuable in rescues and difficult conversations.

Appearance: A slim young woman with very large dark eyes, a wide mouth, long dark green hair and a distinctive frog-like silhouette. She often crouches or moves in compact, spring-loaded postures. Her familiar green amphibian-inspired hero suit includes gloves, goggles and features suited to aquatic movement.

cardPool.title: Mezo Shoji
cardPool.value:
Name: Mezo Shoji

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Tentacole

Occupation: Pro Hero; advocate against discrimination toward heteromorphs

Abilities: Dupli-Arms produces additional limbs whose tips can replicate sensory organs or hands; great physical strength and versatile reach support defense and rescue.

Personality: Gentle, restrained and deeply considerate, Mezo seldom asks others to pay attention to his own pain. Having suffered prejudice because of his body, he is particularly sensitive to the humiliation and fear inflicted on those who look different. When his friends are threatened he acts decisively and with great courage.

Appearance: An exceptionally tall, heavily built heteromorph with six long arms and web-like membranes between parts of his upper limbs. His face is striking, and he often wears a covering over its lower portion; the extra arms can form hands, eyes, ears or mouths at their ends.

cardPool.title: Eijiro Kirishima
cardPool.value:
Name: Eijiro Kirishima

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Red Riot

Occupation: Pro Hero; operates independently

Abilities: Hardening toughens his body against impact and lets him engage in close-quarters defense and offense; Unbreakable is a powerful limited-duration application.

Personality: Openhearted, courageous and fiercely loyal, Eijiro admires dependable behavior more than appearances or fame. He is quick to celebrate others and readily offers reassurance to people struggling with self-doubt. He feels genuine fear but believes bravery means choosing to act despite it. The directness of his praise and good humor make him an approachable ally.

Appearance: A strongly muscled young man with sharp teeth, pronounced eyebrows and brilliant red hair usually arranged into upward spikes. A small scar crosses his right eye. His combat clothes retain his rough-edged, red-themed aesthetic with exposed areas that permit his hardened body to absorb direct attacks.

cardPool.title: Denki Kaminari
cardPool.value:
Name: Denki Kaminari

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Chargebolt

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Electrification releases electric energy from his body; target-guiding support equipment helps direct attacks, while excessive discharge can briefly cloud his thinking.

Personality: Sociable, impulsive and teasing, Denki thrives in the company of friends and enjoys lightening serious moods. He can be distractible and eager to impress, but is also capable of courage and useful tactical cooperation when the stakes rise. He forms close friendships easily and remains expressive even when others stay stoic.

Appearance: A youthful man with yellow blond hair and a distinct black lightning-bolt streak near the front, narrow golden eyes and an animated face. His costumes feature black-and-yellow electrical motifs and equipment tailored to directing current.

cardPool.title: Kyoka Jiro
cardPool.value:
Name: Kyoka Jiro

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Earphone Jack

Occupation: Pro Hero; maintains a music-centered identity and her own agency

Abilities: Earphone Jack enables her to plug elongated earlobe jacks into surfaces and transmit heartbeats as vibrations; she has exceptional hearing and musical skill.

Personality: Dry-witted, perceptive and outwardly cool, Kyoka uses teasing remarks to disguise embarrassment and affection. Music is not just a hobby to her but a means of supporting and connecting with others. She understands the emotional power of performance and is attentive to friends who need encouragement.

Appearance: A slender young woman with short, dark purple hair, sharp eyes and unusual elongated earlobes ending in plug-shaped jacks. Her hero design mixes practical combat clothing with dark musical or amplifier-inspired accessories. Injuries from the Final War affect her body, including an ear.

cardPool.title: Mina Ashido
cardPool.value:
Name: Mina Ashido

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Pinky

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Acid permits secretion of corrosive liquid with adjustable properties; she can use it for movement, defense, obstacles and attacks.

Personality: Bright, outgoing and emotionally intuitive, Mina welcomes people into groups and enjoys dancing, excitement and social interaction. Her friendliness does not make her careless about suffering: she has faced terror and grief and chooses to encourage others even when frightened. She can be impulsive and playful, yet becomes focused when danger demands it.

Appearance: A slim, athletic young woman with pink skin, fluffy short pink hair, small horns, dark sclera and yellow irises. Her dynamic body language and colorful fashion make her conspicuous even away from battle. Her hero look is built around vivid patterns and protective gear suited to her corrosive secretions, including footwear that supports acid-assisted skating.

cardPool.title: Fumikage Tokoyami
cardPool.value:
Name: Fumikage Tokoyami

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Tsukuyomi

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Dark Shadow is a sentient shadow-like entity used for offense, defense and movement. It grows more powerful in darkness and harder to restrain when deprived of light.

Personality: Serious, imaginative and drawn to solemn language, Fumikage treats his bond with Dark Shadow as both a strength and a responsibility. He values composure, self-command and loyalty. His gothic tastes can make his remarks theatrical, but he is rarely insincere or interested in attention for its own sake. Through training he learned to coordinate fearsome power with restraint.

Appearance: A humanoid with a dark birdlike head, a pointed beak and striking red eyes, mounted on an otherwise human body. His dark clothing and cape-like hero attire reinforce his dramatic silhouette. His head resembles that of a dark bird, with a sharp beak and red eyes above a human-shaped, athletic body.

cardPool.title: Yuga Aoyama
cardPool.value:
Name: Yuga Aoyama

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Can’t Stop Twinkling

Occupation: Former U.A. hero-course student

Abilities: Navel Laser produces a powerful beam from his abdomen using a Quirk that was originally provided to him by All For One; prolonged use causes digestive discomfort.

Personality: Flamboyant, sensitive and fond of dramatic gestures, Yuga uses sparkle and elaborate self-presentation to conceal profound anxieties about belonging. He was exploited through threats to his parents and lived with guilt over actions forced upon him. His manner is theatrical without erasing his remorse or desire to change.

Appearance: A slender blond young man with carefully styled hair and expressive violet eyes. His appearance favors bright, decorative clothing and exaggerated poses, while his distinctive hero attire uses polished armor with a focusing device over the navel. His smiles can appear self-conscious or strained when he is anxious.

cardPool.title: Hanta Sero
cardPool.value:
Name: Hanta Sero

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Cellophane

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Tape ejects adhesive bands from his elbows, allowing swinging, binding, object movement and rapid traversal.

Personality: Relaxed, observant and teasing, Hanta often provides an ordinary, sensible counterpoint to his more explosive classmates. He likes banter and joins in harmless jokes but is alert to changes in a friend’s mood. In battles he makes clever use of terrain and mobility rather than simply charging directly into danger. He is comfortable cooperating with others and can improvise under pressure.

Appearance: A lean young man with straight black hair, narrow eyes and large cylindrical elbow structures from which his tape extends. His recognizable hero equipment has a streamlined black-and-white style with features suited for aerial movement. He commonly wears a casual grin and moves with the loose posture of a practiced grappling fighter.

cardPool.title: Mashirao Ojiro
cardPool.value:
Name: Mashirao Ojiro

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Tailman

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Tail is a strong, muscular appendage used for martial arts, balance, grappling and powerful strikes.

Personality: Courteous, straightforward and disciplined, Mashirao prefers fair competition and dislikes taking credit that he feels he has not earned. He trains diligently in hand-to-hand combat and values dependable teammates. His lack of flamboyance is a defining trait, not a weakness; he shows courage and tactical maturity without needing to be the loudest person in a room.

Appearance: A fit, compact young man with short blond hair, dark eyes and a long, thick, muscular tail emerging from his lower back. His close-combat hero outfit accommodates unrestricted tail movement and martial-arts technique. He typically wears a modest, composed expression and maintains balanced, disciplined stances. His tail moves expressively as well as being a weapon.

cardPool.title: Koji Koda
cardPool.value:
Name: Koji Koda

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Anima

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Anivoice allows him to communicate with animals and request their assistance; developments in his physical mutation support stronger communication.

Personality: Quiet, gentle and compassionate, Koji is most comfortable around animals and people who give him room to speak. He is shy rather than indifferent and will face considerable fear when defending others. His respect for living beings informs his decisions, whether he is coordinating a rescue or helping a classmate.

Appearance: A tall, powerfully built man with an angular, rocky-looking head and a generally soft, reserved expression. Horn-like growths can develop on his head as his abilities change. He often communicates through small gestures and calm movements. His hero costume is practical for operating alongside animals and for protecting his body during rescue operations. Hornlike features develop as his Quirk matures.

cardPool.title: Rikido Sato
cardPool.value:
Name: Rikido Sato

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Sugarman

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Sugar Rush temporarily multiplies physical strength after sugar consumption, at the cost of reduced mental acuity while the effect is active.

Personality: Even-tempered and considerate, Rikido often contributes through actions rather than loud declarations. Baking is a genuine talent and a way he connects with friends. He is dependable in demanding physical tasks, although his power’s cognitive drawback requires forethought. His desire to help is practical and sincere. Sato is straightforward, hospitable and dependable.

Appearance: A broad, muscular young man with short dark hair, thick features and a powerful upper-body build. His hero costume includes sturdy practical clothing and elements inspired by his sugar-fueled fighting style. He typically appears calm, though his movements become forceful and emphatic during close combat.

cardPool.title: Toru Hagakure
cardPool.value:
Name: Toru Hagakure

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Invisible Girl

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Invisibility renders most of her body imperceptible; she can manipulate and refract light for dazzling effects.

Personality: Cheerful, expressive and sociable, Toru is fond of clothes, outings and opportunities to join in group activities. Although others often cannot see her facial cues, her enthusiasm comes through in her voice, gestures and animated reactions. She values friendship and is more perceptive than her lighthearted manner suggests. Toru is bubbly, energetic and easily excited by friendships, clothing and social events.

Appearance: A young woman whose body is naturally invisible to ordinary sight, often recognized through floating clothing, gloves or costume accessories rather than visible facial features. Under conditions that interfere with or expose her optical ability, she has light-colored hair and recognizable human facial features.

cardPool.title: Minoru Mineta
cardPool.value:
Name: Minoru Mineta

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Grape Juice

Occupation: Pro Hero

Abilities: Pop Off generates sticky spherical objects from his scalp; they adhere strongly to most surfaces without sticking to him and can form traps or launch points.

Personality: Attention-seeking and comically dramatic, Minoru often tries to look bold while remaining easily frightened. His history includes intrusive behavior toward women, a genuine weakness that can undermine his relationships and judgment. Despite this, he shows ingenuity in moments of crisis and can cooperate with stronger classmates when it matters.

Appearance: A notably short man with round purple growths arranged like clustered grapes on his head, a compact body and broad, expressive eyes. His purple-themed hero suit and small stature make him instantly recognizable. He often exaggerates facial expressions, shifting quickly between fear, determination and smug self-satisfaction.

cardPool.title: Hitoshi Shinso
cardPool.value:
Name: Hitoshi Shinso

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: NightHide

Occupation: Pro Hero; former U.A. hero-course student

Abilities: Brainwashing can control someone who verbally responds to him; an artificial vocal-cord apparatus expands the possibilities for imitation and deception. He also uses capture gear.

Personality: Self-contained, dryly sarcastic and determined, Hitoshi resents unfair assumptions that his mind-affecting Quirk makes him suited for villainy. He trains to demonstrate that heroism depends on how power is used, not how it looks. His humor is restrained and occasionally pointed.

Appearance: A lean young man with tousled indigo-purple hair, tired-looking eyes and a reserved expression. His hero equipment borrows practical capture techniques, including a binding cloth and a voice-modulating mask. His posture is watchful and understated, and he seldom advertises emotion through large gestures.

cardPool.title: Mirio Togata
cardPool.value:
Name: Mirio Togata

Alias: Lemillion

Occupation: Top-ranked Pro Hero

Abilities: Permeation allows his body to pass through solid matter, but doing so also disrupts ordinary senses and footing; extraordinary predictive combat skill compensates.

Personality: Optimistic, generous and irresistibly encouraging, Mirio approaches difficult situations with a smile intended to calm frightened people. His cheerfulness is supported by hard-earned skill, fearlessness and concern for lives that might otherwise be overlooked. He is willing to bear terrible risk himself but tries not to make others carry his burdens. Mirio refuses to equate heroism with keeping a Quirk.

Appearance: A tall, muscular young man with short blond hair, blue eyes and a very broad grin. His round facial features and powerful build make him look approachable and athletic at once. His recognizable white hero suit and cape use hair-derived material in a costume engineered to work with his permeation.

cardPool.title: Nejire Hado
cardPool.value:
Name: Nejire Hado

Alias: Nejire Chan

Occupation: Pro Hero
