Separate alterations: Forced augmentation later made the user larger and less mentally stable. Those changes came from additional powers and medical manipulation, not from ordinary development of Gecko.

Field detail: Adhesion gives practical advantages on buildings, ceilings and irregular surfaces, letting the user seek angles unavailable to ordinary climbers. A permanent nonhuman appearance can alter social interaction but does not determine loyalty or competence.

cardPool.title: Warp Gate
cardPool.value:
Ability: Warp Gate

Overview: Warp Gate created portals within black mist controlled by Kurogiri. It could transport people and objects between locations and redirect movement through connected openings. The power was embedded in a modified body made using Oboro Shirakumo’s remains.

Transit: The dark mist opens connected passages to locations the user can target, allowing an individual or group to step between distant points quickly. The technique supports extraction, reinforcement and redirection of attacks.

Constraints: A portal must be placed accurately, and interruption of concentration can spoil an evacuation. The organic structure of the modified body is important to maintaining the ability.

Field detail: A coordinated group can use portals to withdraw injured allies, insert a rescue team or separate opponents who rely on proximity. A badly chosen exit could place passengers in the path of danger, so reliable targeting is vital.

cardPool.title: Fierce Wings
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fierce Wings

Overview: Fierce Wings originally gave Hawks broad red wings and precise independent control of individual feathers. They could carry people, detect subtle disturbances and cut or intercept targets. Damage weakened the feathers and prolonged use reduced his supply.

Feather control: Large crimson wings once supplied high-speed flight. Individual feathers could be sent out to carry small loads, hear distant vibrations, intercept projectiles or cut targets.

Loss: Repeated destruction reduced effective plumage and impaired flight. The factor was eventually stolen, leaving its former wielder unable to command the feathers naturally.

Field detail: Independent feathers can perform fine manipulations while the main body flies, making simultaneous rescue and scouting possible. A feather carrying a person requires strength and appropriate placement; smaller feathers are more suited to sensing.

cardPool.title: Rabbit
cardPool.value:
Ability: Rabbit

Overview: Rabbit granted Mirko strong legs, powerful leaps, exceptional agility and rabbitlike senses. The Quirk did not regrow amputated limbs.

Traits: Powerful leg muscles allow great jumps, rapid kicks and tight changes of direction. Enhanced hearing and instinctive movement make the user a fearsome close-range fighter, with no need for an emitted projectile.

After injury: Rabbit did not prevent loss of limbs during battles with Nomu or restore them afterward. Mechanical prostheses return mobility through machinery and difficult retraining, not through an unmentioned regenerative ability. The effectiveness of each strike still depends on sound footing and personal conditioning.

Field detail: Leaping strength can close the distance to a fast opponent, while quick footwork makes sweeping attacks hard to predict. Rabbitlike hearing offers early awareness but does not function as a perfect lie detector or sonar.

cardPool.title: Gigantification
cardPool.value:
Ability: Gigantification

Overview: Gigantification allows Mt. Lady to grow into a giant version of herself. Increased size brings formidable force and reach but creates serious risks of collateral damage in crowded spaces. She must manage terrain and the presence of civilians carefully.

Transformation: The user enlarges into a giant while retaining human shape, increasing reach and physical impact substantially. She can brace against huge opponents, catch large falling structures and draw hostile attention away from ground-level evacuees.

Costs: Giant size makes narrow roads, fragile bridges and dense crowds hazardous. Mass and impact can cause destruction even when the hero intends to help.

Field detail: Standing at enormous height can provide a view across collapsed districts and allow access to upper floors, while massive arms may shield a structure from a falling object. These advantages vanish in spaces that cannot contain the transformed body.

cardPool.title: Arbor
cardPool.value:
Ability: Arbor

Overview: Arbor grows and controls wooden structures from Kamui Woods’s body. Branches extend to bind opponents, anchor movement and form rescue supports. Wood remains vulnerable to fire and destructive force, and extensive growth requires accuracy when civilians occupy the same area.

Growth: Wood extends from limbs and torso as branching restraints and stakes, enabling long-distance captures and improvised anchors. A disciplined user can envelop an opponent without needing a weapon that causes severe injury.

Vulnerabilities: Fire and intense energy can damage the material. Destroyed branches and complex entanglements may restrict immediate reconfiguration. The branches arise from the user’s own body rather than from instant control of every tree nearby.

Field detail: The user can rapidly bind several fleeing targets by extending branches along a prepared route. A wooden cage or rail can also provide temporary support during evacuation.

cardPool.title: Fiber Master
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fiber Master

Overview: Fiber Master grants Best Jeanist refined control over textile fibers, including those in clothing. Thick woven materials can create restraints and protective structures; garments on opponents may become a weakness. Use requires concentration, technical understanding and material to manipulate.

Manipulation: Textile threads respond to highly precise control, allowing fabric to bind a target or stretch into sturdy constructions. Denim is a favored material, but other woven fibers can be used.

Boundaries: Fibers must be present, and opponents without useful textiles limit easy restraint. Fire, cutting or violent force can overwhelm a structure.

Field detail: A long strip of woven material can be manipulated to catch a falling person or restrict a weapon arm. Multiple fine threads can apply force with great precision, but material choice strongly affects durability.

cardPool.title: Fat Absorption
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fat Absorption

Overview: Fat Absorption lets Fat Gum absorb impacts with an unusually resilient body and convert stored energy into forceful counterattacks. Expending these reserves can sharply alter his body shape. The Quirk is defensive and offensive but cannot absorb unlimited damage without consequences.

Defense: Impact sinks into a cushion of stored fat, reducing the harm of punches and other blows. Collected power can be turned into a concentrated strike, while spending too much reserve leaves the user drastically leaner.

Judgment: A major counterattack may sacrifice the very protection needed for subsequent rounds. Heavy penetration and repeated punishment can become dangerous even when softened.

Field detail: A body that absorbs a punch can also help cushion another person against a crushing blow. The most decisive counterattack spends energy that was being held defensively, forcing a choice between immediate power and future safety.

cardPool.title: Dragon
cardPool.value:
Ability: Dragon

Overview: Dragon lets Ryukyu turn into a huge flying dragon. The transformed body provides flight, physical might, scales and claws, useful in both rescue and combat. Her size can obstruct movement in narrow indoor spaces and raises the stakes of collateral harm.

Transformation: A human body expands into a scaly dragon with wings, long neck, strong legs and powerful claws. Its mass supports carrying allies, shielding smaller people and confronting large enemies directly.

Practical limits: Large size complicates movement through tunnels and populated streets. Although scales improve durability, the dragon is not immune to extreme force.

Field detail: Strong wings can lift an injured person away from a high ledge while armored scales endure impacts that would injure an ordinary rescuer. The dragon’s size is also a liability in close indoor passages.

cardPool.title: Elasticity
cardPool.value:
Ability: Elasticity

Overview: Elasticity allows Gentle to make touched materials elastic and springy. He can bounce across buildings, deflect movement and stretch surfaces into protective barriers.

Contact: Touched solid surfaces can take on spring-like qualities, absorbing a fall or redirecting motion. The user can create temporary trampolines and invisible-feeling footholds in the air by manipulating its elasticity, permitting agile movement without a flying Quirk.

Constraints: Altered surfaces are not indestructible and must be positioned before a collision. The power cannot guarantee control over an opponent’s entire body from across a city.

Field detail: Elastic surfaces redirect momentum, making a fall survivable or sending a pursuer back along their route. Several prepared surfaces can create an indirect movement path that a less observant opponent misunderstands.

cardPool.title: Love
cardPool.value:
Ability: Love

Overview: Love strengthens someone La Brava sincerely loves when she expresses that affection. Its output is tied to her emotional connection and cannot be deployed as an ordinary boost for any stranger. Her highly advanced computing skills are learned abilities, not manifestations of Love.

Empowerment: When the user declares sincere affection, the person who receives it can gain a dramatic, temporary boost. Depth of feeling determines the effect more than calculation or technical equipment.

Restriction: Love cannot be applied to an arbitrary colleague as if it were a battery. The boost is neither permanent nor a replacement for the subject’s own power.

Field detail: The boost requires genuine emotional attachment, not merely reciting a password or pretending affection. Its effect is best understood through the recipient’s suddenly enhanced capacity to act, while the source remains physically vulnerable.

cardPool.title: Blackwhip
cardPool.value:
Ability: Blackwhip

Overview: Blackwhip was one of the inherited abilities within One For All, projecting dark energy tendrils useful for grappling, restraint, protection and mobility. Emotional turmoil could complicate control.

Projection: Black, flexible tendrils spring from the user’s body and can bind opponents, hook structures, carry items and brace injured limbs. Their reach makes them highly valuable alongside enhanced movement, though delicate manipulation takes training.

Control: Emotional distress originally caused wild, uncontrolled tendrils, threatening allies and the user. Superior control required calm focus and repeated practice.

Field detail: Multiple tendrils can anchor the user while a different strand carries an injured person or restrains an enemy. Using the energy internally to brace damaged limbs became possible through extraordinary control.

cardPool.title: Float
cardPool.value:
Ability: Float

Overview: Float was Nana Shimura’s levitation Quirk and later one of the powers accessible to Izuku through One For All. It enabled sustained aerial movement when combined with other mobility abilities. It is not among Izuku’s natural capabilities after the stockpiled Quirk disappears.

Effect: The bearer can rise off the ground and remain suspended, avoiding ordinary pitfalls and ground-based hazards. Combined with propulsion or grappling, levitation can create rapid three-dimensional movement; by itself it is not unrestricted high-speed flight.

History: Nana Shimura possessed the independent factor before its imprint became one of the powers carried within One For All. Izuku accessed it temporarily during his tenure as bearer.

Field detail: Levitation frees the user from contact with unstable ground or a surface affected by Decay. For fast travel it works particularly well alongside a separate source of horizontal propulsion.

cardPool.title: Danger Sense
cardPool.value:
Ability: Danger Sense

Overview: Danger Sense was a One For All predecessor ability that reacted to hostile danger and negative intent. It could produce painful warnings and became less useful against attackers without malice. It never guaranteed automatic evasion.

Warning: A sharp mental signal alerts the user to hostile intent and impending danger. Its severity can be painful when threats are intense or numerous. It aids positioning only when the body can move fast enough to react.

Blind spots: A person acting without malice may attack or inflict harm without triggering an equally useful warning. Crowded battlefields can produce overwhelming signals.

Field detail: The warning signal is particularly useful when a hostile opponent hides behind cover, but it is harder to interpret in a crowd with conflicting intentions. The sense alerts rather than defeating a threat: only awareness, speed and judgment turn it into successful defense.

cardPool.title: Smokescreen
cardPool.value:
Ability: Smokescreen

Overview: Smokescreen was an inherited One For All ability to emit dense smoke and obscure sightlines. It supported retreat and concealment but could also blind allies or its own user. Izuku no longer has its natural use in the epilogue.

Emission: Purple-gray clouds spread through the field, blocking sight and enabling escapes, ambushes or movement under cover. The user can adjust the quantity but must still navigate within the obscured area.

Limits: A cloud does not prevent area attacks, powerful gusts or opponents who can detect sound and movement by other means. Emitting too much smoke can hinder allies as much as enemies. The factor belonged to an earlier One For All wielder and is not naturally possessed by Izuku in the adult era.

Field detail: A thick visual barrier forces distant shooters to guess or close the gap. Allies with nonvisual senses can exploit it, while those relying on eyesight may become equally disoriented.

cardPool.title: Fa Jin
cardPool.value:
Ability: Fa Jin

Overview: Fa Jin accumulated kinetic energy through repeated motions, then released that energy in bursts for enhanced movement or strikes. It was one of the prior users’ Quirks contained within One For All, not an independent power available to Izuku after losing the inheritance.

Storage: Repeated movement of a limb builds up kinetic energy that can be released as a temporary burst of force or speed. It permits a powerful action without requiring constant maximum output from the broader stockpiling power.

Use: Charging requires time and intentional motion, and the reserve cannot be assumed infinite. It existed as a distinct predecessor Quirk inside One For All.

Field detail: A few deliberate repetitive movements can build up a reserve before a sudden dash or strike. The technique rewards preparation and coordination with other mobility effects, not reckless continuous maximum effort.

cardPool.title: Gearshift
cardPool.value:
Ability: Gearshift

Overview: Gearshift altered the speed of touched objects, later operating on far more potent scales after enhancement through One For All. Its advanced use created an extreme backlash and limited operating time.

Speed control: Contact changes the velocity of a target, bypassing some ordinary restrictions of acceleration. Initially associated with small objects, its power increased tremendously in One For All, allowing extraordinary maneuvers and explosive combat combinations.

Backlash: High-end activation rapidly imposes punishing bodily stress and creates a narrow window for effective use. Repeating extreme performance is far more dangerous than ordinary bursts of enhanced speed.

Field detail: Altering speed at close contact allows abrupt shifts in combat momentum that are difficult for an opponent to anticipate. When supercharged by One For All, those changes become exceptionally violent and stressful to the body.

cardPool.title: U.A. High School
cardPool.value:
Location: U.A. High School

Description: Prestigious Japanese academy for hero education, general studies, business and support development. Its hero course emphasizes rescue, combat, ethics, field internships and the realities of professional licensing. Strong fortifications, movable campus infrastructure and experienced faculty make it a crucial refuge and training center.

Campus and infrastructure: U.A. operates general studies, hero, support and business departments. Hero students study both classroom subjects and practical response, with specialist teachers responsible for combat, rescue and the ethics of professional intervention. Training spaces include artificial urban blocks, disaster environments, sports venues, workshops and dormitories.

Present-day use: Enhanced security grew after repeated villain incursions. During the national crisis, mobile structures and underground systems helped shelter people under threat.

cardPool.title: Musutafu
cardPool.value:
Location: Musutafu

Description: Japanese city that contains U.A. High School and many locations associated with the formative years of Class 1-A.

Urban character: Musutafu contains ordinary family apartments and houses, shopping streets, roads, public transit and the school zone associated with U.A. The concentration of hero training and professional response makes it a busy place even between emergencies.

Civic role: Evacuations and rebuilding changed how residents think about depending on lone celebrity heroes. Schools, businesses and roads remain useful settings for small rescues, investigations and ordinary interactions. It is a functioning city, not a permanent ruin or a self-contained academy compound.

Local texture: Residential blocks sit alongside stores, intersections and commuter routes linking neighborhoods to school and work. An incident here can involve an ordinary shopkeeper or pedestrian as easily as an academy student.

cardPool.title: Ground Beta
cardPool.value:
Location: Ground Beta

Description: U.A. training ground constructed to resemble an urban district, with concrete buildings, artificial roads and rooftops. It allows students and licensed personnel to practice mobility, searching, team tactics and urban rescue in an environment that resembles city blocks.

Layout: Dense blocks of tall artificial buildings, streets, lanes and rooftops imitate the problems of a developed city. Students can practice climbing, ambush awareness, capture techniques and coordinated searches.

Purpose: Because the site is designed for repeated controlled exercises, structural damage can be repaired or reset. Staged fights are not evidence that civilians live in the replica buildings.

Safety operations: Instructors can stage missing-person searches and timed captures, observing whether students damage simulated infrastructure unnecessarily. Rooflines and building interiors permit controlled surprise encounters.

cardPool.title: Unforeseen Simulation Joint
cardPool.value:
Location: Unforeseen Simulation Joint

Description: U.A.’s specialized disaster-response training facility, widely known as the U.S.J. It contains several artificial environmental zones for practicing rescue under varied hazards, including floods, fires, landslides and collapsed urban structures.

Design: The enclosed training dome is split into themed disaster zones, including water hazards, urban wreckage and burning structures. It allows response teams to rehearse civilian evacuation and survival in conditions too dangerous to construct on ordinary city streets.

Security and significance: Its early invasion by villains exposed vulnerabilities in academy defenses and endangered an entire first-year class. The incident influenced later safety decisions, but the facility’s primary purpose remains training for catastrophes. The name is usually shortened to U.S.J.

Training areas: Different environmental compartments demand different equipment and choices.

cardPool.title: U.A. Dormitories
cardPool.value:
Location: U.A. Dormitories

Description: Student residential facilities established to improve security after villain attacks exposed the limits of commuting and ordinary home life. Class 1-A’s dorm building provides private rooms and shared social space where friendships were strengthened.

Living spaces: Private bedrooms are grouped around shared kitchens, lounges and other communal areas. Residents can study together, prepare meals and seek help from classmates without commuting through unsafe streets.

History and use: Dorm residence was introduced as a security response after attacks on students. The building became important to daily class life and the emotional recovery of frightened trainees.

Daily routines: The shared common room is used for conversation and class gatherings, while students personalize private rooms. Living together reduces some travel risks but means conflicts and worries follow residents home.

cardPool.title: Kamino Ward
cardPool.value:
Location: Kamino Ward

Description: Urban district notorious for the confrontation in which All Might defeated All For One publicly and lost the last usable strength of his former heroic identity. A memorial statue of All Might stands here. Following the Final War, the memorial was expanded with representations of ordinary civilians raising their arms to support heroes, acknowledging rescue and solidarity beyond individual celebrity.

Streets and memorial: A densely built urban ward with major roads and the site of an infamous showdown. The All Might statue later became a place where an unsure young person could pause and ask what heroism means.

Civic meaning: The area recalls both the dangers of relying on a single Symbol of Peace and the power of ordinary people to reach toward one another. Local stores and pedestrians continue to exist around the memorial. It is not merely an abandoned combat zone or the residence of All Might.

cardPool.title: Jaku City
cardPool.value:
Location: Jaku City

Description: City and hospital district devastated by the Paranormal Liberation War. A hidden medical facility was used for the modification of Tomura Shigaraki and the creation of dangerous Nomu. Massive destruction, evacuation and reconstruction transformed the district into a reminder of the danger posed by organized superhuman crime.

Medical district: Jaku was home to a major hospital secretly associated with illegal research and the creation or enhancement of Nomu. The hidden work was uncovered during a coordinated hero operation. When catastrophic power was unleashed, surrounding streets, buildings and infrastructure became scenes of mass evacuation.

Aftermath: Severe destruction made reconstruction, debris removal, housing and healthcare urgent priorities. Residents need ongoing services after the main battle ends.

cardPool.title: Gunga Mountain Villa
cardPool.value:
Location: Gunga Mountain Villa

Description: Remote complex formerly associated with the Paranormal Liberation Front. Its facilities and surroundings became part of major conflicts with organized villains. The area includes mountainous terrain, access roads and broad spaces that made coordinated attacks and mass mobilization possible.

Terrain and structure: A mountain property used as a concealed gathering center for the Paranormal Liberation Front. The main complex and its underground areas accommodated large meetings, personnel and preparations for coordinated operations. Its isolated approaches complicated surveillance while giving defenders routes through wooded terrain.

History and condition: Hero forces targeted the site during the wider conflict, and fighting damaged the compound. Nearby mountainous areas became associated with later clashes as well.

cardPool.title: Hosu City
cardPool.value:
Location: Hosu City

Description: City affected by the Hero Killer Stain, Nomu attacks and the broader problem of public confidence in professional heroes. Its streets and alleyways became a formative battleground for young heroes and police cooperation. The city remains a populated urban setting outside the U.A. campus.

Urban features: Broad commercial streets meet smaller alleys, hospitals and ordinary residential districts. Those narrow routes gave dangerous criminals places to ambush a lone responder. Emergency services and police have practical roles beyond the dramatic public battles associated with the district.

History: The Hero Killer’s attacks and simultaneous Nomu incidents shook confidence in professional protection. Young trainees learned how quickly a patrol could become a rescue or law-enforcement crisis. The city remains populated and rebuilds ordinary civic life rather than being permanently under villain control.

cardPool.title: Nabu Island
cardPool.value:
Location: Nabu Island

Description: Remote island community where young U.A. hero students undertook protective duties and confronted a dangerous villain assault. Rural and coastal scenery, residential facilities and transport limitations make it distinct from mainland hero cities. The island’s inhabitants depend heavily on coordinated local response during emergencies.

Geography: An outlying island community with coastal routes, beaches, farms, forested high ground, small settlements and limited access to mainland reinforcement. Residents know one another more readily than in major cities, and local emergencies may have to be handled with whatever people and equipment are immediately available.

History: Hero trainees once undertook community duties here and defended residents during a serious attack. Distance from large hero agencies shaped the danger and made evacuation routes vital.

cardPool.title: I-Island
cardPool.value:
Location: I-Island

Description: Artificial island devoted to technology, scientific research and support-industry innovation. A highly secured research culture, exhibition facilities and international engineering networks distinguish it from normal Japanese cities. Melissa Shield’s work is connected with this world of advanced engineering.

Research environment: This highly secured artificial island hosts laboratories, advanced support-device development and major technology exhibitions. International specialists and visitors gather to examine inventions intended for the professional hero industry. Security restrictions protect research while creating distinct challenges for anyone entering sensitive facilities.

Physical character: Modern towers, research centers and leisure areas coexist on a technologically sophisticated island. A public demonstration can draw audiences from outside Japan, but ordinary laboratories remain governed by access rules.

cardPool.title: Tartarus
cardPool.value:
Location: Tartarus

Description: High-security detention facility designed for extremely dangerous criminals with destructive or difficult-to-contain Quirks. Its systems relied on surveillance, confinement and heavily armed response. The facility suffered a catastrophic breakout during the collapse of national hero security, demonstrating the fragility of even advanced prisons.

Design and security: An island prison built for detainees whose powers make ordinary incarceration dangerous. Heavily layered defenses, surveillance and restrictions on movement were designed to prevent sudden escape or the use of destructive Quirks inside the facility.

Collapse: A coordinated escape overwhelmed the institution during the breakdown of national security, freeing dangerous inmates and destabilizing public confidence. It cannot be treated as a fully operational, untouched prison during the adult era without a separately established rebuilding.

cardPool.title: Central Hospital
cardPool.value:
Location: Central Hospital

Description: Major medical center involved in treating serious injuries and coordinating high-level medical response. Research and specialist care for unusual Quirk-related conditions were crucial during the Final War and the recovery that followed. It is a hospital, not a hero academy or criminal headquarters.

Medical operations: The hospital treats complex traumatic injuries and works with medical specialists familiar with unusual biological powers. It has held critically injured people requiring sustained monitoring and has been involved in emergency response following large-scale combat. Advanced care does not mean every condition is curable.

Professional character: Its wards, examination rooms and restricted areas are governed by medical needs, privacy and physical security. Treatment may last long after public battles are over.

cardPool.title: Hassaikai Compound
cardPool.value:
Location: Hassaikai Compound

Description: Former headquarters of the Shie Hassaikai, a yakuza group that used underground facilities and secure rooms to conceal experiments and criminal operations. Its corridors and hidden infrastructure were central to the rescue of Eri. After the organization’s defeat it no longer serves as a legitimate operating hero facility.

Physical layout: A traditional-looking criminal headquarters concealing numerous interior passages and underground sections. Tight corridors and sealed rooms forced rescuers to consider hostages, escape routes and sudden changes to the building itself. The underground complex helped hide highly abusive experimentation.

Legacy: Police and professional heroes raided the premises to stop production of anti-Quirk ammunition and rescue a captive child. Once exposed, the compound ceased to function as a secure headquarters for the old syndicate.

cardPool.title: Deika City
cardPool.value:
Location: Deika City

Description: City that witnessed large-scale fighting between the League of Villains and the Meta Liberation Army. The resulting destruction and political fallout aided the formation of the Paranormal Liberation Front. It represents the dangers of concentrated extremist mobilization within a seemingly ordinary urban community.

Civic structure: Deika appeared to operate as a normal municipality, but an exceptionally large proportion of its inhabitants were tied to liberationist organizing. Businesses, public spaces and the urban terrain were used to conceal mass political and militant activity. A visitor could mistake the organized preparation for ordinary civic life.

Destruction: Fighting between rival villain factions caused catastrophic damage and exposed the reach of the movement. The clash helped change an underground ideology into a broader paramilitary coalition.

cardPool.title: Lightly Labs
cardPool.value:
Organization: Lightly Labs

Description: Engineering company established by Mei Hatsume after her U.A. education. It develops advanced hero support technology and applies experimental design to real-world limitations. Mei’s work on Izuku Midoriya’s specialized hero suit demonstrates the importance of engineering alongside conventional Quirks.

Work: The company specializes in experimental support equipment and prototype development led by the inventor Mei Hatsume. Her workshop culture prizes testing, iteration and adapting inventions to a user’s movements, bodily limitations and tactical needs. Designs require calibration and repeated trial rather than emerging fully functional from imagination.

Postwar significance: Lightly Labs is associated with the technological project that restores Izuku Midoriya’s ability to serve actively as a hero without giving him a biological Quirk. Its work reflects a growing market for advanced protective systems.

cardPool.title: GeL Inc.
cardPool.value:
Organization: GeL Inc.

Description: Company run by Gentle and La Brava following their rehabilitation. It represents their transition from online notoriety and criminal publicity seeking to a more constructive adult life. Gentle contributes unusual physical abilities and entrepreneurial flair; La Brava brings extraordinary technological ability.

Company: The enterprise is associated with Danjuro Tobita and Manami Aiba, who redirect their former flair for publicity and technical skill toward lawful work. Manami’s cybersecurity expertise gives the company a reputation for confronting digital crises.

Place in society: The firm represents how people once dismissed as irredeemable can contribute after accountability and rehabilitation. Its employees and offices are not established in exhaustive detail; its identity is grounded in a legitimate company associated with the pair. No independent nationwide monopoly or secret armed force is established.

cardPool.title: Bakugo Hero Agency
cardPool.value:
Organization: Bakugo Hero Agency

Description: Professional hero agency led by Katsuki Bakugo, built around his aggressive combat style, heroic accomplishments and expanding leadership. His intimidating public manner and difficult interactions with cameras affect how the public perceives it.

Agency character: Built around the public work of the explosively powerful Pro Hero Dynamight, the agency must manage field response, equipment and staff coordination as well as its leader’s confrontational manner. Strength in a battle does not eliminate scheduling, public trust or the need to cooperate with emergency services.

Adult history: Bakugo openly considers bringing Izuku into his professional operation and has an important role in the support-armor project. His professional standing fluctuates as citizens respond to both successful rescues and his harsh public behavior. The agency is separate from U.A. and from the broader collection of Class A alumni.

cardPool.title: Uraraka Quirk Counseling Initiative
cardPool.value:
Organization: Uraraka Quirk Counseling Initiative

Description: Expanded counseling and education effort promoted by Ochaco Uraraka. It brings professional heroes to schools and prioritizes children whose Quirks or emotional circumstances may require support rather than punishment or neglect. Cooperation with Ingenium, Froppy and Creati helps normalize understanding of abilities and personal differences.

Activities: Uraraka works with other professional heroes to visit elementary schools and improve access to guidance for young children with unusual powers. Their program combines reassurance, demonstrations and attention to students who might otherwise feel ashamed or misunderstood.

Scope: The effort addresses both the practical control of abilities and the emotional circumstances surrounding them. It is a counseling and outreach initiative, not a combat unit or identified single building with a formal national chain of command.

cardPool.title: Class 1-A Graduates
cardPool.value:
Organization: Class 1-A Graduates

Overview: Former students of U.A.’s Hero Course Class 1-A, who confronted the League of Villains and the Final War during their education. Many become Pro Heroes, while their careers diversify into teaching, counseling, independent agency work, and professional public service. Their relationships survive despite busy schedules, and their group funding makes Izuku’s return to hero work possible.

History and members: The class’s original core includes Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo, Ochaco Uraraka, Shoto Todoroki, Tenya Iida, Tsuyu Asui, Momo Yaoyorozu, Kirishima, Tokoyami and their peers. Yuga Aoyama voluntarily left school after the war to take responsibility for earlier wrongdoing; Hitoshi Shinso subsequently entered the class.

After graduation: Many work as licensed heroes, some with agencies or sidekick arrangements, while Izuku pursues teaching alongside field work. Adult careers make frequent gatherings difficult.

cardPool.title: Class 1-B Graduates
cardPool.value:
Organization: Class 1-B Graduates

Overview: Former U.A. students trained alongside Class 1-A in the same hero-course generation. Their group includes Neito Monoma and Juzo Honenuki, whose tactical talents attract increased public recognition. Old school rivalry can remain part of social banter, but alumni follow individual careers and agencies.

Training history: U.A.’s parallel hero-course class includes Neito Monoma, Juzo Honenuki, Itsuka Kendo, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, Setsuna Tokage, Manga Fukidashi and others with varied powers. The class engaged in joint training with Class A, developing its own strengths in teamwork, improvisation and Quirk combinations.

Professional life: Members pursued distinct licensed careers rather than serving under a single continuing class command. Monoma’s copying power and Honenuki’s terrain control contributed to high-profile operations and later professional recognition.

cardPool.title: Hero Public Safety Commission
cardPool.value:
Organization: Hero Public Safety Commission

Overview: National agency responsible for hero regulation and public-safety coordination. Earlier leadership relied on opaque covert tactics and sometimes sacrificed individuals for political stability. During postwar reforms, Hawks assumes a leadership role with a commitment to reducing the burden of violent hero work.

Duties: The commission helps administer and regulate professional hero society, linking the licensed hero network with broader public policy. It has overseen responses to organized crime, confidential operations and the public image of heroes. It is an institution with personnel and procedures, not itself a Quirk or an individual fighter.

Record and reform: Earlier leadership recruited and controlled operatives for clandestine work, sometimes concealing the violence required to maintain a spotless public image. The death and exposure of senior figures opened space for new management.

cardPool.title: League of Villains
cardPool.value:
Organization: League of Villains

Overview: Criminal group that grew around Tomura Shigaraki and attracted outsiders rejected or wounded by society. Members included Himiko Toga, Dabi, Spinner, Twice and Mr. Compress, among others. Its campaigns escalated from targeted assaults to national destabilization and merger into a larger revolutionary network.

Composition: What began as a small alliance collected recruits with very different grievances, including alienation, personal cruelty, radical ideology and loyalty to Tomura Shigaraki. Members relied on coordinated ambushes, disguise, dangerous Quirk combinations and Kurogiri’s transport. Their connections could be sincere even while their actions harmed countless others.

History and end: The group assaulted U.A., abducted a student, struggled with rival criminal factions and eventually joined a much larger liberationist movement. Its members experienced death, capture and betrayal during the wars.

cardPool.title: Paranormal Liberation Front
cardPool.value:
Organization: Paranormal Liberation Front

Overview: Massive villain coalition formed after the League of Villains defeated the Meta Liberation Army. It combined liberationist ideology, influential commercial resources and a widespread army under Tomura Shigaraki. Coordinated raids and uprisings inflicted enormous damage on hero society.

Structure: The coalition combined the League’s inner circle with the Meta Liberation Army’s vast infrastructure. Tomura Shigaraki held supreme command, with influential lieutenants and advisers coordinating different forces. Money, propaganda, businesses, hidden compounds and thousands of fighters gave the front nationwide reach.

Operations and collapse: Hero authorities discovered large connected centers of activity and launched simultaneous strikes. The conflict escalated into mass casualty warfare, prison crises and the near-breakdown of civilian confidence.

cardPool.title: Meta Liberation Army
cardPool.value:
Organization: Meta Liberation Army

Overview: Clandestine organization advocating unrestrained use of Quirks and opposition to restrictive social norms. Re-Destro and allied executives built institutional influence before the group’s confrontation with the League of Villains. Its resources and followers were absorbed into the Paranormal Liberation Front.

Ideology and resources: Inspired by Destro, the movement held that individuals should be free to use their Quirks without the restrictive norms imposed by modern government. Re-Destro built a network of executives, businesses, propaganda and dedicated followers. It presented itself as a liberation movement while preparing coercive, violent action on a massive scale.

Confrontation: The leadership invited the League of Villains into a trap at Deika, expecting to destroy the rival group. Instead, the battle devastated the city and ended with Re-Destro accepting Shigaraki’s authority.

cardPool.title: Wild, Wild Pussycats
cardPool.value:
Organization: Wild, Wild Pussycats

Overview: Professional rescue-hero team specializing in wilderness operations. Members include Mandalay, Pixie-Bob, Ragdoll and Tiger. Their teamwork, search capabilities and disaster preparation helped protect hero trainees during a forest training camp. The team is also part of Kota Izumi’s family and support network.

Team roles: Mandalay coordinates with telepathic messaging, Pixie-Bob alters the earth, Tiger specializes in close combat and Ragdoll was formerly able to Search for targets. The members combine wilderness rescue skills with unusually strong personal bonds and experience mentoring younger trainees. Their cat-themed presentation is deliberately cheerful and accessible.

Challenges: A violent training-camp attack placed the team and its young guests in severe danger. Ragdoll lost her Quirk after it was stolen but remained important to the team. Mandalay also cares for Kota Izumi, who lost his parents.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai
cardPool.value:
Organization: Shie Hassaikai

Overview: Criminal yakuza organization once led operationally by Kai Chisaki, also known as Overhaul. Its schemes involved exploiting Eri’s Rewind power to create Quirk-destroying ammunition and restore criminal authority. The group was dismantled and its leadership imprisoned.

Organization: An old yakuza group operated through debt, rank, loyalty and a reputation inherited from an earlier generation. Its aging boss was displaced in practice by Kai Chisaki, whose obsession with restoring criminal power drove a secret project involving Eri’s biological material. The group used specialized henchmen, restricted premises and clandestine distribution plans.

Fall: Pro Heroes and police traced its operation and raided the compound to free Eri and stop Quirk-destroying ammunition. Chisaki’s methods endangered even members supposedly under his protection. The raid ended the group’s ambitions and left its leader incapacitated.

cardPool.title: U.A. Faculty
cardPool.value:
Organization: U.A. Faculty

Overview: Teachers, administrators and support personnel responsible for educating future heroes and maintaining campus safety. Experienced heroes such as Shota Aizawa and Present Mic provide instruction, while All Might remains involved in school leadership. Izuku Midoriya joins the faculty in the postwar era.

Roles: The school employs educators with specializations in combat, rescue, academic study and support technology. Its familiar teachers include Shota Aizawa, Hizashi Yamada, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Snipe, Power Loader, Recovery Girl and others. Principal Nezu oversees the academy, with Toshinori Yagi serving in leadership in the later period.

Experience: Teachers have protected students through campus assaults, mass evacuations and the Final War. Nemuri Kayama died during the earlier nationwide conflict and should be remembered as a former colleague rather than an active adult-era instructor.

cardPool.title: Nomu
cardPool.value:
Organization: Nomu

Overview: Artificially modified beings created through human experimentation, often implanted with multiple Quirks. Many possess enhanced physical endurance, obedient conditioning and limited independent judgment. Higher-grade variants can show advanced intelligence and exceptionally dangerous adaptability.

Creation and varieties: Nomu are artificial beings built through severe modification and multiple Quirk implantation. Different examples range from relatively obedient low-level creatures to highly developed High-Ends with combat intelligence and exceptional physical ability. Surgical changes and regenerative factors can make them difficult for ordinary heroes to subdue.

Control and history: Their production relied on research associated with Kyudai Garaki and the All For One network. Some were designed as obedient shock troops while others retained fragments of personality or independent instincts.

cardPool.title: Pro Hero Licensing
cardPool.value:
Subject: Pro Hero Licensing

Context: Professional hero work is regulated by licensing, agencies, training standards and public accountability. U.A. students may receive provisional licenses during education; full careers demand years of development. Rankings and publicity influence employment but do not make a hero’s actions automatically ethical.

Legal framework: A person who wishes to act professionally as a hero must train, pass examinations and meet the licensing requirements for authorized response. Student provisional licenses allow supervised participation in specified situations.

Practice and responsibility: Schools prepare candidates in teamwork, communication, rescue assessment and nonlethal capture. Licenses and hero status involve public accountability, and powers can be dangerous if used without considering bystanders. A civilian reaching out to help another person can display heroism without automatically acquiring official police powers.

cardPool.title: Hero Billboard Chart
cardPool.value:
Subject: Hero Billboard Chart

Context: Public ranking of Pro Heroes that reflects reputation, contribution and effectiveness. Mirio Togata leads the adult-era chart, followed in the reunion-era ranking by Shoto Todoroki, Mt. Lady, Kamui Woods and Best Jeanist. Subsequent developments place Izuku Midoriya fourth and Katsuki Bakugo fifth, showing that standings change over time.

Ranking criteria: Professional heroes are listed according to a combination of achievement, public reputation and service, not a simple contest of combat strength. Positions respond to changing public attitudes and noteworthy rescues. A highly skilled hero can rank below someone more popular, and a sharp temperament can depress popularity despite extraordinary performance.

Later standings: In the adult period Mirio Togata holds first and Shoto Todoroki second, with Mt. Lady third. One public snapshot lists Kamui Woods fourth and Best Jeanist fifth while Bakugo sits fifteenth.

cardPool.title: Heteromorph Discrimination
cardPool.value:
Subject: Heteromorph Discrimination

Context: People with visibly nonhuman body types can face segregation, harassment, violence and exclusion. This prejudice contributed to widespread unrest and extremist recruitment. Mezo Shoji’s work emphasizes dialogue, dignity and meaningful action against hatred; public recognition of his efforts symbolizes a broader struggle.

Nature of the harm: People whose Quirks permanently change their faces or bodies may experience exclusion from public spaces, social hostility and open violence. These traits do not turn a person into a criminal or reveal what they believe.

Response: Extremist organizers exploited real grievances to encourage violent confrontation, while other heteromorphs chose rescue, public dialogue and patient reform. Mezo Shoji’s actions and the resulting recognition highlight the difference between opposing prejudice and targeting innocent people.

cardPool.title: Quirk Counseling
cardPool.value:
Subject: Quirk Counseling

Context: Support and guidance for children and adults adapting to innate superhuman traits, unusual bodily needs and social rejection. Inadequate counseling can compound fear, shame and dangerous habits, especially when powers involve biological compulsion. Ochaco Uraraka promotes school outreach and wider access to early assistance so support can begin before crises become violent.

Purpose: Counseling helps children understand the strengths, triggers and potential dangers of their individual powers. Some abilities are difficult to suppress, linked to biological urges or highly visible in ways that draw hostility.

Historical failings: Excessive pressure to appear normal and a lack of informed support left some children isolated and ashamed. Social rejection can worsen a dangerous situation long before violence occurs.

cardPool.title: Postwar Hero Society
cardPool.value:
Subject: Postwar Hero Society

Context: Following the defeat of All For One and the collapse of his criminal networks, Japan rebuilds damaged communities and its public institutions. Fewer new villains emerge, yet the work of heroes expands beyond battles to include education, prevention, rescue, reconciliation and addressing prejudice. Civilians are increasingly recognized as active participants in protecting one another.

Civic transition: Mass rebuilding demanded coordinated effort from heroes, medical workers, engineers, volunteers and ordinary residents. As organized villain attacks decline, emergencies do not disappear; rescue, counseling, prevention and community trust take a larger share of public attention.

Institutional limits: The loss of an old Symbol of Peace revealed how fragile a society becomes when everyone assumes one person will handle its dangers. Reform efforts address discrimination and poor early intervention as well as security.

cardPool.title: Support Technology
cardPool.value:
Subject: Support Technology

Context: Engineered equipment can complement Quirks, compensate for disability or give Quirkless people ways to work as heroes. Advances include adaptive prosthetics, armor, sensing systems, mobility supports and specialized training hardware. Equipment is subject to maintenance, durability, energy and cost limitations.

Categories: The industry produces mobility systems, reinforced costumes, environmental sensors, rescue tools, prostheses, communication devices and weapons designed around individual fighting styles. Equipment can protect a body from its own Quirk or allow a person with an impaired ability to regain practical independence.

Engineering limits: A complex prototype takes testing and funding, while field use requires repairs, replacement parts and training. Mechanical devices may imitate the outcome of some Quirks without creating or restoring their biological factor.

cardPool.title: One For All Vestiges
cardPool.value:
Subject: One For All Vestiges

Context: One For All carried impressions of previous holders inside a shared inner realm. These vestiges preserved memories and provided guidance or resistance to outside control. Their existence was tied to the Quirk’s accumulated factors, and their sacrifice during the final struggle ended Izuku’s access to the inherited abilities.

Inner landscape: The shared accumulated factor preserved impressions of successive bearers, often appearing as distinct figures with memories and advice. The space where they communicated was connected to the inherited power itself; it was not a physical room anyone could enter by ordinary travel.

Final conflict: These imprints could resist attempts at domination and ultimately served as a way to confront the hatred inside Tomura Shigaraki. Their deliberate transfer came with the destruction of Izuku’s natural access to the stockpiled inheritance.

cardPool.title: Deku Support Suit
cardPool.value:
Item: Deku Support Suit

Overview: Advanced powered armor developed by Mei Hatsume and Melissa Shield, drawing on data gathered from All Might’s prior armored battle. Class 1-A alumni funded its construction, with Katsuki Bakugo instrumental in supporting the project.

Design: The powered system combines protective plating, movement support and combat-response capabilities informed by accumulated data from advanced armor used in a major battle. It was engineered through international collaboration and financed by alumni who understood its intended user’s reflexes and style.

Operation: The suit allows a skilled user without an innate power to join dangerous rescue work while relying on learned fighting tactics and situational awareness. Its exact inventory of weapons and duplicate Quirk effects is not completely documented; it should not be credited with every ability once possessed through One For All.

cardPool.title: Armored All Might Suit
cardPool.value:
Item: Armored All Might Suit

Overview: Specialized armored fighting system used by Toshinori Yagi against All For One after his retirement from ordinary superpowered hero work. Its many tools were inspired by the abilities and experiences of Class 1-A, using engineering rather than restored One For All energy. Battle data from this equipment helped inspire the later suit built for Izuku.

Configuration: A high-grade technological combat system assembled to let an experienced but Quirkless former hero resist a vastly stronger adversary. It employs multiple specialized tools designed around the tactics of young hero students. These modules compensate for human limitations through protective structure, mobility and carefully timed countermeasures.

History and limitations: It was used under desperate conditions and suffered extreme destruction in combat. Its data later informed more advanced protective equipment for another Quirkless hero.

cardPool.title: Mirko Prosthetic Limbs
cardPool.value:
Item: Mirko Prosthetic Limbs

Overview: Advanced replacement limbs used by Rumi Usagiyama after the loss of multiple natural limbs during major battles. They preserve a degree of explosive mobility appropriate to her uncompromising fighting style and are repeatedly upgraded. Their performance comes from engineering and personal training, not regeneration granted by the Rabbit Quirk.

Function: Artificial limbs restore mechanical leverage and combat movement after devastating amputations. Strong anchoring and repeated adjustments are essential to survive abrupt landings, kicks and rapid shifts in position. The hero’s body must adapt to the altered weight and contact points through intensive physical training.

Limits: A prosthetic can break, jam or need replacement after a hard fight. Designs may be upgraded as engineers learn more about the wearer’s movement, but they are not equivalent to biological regeneration.

cardPool.title: Shinso Voice Persona Chords
cardPool.value:
Item: Shinso Voice Persona Chords

Overview: Specialized voice-altering equipment allowing Hitoshi Shinso to imitate other people’s speech. Used with Brainwashing, it increases his ability to draw verbal responses from targets who know his powers. Voice imitation alone does not control anyone; the target must respond and the Quirk’s usual conditions still apply.

Mechanism: A voice-modifying apparatus worn near the mouth changes spoken sound into the recognizable voice of another person. It can draw a reply from someone who would refuse to answer Hitoshi Shinso directly. The equipment does not release mind-altering waves; the relevant Quirk must still activate through verbal response.

Operational cautions: Visual identification, suspicion and barriers to conversation can defeat the deception. The mask requires functional electronics and sufficiently intelligible speech.

cardPool.title: Aoyama Navel Laser Belt
cardPool.value:
Item: Aoyama Navel Laser Belt

Overview: Focusing equipment worn by Yuga Aoyama to channel laser output from his abdomen. It helps direct a biologically troublesome power and forms a prominent part of his hero costume. The device is not the source of his Quirk, and removal does not make his body naturally compatible with the ability.

Construction: The waist device surrounds the abdomen and directs a powerful beam from the body through an external focusing mechanism. It is a support item worn with other metallic and white hero-costume components, not an artificial gun whose power exists without the user. The equipment helps manage a difficult and painful Quirk.

Limitations: Increasing firing time does not eliminate digestive upset or the strain of mismatched biology. A damaged belt may interfere with aiming and allow dangerous leakage.

cardPool.title: Quirk-Destroying Bullets
cardPool.value:
Item: Quirk-Destroying Bullets

Overview: Special ammunition manufactured through the abuse of Eri’s Rewind biological material by the Shie Hassaikai. Their purpose was to attack Quirk factors rather than inflict ordinary ballistic injury alone.

Origin: The Shie Hassaikai developed these drugs from biological material associated with Rewind, exploiting a captive child to attack the Quirk factor of a target. Different formulations could temporarily suppress or, in the perfected form, permanently destroy normal access to a Quirk.

Aftereffects: Mirio Togata lost use of Permeation after being struck and later regained it through Eri’s power.

Although their project promised power over the hero profession, the underlying method depended on destructive interference with biology. Both the criminal supply chain and the victims’ treatment are distinct matters: ending manufacture did not immediately reverse injuries already caused.

cardPool.title: Rise of All Might
cardPool.value:
Event: Rise of All Might

Overview: Toshinori Yagi inherits One For All from Nana Shimura and dedicates his life to fighting organized villainy. His public image as the Symbol of Peace helps reduce fear and crime while also creating unrealistic dependence on a single extraordinary protector. His long struggle with All For One changes both national hero culture and the lives of their successors. Before the peak of his career, Toshinori was trained by Nana Shimura and Gran Torino and learned that great strength carries responsibility as well as danger.

Hidden consequences: His duel with All For One left lasting internal injuries that eventually restricted the time he could maintain his famous muscular appearance. The public rarely understood how fragile that symbol had become. The resulting culture celebrated exceptional individuals but struggled to share responsibility among ordinary people and institutions.

cardPool.title: U.A. Training Camp Attack
cardPool.value:
Event: U.A. Training Camp Attack

Overview: The League of Villains attacks students and professional instructors during a forest training camp. The assault places young heroes in deadly danger, leaves Kota Izumi deeply affected and results in Katsuki Bakugo’s abduction. The incident exposes the limits of ordinary school security and accelerates conflict between public institutions and organized villains. A wilderness training program assembled first-year hero students under professional supervision. League attackers infiltrated the area, setting fires and launching separate assaults that scattered trainees and mentors. Several students fought to escape or protect nearby children despite limited experience and serious injuries. The attackers’ principal goal included capturing Katsuki Bakugo, believing his fierce temperament made him recruitable. Their success triggered a hostage crisis and a police-hero operation to recover him.

cardPool.title: Kamino Incident
cardPool.value:
Event: Kamino Incident

Overview: Professional heroes confront the League of Villains and All For One in Kamino. All Might defeats his old enemy in a decisive public battle but expends the remaining capacity of One For All. His retirement brings the end of the Symbol of Peace era and a new sense of insecurity. A memorial later transforms the location into a symbol of shared courage. Heroes and police raided League positions to retrieve the abducted student. The confrontation drew out All For One, whose overwhelming collection of Quirks turned a neighborhood into a public battleground. All Might fought beyond his failing limits while other heroes focused on evacuation and preventing further destruction. All Might ultimately defeated All For One with the final power he could muster and then publicly revealed he could no longer serve as the same superhuman protector. His declaration that the next generation must carry on reshaped national expectations.

cardPool.title: Shie Hassaikai Raid
cardPool.value:
Event: Shie Hassaikai Raid

Overview: Pro Heroes, police and students investigate and assault the Shie Hassaikai to rescue Eri and stop the manufacture of Quirk-destroying ammunition. The operation causes casualties and serious injuries, while exposing how criminal enterprise exploited a child’s power. The experience shapes Izuku and Mirio’s later responsibilities. Investigation linked the yakuza to trafficking in ammunition capable of suppressing or erasing Quirks. A joint police and hero response entered the Hassaikai compound, navigating changing corridors, hidden rooms and dangerous defenders. Rescuers sought Eri while attempting to stop production without needlessly harming her or other captives. Mirio Togata lost his Quirk while defending Eri, and Sir Nighteye died from injuries suffered in the raid. Izuku confronted Kai Chisaki after Eri escaped his control.

cardPool.title: Deika Liberation Conflict
cardPool.value:
Event: Deika Liberation Conflict

Overview: The League of Villains confronts the Meta Liberation Army in Deika City. Intense fighting devastates the region and strengthens Tomura Shigaraki’s destructive capabilities. After the battle, defeated liberationist leaders join forces with the League, helping create the Paranormal Liberation Front and escalating the threat beyond isolated gangs. Meta Liberation Army leaders challenged the League of Villains in a city where many inhabitants were already aligned with their movement. Fighting spread among streets and buildings as the rival factions revealed dangerous abilities and personal histories. Enormous civilian and structural losses followed. Shigaraki’s destructive Quirk reached an unprecedented scale and the Army’s leader accepted his power rather than continue futile resistance. The merger brought the League a broad network of fighters, financing and propaganda.

cardPool.title: Paranormal Liberation War
cardPool.value:
Event: Paranormal Liberation War

Overview: A nationwide hero offensive targets the Paranormal Liberation Front and the hospital where Tomura Shigaraki is being altered. The battle unleashes multiple Nomu and causes widespread destruction, deaths and public distrust. Midnight dies and several leading heroes suffer grievous injuries. The ensuing collapse of confidence produces mass evacuations and violent unrest. Professional heroes, police and trained students launched raids on a mountain assembly point and a hospital complex supporting the Front. The operation was intended to interrupt Shigaraki’s experimental transformation and arrest leaders before their forces could mobilize. Instead, numerous Nomu were released, giant combatants ravaged populated areas and Shigaraki’s Decay spread across the terrain. Casualties included the hero Midnight and many civilians. Survivors such as Endeavor, Hawks, Eraser Head and Mirko sustained lasting injuries or losses.

cardPool.title: Dark Hero Period
cardPool.value:
Event: Dark Hero Period

Overview: After mass prison breaks and mounting public anxiety, Izuku operates apart from his classmates while pursuing those connected to All For One. Exhaustion and self-sacrifice threaten his wellbeing. Former classmates intervene, demonstrating that communal support is necessary even for the most powerful protector. Public attitudes toward sheltering vulnerable heroes begin to shift. With society frightened and villain attacks multiplying, Izuku left the shelter of ordinary school life to track enemies linked to All For One. He worked with remaining professionals while steadily exhausting his own health and avoiding friends to keep them from danger. His isolation embodied the old belief that a sufficiently strong hero must carry everything alone. His classmates confronted him, refusing to abandon him simply because he wanted to protect them.

cardPool.title: Final War
cardPool.value:
Event: Final War

Overview: Heroes launch a coordinated effort to separate All For One’s forces and prevent his schemes from succeeding. Many groups battle across Japan. Izuku confronts Tomura Shigaraki and sacrifices One For All in an attempt to reach the person beneath the villain’s hatred. Other clashes leave extensive injury and loss, including final confrontations involving the Todoroki family and Himiko Toga. All For One and Tomura are defeated and the surviving communities begin recovery. A coordinated hero plan separated the main enemy forces into different battlefields so they could not easily combine their strengths. Conflicts took place over fortified arenas, cities and evacuation routes. Fighters faced All For One, Shigaraki, major Nomu and other remaining leaders while civilians and support workers contributed information, engineering and emergency aid.

cardPool.title: Reconstruction and Graduation
cardPool.value:
Event: Reconstruction and Graduation

Overview: The years immediately following the Final War involve funerals, rebuilding, rehabilitation, social reckoning and the completion of disrupted schooling. U.A. students continue training while grieving their losses. Izuku’s last One For All embers fade by graduation, and he eventually finds a vocation teaching future heroes. International support and local volunteers joined professional teams clearing damaged neighborhoods and restoring transport, schools and homes. Survivors mourned lost people while injured heroes underwent prolonged treatment. U.A. resumed lessons and held delayed graduation activities, but the experience changed how its students understood future responsibilities. Yuga Aoyama chose to leave school and begin earning his place independently after admitting his role as an unwilling informant. Hitoshi Shinso transferred into the hero class in his place.

cardPool.title: Eight Years After the Final War
cardPool.value:
Event: Eight Years After the Final War

Overview: Approximately eight years after the decisive conflict, former Class 1-A students pursue professional careers and public-service work. Izuku Midoriya teaches at U.A. while many classmates work as Pro Heroes. Mirio Togata leads the ranking, Shoto Todoroki rises to second and Ochaco Uraraka expands Quirk counseling. Hero society seeks prevention and social care rather than celebrating battle alone. Around eight years after the war, many former U.A. classmates are working as adults.

Public aspirations begin shifting: children can imagine becoming engineers, clinicians or technical specialists rather than treating Pro Hero rankings as the only meaningful measure of success. Helping a stranger remains the simplest example of responsibility even as the professional world changes.

cardPool.title: Class 1-A Reunion
cardPool.value:
Event: Class 1-A Reunion

Overview: Former classmates gather to recognize Shoto Todoroki’s number-two ranking. Their conversation reveals different professional pressures, including Katsuki Bakugo’s volatile popularity and Izuku Midoriya’s intention to remain a teacher. Izuku and Ochaco Uraraka mutually acknowledge a desire to spend more time together. The gathering highlights lasting friendship without suggesting every graduate has the same career or relationship. The former classmates gather to congratulate Shoto on reaching second place among professional heroes. Conversation turns from hero rankings to daily schedules, agency work and how falling rates of villain attacks are changing their jobs. Katsuki’s poor public relations contrast with his skills, and Izuku insists he likes teaching even after obtaining equipment for fieldwork. Shoto expresses interest in enjoying ordinary parts of life, including creating bowls and chopsticks for soba.

cardPool.title: Deku Returns to Hero Work
cardPool.value:
Event: Deku Returns to Hero Work

Overview: Class 1-A alumni fund an advanced suit developed by Mei Hatsume and Melissa Shield for their Quirkless former classmate. All Might delivers the equipment to Izuku, who resumes active Pro Hero work without abandoning teaching. Later hero rankings place him fourth, while Katsuki Bakugo rises to fifth. This development marks a technological path to heroism rather than the return of his lost biological inheritance. Years of research into powered combat equipment build on data gathered during All Might’s desperate armored confrontation.

The timing matters: the armor arrives years after the original power disappears, making the return the product of research and friendship rather than hidden stockpiled energy. The later ranking reflects actual public response to his professional activity, not a retrospective award for his earlier exploits.

cardPool.title: Toya Todoroki Final Years
cardPool.value:
Event: Toya Todoroki Final Years

Overview: After suffering catastrophic injuries in the Final War, Toya Todoroki remains in severe medical condition. His surviving family members confront their painful history while recognizing that neither apologies nor sacrifice can undo decades of harm. Toya dies during the years before the adult reunion, leaving the family to reckon with grief and the consequences of his choices. After the war, Toya remains alive but severely damaged inside a special medical care unit. Speaking is painful and limited; his family is given only short opportunities to see him.

Toya eventually dies before the eight-year reunion. The family mourns him while its surviving members continue making their own choices: atonement, distance, employment and new relationships do not all follow the same path. His death does not retroactively excuse his violence or erase the abuse that helped shape it. No single meeting reconciles the family.

cardPool.title: Jin Bubaigawara
cardPool.value:
Name: Jin Bubaigawara

Age: 31 (at death)

Alias: Twice

Occupation: Deceased former League of Villains member

Abilities: Double created complete duplicates of people or objects when the user knew their measurements. Copies could multiply in large numbers; each was less durable than the original.

Personality: Jin was talkative, theatrical and frequently spoke in contradicting pairs of statements, as if arguing with himself. A terrible incident involving his own duplicates left him unsure whether he was the original, and this fear fed profound anxiety about personal identity. His friendship with Himiko Toga and loyalty to the League were unusually sincere.

Appearance: An adult man with a lean frame, messy blond hair and a small amount of facial hair. His villain attire was a tight black bodysuit with pale markings and a mask covering most of his face, leaving only the eyes visible. He sometimes removed the covering but feared losing control of his sense of self.

cardPool.title: Mirai Sasaki
cardPool.value:
Name: Mirai Sasaki

Age: 38 (at death)

Alias: Sir Nighteye

Occupation: Deceased Pro Hero and former sidekick of All Might

Abilities: Foresight let him view a target’s future after specified contact and eye contact, with strict time limits and conditions. He also fought using specially weighted seals and precise tactics.

Personality: Mirai was austere, sharply analytical and unusually demanding of people who joined his agency. He prized humor in heroes but expressed that preference through severe and sometimes intimidating tests. He believed public reassurance required deliberate preparation rather than empty smiles.

Appearance: He was a tall, slim adult with a long angular face, narrow eyes, tidy dark hair and square glasses. He usually wore a fitted office suit, tie and clean gloves rather than a flashy hero uniform, carrying himself like a disciplined businessman. His expression was stern and often unreadable; a small change in his brows could signal disapproval.

cardPool.title: Nezu
cardPool.value:
Name: Nezu

Alias: Principal Nezu

Occupation: Principal of U.A. High School

Abilities: High Specs grants exceptional intelligence and reasoning ability. His small animal body requires tailored equipment and cannot be confused with the human anatomy of most faculty.

Personality: Nezu is courteous, playful and intellectually formidable, frequently speaking in a tone that makes serious analysis sound almost whimsical. He enjoys elaborate tests of reasoning and tends to plan several layers ahead. His understanding of cruel experimentation gives him a deeply personal concern for how society treats beings perceived as unusual.

Appearance: He is a small, white-furred mammalian figure with a pointed muzzle, dark eyes, rounded ears and a long tail. He often wears an immaculate suit, vest and shoes sized for his proportions, sometimes carrying a cup of tea. His body language is animated and expressive, combining the appearance of a friendly animal with a dignified administrator.

cardPool.title: Itsuka Kendo
cardPool.value:
Name: Itsuka Kendo

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Battle Fist

Occupation: Pro Hero; former U.A. Class 1-B student

Abilities: Big Fist enlarges both hands to huge size, increasing their usefulness in striking, restraint and shielding. It does not enlarge the entire body.

Personality: Itsuka is outgoing, sensible and dependable, frequently acting as a counterweight when classmates become competitive or arrogant. She has a strong sense of fair play and wants the people around her to perform well rather than simply humiliating a rival class. Practical compassion matters more to her than drawing applause.

Appearance: She is a tall, athletic young woman with a strong posture, turquoise eyes and orange hair tied in a high ponytail. Her hero clothing includes a dark, Chinese-influenced outfit designed to leave room for the rapid expansion of her hands. The enlarged fists become enormous compared with her ordinary arms when her Quirk is active.

cardPool.title: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu
cardPool.value:
Name: Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu

Age: Approximately 24–25 (later epilogue)

Alias: Real Steel

Occupation: Pro Hero; former U.A. Class 1-B student

Abilities: Steel transforms the body into tough metal, supporting powerful physical combat and protection against impact. Prolonged exertion and heat impose limitations.

Personality: Tetsutetsu is loud, passionate and eager to prove himself in direct competition. He admires people with steadfast courage and is quick to treat a rival as a friend after a fair contest. His straightforward manner can appear reckless, yet he does not shy away from protecting someone when an attack would injure them.

Appearance: He is a broad-shouldered, muscular young man with spiky pale gray hair, dark eyes and a square, strongly expressive face. His appearance resembles a rough, energetic fighter even without using his Quirk. When transformed, his body takes on a metallic texture and shine.

cardPool.title: Chiyo Shuzenji
cardPool.value:
Name: Chiyo Shuzenji

Alias: Recovery Girl

Occupation: U.A. school nurse and healing specialist

Abilities: Heal accelerates a patient’s natural healing processes through a kiss but consumes the patient’s stamina and cannot reliably overcome every critical injury.

Personality: Chiyo is practical, affectionate and capable of sharp reprimands when students take foolish risks. She does not confuse bravery with reckless self-injury and has repeatedly warned ambitious hero trainees against relying on medical recovery as an excuse to destroy their bodies. She values the ordinary discipline of proper first aid and rest.

Appearance: She is a very short elderly woman with pale gray hair arranged in small curls, a lined face and large dark eyes behind her medical headwear. Her white and pink nurse’s clothing and cane form a familiar part of U.A.’s infirmary. Her small body does not prevent her from being authoritative.

cardPool.title: Naomasa Tsukauchi
cardPool.value:
Name: Naomasa Tsukauchi

Alias: None established

Occupation: Police detective involved in major villain investigations

Abilities: Experienced investigator and coordinator; no reliably established named Quirk is required for his professional role.

Personality: Naomasa is diligent, observant and earnest about civilian safety. He recognizes the importance of cooperation between police and licensed heroes and is willing to challenge decisions when they create unnecessary danger. His measured temperament provides a stabilizing influence among people whose powers could otherwise encourage impulsive action. He values evidence, timing and the legal responsibilities attached to arrests.

Appearance: He is an adult man with neatly kept dark hair, a plain but professional appearance and a serious expression. A business suit or police clothing fits his everyday duties better than a battle costume. He commonly carries himself with calm attention, listening before offering a conclusion.

cardPool.title: Double
cardPool.value:
Ability: Double

Description: Double creates a near-identical duplicate of a known person or object based on accurate measurements. A copy can act independently, use its original’s Quirk and be destroyed by sufficient force. The user must retain enough information about the target to construct a convincing duplicate.

Applications: A duplicate can assist rescue, distract an opponent, act as a decoy or multiply into an army when copies reproduce themselves. Copies of a person are not mindless puppets; they carry recognizable habits and can disagree or act unpredictably.

Limits: A duplicate is less durable than its original and can collapse into mudlike material after taking damage. Multiplication does not erase the danger to innocent people caught between the copies.

History: The Quirk’s broad replication potential made it one of the League of Villains’ greatest strategic advantages. Its original bearer died before the last nationwide conflict.

cardPool.title: Foresight
cardPool.value:
Ability: Foresight

Description: Foresight grants the ability to perceive future actions and events associated with an individual. Activation requires close, deliberate interaction involving physical contact and eye contact. It is not continuous global awareness of every possible event.

Applications: The wielder can anticipate a chosen person’s movements, avoid attacks and investigate how an unfolding incident may proceed. The ability is especially valuable with disciplined observation and carefully prepared teams.

Limits: The power has strict timing restrictions and cannot be used without consequence on every person encountered. Its predictions can leave the user emotionally convinced that a terrible outcome is inevitable, leading to hesitation or overconfidence.

History: Foresight was employed by the investigator and hero Sir Nighteye in professional operations before his death during the Shie Hassaikai case.

cardPool.title: Stain Bladed Weapons
cardPool.value:
Weapons: Stain Bladed Weapons

Description: A varied arsenal of swords and smaller edged weapons carried by Chizome Akaguro. Blades increase his reach and, more importantly, give him opportunities to draw blood. His clothing supports carrying multiple weapons while remaining mobile.

Use: Close-range cuts or a blade thrown in an ambush can create blood access necessary for Bloodcurdle. The same weapons can intimidate or deflect attacks in ordinary combat. Their danger comes from trained precision combined with a Quirk condition, not from an enchanted property of the metal.

Limitations: A blade can be lost, trapped, broken or intercepted. The Quirk is not contained inside the weapon, and another person wielding it does not automatically paralyze an opponent.

Handling: Their effectiveness depends on accurate strikes and reaching an opponent; carrying several blades offers replacements if one is lost.
